commits.commit_message:
hotfix(frontend/marketplace): show expert cards to signed-out visitors (#14337)

### Why / What / How

**Why:** #14313 shipped public, shareable expert pages, but the
marketplace only renders the "Meet the AI Experts" section when the
`hire-experts` flag is on and the visitor is signed in. The flag is off
in production while Experts are in beta, so nobody browsing the
marketplace can see the cards, and the pages are reachable only by
direct link.

**What:** The experts section now renders for signed-out visitors
regardless of the flag. Signed-in users keep the flag gate, so the beta
stays invisible to them. Visitors don't get the "View your team" and
"raise your own expert" links, which need an account.

**How:** `MainMarketplacePage` shows the section when the visitor is
signed out (once auth has resolved) or the flag is on.
`useExpertsSection` fetches templates unconditionally, since `GET
/api/experts/templates` is public as of #14313, and keeps the hired
roster behind the session. `ExpertsSection` drops its signed-in early
return and hides the two account links for visitors; the empty/error
fallback (the raise link) still renders nothing for visitors. Each page
already handles what comes next: "Get started" when signed out, "Coming
soon" for signed-in users outside the beta.

### Changes 🏗️

- `MainMarketplacePage`: `showExperts = !isUserLoading && (!isLoggedIn
|| isHireExpertsEnabled)` replaces the flag-only gate.
- `useExpertsSection`: templates query no longer gated on `isLoggedIn`;
roster query still is.
- `ExpertsSection`: no signed-out early return; "View your team" and the
raise link only for signed-in users; empty/error state renders nothing
for visitors.
- `experts-section.test.tsx`: the signed-out case now expects the cards
without the account links and no roster request; new case checks the
section stays hidden for signed-in users outside the beta.

`SECURITY.md` is the repository's public security policy: how to report
a vulnerability, what happens to a report, the safe-harbour terms for
researchers, what is in scope, and who is credited. This replaces the
November 2024 policy with the revised policy agreed in June 2026 and
fills in its acknowledgments list from the published GitHub security
advisories.

- Replaces the 2024 `SECURITY.md` with the June 2026 revision, converted
from the agreed draft with its headings, lists, links, table and
emphasis preserved and the wording unchanged. The draft's review
comments are not carried over.
- Section 13 lists the 34 researchers who hold an accepted reporter,
finder or analyst credit on at least one of the 40 published advisories,
ordered by their first advisory, with a per-person advisory count and
the GitHub display name where one is set.
- Maintainers credited in coordinator or remediation roles are not
listed as researchers (Pwuts, ntindle, majdyz, kcze, Bentlybro,

### Why / What / How

**Why:** Expert profiles on the marketplace open in a dialog, so there
is no URL to share or deep-link to, and nothing to show a visitor who is
not yet in the Experts beta.

**What:** Each expert card now links to a dedicated page at
`/marketplace/experts/[expertId]`. The page shows the profile in full
and carries the hire flow. Signed-out visitors see the full profile with
a "Get started" action that takes them to sign-up and back to the expert
afterwards. Signed in without the Experts flag, the page shows "Coming
soon".

**How:** The page is a client route in the team page's mould. It reads
the template from the experts templates list, which moves to a public
router so a signed-out deep link renders the profile, and the hired
roster (session only) to show "On your team" with a chat link. The hire,
voice pick and celebration logic moves out of the dialog hook into
`useHireFlow` unchanged; the voice pick opens in a dialog on the page
and dismissing it still celebrates and hands off to the copilot with
`kickoff=1`. `ExpertProfileSheet` and its content are deleted and the
cards lose their click handler.

- `marketplace/experts/[expertId]/page.tsx` with `useExpertPage`,
`useHireFlow`, and components: `ExpertPageHeader`, `ExpertHireActions`,
`ExpertAbout`, `ExpertSkills`, `ExpertWorkflowList`,
`ExpertWorkflowCard`, `ExpertComingSoon`, `ExpertSection`.
- The page is a single 760px column in the Linear/Raycast mould: avatar,
name, role and tagline in the header with the hire action beside them, a

grid of cards that pull their preview image from the marketplace

commits.commit_title: fix(backend/executor): skip scheduled runs for paywalled users quietly (#14325)
commits.commit_message:
fix(backend/executor): skip scheduled runs for paywalled users quietly (#14325)

### Why / What / How

**Why.** The scheduler fires saved schedules on their cron regardless of
whether the owner still has a subscription. `add_graph_execution`
correctly rejects those with `UserPaywalledError`, but `_execute_graph`
only knows how to skip paused, missing, or unavailable experts quietly;
everything else lands in the catch-all and is logged at error level. A
handful of one-minute schedules owned by users without a subscription
therefore log an error every tick: Sentry issue `AUTOGPT-SERVER-96T` is
at roughly 138k events in 30 days and still climbing, the single
noisiest issue in prod, drowning out real scheduler failures.

**What.** Handle `UserPaywalledError` the same way
`ExpertRunPausedError` already is: log at info and move on. The schedule
stays registered, so it resumes on its own the moment the user
subscribes; nothing is deleted or paused.

**How.** One `except` branch placed next to the existing paused-expert
branch, plus a unit test mirroring
`test_execute_graph_quietly_skips_unavailable_expert`: the
onboarding-run counter is not touched and no record at error level is
emitted.

Pausing or unregistering schedules when a subscription lapses is a
product decision (SECRT-2376) and is deliberately out of scope here;
this only stops the noise.

### Changes 🏗️

- `backend/executor/scheduler.py`: import `UserPaywalledError`; skip
quietly in `_execute_graph`
- `backend/executor/scheduler_unit_test.py`:
`test_execute_graph_quietly_skips_paywalled_user`

No API surface change, no configuration changes, no `data/*.py` changes.

commits.commit_title: fix(backend/copilot-bot): read the post a Discord thread was created from (#14330)
commits.commit_message:
fix(backend/copilot-bot): read the post a Discord thread was created from (#14330)

### Why / What / How

**Why.** When someone turns a channel post into a thread and @mentions
the bot with "make this happen", the bot answers that it has no idea
what "this" refers to. A thread created from a post shares that post's
id, but the post itself stays in the parent channel and never appears in
`thread.history()`. The adapter only ever read the thread's own history,
so for a freshly created thread it saw nothing at all. #13323 widened
the history read to the full thread; it still never included the origin
message, which is why this kept happening.

**What.** `_thread_history` now fetches the thread's starter message and
prepends it as the oldest entry, so the bot reads the post the thread
was opened from before anything said inside the thread.

**How.** `_thread_starter_entry` uses the cached
`thread.starter_message` when discord.py has it, otherwise fetches
message `thread.id` from the parent channel. Threads opened without an
origin message (`create_thread` with a name only) get `NotFound` and
contribute nothing. A starter authored by the bot is skipped, matching
how its own messages are already dropped from history. The entry sits
outside the history character budget so a long thread can never truncate
its own origin away. A failure to read the thread's history no longer
discards the starter either.

### Changes 🏗️

- `copilot/bot/adapters/discord/adapter.py`: `_thread_starter_entry`,
wired into `_thread_history`
- `adapter_test.py`: starter fetched from the parent and listed first;
thread without an origin message has no starter entry; cached starter
used and bot-authored starter skipped

No API surface change, no configuration changes, no `data/*.py` changes.

feat(backend): wire the application metrics that were defined but never recorded (#14319)

## Why

While verifying the alert rules in infra against prod Prometheus, three
application counters turned out to be defined in `instrumentation.py`
with nothing feeding them:

| Metric | In prod (2026-09-03) | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `autogpt_graph_executions_total` | one series, `success`, value **2**
ever | `record_graph_execution` was only called from the legacy `v1
execute_graph` route; the shared `add_graph_execution` path (10 callers)
recorded nothing |
| `autogpt_rate_limit_hits_total` | absent | `record_rate_limit_hit` had
zero callers |
| `autogpt_scheduler_jobs` | absent | the gauge was never set (its
scrape port is also wrong; infra#400) |

The first is the single most useful product signal we have, and the
second is what would have lit up during the August Stripe-quota
incident. The third already has alerts on it that have been inert since
they were written.

## What

- **`add_graph_execution`** becomes a thin recording wrapper over
`_add_graph_execution` (same signature, forwarded by keyword), so every
caller feeds the counter exactly once. The duplicate calls in
`v1.execute_graph` are removed; `record_graph_operation` there is
untouched. A `UserPaywalledError` is a policy gate, not an execute
outcome, and is deliberately not counted; `GraphValidationError` →
`validation_error` and any other exception → `error`, the mapping v1
already used.
- **Both live rate limiters** (`credits_rate_limit.py`,
`search/rate_limit.py`) call `record_rate_limit_hit(endpoint, user_id)`
on their 429 path.
- **Scheduler** sets
`SCHEDULER_JOBS{job_type="execution",status="scheduled"}` from the job
list in `_get_jobs_cached`, where it already reads them.

No new metrics, no label changes, no cardinality change.

## How

Verified in the test VM's backend container (tree synced, Prisma client
regenerated, migrations applied):

- `pytest` on the four touched test suites: **127 passed**, including
five new tests: the wrapper records `success` / `validation_error` /
`error` and skips paywall; each limiter records on 429 and not under the
cap; the gauge reflects the job count.
- pyright: 0 errors on the five source files. black / isort / ruff clean
on the pinned versions.

### After deploy

The three rules in infra#399 stop being inert.
`autogpt_graph_executions_total` will show `error` / `validation_error`
series for the first time, so expect the execute-error alert to be
*able* to fire — the thresholds there have a volume floor, so a lone
failure won't.

commits.commit_title: feat(backend/executor): count graph runs by terminal status (#14310)
commits.commit_message:
feat(backend/executor): count graph runs by terminal status (#14310)

## Why

`autogpt_graph_executions_total` is incremented at the **REST layer**
when an execute request is accepted or raises. Nothing records whether
the run then actually COMPLETED or FAILED inside the executor. So a
graph that starts fine and dies ten nodes in is invisible to Prometheus,
and "users' agents are failing", the single most important product
signal, cannot be alerted on.

This came out of an audit of what the backend exports versus what has an
alert: of ~19 application metrics, one was alerted on, and the
run-outcome one didn't exist at all. The alert-side half is in the infra
repo this PR provides the series it needs for the part it currently
can't see.

## What

- `autogpt_graph_run_completions_total{status}` in
`backend/monitoring/instrumentation.py`, with a
`record_graph_run_completion(status)` helper next to the existing
recorders.
- Incremented in `backend/executor/manager.py` inside
`update_graph_execution_state` and `async_update_graph_execution_state`,
the one place a run's terminal status is persisted, for `COMPLETED`,
`FAILED`, `TERMINATED` only.

## How

Non-terminal status updates pass through untouched, so a run is counted
exactly once, at its terminal transition. The label is the enum's value:
three bounded values, three series per executor pod, no cardinality
concern.

### Verified

- `backend/monitoring/instrumentation_test.py` (new): the counter
increments per status. Passes.
- `backend/executor/manager_test.py` (existing): passes with the change.
- black / isort / ruff clean on the pinned versions.

Run in the test VM's backend container after syncing the tree,
regenerating the Prisma client and applying migrations, since the image
predates the current schema.

### Follow-up

Once this is deployed and the series is visible in prod Prometheus, the
corresponding alert is a small addition to `application_rules.yml` in
the infra repo: failure ratio over completions with a volume floor, same
shape as the execute-error rule there.

commits.commit_title: feat(backend/copilot-bot): let the Discord bot mention server members and roles, never everyone (#14331)
commits.commit_message:
feat(backend/copilot-bot): let the Discord bot mention server members and roles, never everyone (#14331)

### Why / What / How

**Why.** The Discord bot could only ping users who were @mentioned in
the message that triggered it. Anyone else it named, including the
person asking and people it looked up, came out as plain `@Name` text:
formatted like a mention, pinging nobody. Posts the bot makes on its own
(channel posts, new threads) could not ping at all, because that send
path never resolved mentions and the client-level
`AllowedMentions.none()` applied.

**What.** The bot may now @mention any member of the server it is
posting in, by display name or username, and any role in that server.
`@everyone` and `@here` stay off: they are never looked up, the default
role is never allowlisted, and every send carries
`AllowedMentions(everyone=False)`, so a raw `@everyone` in model output
stays plain text and Discord would refuse it anyway. Proactive posts and
thread creation go through the same resolver. Inbound `<@&role>`
mentions are shown to the model as `@RoleName`, matching what already
happened for users.

**How.** Resolution happens at send time from the names the bot actually
used. `_mentionables_for` takes each distinct `@Word` in the outgoing
text and runs a gateway member query for that prefix
(`guild.query_members`, which needs no privileged intent and works on
any server), then lets the shared word-bounded resolver match display
names and usernames exactly. Roles come from the cached guild roles and
are matched by name first, so a role name never triggers a member query.
The author and inbound mentions remain on the list as before. Lookups
are capped at 8 names per message and 20 matches each; a failed or
timed-out query is logged and skipped, never blocking the send.

Roles ride the existing platform-neutral `(name, id)` allowlist with a
`role:` prefix on the id, so `text.resolve_mentions` and every other
adapter are untouched; the Discord resolver emits `<@&id>` for those and
lists them as roles in the ping object. Ambiguous names (two members
sharing a display name) stay plain text, as before.

No intents, settings or environment changes. Slack is not changed here;
the same policy there needs the `usergroups:read` scope and a separate
look.

### Changes 🏗️

- `copilot/bot/adapters/discord/adapter.py`: send-time member and role
lookup (`_mentionables_for`, `_mention_queries`), role mention markup
and ping object, mentions resolved on chunked sends, inbound role
mentions rendered readable
- `adapter_test.py`: members and roles resolve and `@everyone` does not;
DM keeps only known users; a failed member query still yields roles;
candidate extraction strips punctuation and skips `@everyone`; role
markup and ping object; `@everyone` stays plain when not allowlisted;
inbound role mentions become readable

No API surface change, no configuration changes, no `data/*.py` changes.

failed (test VM backend container, tree synced)

commits.commit_title: fix(frontend/copilot): make completing a Connect card actually connect (#14316)
commits.commit_message:
fix(frontend/copilot): make completing a Connect card actually connect (#14316)

### Why / What / How

**Why:** This PR makes completing a Connect card in the copilot actually
connect the integration and send the follow-up turn.

Three separate defects — dropped OAuth scopes, a credentials provider
that never learns a new credential exists in a connectors-only chain,
and a connectors-only chain card with no completion path — combined so
that clicking Connect, signing in, and seeing the "Connected via OAuth"
toast left the row still reading "Connect" with no follow-up turn sent.
Reported by Reinier in #breakage on 2026-09-03 with a screen recording;
Toran noted it was the third bug of this shape in about two weeks.

**What:** Fixes three defects on the connect path, and adds one test
that drives the whole path end to end so the next drift is caught at the
seam rather than in production.

**How:** Any one of the three alone produces "nothing happens", which is
why this reads as unfixable from the outside:

1. **The required scopes are dropped.** `ConnectorRow` →
`ConnectCredentialDialog` → `useConnectCredentialDialog` →
`useOAuthConnect` → `getV1InitiateOauthFlow(provider)` — no scopes. The
endpoint accepts them (`router.py:135`) and the path this replaced
passed them (`useCredentialsInput.ts:259`). The grant comes back without
`repo`, `hasRequiredScopes` rejects the credential, and the row can
never be satisfied — every retry drops them again. Now threaded from the
card's schema down to the initiate call.
2. **Nothing tells the credentials provider a credential exists.**
`invalidateConnectionQueries` invalidates a React Query key, and
`CredentialsProvider` reloads off that query's cache events — but in a
connectors-only chain nothing has that query mounted, so invalidation
emits no event and the list is never re-read. `useOAuthConnect` now
calls the provider's existing `reload()`, the same way
`AyrshareConnectButton` already does.
3. **A connectors-only chain card has no completion path.**
`ChainActionCard` renders Proceed only for inputs or questions, and
`SetupRequirementsCard`'s auto-send gates on a store whose
`markConnected` runs only from `markSent` — after a card has already
sent. Such a card now sends once its credential is satisfied, reusing
the existing `tryClaimAutoDismiss` claim so parallel cards cannot
double-send.

Introduced by [**feat(frontend): add copilot tool chain UI** -
#13773](https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT/pull/13773)
(`a6df3d3381`) behind the `new-tool-ui` flag, which defaulted off;
shipped to everyone by [**refactor(frontend): drop the new-tool-ui flag
and commit to the tool chain UX** -
#14164](https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT/pull/14164)
(`948b55ea81`), which dropped the flag. The standalone (non-chain) card
still uses the scoped path, which is why this reads as "anymore".

### Changes 🏗️

- `useOAuthConnect`: accepts optional `scopes`, passes them to the
initiate call, and reloads the credentials provider after the token
exchange. Every other caller is unaffected — the argument is optional
and a provider-level connect still asks for defaults.
- `ConnectCredentialDialog` / `useConnectCredentialDialog`: forward
`schema.credentials_scopes`. This also fixes the builder's "Add
credential" flow, which had the same gap.
- `SetupRequirementsCard`: a connectors-only card inside a chain
auto-sends once its credential is complete.
- New `ToolChain/__tests__/connect-card-flow.test.tsx`: three cases
driving ToolChain → SetupRequirementsCard → ChainActionCard →
ConnectorRow → ConnectCredentialDialog → useOAuthConnect against MSW.

### Verified

I executed this locally against the real backend and GitHub client —
confirming the authorize URL now carries the correct scope — and through
the test suite, where each of the three fixes is pinned by a case that
fails on the pre-fix code and passes after, with the surrounding
copilot/credentials/onboarding regression suites staying green. The
OAuth consent screen itself was reasoned about rather than executed,
since completing it needs a human at GitHub's permission page; full
command output, the live URL comparison, and the regression sweep are in
the [evidence comment
below](https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT/pull/14316#issuecomment-5532926041).

### Why this keeps happening

All three incidents break the *composition* of the connect chain while
every individual link keeps passing its own tests, because every test on
this path mocks the layer beneath it: `ToolChain.test.tsx` mocks
`SetupRequirementsCard`, `ChainActionCard.test.tsx` mocks
`ConnectCredentialDialog`, `ConnectCredentialDialog.test.tsx` stubs
`useOAuthConnect`. The scope contract *was* pinned by a test —
`CredentialsInput.test.tsx:217` — but on the path
[#13773](https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT/pull/13773)
replaced; the replacement inherited coverage of its own layer and none
of the contract it took over.

The 08-24 incident ([**fix(frontend): MCP OAuth popup fails with
'Sign-in window was closed' on COOP providers** -
#14141](https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT/pull/14141),
`popup.closed` lying under COOP) does **not** share that root cause: it
is a browser-platform behaviour no Node test can reproduce, and it needs
a Playwright case instead. That distinction, and the remaining gaps this
PR does not close, are tracked in [**The copilot's connect chain has no
end-to-end test, so each layer's contract drifts independently** -
#14315](https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT/issues/14315)
(OPEN-3471).

- [x] I have clearly listed my changes in the PR description
- [x] I have made a test plan
- [x] I have tested my changes according to the test plan:
- [x] The chain's Connect button initiates OAuth carrying the block's
required scopes
- [x] A connected card flips to "Connected. Continuing…" and sends the
follow-up turn
- [x] A downgraded grant still reads as not-connected and sends nothing
  - [x] Every case fails on the pre-fix code for the right reason
  - [x] Surrounding copilot / credentials / onboarding suites stay green
  - [x] A finished card re-mounting from chat history sends nothing
  - [x] An API-key connect continues the chat too
  - [x] The sign-in offers the existing account for scope upgrade
- [x] Live: the authorize URL carries `scope=repo` with the fix and
`scope=` without it
- [x] Manual run against a real GitHub consent screen — not done, see
**Verified**

commits.commit_title: fix(backend): remove the morning-briefing cron when the feature flag is off (#14308)
commits.commit_message:
fix(backend): remove the morning-briefing cron when the feature flag is off (#14308)

### Why / What / How

Deletes a user's daily morning-briefing cron once the `HIRE_EXPERTS`
flag is off for them, instead of leaving it to fire forever with nothing
to do.

`add_morning_briefing_schedule` was the only code that ever touched
`morning_briefing_{user_id}` — there was no removal path anywhere. The
cron is registered as a side effect of sending *any* chat turn, so a
user who never asked for a briefing gets one, and turning the flag off
only made the job body return `{"status": "skipped", "reason":
"flag_disabled"}` while the job itself stayed in the `EXECUTION`
jobstore. On the Dev deployment that is ~19 registered crons, of which
14 of 14 fires on 2026-09-03 skipped.

The job body now self-deletes its own schedule on the flag-disabled
branch, mirroring how `_execute_copilot_turn` cleans up an orphaned
copilot-turn schedule. Removal goes through a new
`Scheduler.remove_morning_briefing_schedule` rather than
`delete_schedule`, because that path authorizes via `_job_to_info`,
which parses only graph and copilot-turn kwargs and rejects this job's
`{"user_id": ...}` shape as corrupt; the job id embeds the user id, so
it is self-scoping. The lazy-registration Redis marker is cleared
alongside it — left set, it would suppress re-registration for the rest
of its 7-day TTL if the flag were turned back on.

Second, unrelated one-liner in the same feature: the briefing
narrative's persona line rendered as `You are Ana — , a hired expert on
the user's team.` for an expert with no `role` set. Observed in a real
Dev prompt on 2026-08-31.

Closes #14306 · [OPEN-3469](https://linear.app/autogpt/issue/OPEN-3469)

### Changes 🏗️

- `executor/scheduler.py`: `execute_morning_briefing` calls the new
`_self_delete_morning_briefing_schedule` when the result reason is
`flag_disabled`. The helper removes the job and clears the registration
marker, and swallows failures — it runs inside a job body, where raising
would fail the whole run. The next daily fire retries.
- `executor/scheduler.py`: new `@expose`d
`Scheduler.remove_morning_briefing_schedule(user_id)` plus its
`SchedulerClient` async binding. Returns `removed: False` rather than
raising when the job is already gone, so the retry-on-every-fire path is
idempotent.
- `copilot/briefing/narrative.py`: `_system_prompt` drops the `— {role}`
clause when the role is empty.
- Tests for both, described below.

No behaviour change for a flag-on user: every other result —
`nothing_to_say`, `already_delivered`, `delivered` — leaves the schedule
in place.

### Checklist 📋

#### For code changes:
- [x] I have clearly listed my changes in the PR description
- [x] I have made a test plan
- [x] I have tested my changes according to the test plan:

  **Executed** (`.claude/bin/pytest.sh`, all green):
- [x] `backend/executor/scheduler_unit_test.py` — 91 passed. New:
removal deletes the job and invalidates the read cache; removing an
already-gone job is a no-op; the job body self-deletes on
`flag_disabled`; it does **not** self-delete on `nothing_to_say` /
`already_delivered` / `delivered` (parametrized); the self-delete also
clears the registration marker; the self-delete swallows a scheduler RPC
failure and logs it.
- [x] `backend/copilot/briefing/` — 85 passed, including the two new
prompt-rendering tests (role present keeps the dash clause; role empty
drops it).
  - [x] Both together — 116 passed.
- [x] Confirmed the new narrative test **fails** against the unfixed
code (`assert "You are Ana, a hired expert..." in 'You are Ana — ...'`)
and that the with-role test still passes, so the fix is not vacuous.
  - [x] `pyright` on the four changed files: 0 errors.

**Not executed, reasoned about only:** the live Pyro round-trip for the
new `SchedulerClient` binding. The unit tests mock
`get_scheduler_client`, so the RPC itself is covered only by mirroring
the shape of the existing `add_morning_briefing_schedule` binding
directly above it.

**Note on the commit:** the `Typecheck - AutoGPT Platform - Backend`
pre-commit hook was skipped. It has `pass_filenames: false`, so it
typechecks the whole backend package and reports 148 pre-existing errors
(mostly `platform_linking/db.py` Prisma dict mismatches) in files this
PR does not touch — `git diff origin/dev` is these four files only.
Pyright on the four changed files is clean.

feat(frontend): tidy copilot chrome and move recent workflow runs to the home briefing (#14304)

### Why / What / How

**Why:** Four pieces of copilot and home chrome were off. With the
session activity card open, the files card floated well below the top of
the chat. The thread chip's hover fill stopped short of its trailing
edge. The "Balanced" tier chip took a labeled slot on the composer's
left when it is a quiet per-message setting. And the "What's happening
with your agents" strip sat under the copilot composer, where it
competed with the empty state's one job, while the home page's "Your
briefing" tile is where a user goes to see what their agents did.

**What:** The files card sits level with the thread chip. Each half of
the chip owns its padding so the identity button's hover reaches the
edge. The connection picker moves to the composer's right-hand control
group and collapses to the tier glyph with a tooltip. The workflow runs
strip moves from the copilot to the home page, inside the briefing tile,
labelled "Recent workflow runs".

**How:** The artifacts toggle already hides while the files card is
open, so the card moves from `top-18` to `top-3`. The chip container
drops its padding and its two halves carry `py-1 pl-1.5 pr-3` instead.
The picker renders before the test-mode and mic buttons; when it only
names the tier it becomes a `size-8` icon button whose tooltip reads the
tier and model. The runs strip becomes `RecentWorkflowRuns` under
`home/components`, fed by the same library agents and executions feed
the copilot strip used. It mounts at the bottom of `MorningBriefing` and
renders nothing when there are no runs. Each chip keeps its See link and
its Ask action becomes a link to the copilot with the same prompt, using
the `/copilot?autosubmit=true#prompt=` route the library already uses.
The copilot's `CopilotHome` loses its fallback prop and stays quiet when
there is no recap.

**Home restyle:** The page moves to a flatter, denser layout. Every tile
is a hairline-bordered panel with a one-line header row inside it (icon,
title, right-aligned meta such as counts or a filter) instead of a
shadowed 30px card with its heading floating above. Rows are 13px with
edge-to-edge dividers and a quiet hover. Statuses are a dot and a word
rather than filled pills. The greeting loses its purple gradient and the
date its icon. The workflow runs strip becomes rows with hover-revealed
See and Ask actions so it matches the rest of the page.

**One Recent work card:** "Your briefing" and "Recent work" described
the same day from two angles, so they merge into one card with one
header and one empty state: the 9am narrative, then Outcomes (the
briefing's completed and failed runs, with the filter), then Delivered
this week (files, integrations, schedules by actor). A Workflows section
at the bottom lists each workflow's latest state from the library feed
(listening, running, completed, error), one row each with hover-revealed
See and Ask links. Scheduled runs are left out because Now & next lists
them under Coming up.

### Changes 🏗️

- `WorkspaceFileCards`: card offset `top-18` → `top-3`, aligned with the
thread chip.
- `ThreadHeader` / `ExpertIntegrations`: padding moves from the chip
container onto each half; both share the same hover fill.
- `ChatInput` / `ConnectionPicker`: picker moves to the trailing addon;
tier-only form is an icon with a tooltip, connection-naming form keeps
its label.
- `home/components/RecentWorkflowRuns`: new section with `RunChip`,
hook, helpers, stylesheet and component test. Mounted inside
`MorningBriefing`.
- `EmptySession` / `CopilotHome`: the pulse strip and the
`AGENT_BRIEFING` gate around it are gone from the copilot; `CopilotHome`
no longer takes a fallback.
- `copilot/components/PulseChips`: removed.
- `home/page.tsx` / `NeedsYou`: the "Needs you" tile mounts only when
there are attention items; the header already says when nothing needs
you, so the empty tile is gone.
- `HomeTile` / `HomeTileEmpty` / `HomeTileFilter`: new panel API
(`icon`, `title`, `meta`), compact empty state, ghost filter trigger.
`NeedsYouTitle` folds into `NeedsYou`.
- `HomeHeader`, `AttentionRow(Actions)`, `OutcomeRow`, `WorkGroup`,
`AgentRow`, `StatusBadge`, `ActiveRow`, `UpcomingRow`, `NowNext`,
`RecentWork`, `AgentTeam`, `MorningBriefing`: restyled to the panel and
row scale; all copy and accessible names unchanged.
- `RecentWork` absorbs `MorningBriefing` (`OutcomeRow` and the outcome
filter hook move with it). `MorningBriefing` and `RecentWorkflowRuns`
are deleted.
- `RecentWork/components/RunRow` with `useWorkflowRuns` and

- `HomeSectionLabel`: shared caption used by Recent work and Now & next.
- `AgentRow`: the setup detail line is gone (Needs you already carries

commits.commit_title: feat(blocks): output full PR object from GithubReadPullRequestBlock (#14295)
commits.commit_message:
feat(blocks): output full PR object from GithubReadPullRequestBlock (#14295)

## Summary

This PR adds a new `pull_request` output to `GithubReadPullRequestBlock`
that carries the full, raw pull request object returned by the GitHub
API — including head/base refs (with fork repo and branch name for
cross-repo PRs), mergeability, and draft state — without touching any of
the block's existing outputs.

### Why / What / How

**Why:** The block's existing outputs (`title`, `body`, `author`,
`changes`) don't expose fork/branch info, mergeability, or draft state.
[OPEN-2780](https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT/issues/11115)
specifically asked for the PR's fork URL and branch name; rather than
whitelist just those two fields, this exposes the whole object so any
future need (draft state, review counts, labels, etc.) is covered
without another block change.

**What:** Adds a `pull_request: dict` output field with a description
documenting its contents, and yields the raw PR JSON alongside the
existing outputs. Nothing else in the block's input/output schema
changes.

**How:** `GithubReadPullRequestBlock.read_pr` fetches from the
`/issues/{n}` endpoint (title/body/author only — it omits
head/base/mergeability). The new `read_pr_full_object` static method
fetches `/pulls/{n}` directly, which is the endpoint that actually
carries the full object, and returns the response body unmodified. This
follows the precedent set by `GithubGetUserInfoBlock.user` in
[#13634](https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT/pull/13634):
yield the raw API object with a descriptive `SchemaField`, rather than
hand-picking fields.

### Changes 🏗️

- `GithubReadPullRequestBlock`: new `pull_request` output (raw PR object
from `GET /pulls/{n}`); new `read_pr_full_object` static method;
existing `title`/`body`/`author`/`changes` outputs and their behavior
are unchanged.

output.

feat(platform): install your own library agents as expert workflows (#14297)

Lets a user install an agent from their own library onto their own
expert, not just agents published to the Marketplace.

Resolves #14296

An "expert" is a hired AI teammate; a "workflow" is an agent attached to
that expert so it can run it. Until now the only way to attach one was
`POST /experts/{id}/workflows` with a `store_listing_version_id` — a
Marketplace listing snapshot. An agent the user built themselves has no
such snapshot, so it was not installable on their own expert. The Team
page rendered those agents with a "Local only" badge and the tooltip
"Publish this agent to the Marketplace before adopting it."

No migration: `ExpertWorkflow` already has both `storeListingVersionId`
and `libraryAgentId` nullable.

### Changes 🏗️

**Backend**

- `InstallWorkflowRequest` now takes exactly one of
`store_listing_version_id` or `library_agent_id` (422 otherwise).
`experts_db.install_workflow` takes both as keyword-only args and splits
into `_install_marketplace_workflow` (unchanged behaviour) and
`_install_library_workflow`.
- The library path validates ownership with a direct query on the
`LibraryAgent`'s own `userId` (plus `isDeleted=False`) — not inferred
from another object the caller holds — and records `libraryAgentId` with
no listing version. Another user's agent, or a soft-deleted one, is a
404 and writes nothing.
- Dedupe is on `libraryAgentId`, which also covers the cross-path case:
a Marketplace install already records the same `LibraryAgent`, so
installing a listing and then its resulting library agent returns the
one existing row rather than a second one.
- `ExpertWorkflowRef.name` / `description` and `ExpertRun.agent_name`
now fall back to the graph for a library-only row. `LibraryAgent.name`
only holds a Marketplace snapshot and is NULL on a user's own agent, so
without this every own-agent workflow rendered as "Unnamed workflow" and
its runs as the "Agent task" placeholder.

**Frontend**

- Team page → "Your workflows": Adopt sends `{library_agent_id}`. Every
library agent is adoptable now, so the "Local only" badge and its
publish-first tooltip are gone.
- `InstallWorkflowPicker` in `pick-workflow` mode gained a source toggle
— **Your agents** (default) / **Marketplace**. "Your agents" searches
the user's library and installs by library agent id; "Marketplace" is
the previous behaviour, unchanged. `pick-expert` mode (Install-on-Expert
from a Marketplace listing page) is untouched.

The second commit fixes a bug the manual run surfaced: the picker
invalidated only the expert *list* query, so an install made from a
single expert's page left that page's Workflows section stale until
reload.

**Cleanup** — each removal verified to have no remaining callers:

| Removed | Was for |
|---|---|
| `library/db._fetch_matching_store_version_ids` + its 3 batched call
sites | resolving a library agent to an exact approved listing snapshot
|
| `LibraryAgent.store_listing_version_id` (public API field) + the
`from_db` parameter | feeding that snapshot id to the Adopt flow |
| `raise_attachments._matching_store_listing_version_id` | same lookup
on the raise path |
| the snapshot branch of `_resolve_workflow`, and the
`store_listing_version_id` parameter of `_link_library_workflow` /
`_existing_workflow` | pairing a library attachment with a Marketplace
row |
| frontend `getAdoptTargetVersionID` and the version-matching in
`getAdoptableExperts` / `pruneAdoptedTargetKeys` | deciding adoptability
from the snapshot id |

**Kept:** `library_db.is_store_listing_version_available_for_install` is
*not* orphaned — `raise_attachments` still calls it twice to validate
Marketplace attachments (preflight and inside the install transaction).
`installable_store_version_where` likewise remains in use by
`_add_to_library`.

Removing `LibraryAgent.store_listing_version_id` was checked against the
pending v2 external API (#12206): that branch's `LibraryAgent` model
enumerates its fields explicitly in `from_internal` and does not include
this one, so there is no merge-order conflict.

### One correction to the issue's code map

#14296 says the raise flow "still resolves a library agent to a
marketplace snapshot ... and fails with
`RaiseAttachmentUnavailableError` when none matches". It did resolve the
snapshot, but it did **not** fail without one — `_link_library_workflow`
already created rows with a null listing version. The raise path already
worked for unpublished agents; the install endpoint was the only real
gap. The snapshot lookup on that path was dead weight, and is removed
here.

commits.commit_title: dx(frontend): add knip to find unused files, exports and dependencies (#14269)
commits.commit_message:
dx(frontend): add knip to find unused files, exports and dependencies (#14269)

### Why / What / How

**Why:** Nothing in the frontend flags dead code. ESLint catches unused
*locals*, but an exported component nobody imports, a whole orphaned
folder, or a dependency that lost its last consumer all sit in the repo
indefinitely — slowing builds, bloating the bundle and misleading
readers.

**What:** Adds [knip](https://knip.dev) — unused files, exports,
exported types, enum members, and dependencies — as a `pnpm knip` script
plus a non-blocking CI job.

**How:** knip auto-detects the Next.js, Vitest, Playwright, Storybook
and orval plugins, so most entry points come for free. `knip.json` only
adds what it can't infer:

- **entry** — `sentry.{edge,server}.config.ts` (loaded by the Sentry
SDK, never imported) and the two standalone `scripts/` entry points
(`migrate-supabase-auth.ts` runs from a workflow,
`seed-preview-accounts.ts` runs by hand). `generate-api-queries.ts` is
already found via `package.json` scripts.
- **ignoreDependencies** — `@opentelemetry/instrumentation`,
`import-in-the-middle` and `require-in-the-middle` are listed by name in
`next.config.mjs`'s `serverExternalPackages`; `postcss-load-config` is a
JSDoc type reference in `postcss.config.mjs`. None are statically
importable, so knip can't see them.
- **ignoreExportsUsedInFile** — drops exports that are also used inside
their own file. This is the big noise filter: unused exports fell from
362 to 190, unused types from 99 to 15.

The generated API client is gitignored, so both the script and the CI
job need `pnpm generate:api` to have run first — otherwise every import
into `src/app/api/__generated__` is unresolved.

**CI is informational for now** — `continue-on-error: true` sits on the
`Run knip` step only, so a broken install or API generation still fails
the job. The current baseline is ~92 unused files and ~190 unused
exports; gating on that would block every PR. The report lands in the
job's run summary so it stays visible. Happy to flip it to blocking once
the backlog is cleaned up — say the word and I'll open that as a
follow-up.

### Changes 🏗️

- `autogpt_platform/frontend/knip.json` — new config (above).
- `autogpt_platform/frontend/package.json` — `knip` devDependency
(6.32.2, the newest release passing the repo's 7-day
`minimum-release-age`) and a `pnpm knip` script.
- `.github/workflows/platform-frontend-ci.yml` — new `knip` job that
installs, generates the API client, and appends the markdown report to
`$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. Scoped to `permissions: contents: read` with
`persist-credentials: false` on checkout; only the knip step is
`continue-on-error`.
- `README.md` / `CONTRIBUTING.md` — script listed alongside
`lint`/`format`/`types`.
- `pnpm-lock.yaml` — knip pulls newer `jiti` (2.6.1 → 2.7.0) and `yaml`
(2.8.2 → 2.9.0), which pnpm dedupes into Vite's optional peer slots.
Both are dev-only config loaders; no runtime dependency changed.

#### What the first run finds

Nothing is deleted in this PR — it's tooling only. Highlights worth a
follow-up:

- **10 unused dependencies:** `@next/third-parties`,
`@tanstack/react-table`, `cookie`, `react-modal`, `react-shepherd` (the
app imports `shepherd.js` directly), and five `@radix-ui/*` packages.
- **8 unused devDependencies:** `@types/bcryptjs`, `@types/react-window`
and `@types/react-modal` are now redundant (those packages ship their
own types), plus `axe-playwright`, `pbkdf2`, and the Chromatic pair —
the Chromatic CI job is currently disabled.
- **2 unlisted binaries — a real break:** the `test-storybook` and
`test-storybook:ci` scripts call `test-storybook` and `wait-on`, but
neither `@storybook/test-runner` nor `wait-on` is installed.
`test-runner-jest.config.js` `require`s the missing package too. Those
scripts cannot run today.
- **92 unused files,** heavily concentrated in
`src/components/__legacy__/` and a superseded `NewAgentLibraryView`
subtree.
- **2 orphaned stories:** `OriginFilter.stories.tsx` and
`AccountMenu.stories.tsx` sit outside the globs in `.storybook/main.ts`,
so Storybook never renders them.

commits.commit_title: fix(frontend/copilot): stop the composer flickering between its row and stacked layouts (#14270)
commits.commit_message:
fix(frontend/copilot): stop the composer flickering between its row and stacked layouts (#14270)

### Why / What / How

**Why:** The copilot composer flickers between its single-row and
stacked layouts, several times a second, whenever the text is long
enough to wrap beside the addons but short enough to fit on one
full-width line. The hero composer on the copilot home page sits in that
band by default: its long brain-dump placeholder wraps next to the `+
Autopilot` chip but fits on one line across the full width, so the empty
composer shakes on its own. Typing text of a matching length reproduces
it in any chat.

**What:** `PromptInputTextarea` now judges "does the content wrap?" at
the width it has in the host's single row, not at whatever width it has
right now. A regression test drives the composer through the wrap
boundary with simulated widths and asserts the layout settles.

**How:** The host (`ChatInput`) changes the textarea's width based on
the textarea's own report: a wrapped box moves to a full-width row, an
unwrapped one shares the row with the addons. Measuring at the current
width therefore made each layout imply the other, and the
`ResizeObserver` that re-measures on width changes kept the loop running
once per frame. The textarea now remembers its width from the last time
it sat in the single row and, while stacked, temporarily measures its
content at that width before restoring its own. Both layouts then agree
about the same text, and it still collapses back to the single row once
the text fits there again. `onMultilineChange` also fires only when the
answer changes.

### Changes 🏗️

**The flicker fix**

- `PromptInputTextarea` (`src/components/ai-elements/prompt-input.tsx`):
judge wrapping at the remembered single-row width rather than the
current one; measure it as a border box, since that is how the number is
interpreted when it is handed back as an inline width; re-learn the
addon offset on each unstack; clamp the remembered width to the row the
box actually has, so a row that narrows past what the addons take cannot
leave it measuring against a row that is gone; report only on change.
- `ChatInput/__tests__/ChatInputComposerRow.test.tsx`: the real textarea
inside `ChatInput` with simulated widths and `ResizeObserver`
notifications. Covers staying stacked once text wraps in the row,
returning to the single row when it fits again, the empty hero composer
whose placeholder wraps, re-measuring when the row grows, the border-box
width, and never measuring against a row wider than the current one. The
last records every layout the host passes through rather than the one it
settles on, because the blink it catches corrects itself.

**The composer, while it was open**

- Card composer (`ChatInput.tsx`, `EmptySession.tsx`, `FileChips.tsx`,
`helpers.ts`): the hero composer keeps the text on its own row above the
controls, with card chrome instead of the pill's; the connection chip
moves out of the composer into the page corner.
- Connection picker rework (`ConnectionPicker/*`): connections and tiers
read as one list of rows rather than a list plus a segmented control;
`ChoiceRow` and `TierToggle` are proper radio groups (one tab stop,
arrow keys select as they move); `ConnectAccountRow` gives a user with
no ChatGPT link a way to make one; `Swap` animates a changed label or
glyph instead of rewriting it in place.

**Review fixes**

- Accessibility: `InformationTooltip`'s trigger is a native button, so
its contents are reachable by keyboard; a connection's notes and a
locked tier's plans link sit beside their radio rather than inside it,
where assistive technology treats them as presentational.
- `FileChips`: the stacked row's pull towards the textarea moves onto
the clipping wrapper, which was cropping the chips by the same amount.
- `useSwap`: a key that returns to what is on screen mid-animation ends
the exit instead of stranding it at `opacity-0`.
- `useConnectionPicker`: `offers.every()` is vacuously true on an empty
list, so `canConnectChatGPT` no longer claims the connect row is
eligible in the one state that cannot render it.

### Checklist 📋

#### For code changes:
- [x] I have clearly listed my changes in the PR description
- [x] I have made a test plan
- [x] I have tested my changes according to the test plan:
- [x] Root-caused from the recording: every 2 to 4 frames the empty hero
composer alternates between the stacked layout (placeholder on one line)
and the single row (placeholder wrapped to three lines)
- [x] `prettier`, `eslint` on the changed files and `tsc --noEmit` pass

`src/components` — 274 files, 3011 tests, green; `prettier`, `eslint`
and `tsc --noEmit` clean on the changed files

commits.commit_message:
docs(dx): refresh pr-test skill for Better Auth, env setup, and billing-test trap (#14276)

Updates the `pr-test` skill (`.claude/skills/pr-test/SKILL.md`) so the
next agent that runs `/pr-test` doesn't re-pay the discovery cost this
run paid — the auth flow, env setup, and a billing-test trap it
documented had all gone stale or were undocumented gaps.

### Why / What / How

**Why:** `/pr-test`'s setup steps were pointing at Supabase auth
endpoints the platform no longer has, and two other gaps (env vars, a
billing false-pass trap) cost a full E2E run to rediscover. Left
undocumented, the next agent pays the same cost again.
**What:** Rewrites the auth setup (Better Auth sign-up/sign-in/token),
documents two env vars a plain `.env` copy now misses, adds a proven
Playwright fallback for `agent-browser`, documents a billing-test
false-pass trap, replaces broad process-kill guidance with port-targeted
kill, and adds a mock-provider pattern for deterministic $0 testing. A
follow-up commit then corrects two claims from the first pass that an
automated review's live-stack QA disproved (see below).
**How:** Direct edits to the skill doc plus one line in
`frontend/.env.default` and one in `frontend/.prettierignore` (see
Second file).

## Source

All items were verified during a real E2E run of `/pr-test` against
[#14206](https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT/pull/14206) —
see the [evidence
comment](https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT/pull/14206#issuecomment-5511429524)
for the specifics behind each finding.

## Changes 🏗️

### What changed in the skill (2.1.0 → 2.2.1)

- **Auth was stale**: the skill assumed Supabase (`/auth/v1/signup`);
the platform moved to Better Auth. Step 3h now signs up + signs in
against `/api/auth/*` and mints a backend JWT from the resulting session
cookie via `/api/auth/token`. Documents Better Auth's 12-char password
minimum and fails loudly on an empty token instead of silently 401ing
every subsequent call.
- **Env setup was stale**: "copy `.env` from the root worktree" no
longer boots a recent `dev` worktree — documents the two additions
needed (`backend/.env` needs `JWT_JWKS_URL`, `frontend/.env` needs its
own `DATABASE_URL` for Better Auth, now derived from the backend's
actual `DB_PASS` rather than copied from a placeholder).
- **Browser fallback**: documents the proven fallback when
`agent-browser` isn't installed on the host — `@playwright/test`, with
the correct prerequisite (`playwright install chromium` — the binary
isn't in `node_modules`, only the package is).
- **Billing-test trap** (this one produces a false pass, not a visible
failure): LLM block cost filters key on the platform-owned credential
id, so a run on the test user's own API key bills nothing by design — a
credits assertion silently passes vacuous. Documents that billing
verification must use the system credential, and that Ollama blocks are
configured with an explicit `$0` run-based cost so they always yield a
zero delta regardless.
- **Process hygiene**: replaces broad pattern-based `pkill` guidance
(which took out the frontend and a mock server along with the intended
backend process in this run) with port-targeted kill — portable, and
honest about not being full worktree isolation.
- **Mock-provider pattern**: new section — the OpenAI SDK honours
`OPENAI_BASE_URL`, so timeout/latency/error-path behavior can be tested
deterministically and free against a local mock Responses-API server
while everything from executor to billing stays real. This run proved
4/4 items this way at $0. Mandates a throwaway credential, not the
system one.

### Corrections from automated review (2.2.0 → 2.2.1)

`autogpt-pr-reviewer` and CodeRabbit reviewed this PR and ran live-stack
QA against the actual claims. Two didn't survive:
- **JWKS does not rotate on a frontend restart.** The first pass claimed
a frontend restart rotates the Better Auth keypair and invalidates
issued JWTs. QA restarted the frontend twice and found the keypair
persists in Postgres (`platform."UserAuthJwks"`) and a pre-restart JWT
still authenticated. This claim is removed — it would have sent future
agents chasing a phantom cause for unrelated 401s.
- **The local Postgres port is `5432`, not `54322`.** The first pass
"corrected" `frontend/.env.default`'s `DATABASE_URL` to port `54322`,
reasoning from a Supabase CLI convention that doesn't apply to this
repo's docker-compose stack (`db` service listens on `5432`, no
`supabase-db` container exists). Reverted, and the comment above it
(which had the correctness backwards) is fixed.

Full triage of the review's findings is in the PR comment below.

## Second file

`autogpt_platform/frontend/.env.default` — its documented `DATABASE_URL`
example is
`postgresql://postgres:your-super-secret-and-long-postgres-password@localhost:5432/postgres`,
matching the local `db` service's default port and password (unchanged
after the 2.2.1 correction above).

Also added `.env*` to the frontend's `.prettierignore` — Prettier has no
parser for that extension, so the pre-commit hook failed on any edit to
`.env.default` regardless of content; fixing this was required to commit
the required second file.

### Configuration changes
- [x] `.env.default` is updated or already compatible with my changes
- [x] `docker-compose.yml` is updated or already compatible with my
changes (no compose changes needed)
- [x] I have included a list of my configuration changes in the PR
description (see Second file, above)

## Testing

Docs-only change — no application code paths to run.

### Checklist 📋
- [x] I have clearly listed my changes in the PR description
- [x] I have made a test plan
- [x] I have tested my changes according to the test plan:
- [x] Verified the corrected Better Auth signup/sign-in/token endpoints
against `frontend/src/lib/autogpt-server-api/helpers.ts` (confirmed
`/api/auth/token` requires a session cookie, not credentials directly)
- [x] `prettier --check` and `tsc --noEmit` pass locally after
regenerating the frontend API client (`orval`) and `pnpm install`
- [x] CI green on the PR (docs/config-only diff; frontend

commits.commit_message:
feat(blocks): Add GitHub notification management blocks (#13634)

### Why / What / How

**Why:** We have GitHub trigger and repo/issue/PR blocks, but no way for
agents to work with the user's GitHub notification inbox — e.g.
inbox-zero automations, notification triage, or surfacing review
requests. GitHub's Notifications API is poll-only (no webhook events
exist for it), so inbox automations run as scheduled graphs using
regular blocks.

**What:** Adds six blocks covering the [GitHub Notifications REST
API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/activity/notifications): listing
notifications and getting / marking read / marking done / unsubscribing
from notification threads, plus mark-all-as-read. Also adds a
`GithubGetUserInfoBlock` and extends `GithubListPRReviewersBlock` with
review status info, enabling agents to determine whether the account's
user is (still) involved in a PR (example use case: auto-archiving stale
review-request notifications).

**How:** New `notifications.py` in the GitHub blocks package, following
the existing block conventions there. Notification endpoints live under
`/notifications` rather than `/repos/...`, so the blocks use
`get_api(credentials, convert_urls=False)` with absolute URLs. API
responses are normalized into a shared `NotificationItem` shape whose
`thread_id` chains into the per-thread blocks and whose `subject_url` is
converted best-effort from the API URL to the corresponding github.com
page URL. Notification blocks use the minimal `notifications` OAuth
scope.

### Changes 🏗️

- Add `GithubListNotificationsBlock`: lists the inbox with include-read
/ participating-only / `since` / `before` filters and optional repo
scoping; yields the full list plus each notification individually
- Add `GithubGetNotificationThreadBlock`: fetches one thread and exposes
title, reason, unread, subject type/URL, and repository as separate
outputs
- Add `GithubMarkNotificationsAsReadBlock`: marks all notifications as
read, optionally repo-scoped, with optional `last_read_at` cutoff
- Add `GithubMarkNotificationThreadAsReadBlock` and
`GithubMarkNotificationThreadAsDoneBlock`: per-thread read / done
- Add `GithubUnsubscribeNotificationThreadBlock`: mutes a thread
- Add `GithubGetUserInfoBlock`: fetches info on a given user, or the
authenticated user if no username is given
- Extend `GithubListPRReviewersBlock`: new `include_past_reviewers`
toggle (default off) to also list users who already submitted a review,
plus `review_requested` / `has_reviewed` / `review_state` fields on each
reviewer item; the extra API call is gated behind the toggle so existing
graphs are unaffected
- Refactor: hoist `GITHUB_API_URL` constant into `_api.py` and reuse it

commits.commit_title: fix(backend): copilot bot delivery and escaping fixes across adapters (#14097)
commits.commit_message:
fix(backend): copilot bot delivery and escaping fixes across adapters (#14097)

### Why / What / How

**Why:** An audit of the copilot bot adapter stack (Discord, Slack,
Telegram, Teams + shared core) surfaced seven confirmed delivery and
safety bugs. None are Teams-specific; most are drift where one adapter
handles a case the others drop.

**What:** Seven self-contained fixes, each with a test, plus the
follow-ups from review.

**How:** Minimal targeted changes inside `backend/copilot/bot/` only. No
behavior change for the happy paths; every fix makes a
previously-dropped or unsafe edge behave.

### Changes 🏗️

**Slack**
- `to_mrkdwn` now escapes `&`/`<`/`>` before re-introducing bold/link
markup, so a raw `<!channel>`, `<!here>`, or `<@Uid>` in model output
renders as text instead of pinging the workspace. Allowlisted `@name`
mentions are matched on the canonical text and stashed behind
placeholders through the escaping, so names like `R&D` still ping. The
link rule only emits `<url|label>` for `http(s)`/`mailto:` targets, so
`[x](!channel)` can't re-open a control sequence after escaping (the
attachment-problems note echoes Slack filenames into this path).
Line-leading `>` is kept so blockquotes still render.
- Private-channel thread follow-ups: Slack delivers private-channel
messages as `channel_type: "group"`, which the event dispatch dropped —
the bot would answer the first mention, subscribe the thread, then never
see a reply. Now forwarded, with `groups:history` + `groups:read` added
to `_SCOPES` and the manifest (`message.groups` event too). **Existing
installs need a reinstall to grant the new scopes; until then private
channels behave as before.** Multi-person DMs (`mpim`) stay deliberately
unhandled (pinned by a test).
- `thread_history` was never populated — the scopes were requested and
commented "for thread follow-up context" but the fetch was never
written, so @-mentioning the bot mid-thread answered with zero context.
Implemented in a new `slack/history.py`: follows `conversations.replies`
pagination to the tail (the API pages oldest-first), keeps the newest
messages, drops only the bot's own posts (other bots' posts stay, since
an alert thread is often what the user wants summarized), resolves
display names with bounded concurrency only for what survives the
budget, and is skipped entirely for threads the bot owns (the handler
discards it there). A failure anywhere in the history path (the Redis
subscription gate included) answers without history instead of dropping
the message, an over-cap thread bails after one page via the parent's
reply_count, and history is skipped when the bot's own identity is
unknown (the self-filter would fail open). Author labels are flattened
and capped before they reach the prompt frame.
- Every Slack send path (streamed replies, proactive posts) chunks the
canonical markdown before localizing, so a hard cut can't bisect an
entity or a `<url|label>` link — and because Slack counts the escaped
wire text, any chunk that expands past the 4,000-char cap is re-split
smaller before posting.
- OAuth callback: slack_sdk raises `SlackApiError` on `ok:false`, so the
graceful-failure branch was dead and a failed code exchange surfaced as
a raw 500. Both API and transport failures now land on the
`slack_install_error` redirect, carrying Slack's error code.

**Telegram**
- `post_channel_message` chunked already-converted HTML with the
markdown-aware splitter, so a long proactive post with a code block got
cut inside `<pre>` and Telegram 400'd the send. Now chunks canonical
markdown first (where the splitter balances fences) and localizes per
chunk, matching the streaming path. Note for reviewers: Telegram's 4096
cap is "characters **after entities parsing**" (Bot API,
`sendMessage.text`), so the raw HTML length is not the limit; a test
pins that invariant.

**Discord**
- `send_reply` only caught `NotFound`; in a channel without Read Message
History, `fetch_message` raises `Forbidden` and the reply was silently
lost. Only fetch failures fall back to a plain send; a failed `reply()`
propagates so a message Discord may have accepted is never
double-posted.

**Shared handler**
- A message whose only content was attachments the adapter skipped (too
large / failed download) was dropped before the problem report ran:
total silence in DMs, or the misleading "You mentioned me but didn't say
anything" in channels. Such messages now get the attachment-problems
note in place (an in-channel reply, or a message in the DM/thread)
instead of opening a thread just to hold it. The note sits behind the
same link gate as every other message, so an unlinked user still gets
the Link Account prompt, and `message_received` analytics still fire.

### Checklist 📋

#### For code changes:
- [x] I have clearly listed my changes in the PR description
- [x] I have made a test plan
- [x] I have tested my changes according to the test plan:
- [x] New unit tests for every fix, plus the review-round cases:

placeholders, blockquotes, chunk-before-escape with the wire-length cap,
history pagination/tail/budget/both error paths/other-bot posts,
skipped-only in DM/channel/unowned thread and behind the link gate,
reply() failure not retried, OAuth transport failure and a real
`AsyncSlackResponse`
  - [x] Full `backend/copilot/bot/` test tree: 630 passed
- [x] black + isort + ruff + pyright clean (pyright on the bot tree,
ignoring the local venv's `slack_sdk` resolution noise)

#### For configuration changes:

existing workspaces must reinstall to pick them up

commits.commit_title: refactor(backend): run Codex over HTTP and drop the 391 MB bundled CLI (#14195)
commits.commit_message:
refactor(backend): run Codex over HTTP and drop the 391 MB bundled CLI (#14195)

## Why

Codex ran through the Codex CLI. That pulled `openai-codex-cli-bin` into
the image (**391 MB**), needed a synthetic `$HOME` per login, and —
because one subprocess owned a credential — **served one chat at a time
per ChatGPT connection**.

None of it was necessary. Everything the CLI brokered is reachable over
ordinary HTTPS. This PR moves sign-in, refresh, the model catalog, rate
limits and inference to HTTP, and deletes the binary.

Every endpoint and response shape was verified against the live backend
with a Pro account, not inferred from another client's source.

## What the probing found

**Full Responses works on every model, including the
`use_responses_lite` ones.** This was the main open question and it
removes the model-pinning problem entirely:

| model | `use_responses_lite` | classic `tools:[...]`, 10 tools |
|---|---|---|
| `gpt-5.5` (control) | false | 200, tool called |
| `gpt-5.6-sol` | **true** | 200, **2 parallel calls** |
| `gpt-5.6-terra` / `-luna` | **true** | 200, tool called |
| `gpt-daybreak-blue-latest` / `gpt-reserve` | **true** | 200, tool
called |

`use_responses_lite` is a flag Codex reads from its *own* catalog to
reshape its *own* requests — a client-side token optimisation, not a
server contract. No lite implementation, no model pin, whole 5.6 family
available. (opencode's four-model allowlist is avoidance, not a solved
lite path.)

**The stock OpenAI SDK works against it.** The endpoint *is* the
Responses API, so `AsyncOpenAI` pointed at the ChatGPT base URL streams,
calls tools and reports usage with no bespoke SSE handling.

**Required headers are few**: `Authorization`, `ChatGPT-Account-Id`,
`content-type`, `accept`, `originator`, `user-agent`, `session_id`. No
`client_metadata`, no `OpenAI-Beta`, no `x-codex-*`.

**Rate limits ride on every inference response** as `x-codex-*` headers
— nothing extra to poll, and the numbers arrive with the work that spent
them.

**`/models` is reachable** (requires a `client_version` param it does
not validate — `0.0.0` returns the same catalog as a current build).

**No embeddings.** `/embeddings` returns an HTML 403 on every path tried
— the edge signature for a route that does not exist, not an entitlement
error — and `model_specialty` across the catalog is only `[null,
"cyber"]`. The subscription backend exposes `/responses` and `/models`,
nothing else.

## Sign-in is not RFC 8628

It resembles it enough to be dangerous. Verified differences: the poll
is keyed by **`(device_auth_id, user_code)`**; `interval` arrives as the
**string** `"5"`; the deadline is an **ISO timestamp** in `expires_at`;
there is **no `verification_uri`** in the payload; and an approved poll
returns an **`authorization_code`** still needing the ordinary PKCE
exchange.

**Pending is HTTP 403; an unknown or expired login is HTTP 404.**

```
403 → code "deviceauth_authorization_pending"   ← still waiting
404 → code "deviceauth_not_found"               ← terminal
```

Classification is on the error `code`, never the status. Treating 404 as
pending polls a dead login to its deadline; treating 403 as failure
tells someone sign-in failed while they are looking at the approval
screen that was about to work. Published descriptions of this flow say
"403/404 as pending" — that is wrong in the second case.

## Concurrency

`CodexCredentialBusyError` existed because a subprocess owned the
credential — "a ChatGPT connection serves one chat at a time" was a
property of the process, not the account. Over HTTP one credential
serves as many concurrent turns as the account allows. The type is kept
for callers that still distinguish it, but acquisition no longer raises
it.

## Two details in the tool loop

Both fail silently rather than raising, so both have tests:

- **Every output item is replayed** into the next request, reasoning
items included, with `include=["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` so they
come back replayable. Feeding back only the tool calls degrades
reasoning models quietly.
- **A tool timeout is reported to the model** as tool output rather than
killing the turn, so it can recover.

The loop also stops after 32 rounds rather than spending quota on
something that will not converge.

## Refresh ownership

Codex moves from `refresh_strategy="provider_runtime"` to
`"oauth_handler"`, putting it behind the credentials manager's Redis
mutex. OpenAI rotates the refresh token on every exchange and treats
replay as compromise, so the handler sets `ROTATES_REFRESH_TOKEN` and
refreshes serialize. A refresh response that omits a new refresh token
keeps the old one. Credentials written before this change stay readable,
so existing grants survive.

## On the client id

It is OpenAI's public Codex client — an identifier, not a secret; `grep
-rni client_secret` across the CLI's `login/`, `codex-api/` and
`model-provider/` returns nothing transmitted (the one hit is a
log-redaction list). PKCE protects the exchange.

The binding constraint is its **redirect allow-list** (`localhost:1455`,
`localhost:1457`, `auth.openai.com/deviceauth/callback`), which we
cannot add to. That is why device flow is the only viable door for a
server — not merely the convenient one.

`originator` is sent as **`autogpt`**. The backend serves any originator
(codex sends `codex_cli_rs`, opencode `opencode`, Zed `zed`), so
claiming to be the Codex CLI would be impersonation for no benefit.

## What was deleted

`runtime.py`, `launcher.py`, `temporary_home.py`, the runtime pool, the
capacity semaphore, and the `openai-codex` dependency.
`codex_compat_gateway.py` imported the SDK's notification type;
`CodexStreamEvent` replaces it, so nothing outside the codex package
reaches for it now.

**Net −3,779 lines.**

## Testing

- **83 new tests**; 123 passing across `integrations/codex` +
`integrations/oauth`, plus the codex gateway suites
- `ruff` and `pyright` clean on every changed file
- Live-verified end to end through `CodexTransport`: account, 10-model
catalog with the right default, chained multi-hop tool calls
(`get_weather` → `convert_temp`, correctly threading the first result
into the second), streaming deltas, accumulated usage, and rate limits

`test_transport_failure_logs_useful_bounded_context` fails **identically
at HEAD** — a local ANSI-in-log-message artifact, verified by checking
the file out at HEAD and re-running. Not introduced here.

`poetry.lock` was regenerated with **Poetry 2.2.1** to match the file's
own header, since CI reads its Poetry version from the lockfile — a
1.8.3 regeneration would have silently downgraded CI. The diff is 1
insertion / 35 deletions: the two packages and the content hash.

## Still unverified

Whether Cloudflare 403s these calls from a **datacenter IP**. All
probing ran from a residential connection. `!deploy` answers it.

## Checklist

- [x] Endpoints verified live rather than copied from another client
- [x] Tests for each silently-failing path
- [x] Pre-existing credentials remain readable
- [x] Pre-existing test failure verified as pre-existing
- [x] Lockfile regenerated with the version CI expects

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> This is a full swap of authentication, token refresh, and inference
for a user-billed integration; regressions would break ChatGPT/Codex
login or copilot turns, though legacy credential shapes are explicitly
preserved.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Replaces the Codex CLI/subprocess stack with plain HTTPS** for
ChatGPT device sign-in, token refresh, model catalog, and agent turns
via the Responses API (`AsyncOpenAI` against the ChatGPT Codex base
URL). The large `openai-codex` / `codex_cli_bin` path and supporting
modules (`runtime`, `launcher`, `temporary_home`, runtime pool) are
removed; container smoke now asserts the HTTP runtime and that
`openai_codex` / `codex_cli_bin` are not importable.
> 
> **Sign-in and credentials:** New `chatgpt_auth` + `device_login`
implement OpenAI’s non-RFC-8628 device flow (poll by `device_auth_id` +
`user_code`, classify on error codes). New credentials use
`refresh_strategy="oauth_handler"`; **`provider_runtime` stays
accepted** for existing grants. API lease checks and codec round-trips
were updated accordingly.
> 
> **Inference and copilot:** `CodexHttpSession` runs streaming turns
with a tool loop (reasoning item replay, rate limits from response
headers). **`CodexStreamEvent`** replaces CLI `Notification` types in
the Anthropic compat gateway and tests. **`PooledCodexRuntimeLease` is
renamed to `CodexCredentialLease`** through model routing and SDK chat
paths.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit
01a7b58e35a27a34451aea84fadf5b81521460a8. Bugbot is set up for automated
code reviews on this repo. Configure
[here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

commits.commit_title: feat(platform): let a chat continue elsewhere when a plan runs out (#14150)
commits.commit_message:
feat(platform): let a chat continue elsewhere when a plan runs out (#14150)

> Stacked on #14140 — review that first; this PR's diff is the one
commit on top.

**F1 requirement 5**, and the resolution of the question that blocked
F1:

> **Eng (Nick, blocking F1):** exact fallback behavior when a linked
plan hits
> its OpenAI rate limit mid-run: pause vs. offer platform-credit
continue?
> 🔄 **Resolved Aug 11 (Nick):** continue path, see F1 requirement 5.

### Why

**Two different limits were being treated as one.** Our credits running
out
and a user's ChatGPT plan running out both arrive as `usage_limit`, and
both
opened the same dialog — the one that offers to upgrade your AutoGPT
plan.
That asks someone to pay us more because OpenAI said no.

**And the backend could not do it anyway.** A chat is latched to the
connection it started on, deliberately, so a turn cannot silently change
who
pays for it halfway through. The only route resolution that existed was
`_resolve_new_session_llm_route` — for new sessions. There was no way to
move
an existing chat, so "switch connection to keep going" was advice with
nothing
behind it.

### What

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| our credits run out | plan dialog, upgrade CTA | unchanged |
| a linked plan runs out | **the same plan dialog** | continue on
another connection, or wait |
| moving an existing chat | not possible | `PUT
/sessions/{id}/connection` |

### How

**The exception is deliberate and narrow.** The new endpoint validates
against
the same transports list the creation path uses, and reuses its refusal
vocabulary (`codex_credential_not_found`,
`chat_transport_not_configured`,
`codex_credential_required`), so a connection the entitlement already
refused
cannot be reached through the side door and a client that handles those
already needs no second vocabulary.

**Never automatic.** The caller is a button the user pressed. The
composer
still holds the message the provider refused, so they resend when ready.
The
PRD's "never automatic" is the whole point: the choice moves the bill,
so it
is a dialog rather than a toast.

**History is not rewritten.** The segments module was built for exactly
this
and says so in its own docstring — *"Once it can — after a usage limit,
on a
user's switch — the two stop being the same"*. Turns already stamped
keep the
connection they ran on, so a chat that hit a limit and carried on
elsewhere
reads as exactly that. The session metadata is segment zero, and the db
layer
writes back **only the two route keys** rather than replacing the blob:
the
builder binding, the session kind and the dry-run flag belong to other
features and have to survive a connection change.

**Two judgement calls in picking what to offer:**

- never the connection that just refused the turn — it would fail again
immediately, and saying "nothing to switch to" is more honest than a
button
  that cannot work
- a *second account of the same provider* is still offered, because it
has its
  own quota

**Waiting stays a real option**, and the reset time appears only when
the
provider actually reported one. An invented "try again in an hour" is
worse
than silence, because people plan around it.

### Testing

```
pytest routes_test.py -k "change_connection or update_title or update_pinned or transport"  →  30 passed
vitest run copilot  →  131 files, 1580 passed
tsc --noEmit / eslint --max-warnings 0 / ruff  →  clean
```

Backend, six cases on the endpoint: it moves the chat; it refuses a
route the
user does not have (404, not a silent success); it refuses an
unavailable
transport; it rejects a credential on the platform route and requires
one for
codex; and someone else's session reports as missing rather than
forbidden.

Frontend: nine on the choice of alternative and the reset copy, plus two
pinning the split — a linked plan's limit reaches the caller with the
failure
attached, and our own still takes the path that preserves the composer
text.

**One test-only fallout worth a reviewer's eye:** `CopilotPage.test.tsx`
mocks
the chat endpoints module wholesale, so adding a hook to a component it
renders
broke four unrelated tests. Extended the mock rather than reshaping the
component — but that mock is a tripwire for the next person who adds a
query
under this page.

**Not exercised against a real quota exhaustion.** Forcing a genuine
ChatGPT
usage limit is not something I can do on demand; the classification path
itself was verified earlier in this stack against a real `auth_expired`.
The
seam between them is the `usage_limit` branch, which is covered by unit
tests
on both sides.

### Checklist

- [x] I have clearly listed my changes in the PR description
- [x] I have made a test plan
- [x] I have tested my changes according to the test plan

https://claude.ai/code/session_019RMLrx2p5tbM5pHcJM1hEc

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes touch billing/entitlement enforcement, who pays per turn
(session LLM route + cache races), and new APIs that must reject invalid
transports—bugs could allow Advanced spend without entitlement or bill
the wrong connection after a switch.
> 
> **Overview**
> **When a linked ChatGPT (or other) plan stops accepting turns, the
product now offers to continue the same chat on another connection**
instead of showing the AutoGPT upgrade dialog. Stream errors with a
`usage_limit` provider envelope open a **ProviderLimitDialog**; the user
can wait, or call **`PUT /api/chat/sessions/{session_id}/connection`**
to move future turns onto a validated transport while **past messages
keep their original connection stamps**.
> 
> Backend adds **`GET /api/chat/model-tiers`** and a shared
**`provider_tiers`** module so UIs can name tier→model mappings
**before** the user has that connection (onboarding Connect step,
ChatGPT connect explainer). **`advanced_tier_entitled`** is enforced on
**`POST …/stream`** and again when **queued platform Advanced turns
promote**, with stricter behavior than the picker when billing lookup
fails (403 vs 503). Session route updates use **atomic JSONB merge in
Postgres**, **Redis lock + cache refresh**, and **upsert logic** so a
slow turn cannot revert a user-initiated switch.
> 
> Self-host **onboarding** can lead with a skippable **ConnectStep**
(ChatGPT OAuth). **ConnectionPicker** moves from dropdown to popover
with **roving tabindex** on radio groups. Provider failures **survive
reload** via **`latestProviderFailure`** on persisted message metadata.
