docs(platform): sync GitBook documentation into dev (#14170)

### Why / What / How

GitBook contains the published single-container operations guide, while
`dev` contains the canonical generator and newer generated integration
documentation. The branches need a deliberate content reconciliation
without regressing either side.

This PR brings the GitBook-authored single-container guide and its
navigation entry into `dev`. It also updates the guide for the current
stock Docker shutdown behavior, interrupted-migration recovery, and the
`BEHAVE_AS` multi-tenant boundary introduced after the GitBook version
was published.

The head is a common descendant of current `dev` (`571df3a94d`) and
`gitbook` (`727c4eb4d9`). All generator-owned integration documentation
remains aligned with `dev`. The effective 19-file diff is limited to the
reconciled docs, single-container reference env/README/bootstrap guard
and focused tests, the narrow CI path for the canonical guide, focused
generator title coverage, and one Stripe Link null-normalization fix
with its regression test.

Paired reciprocal PR:
[#14171](https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT/pull/14171)
(`dev` → GitBook).

### Changes 🏗️

- Add `docs/platform/single-container.md` to `dev`, list it in the
platform `SUMMARY.md`, and cross-link it from the existing self-hosting
and installer guides.
- Update stop commands and first-boot migration recovery guidance for
the current single-container implementation.
- Document the bounded stock-timeout shutdown, abandoned `RUNNING` rows,
group-qualified Supervisor names, Docker Desktop memory troubleshooting,
database pool tuning, and the backend/frontend limits of
`BEHAVE_AS=cloud`.
- Reject anonymous `/data` volumes, make backup restart handling
state-aware, restart before checksum work, show how to launch a restored
volume, and eliminate the upgrade cutover write gap.
- Align the single-container README and reference env with the canonical
guide, including loopback-only port examples, and add direct tests for
email-verification refusal plus `BEHAVE_AS` default/override behavior.
- Add interrupted-migration contract coverage, document
signup/proxy/server-key boundaries, exclude regenerable cache from
backups, and align password/tag/image guidance with current code and
publishing workflows.
- Execute the published backup, checksum, restore, validation, and
restored-launch Bash directly against a disposable Docker model,
including concurrency, signals, failure cleanup, relative paths, Bash
3.2, and state-preservation cases.
- Validate restored PostgreSQL listening and authentication policy, keep
the Docker emulator in a separately linted module, and run the appliance
workflow for changes to the canonical operations guide.
- Label and verify per-run restore-volume ownership so a same-name
creation race cannot populate or remove another process's volume; reject
PostgreSQL `hba_file` redirects during offline validation.

restore validation, make the Docker emulator execute the published shell
fence before adding diagnostics, and test the direct and sourced
bootstrap paths.
- Document how to enable the optional chat-bot services and the required
Discord/Telegram settings.
- Replace every Stripe Link placeholder with implementation-backed MPP,
profile, payment-method, approval, and virtual-card guidance, and
directly test the generator's non-obvious brand-title mappings.

- Close superseded PR #13760, whose remaining operational changes used
the obsolete 360-second stop timeout.

`MANUAL` region; replace only the previously unfilled Stripe Link
placeholders.

commits.commit_title: fix(backend/copilot): make expert delegation and team state stale-proof (#14155)
commits.commit_message:
fix(backend/copilot): make expert delegation and team state stale-proof (#14155)

### Why / What / How

**Why** — the `<team_context>` roster (expert names + ids) is injected
only into a session's **first** user message. Any session opened before
the team was hired never learns the ids, and team changes
mid-conversation are invisible. Observed failure loop (real transcript):
the model delegates by name → exact-id lookup fails → it replays a spent
single-use `confirm_expert_change` id → the "unknown or expired" error
implies the expert doesn't exist → it re-proposes an expert who is
already on the team, over and over.

**What** — delegation tools now resolve a teammate by name when the id
misses, lookup failures carry the roster so the model can self-correct,
a read-only `list_team` tool gives an authoritative roster read, and
`raise_expert` refuses to re-raise a name that already exists.

**How** — name resolution and the roster-hint error live in
`expert_delegation.py` and are shared by both delegation tools, so the
bound can't be bypassed by switching tools. `list_team` registers in the
`delegation` tool group (available to AutoPilot and expert sessions
alike, gated on the hire-experts flag) and in the `ToolName` Literal.
Ambiguous names stay **unresolved on purpose** — the model gets the
roster instead of the tool guessing between twins.

### Changes 🏗️

- `delegate_to_expert` / `handoff_to_expert` resolve a **unique, active
name** when the id lookup misses (shared `resolve_target_expert`), with
a post-resolution self-delegation re-check — a name can resolve back to
the caller after the raw-id check has already passed.
- Lookup-failure errors now carry the roster (`Vera (expert_id: …); Max
(…)`) so the model self-corrects on the next call instead of guessing.
- New read-only **`list_team`** tool (delegation group): name,
expert_id, role, paused state. Never writes.
- `raise_expert` refuses a duplicate active name, pointing at the
existing expert's id, role, and the tools to use instead. Best-effort: a
roster read failure does not block a legitimate raise.
- The stale-confirmation error now says an already-confirmed change is
**APPLIED** and to check `list_team` before re-proposing.
- `ResponseType.TEAM_ROSTER` added to the API schema (`openapi.json`
synced).

Added during review:
- A transient id-lookup failure no longer masquerades as "no such
expert". `Expert.id` is a plain string column, so a bare name *misses*
rather than raises — meaning any exception there is a real DB failure,
and it now reaches the caller's "try again" handler instead of producing
`No active expert matching 'expert-b' ... Use one of these expert_ids:
Bea (expert_id: expert-b)`.
- Roster hints omit **paused** teammates, whom both delegation tools
refuse anyway.
- The duplicate-name check **fails closed**: an unreadable roster
returns a retryable error rather than passing for "no duplicate"
(nothing downstream enforces name uniqueness). Only the read is guarded
— a matching bug propagates instead of being retried forever.

No configuration changes.

### Checklist 📋

#### For code changes:
- [x] I have clearly listed my changes in the PR description
- [x] I have made a test plan
- [x] I have tested my changes according to the test plan:
- [x] `delegate_to_expert_test.py` — name resolution, roster-in-error,
ambiguous name stays unresolved, name-resolves-to-caller is refused
  - [x] `handoff_to_expert_test.py` — same matrix for handoff
- [x] `list_team_test.py` — roster, archived exclusion, paused flag,
empty team, DB failure, missing auth
- [x] `expert_change_test.py` — duplicate-name refusal, archived-name
reuse is allowed
- [x] Full copilot suite green locally (`poetry run pytest
backend/copilot/` — 5581 passed; the only failures are the pre-existing
`agent_browser_integration_test` / `run_agent_test` cases that need a
real browser and local services)
- [x] `test_db_failure_is_not_reported_as_a_missing_expert` (both
delegation tools), `test_roster_hint_omits_paused_teammates`,
`test_raise_refuses_when_the_roster_cannot_be_read`,
`test_a_matching_bug_is_not_dressed_up_as_a_roster_outage` — each
verified failing without its fix
- [x] `poetry run lint` clean for the touched files (`pyright
backend/copilot/tools/` → 0 errors)

commits.commit_message:
fix(frontend): keep the DataFast signup goal named `signup` (#14173)

### Why

#14167 renamed the goal to `signup_completed`, matching the "Site to

fix(frontend): send the DataFast signup goal under the name the funnel expects (#14167)

### Why

The DataFast "👤 Create Account" funnel step has **never** recorded a
single event. Two independent bugs, either one of which is enough to
zero out the step:

1. **The goal name does not match the funnel.** The code sends `signup`,
but the "Site to Paid" funnel step matches `signup_completed`. Querying
the DataFast API for the site's full history (2025-09-30 → today)
returns 45 goals — neither name appears at all.
2. **`DATAFAST_API_KEY` is not set in Vercel production**, so the
request is never made. That is an ops fix, not a code one, but it also
produced ~4,400 handled Sentry events in 20 days, because a deploy-time
misconfiguration was being reported once per signup:

   | Issue | Path | Events (20d) |
   |---|---|---|
   | BUILDER-8R0 | `POST /signup` | 1,522 |
   | BUILDER-8QZ | `GET /auth/callback` | 2,913 |

Signup itself was never affected — `scheduleAccountCreatedGoal` swallows
the error. The errors are raised *after* the consent-cookie and
visitor-ID checks, which confirms the rest of the pipeline works:
consent mirroring and `datafast_visitor_id` both land correctly.

### What changed

- Send the goal as `signup_completed`, via a named constant tied by
comment to the funnel step it has to match.
- Report a missing or malformed `DATAFAST_API_KEY` **once per server
instance** instead of once per signup, and return `null` rather than
throwing. Same visibility for a real misconfiguration, without burying
the signal — which is why this went unnoticed for 20 days.
- Cover the once-per-instance reporting with a test.

### Still required after merge

Set `DATAFAST_API_KEY` in the **Vercel production** environment (a `df_`
website key from DataFast → Website Settings → API). Production only —
there is a single DataFast website record shared by all environments, so

commits.commit_message:
feat(platform): show live compaction progress in the Copilot chat (#14143) ### Why / What / How **Why:** Context compaction in the Copilot chat is emitted as an instantly-completed tool row *after* the compression work finishes, followed by a long unexplained silence while the transcript re-uploads, the CLI restarts, and an uncached ~100K-token prefill runs. The completed row also silences the remaining `data-status` narration, and the copy ("Earlier messages were summarized to fit within context limits") reads like an apology for the system doing the user a favour. **What:** Turns compaction into one continuous, honest progress moment spanning both the summarization and the post-compaction context rebuild — a live `CompactionCard` with a progress bar that can never land early, phase-aware copy ("Condensing our conversation…" → "Reloading context…"), and a payoff frame with real numbers ("Condensed 412 messages · 128K → 31K tokens"). **How:** Three layers: 1. **Backend ordering fix** — the pre-query emitter is split into `emit_pre_query_start` / `emit_pre_query_end` / `abort_pre_query`, and the row now opens *before* the compression work runs, predicted by a cheap token-estimate pre-check (`_expect_pre_query_compaction`) that mirrors the query builder's actual branch conditions. Wrong predictions are retired; missed ones fall back to a self-contained row. The stream's error path closes any open row. 2. **Wire protocol** — a new transient `data-compaction` SSE data part (`summarizing` / `rebuilding` phases + token/message stats), modelled on `data-status`. The durable record is the tool row's `output`, now a JSON payload (`summary` + camelCase stats) with full back-compat for legacy plain-sentence rows already in the database. 3. **Frontend `CompactionCard`** — an rAF-driven asymptotic progress curve (per-phase exponential approach to a ceiling below 100%, exponential ease to exactly 100% on completion), routed from `tool-context_compaction` parts, excluded from tool chains / collapsed groups / the thinking indicator, gated to the actively-streaming message and to the latest compaction row, and degrading gracefully for replayed and legacy rows. ### Changes 🏗️ **Backend** - `stream_registry.py`: register `data-compaction` in `_reconstruct_chunk`, plus a guard test asserting **every** `ResponseType` survives the executor → Redis → rest_server relay. Without this the feature was inert in any real deployment while every test stayed green — the third time this bug class has landed here. - `response_model.py`: `ResponseType.COMPACTION` (`data-compaction`) + `StreamCompactionProgress` event - `sdk/compaction.py`: `CompactionStats`, JSON tool-row output via `build_compaction_output` (always carries `summary` for back-compat), split pre-query emitters with abort support, `rebuilding` phase appended on both compaction paths - `sdk/service.py`: compaction stats plumbed out of `_compress_messages` / `_build_query_message` (replacing the `was_compacted` boolean), `_will_compact` + `_expect_pre_query_compaction` pre-checks, emission reordered to open the row before the work, open rows closed on stream error **Frontend** - New `CompactionCard/` (component + `useCompactionProgress` rAF hook + pure curve/parsing/copy helpers + Storybook stories) - `MessagePartRenderer`: routes `tool-context_compaction` to the card; renders aborted rows (empty output sentinel) as nothing - `ChatMessagesContainer`: derives the live phase from `data-compaction` parts (only for the streaming message and the latest compaction row), filters the data part from renderable parts, keeps compaction out of `hasInflight` - Chain/grouping helpers: compaction excluded from tool chains and collapsed tool groups; status-message derivation skips `data-compaction` **Tests:** new backend unit tests (event shape, emitter split/ordering/abort, pre-check mirroring, stats plumbing) and frontend tests (curve/parsing/label helpers, component states, page-level SSE integration incl. multi-cycle, abort, stream-stop, replayed-JSON and legacy-row back-compat). ### Known limitations / follow-ups > **Two open questions for a human reviewer** — both left as unresolved review threads rather than quietly decided: > > 1. **The numeric payoff does not appear on the path that actually runs.** QA forced six real compactions across six sessions; all six went through the SDK-internal path, none through the pre-query path. `emit_end_if_ready` hardcodes `build_compaction_output(None)` and `emit_start_if_ready` sends no `tokensBefore`, so on that path the card shows the generic copy. The live bar and the phase copy (`Condensing our conversation…` → `Reloading context…`) *do* work there — what is missing is only the numbers. Deriving them is feasible (the tracker holds the transcript path and can read the compacted entries; the builder knows the before-state) but it is new work rather than a fix. > 2. **A failed compression is now silent.** It used to persist a row claiming the conversation had been summarized when the entire history had actually been dropped; that false claim is fixed, but the replacement says nothing at all. Doing it properly needs a third terminal state for the row (something like "Started a fresh context"), which is new copy and new UI. - **Progress time constants are still educated guesses.** Tuning `tauMs` against production p50/p90 compaction timings needs production log access and is left as a follow-up; the constants are documented in `CompactionCard/helpers.ts`. - **The bar does not ease to 100%.** It stops when the row settles rather than gliding to full. The `done` phase this would have needed is not implementable backend-side — `rebuilding` ends when the response adapter emits the first content chunk, which `CompactionTracker` never sees — so rather than leave unreachable machinery behind, the `done` union member, `PHASE_CURVE.done`, `finishProgress` and their tests were deleted and the wire contract is now `Literal["summarizing", "rebuilding"]`. The settled row still lands with the real numbers. Purely cosmetic; tracked with the `tauMs` follow-up. - **The SDK-internal heartbeat race survives** — if a real SDK message beats the 10s heartbeat, that path still emits a collapsed row (pre-existing; fixing it needs a hook-to-generator queue). - **`data-compaction` parts are not persisted** — refreshing mid-compaction shows the settled row instead of the live bar (accepted; the window is short). - **Codex turns compress at the Sonnet threshold.** The pre-check and the compressor now share one model so they cannot disagree, but they unify on the *compressor's* model; threading the runtime model into compression needs a signature change across mocks in two files this PR doesn't otherwise touch. Pre-existing, separate PR. - **The live progress bar has no end-to-end verification.** Automated QA could not force a genuine compaction against a seeded history (the session loader reported `db_msg_count=1`), so the rAF curve and the phase transitions are covered by integration tests and a relay round-trip test, but not by a live run. The manual E2E box below is honestly unchecked. ### Checklist 📋 #### For code changes: - [x] I have clearly listed my changes in the PR description - [x] I have made a test plan - [x] I have tested my changes according to the test plan: - [x] Backend: `response_model_test.py`, `sdk/compaction_test.py`, `sdk/service_helpers_test.py`, `sdk/prompt_too_long_test.py`, `sdk/query_builder_test.py`, `sdk/context_fallback_test.py`, `sdk/mode_switch_context_test.py`, `sdk/service_test.py` — all green; scoped pyright on `service.py` clean - [x] Frontend: `CompactionCard/__tests__/*`, `copilot/__tests__/compaction-progress.test.tsx` (9 tests incl. abort/multi-cycle/stream-stop/replay, timing-stable across repeated runs), plus the neighbouring ChatMessagesContainer / ToolChain / GenericTool / ChainMessageParts / expert-threads suites — all green; `tsc --noEmit` and lint clean - [ ] Manual E2E against a running stack (not run in this worktree) #### For configuration changes: - [ ] `.env.default` is updated or already compatible with my changes - [ ] `docker-compose.yml` is updated or already compatible with my changes - [ ] I have included a list of my configuration changes in the PR description (under **Changes**)
Examples of configuration changes - Changing ports - Adding new services that need to communicate with each other - Secrets or environment variable changes - New or infrastructure changes such as databases

commits.commit_title: fix(frontend): MCP OAuth popup fails with 'Sign-in window was closed' on COOP providers (#14141)
commits.commit_message:
fix(frontend): MCP OAuth popup fails with 'Sign-in window was closed' on COOP providers (#14141)

### Why / What / How

**Why:** Connecting an MCP server whose OAuth provider serves
`Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` (e.g. Stripe's
`access.stripe.com` MCP authorize pages) always fails with a bogus
**"Sign-in window was closed"** error, even though the user completes
authorization and the callback page reports "Sign-in complete". Screen
recordings show the error banner appearing while the user is still on
Stripe's permission screen.

**What:** `openOAuthPopup` no longer polls `popup.closed` for
cross-origin flows (`useCrossOriginListeners: true`). Same-origin flows
keep the existing immediate reject on close.

**How:** When the popup navigates to a COOP `same-origin` page, the
browser swaps its browsing context group and severs the opener's
`WindowProxy` — from that moment `popup.closed` reads `true` while the
window is still open. The old close-poll saw this ~1s into the flow,
waited its 3s grace, rejected with `OAUTH_ERROR_WINDOW_CLOSED`, and
aborted the controller — tearing down the BroadcastChannel and
localStorage listeners minutes before the user finished signing in. The
callback page then broadcast its successful result to nobody, so no code
exchange happened and no credential was stored.

The close-poll cannot distinguish a COOP-severed handle from a genuinely
closed window, so cross-origin flows now skip it entirely and rely on
the callback result, the overall timeout (5 min default), and the
caller's explicit abort — the same treatment the popup-blocked new-tab
fallback already had for the same reason (see the pre-existing comment
about COOP there). This affects all five call sites (copilot
`MCPSetupCard`, builder `MCPToolDialog`, `McpConnectPanel`,
`useOAuthConnect`, `CredentialsInput`).

Known trade-off: if a user manually closes the provider window mid-flow
in a cross-origin flow, the UI now stays in its connecting state until
the overall timeout or an explicit cancel, instead of failing fast.
There is no reliable close signal under COOP, so this is inherent; a
cancel affordance on `MCPSetupCard` would be a follow-up.

### Changes 🏗️

- `frontend/src/lib/oauth-popup.ts`: restrict the `popup.closed` poll to
same-origin flows; remove the now-dead 3s grace machinery and
final-localStorage-sweep (the periodic 500ms localStorage poll and
BroadcastChannel listener already cover result delivery for cross-origin
flows).
- `frontend/src/lib/oauth-popup.test.ts`: new regression test — a
cross-origin flow whose handle reports `closed` early (COOP swap) must
survive 30s and resolve when the result lands; retitled/adjusted the
tests that asserted the removed grace-window behavior; same-origin
immediate-reject and provider-side-cancel tests unchanged and passing.

tests — 41/41 pass

commits.commit_title: fix(frontend): show budgets in dollars and stop tab panels clipping run cards (#14073)
commits.commit_message:
fix(frontend): show budgets in dollars and stop tab panels clipping run cards (#14073)

### Why / What / How

**Why.** Three unrelated-but-small UI problems that showed up while
walking the raise → team → library flows:

1. **Budgets were shown in credits.** The backend meters spend in
credits, and we were leaking that unit straight into the UI — "500
credits", "12 / 50", "Custom credits…". Nobody reasons about their
weekly spend in credits, and the `$X/week` we did show was bolted on as
a parenthetical.
2. **Run cards were being clipped** in the new agent library layout. The
runs list was capped at `max-h-[76vh]` with a wrapper of
`lg:[&>div]:min-h-0` selectors in `NewAgentLibraryView` — a workaround,
not a fix, and it still clipped at some viewport sizes.
3. **Copy referred to the expert as "it".** Everywhere else in the
product an expert is a "them".

**What / How.**

*Dollars.* New `src/lib/credits.ts` is the single conversion boundary
between the credit-denominated API and the dollar-denominated UI.
Credits go through `creditsToUsdLabel` on the way into a view; dollars
typed by a user come back through `parseUsdToCredits` on the way out.
Nothing else in the UI does the `/100` itself. The custom-budget input
now accepts what a person would actually type (`5`, `$5`, `7.50`,
`1,000`) and rejects anything finer than cents. Internal state and the
API payload stay in credits — only the presentation layer changed.

*Clipping.* The real cause was upstream of the runs list: Radix marks
inactive tab panels with the `hidden` attribute, but the UA rule behind
`[hidden]` is weaker than any author `display` utility. A panel styled
`flex` therefore stayed laid out, kept its height in the column, and
squeezed the active panel. Pinning `data-[state=inactive]:hidden` on
`TabsLineContent` is specific enough to win. With inactive panels
genuinely out of the flow, `SidebarRunsList` can use plain `flex-1` /
`min-h-0` and the `max-h-[76vh]` cap plus the whole
`NewAgentLibraryView` wrapper div and its descendant selectors go away.

### Changes 🏗️

- **New** `src/lib/credits.ts` — `CREDITS_PER_USD`, `creditsToUsdLabel`,
`usdToCredits`, `parseUsdToCredits`. `creditsToUsdLabel` moved here out
of `raise/helpers.ts`.
- **Raise flow** — budget presets read `$5 / week` / `$10 / week`;
custom input is labelled "Custom weekly budget in dollars", uses
`inputMode="decimal"`, and accepts `$`/comma/decimal input;
`parseCredits` → `parseBudget` (delegates to `parseUsdToCredits`);
`kitBudgetLabel` returns `$5 / week` instead of `500 credits ($5/week)`;
hook state renamed `customCredits` → `customAmount`.
- **Team card** — `CreditsMeter` → `SpendMeter`; label "Credits this
week" → "Spend this week"; figures render as `$12 / $50`; the progress
bar's `aria-label` is now "Weekly spend" and its `aria-valuetext`
announces dollars ("$12 of $50 spent this week").
`aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuemax` stay in raw credits so the ratio is
exact.
- **TabsLine** — `data-[state=inactive]:hidden` on `TabsLineContent` so
inactive panels leave the flow regardless of their `display` utility.
- **Library sidebar** — `SidebarRunsList` root and all four tab panels
use `min-h-0 flex-1`; dropped `max-h-[76vh]` and `h-full`; removed the
wrapper `div` and its `lg:[&>div]:min-h-0` descendant selectors from
`NewAgentLibraryView`.
- **Copy** — expert referred to as "them"/"they" rather than "it" across
the raise prompts and `SkillsStep`.
- **Tests** — `CreditsMeter.test.tsx` → `SpendMeter.test.tsx` with
dollar assertions incl. an over-budget case that exercises the cents
path (`$80.25 of $50`); `parseBudget` covers `$7.50`, `1,000`, sub-cent
rejection, and the max-budget ceiling; raise/team page tests updated to
the new labels.

### Checklist 📋

#### For code changes:
- [x] I have clearly listed my changes in the PR description
- [x] I have made a test plan
- [x] I have tested my changes according to the test plan:
- [x] `pnpm test:unit` over `raise/` and `team/` — 194 tests across 23
files pass
  - [x] `pnpm types` — clean
  - [x] `prettier --check` on all changed files — clean
- [ ] `/raise` — budget step offers `$5 / week` and `$10 / week`; typing
`7.50` in the custom field enables submit and stores 750 credits;
`12.555` leaves it disabled
- [ ] `/team` — expert card reads "Spend this week" with `$12 / $50`;
meter fill matches the ratio
- [ ] `/library/agents/[id]` with the new layout flag — switch between
Runs / Scheduled / Triggers / Templates and confirm no card clipping at
1512×949 and at a short viewport, and that each list scrolls within its
own column

commits.commit_message:
fix(frontend/copilot): clear the composer as soon as a message is sent

`onSend` resolves only when the whole assistant stream finishes, so
clearing after the await left the sent message sitting in the composer
for the entire turn. The eager clear that fixes this already existed but
rode the `new-tool-ui` flag, so everyone outside that cohort — including
dev — kept the stale text.

Drop the flag branch: the composer and its attachment chips now clear on
submit for everyone, and a failed send restores the draft with a toast
instead of rejecting into an unhandled promise.

The old tests all resolved `onSend` immediately, which passed either way;
the two new ones hold the send promise open and assert the composer is
already empty.

feat(platform): expert team tools and copilot chat polish behind flags (#14099)

### Why / What / How

**Why:** The expert-team tools (delegate/handoff/hire/raise/update from
chat) and the copilot chat polish built alongside them must not change
anything for users outside the beta cohorts. Everything user-visible in
this PR therefore rides an existing feature flag, and users without the
flags keep today's behaviour bit for bit.

**What:**
- Expert team from chat, gated by **`hire-experts`**:
- `delegate_to_expert` — run a task as a *teammate* (their identity,
memory namespace, and weekly budget), with cross-scope polling via
`get_sub_session_result` guarded by the recorded delegating-session id.
- `handoff_to_expert` — transfer ownership of a task to a teammate
(expert sessions only).
- `hire_expert` / `raise_expert` / `update_expert` + one shared
`confirm_expert_change` — preview→confirm staffing changes from the
Autopilot chat (`expert_admin` group, never available inside an expert
session).
- `<team_context>` roster block for expert sessions (self excluded) with
the delegation rule.
- Home "Needs You" **question items**: `ask_question` parks the pending
question on the session; replying clears it; Home links back into the
chat.
- Chat/tool UI polish, gated by **`new-tool-ui`**:
- Always-on thread header (expert identity or Autopilot), chat minimap,
workspace file cards + artifacts tab in the context panel, sub-session
live view inside the chain, expert change cards, truncated-output
preview cards, spinner/swap-text glitch fixes, eager composer clear with
restore-on-failure, and a resume fix that drops db-hydrated partial
turns before the GET-resume replays them.

**How:**
- Backend: a new `delegation` tool group; both engines (baseline + SDK)
disable `experts`, `expert_admin`, and `delegation` groups whenever
`is_feature_enabled(Flag.HIRE_EXPERTS, user_id)` is false (fail-closed
for anonymous turns), and keep the existing expert_id-based split when
it is true. The gate is enforced at *execution*, not just at
schema-build time: `execute_tool` re-checks the tool's group and refuses
anything disabled, so a model that names a hidden tool anyway (replayed
transcript, flag flipped mid-session) cannot reach `tool.execute`. The
delegation prompt rules are gated on the same boolean, so flag-off turns
are never told to call tools they cannot run. Home's
`_get_pending_questions` returns `[]` without the flag, so the dashboard
payload is unchanged for old users.
- Frontend: every shared component that the new UI restyles branches on
`useGetFlag(Flag.NEW_TOOL_UI)` back to its exact old markup/behaviour
(context panel close button + tabs, panel toggle, artifact card
shape/icons, message-action hover opacity, composer clear timing, resume
trim). Expert-side sidebar/recent-chat changes sit behind the
already-flagged `HIRE_EXPERTS` surfaces.
- Old tool UI compatibility: the new tools render through the legacy
`GenericTool` path with proper display names (`delegate_to_expert` →
"Teammate hand-off", etc.), so a `hire-experts`-on / `new-tool-ui`-off
user sees sensible legacy cards and nothing breaks.
- `ask_question`'s pending-question write is intentionally unflagged
(invisible metadata; the Home read is what's gated), so flipping the
flag on later surfaces existing questions rather than losing them.

### Changes 🏗️

- Backend: 6 new copilot tools + `expert_proposal` store, tool-group
flag gating in both engines, `ChatSessionMetadata` provenance +
`pending_question` fields, Home question attention items,
`experts/errors.py` extraction, DB-manager exposure for
hire/raise/counts.
- Frontend: ToolChain sub-session live view + expert cards +
superseded-row dedup, ChatMinimap, WorkspaceFileCards, ArtifactsTab,
flag-gated restyles listed above, legacy display names for the new
tools, sidebar team-roster removal (flagged surface),
collapsed-by-default recent-chat groups (flagged surface).
- `openapi.json` re-exported byte-exact via `export-api-schema` +
prettier.

- [x] `pnpm types`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format` clean; full `pnpm
test:unit` green (5715 tests)

delegate/handoff/expert-change tests), home attention/routes/service,

`openapi.json`
- [x] Flag-off behaviour: old context-panel close button restored,

commits.commit_title: feat(blocks): make the AutoPilot transport an explicit choice (#14070)
commits.commit_message:
feat(blocks): make the AutoPilot transport an explicit choice (#14070)

### Why / What / How

AutoPilot can run on platform credits or through a connected
ChatGPT/Codex account. Inferring the billing route only from an attached
credential made the choice invisible, made switching back to platform
credits unreliable, and allowed stale credential metadata to misclassify
platform-funded usage.

This PR makes the route explicit while preserving nodes saved or
imported before the field existed. `transport=None` remains the legacy
sentinel: an attached connection keeps its original ChatGPT billing
route, while an explicit `platform` choice never resolves,
entitlement-checks, preflights, persists, or attributes usage to that
stale connection.

The credential schema maps only `codex_app_server` to Codex; `platform`
is deliberately credential-free. Graph aggregation, Copilot preflight,
and execution share `CredentialsFieldInfo.requires_credentials()`,
scoped so required credential fields still fail closed. Runtime
validates new and resumed sessions against the selected route. A narrow
atomic startup backfill normalizes stored legacy nodes that contain a
real Codex credential. Imports created before the transport field remain
compatible; exports preserve an explicit ChatGPT route after credential
references are stripped, so recipients must reconnect or switch to
platform credits rather than silently changing who pays.

### Changes 🏗️

- Add an explicit AutoPilot transport selector with a visible
placeholder and user-facing `AutoGPT Platform` / `ChatGPT` labels.
- Show the ChatGPT connection only for Codex or for a legacy node that
already has a saved connection.
- Clear unused credential metadata before schema validation on explicit
platform runs so empty or stale references cannot block execution or
mislabel billing attribution.
- Preserve legacy unset-transport billing and render its saved
connection.
- Fail closed when Codex has no connection, a required credential
discriminator is invalid, a future transport is unsupported, or a
resumed session uses a different route.
- Return actionable errors for missing and route-mismatched sessions.
- Skip credential slots, setup cards, resolution, and entitlement checks
for optional credential-free selections across graph, Copilot, and
executor paths.
- Backfill matching stored nodes from the data layer with one atomic,
idempotent JSON update; apply mode no longer performs a redundant count
query and startup waits at most 30 seconds.
- Add focused frontend/backend coverage plus a real-Postgres migration
test for matching, exclusions, and idempotency.
- Consolidate duplicate frontend provider resolution and remove an
unreachable schema guard.

### Checklist 📋

#### For code changes:
- [x] I have clearly listed my changes in the PR description
- [x] I have made a test plan
- [x] I have tested my changes according to the test plan:
  - [x] `poetry run format` (Ruff, isort, Black, Prisma stubs, Pyright)
- [x] 73 focused backend credential, routing, Copilot, and migration
unit tests
  - [x] `pnpm format` and `pnpm types`
  - [x] 66 focused frontend transport and credential tests
- [x] Hosted QA applied the migration to seeded rows and verified
exclusions and idempotency
- [ ] Full GitHub backend/frontend/full-stack matrix on the latest head

The local real-Postgres test attempt was blocked before the test body by
the shared server fixture waiting for RabbitMQ on `127.0.0.1:5672`; the
same SQL behavior was exercised successfully by hosted QA, and the
checked-in database test will run in CI.

#### For configuration changes:

- [x] `.env.default` is already compatible
- [x] `docker-compose.yml` is already compatible
- [x] No configuration changes are required

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes who pays for AutoPilot runs (platform credits vs ChatGPT),
credential resolution, graph validation, and a startup JSON backfill of
stored nodes. A routing or migration bug could misbill users or break
save/run of existing graphs.
> 
> **Overview**
> Makes AutoPilot billing an explicit **Transport** choice (`platform`
vs `codex_app_server`) instead of inferring it from whether a ChatGPT
credential is attached.
> 
> `transport` stays optional so legacy nodes (credential, no field) keep
billing the connection, while an explicit `platform` choice never uses a
leftover credential. Codex without a connection fails closed; resumed
sessions must match the selected route.
> 
> Graph aggregation, Copilot preflight, and the executor skip optional
credential-free selections via `requires_credentials()`, so platform
runs do not resolve, entitlement-check, or persist stale Codex metadata.
Required unmapped credentials still fail closed.
> 
> The builder hides the ChatGPT connection when it does not apply,
strips unused credential metadata on save, and gates optional enum
options (including `anyOf`). A guarded, idempotent startup backfill sets
`transport=codex_app_server` on stored AutoPilot nodes that already have
a real Codex credential.

commits.commit_title: fix(backend/executor): fail a run that was denied by entitlement (#14060)
commits.commit_message:
fix(backend/executor): fail a run that was denied by entitlement (#14060)

## Why

A run denied by entitlement reported **`COMPLETED` with `error: null`**,
while the node inside carried the real denial:

```
AgentGraphExecution:  status=COMPLETED, error=null
AgentNodeExecution:   status=FAILED,    error="A Max plan or higher is required to use ChatGPT."
```

Anything keying off graph-level status — the UI, notifications,
analytics — saw a clean success. Observed while verifying #14058 at the
PRO tier.

## What

Classify `UserPaywalledError` as a typed failure reason, and widen the
graph status check from one hardcoded reason to any typed reason.

## How

Node errors are **deliberately** non-fatal: a graph may wire an error
output onward, so a failing node is not by itself a failing run. Only
*typed* failures promote to graph stats via `_propagate_node_failure`.
`UserPaywalledError` was already a typed exception — it simply had no
classification, so it never promoted, and the status check special-cased
the single reason that existed at the time:

```python
elif (error is not None
      or execution_stats.failure_reason == ExecutionFailureReason.INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE):
```

Two changes:

1. `get_execution_failure_reason` classifies `UserPaywalledError` → new
`ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED`.
2. The status check becomes `execution_stats.failure_reason is not
None`.

**Untyped node errors keep their current behaviour.** This only affects
failures the system already trusts as terminal — the generalisation was
a no-op the moment before this PR added the second reason, which is what
makes it safe.

### Why `UserPaywalledError` moves

Classifying it from its old home is a genuine import cycle:

```
util.exceptions <- data.model <- data.user <- copilot.rate_limit
```

So it moves to `util/exceptions` (where it belongs — it is a general
execution concern, not a copilot rate-limit one) and is **re-exported
from `rate_limit`**, leaving every existing call site untouched. A test
pins the re-export. The repo forbids inner imports, so a lazy import was
not an option.

### Falls out of the same change

`util/metrics` already suppresses Sentry reports for classified
failures, so a paywall denial stops being reported as a platform bug.
That is the correct outcome — it is expected business logic, not a
defect.

`openapi.json` moves by one line: the `ExecutionFailureReason` enum
gains a member.

## Testing

33 tests in `exceptions_test.py`, 3 new: classification by type, the
re-export, and that the same wording as a plain `RuntimeError` is
**not** classified (classification is by type, never by message text —
matching the existing rule for balance errors).

## Checklist

- [x] Tests pass locally
- [x] `poetry run format` / `lint` / pyright clean
- [x] Every `UserPaywalledError` import site verified to still resolve
- [x] Untyped node-error semantics unchanged

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes graph execution status and failure classification for
paywalled runs, which affects UI, analytics, alerts, and Sentry
filtering. Untyped node errors are intended to stay non-fatal.
> 
> **Overview**
> Entitlement denials no longer look like successful runs.
`UserPaywalledError` is now a typed `ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED` failure, so
the graph is marked **FAILED** instead of **COMPLETED** with a null
error while the node still held the denial.
> 
> The executor treats any classified `failure_reason` as terminal (not
only insufficient balance). Paywall errors are known outcomes: they skip
LLM activity-status generation, stay out of Discord “unknown error”
pages, and are already filtered from Sentry via typed classification.
> 
> `UserPaywalledError` moves to `util.exceptions` to break an import
cycle and is re-exported from `copilot.rate_limit` so existing imports
keep working. OpenAPI gains the new enum member. Untyped node errors are
unchanged.
>

commits.commit_title: fix(frontend): say when a connection was removed instead of quietly swapping it (#14059)
commits.commit_message:
fix(frontend): say when a connection was removed instead of quietly swapping it (#14059)

## Why

Disconnecting and reconnecting an integration can mint a new credential
id, leaving an agent configured with an id that no longer resolves. The
builder already clears invalid references and may auto-select a lone
replacement, but doing that silently hides an important configuration
change.

The usable credential list is also filtered by type, scopes, and
discriminator, so absence from that list does not necessarily mean the
credential was deleted.

## What

- Clear a selected credential when it is no longer usable for the field.
- Use the provider's unfiltered credential list to distinguish a deleted
connection from one that is merely filtered out.
- When a deleted connection has one usable replacement, preserve the
existing auto-heal behavior and report the replacement.
- When no single replacement can be chosen, explain that the removed
connection must be replaced.
- Dismiss the notice after every explicit selection path, including
dropdown, OAuth, and credential creation.
- Do not show the external-removal notice while the user is deleting
that credential themselves.
- Render the notice as an accessible warning and use the existing
credential display-name fallback when a replacement has no title.

## How

`useCredentials` now exposes the provider's unfiltered credentials
alongside the filtered `savedCredentials` list. `useCredentialsInput`
reconciles selection against both lists, resets auto-selection only when
reconciliation clears a value, and funnels explicit changes through one
notice-clearing handler. The hook's return type also reflects its real
loading contract: it returns `null` while loading and loaded data
afterward.

## Testing

- `pnpm format`
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm types`
- `vitest` credential input, credential hook, and the previously failing
expert-kickoff suites: 29/29 passing
- Full frontend unit run: 5,136/5,142 passing under full contention;
five unrelated failures passed in a focused rerun, and the remaining
Raise test fails in an untouched router mock while the downstream
stack's hosted frontend CI is green

## Checklist

- [x] Removed credentials are reported accurately
- [x] Filtered-but-existing credentials are not reported as deleted
- [x] Manual deletion does not produce a misleading notice
- [x] Explicit selections dismiss the notice
- [x] Existing lone-credential auto-selection is preserved
- [x] Formatting, lint, types, and focused tests pass locally

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches credential selection and auto-heal in the agent builder, which
can change which connection a node uses. Logic is frontend-only with
tests covering heal vs. filter vs. user-delete cases.
> 
> **Overview**
> When a node’s saved credential id no longer exists (typical after
disconnect/reconnect), the builder still auto-selects a lone remaining
connection, but now **shows a warning** instead of swapping silently. If
nothing usable remains, it asks the user to pick a replacement.
> 
> `useCredentials` exposes unfiltered `allProviderCredentials` so a
credential that is only filtered out (type/scopes) is cleared without
being reported as deleted. Explicit picks, OAuth reconnect, and
in-progress user deletes dismiss or skip the notice. Loading is treated
as `null` rather than an empty list, so stale selections are no longer
skipped.
>

code reviews on this repo. Configure

commits.commit_title: fix(platform): stop codex transport reaching non-entitled users (#14058)
commits.commit_message:
fix(platform): stop codex transport reaching non-entitled users (#14058)

## Why

The ChatGPT/Codex transport is gated to Max and above, but it was
reaching users below that tier. While investigating, a worse symptom
turned up: **the AutoPilot block was unusable for everyone** — adding it
to a canvas and saving returned `HTTP 500` with a body of just `'id'`.

That second one is not limited to non-entitled users. A paying Max
customer hits it the moment they add an AutoPilot block without having
connected ChatGPT, because the form emits a half-populated credential
object with no user interaction at all.

## What

Six distinct defects. **Only #3 and #6 are codex-specific** — the rest
are general bugs the codex work happened to trip first.

| # | Defect | File | Blast radius |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Graph activation indexed `creds_meta["id"]` on a meta that had
none | `graph_lifecycle_hooks.py` | every AutoPilot save |
| 2 | Builder stripped only the literal key `credentials`, not
`*_credentials` | `FormCreator.tsx` | 5 blocks, 9 fields |
| 3 | Aggregation fell back to an un-discriminated union, advertising
codex as required | `data/graph.py` | `CodeGenerationBlock` |
| 4 | Required asterisk came from a node toggle instead of the schema |
`CredentialField.tsx` | AutoPilot + MCP Tool |
| 5 | An unavailable provider left a titled row with no control beneath
it | `CredentialField.tsx` | any gated provider |
| 6 | The transport dropdown offered a value whose provider the account
cannot connect | `gateDiscriminatorOptions.ts` | `CodeGenerationBlock` |

Plus an auth-bootstrap fix that #5 depends on: the credentials provider
published an empty map while `isLoggedIn` was still false during auth
init, making "loading" and "not available to you" indistinguishable —
entitled users saw a flash of the wrong state on every page load.

## How

**#3 is the subtle one.** `combine()` flattens a *dependent* pair into a
cross-product. Code Generation's credential is the coupled set
`{(openai, api_key), (codex, oauth2)}`, but the un-discriminated union
advertises `{codex, openai} × {api_key, oauth2}` — asserting two pairs
that don't exist. The fix resolves the discriminator from the block's
schema default, which is what the executor already does at run time
(`blocks/_base.py` builds `input_schema(**input_default)`, so pydantic
fills it).

Deliberately scoped to fields where the credential **type** depends on
the discriminator. For mapping-only discriminators — every LLM block —
the type set is a singleton, product equals sum, and the union is
faithful. Those keep their aggregated slot key, which matters because
**persisted presets and schedules are stored under it**; collapsing it
would silently orphan them. A test asserts exactly one block satisfies
the trigger condition today, so the next block to add
`discriminator_type_mapping` inherits this consciously.

**#6** closes the dead end the other fixes exposed: you could still
*pick* `codex_app_server` on a non-entitled account, then be told it was
unavailable. The filter is keyed off the credential field's own
`discriminator` / `discriminator_mapping`, so it follows the schema
instead of hardcoding codex. Blast radius is exactly one option —
`list_providers` removes a single provider (codex, on non-entitled
accounts) and returns every other provider unconditionally, so LLM
blocks, which discriminate on `model` across eight always-present
providers, keep every option. A test pins that. Two values are never
filtered: one already saved on a node (hiding it would silently rewrite
the node), and the last remaining option.

**Runtime enforcement is untouched** and remains the security boundary.
Everything here is UX.

`single-container/entrypoint.sh` makes `BEHAVE_AS` overridable (same
`local` default). It was hardcoded and overrode `docker run -e`, leaving
the image unable to exercise any entitlement-gated feature.

## Verification

Tests: **4882 frontend** (467 files), **97 backend** across touched
areas. 15 new tests; every fix has one that fails without it.

Also verified manually against a running single-container build at three
subscription tiers, each confirmed in the database:

| Surface | NO_TIER | PRO | MAX |
|---|---|---|---|
| AutoPilot codex field | absent | absent | present, no asterisk |
| Select codex transport | — | "Not available on your account." | "Sign
in with ChatGPT" |
| Settings → Integrations | — | no match | OpenAI / ChatGPT |
| Copilot chat transport | platform only | platform only | platform +
ChatGPT |
| `has_codex_access` | False | False | True |
| Save a graph | 200 | 200 | 200 |

Key assertions:

- **The persisted record, not the toast.** A save can return 200 while
still writing the malformed object, so the node row was read back: no
`codex_credentials` key. The field *is* in the schema with `advanced:
false`, so its absence is the fix rather than the field being missing.
- **The union is gone from the run dialog.** A default-transport Code
Generation graph asks for OpenAI only. A single row accepting both
openai and codex — the bug in its user-facing form — was never observed
on any account.
- **Runtime enforcement still denies.** Proven at PRO (clears the
general paywall, below the codex gate): a real queued execution failed
with `"A Max plan or higher is required to use ChatGPT."`
- **Self-hosters unaffected.** Under `BEHAVE_AS=local`,
`has_codex_access` returns True for NO_TIER and PRO — the `allow_local`
carve-out, the exact inverse of the cloud result.

The manual pass earned its keep by finding a bug in the fix itself:
non-entitled users selecting the codex transport got the "not available"
explanation under a field **still marked required**, because the
hide-logic only covered the optional case. Fixed, with tests pinning
both directions.

## Known gaps

- **MCP Tool asterisk, E2E** — untested; the block only instantiates
after a live MCP server handshake. Unit-covered against its exact schema
shape, and the same optional-credential class is demonstrated in the UI
by AutoPilot.
- **Marketplace install** — not exercised.
- **Counterfactual E2E** — the fixed build is proven correct end to end;
that the *unfixed* build fails rests on unit tests reproducing
`KeyError: 'id'`, not a second container built from master.

## Follow-ups (stacked on this PR)

These ship as a stack on top of this branch rather than growing this PR.

1. **Codex reconnect mints a new credential id.**
`credentials_from_bundle()` builds without an `id`, so reconnecting
breaks every graph referencing the old one. AutoPilot's optional field
fails *silently* — the stale ref is cleared and the node falls back to
the platform transport, so the user reconnects, sees a connected
account, and their agent quietly stops using their ChatGPT plan.
`checkpoint_credentials_from_bundle` already preserves the id for token
rotation; login just doesn't reuse that path.
2. **A denied run reports success.** `AgentGraphExecution` shows
`COMPLETED` / `error: null` while the node inside carries the real
paywall failure. Anything keying off graph-level status misses the
denial.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests pass locally (frontend 4889 across 467 files, backend 97)
- [x] `pnpm format` / `pnpm lint` / `pnpm types` clean
- [x] Manually verified at three subscription tiers
- [x] Follow-ups identified and scoped out

>

required) credential for users who cannot connect it, and fixes the

commits.commit_message:
feat(stripe-link): pay MPP merchants, and say which block to use when (#14066)

> Stacked on #14063 — review #14062 and #14063 first.

## Summary

Lets an agent actually complete a purchase. Everything below this PR
could obtain a payment credential; nothing could spend one.

Adds the two blocks that close the loop for merchants speaking the
Machine Payments Protocol — no checkout form, no card number, nothing
for a human to type — and rewrites the descriptions across all seven
Link blocks so the two payment paths are distinguishable without reading
the source.

## The two paths

| | **Virtual card** (Create Card Spend Request) | **Shared Payment
Token** (Create Token Spend Request) |
|---|---|---|
| For | Ordinary merchants with a checkout form | Merchants answering
HTTP 402 |
| Yields | PAN, CVC, expiry to enter | A token spent programmatically |
| Needs | — | `network_id` from Get Payment Challenge |

## Changes

- **Get Payment Challenge** — probes a merchant and, if it answers 402
with a Stripe challenge, returns `network_id`, `amount` and `currency`
for the spend request. Reports `supports_mpp: false` for ordinary
merchants *and* for 402s offering only onchain methods, so a graph can
branch to the card flow rather than fail.
- **MPP Pay** — takes an approved SPT spend request and spends it:
probe, build the credential from the challenge, retry with
`Authorization: Payment ...`. Refuses an unapproved request and explains
the mismatch when handed a card request.
- **Descriptions** for all seven blocks, stating where each sits in the
sequence.

## The credential format is undocumented

There is no spec. It was read out of `Credential.serialize` in
`mppx@0.8.15` — unpadded base64url of `{challenge, payload: {spt}}`,
with the challenge's `request` passed through byte-for-byte because the
server HMAC-binds it — and confirmed by settling a real payment.
`mpp_test.py` pins that shape, including that unknown challenge fields
must not be echoed back, so a format change fails loudly here rather
than silently at payment time.

## Verified live

A real $1.00 payment to Stripe's own MPP demo merchant
(`climate.stripe.dev`), end to end: device auth → approval → SPT spend
request → approval → token retrieved → credential accepted and verified
→ `200 {"contribution_id": "pi_3U5ef2…", "impact": "~2.67kg of permanent
carbon removal"}`.

An earlier attempt on an unfunded card returned a clean
`verification-failed` 402 quoting the real reason, so the decline path
is legible too.

## Security

Both hops go through `backend.util.request.Requests`, which validates
URLs and blocks private networks. This matters more than usual here: the
URL is agent-supplied and the retry attaches a bearer payment
credential, so an unvalidated client could be steered into handing a
payment token to an arbitrary or internal host. Caller-supplied headers
are spread *before* transport headers so they cannot displace
`Authorization` or `Content-Type`, and the merchant-controlled challenge
blob is size-bounded and type-checked.

## Testing

`_pay_with_token` end to end with a recording client: the first hop is
unauthenticated (that is what elicits the challenge), the credential is
attached only on the retry, a 200 on the first hop never sends the
token, a 402 without a Stripe method raises, and caller headers cannot
displace the credential. Plus challenge parsing (multi-method headers),
the credential wire shape, and both decode guards. Backend-wide pyright
and ruff clean.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Sends a bearer Shared Payment Token to agent-supplied merchant URLs
and completes real charges. SSRF, header spoofing, and paid-vs-unpaid
reporting are security- and money-sensitive.
> 
> **Overview**
> Agents can now finish a Machine Payments Protocol purchase: probe a
merchant’s HTTP 402, then spend an approved Shared Payment Token with no
checkout form or card number.
> 
> **Get Payment Challenge** reads a Stripe `WWW-Authenticate: Payment`
challenge and yields `network_id`, amount, and currency for Create Token
Spend Request. It reports `supports_mpp=false` for ordinary or
onchain-only merchants, and `payment_required` so graphs can branch to
the virtual-card flow. Failed probes (e.g. 503) error instead of looking
like “not MPP.”
> 
> **MPP Pay** loads an approved SPT spend request, probes
unauthenticated, then retries with `Authorization: Payment …`
(mppx-shaped, HMAC-bound `request` blob). Unapproved or card-type
requests are refused. `paid` is true only when the credential-bearing
retry returns 2xx.
> 
> Requests go through SSRF-guarded `Requests` (no redirects, redacted
block errors). Caller `Authorization` cannot displace the credential;
challenge blobs and merchant bodies are size-bounded. Existing Link
block descriptions are rewritten so the card vs token sequences are
distinguishable.
>

commits.commit_message:
feat(stripe-link): enrich the approval sheet, handle requires_action (#14063)

> Stacked on #14062 — review that one first.

## Summary

Makes the Stripe Link spend request usable for real purchases: a richer
approval sheet, correct handling of 3D Secure, and a second credential
type for merchants that take payment programmatically.

## Why

Inspecting the raw spend-request object the Link app renders showed
`spend_information` arriving as `{line_items: [], totals: []}` — the
user approving a charge saw an amount and no breakdown. Separately,
`requires_action` was treated as terminal, so an agent hitting 3DS would
stall silently rather than poll.

## Changes

- **Approval-sheet fields** — `line_items`, `totals`, `metadata`. Link
formats what we send (it echoed back `displayable_quantity: "(x1)"` and
`displayable_unit_amount: "$0.25"`), so raw integers are correct.
Omitted when empty, since an explicit `[]` is not the same as
unspecified.
- **`requires_action`** — yields `next_action_type`,
`next_action_message`, `next_action_url` and `auto_resumes`. That last
one is the distinction that matters: 3DS resolves itself and the caller
should keep polling; anything else needs the user to act and a fresh
request.
- **Shared Payment Tokens** — a dedicated **Create Token Spend Request**
block posting `credential_type: shared_payment_token` and `network_id`.
(Originally a `credential_type` discriminator on one create block; split
in two once the card flow became deployment-gated, since a single block
cannot be half-available.)
- **`connection_label` bounded to 32 chars** — Link truncates there, and
the label is the *headline* of the approval sheet (`"<label> is
requesting to spend $X"`), so a long host rendered as `AutoGPT on
prompt-neat-flea.ngro`. A clean `AutoGPT` beats a severed hostname; a
real deployment still gets the host.
- **Link's error message is surfaced** — `raise_for_status()` reported
`400 Bad Request` and discarded the explanation.

## Verified live

Against a real Link account, not mocks. The approval sheet renders the
itemised breakdown and the corrected title. Two constraints were found
only by calling the API:

- `merchant_name`/`merchant_url` are **rejected** for
`shared_payment_token` — the merchant is identified by `network_id`. The
block omits them automatically.
- `request_approval` in the create body and `POST
/spend_requests/{id}/request_approval` are alternatives, not a sequence;
calling both returns 409.

## Security note

~~`shared_payment_token` is emitted as a block output...~~ **Resolved:**
the SPT output was removed entirely. `StripeLinkMPPPayBlock` fetches the
token in-process and never emits it, so nothing consumed the output —
removing it takes a persisted bearer credential off the table rather
than defending one. The card fields in #14062 are now gated to
self-hosted deployments; see that PR.

## Testing

Presentation fields reaching the request and being omitted when empty;
both 3DS resolutions; the SPT create body (merchant fields dropped,
`network_id` present) and the card body; `network_id` enforcement; both
`link_api_request` error paths; the label bound. Backend-wide pyright
and ruff clean.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Touches payment spend-request creation, user-facing approval amounts,
and 3DS polling. A bug in totals matching, auto_resumes, or merchant
identity could mis-authorize charges or issue duplicate credentials.
> 
> **Overview**
> Makes Stripe Link spend requests usable for real checkouts: a richer
approval sheet, a dedicated Shared Payment Token create path, and proper
handling of `requires_action` (3D Secure).
> 
> **Create** is split into card vs token blocks that share
`_BaseSpendRequestInput`. Card still uses merchant name/URL (self-hosted
only). Token posts `credential_type: shared_payment_token` and
`network_id` from the 402 challenge, and stays available on Cloud. Both
can send `line_items`, `totals`, and `metadata` (omitted when empty). A
validator rejects a `totals` line of type `total` that does not match
the authorized `amount`.
> 
> **Status polling** now surfaces `requires_action` with next-action
type/message/URL and `auto_resumes` (keep polling for 3DS; start over
only when Link says `new_spend_request`). Nested nulls no longer crash
after `status` is emitted.
> 
> **API client** treats non-2xx (including redirects) as errors,
surfaces Link’s `error.message` (truncated) into the block error output,
and logs raw bodies instead of persisting them. Device-auth
`connection_label` is capped at 32 characters so the approval-sheet
headline is not a truncated hostname.
>

aa55da8e803e42643bf39d346c3640257df539fe. Bugbot is set up for automated
code reviews on this repo. Configure
[here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

commits.commit_title: feat(platform): device code OAuth flow + Stripe Link wallet blocks (#14062)
commits.commit_message:
feat(platform): device code OAuth flow + Stripe Link wallet blocks (#14062)

## Summary

Adds OAuth 2.0 Device Code Grant (RFC 8628) as a first-class auth
method, and Stripe Link as its first consumer — so an agent can hold a
one-time-use payment credential from a user's Link wallet, with the user
approving every spend.

This started as an exploration branch from April that never opened a PR.
It has been brought up to current `dev` and made to actually work; the
exploration doc is kept as `blocks/stripe_link/EXPLORATION.md` because
the option analysis it records is still the rationale for the design.

## Why a new auth flow

AutoGPT's OAuth support assumes the Authorization Code Grant: redirect,
callback, exchange `code` once. Link CLI uses the Device Code Grant —
show a code phrase, the user approves on another device, and the client
*polls* for the token. Those don't map onto each other, so
`BaseDeviceAuthHandler` sits alongside `BaseOAuthHandler` rather than
inside it. It is provider-agnostic and reusable for any CLI/IoT-style
provider.

This is **not** the same mechanism as the existing Codex "device login",
which spawns a sandboxed Codex CLI subprocess and harvests its auth
bundle. The two share a user-facing shape and nothing else; they stay
independent.

## Changes

**Auth**
- `BaseDeviceAuthHandler` (RFC 8628) + `DEVICE_HANDLERS_BY_NAME`
registry
- `StripeLinkDeviceAuthHandler` — device code, polling, refresh, revoke
- `POST /{provider}/device-auth/initiate` and `/poll`
- Polling-safe state tokens: `peek_state_token` (non-consuming) and
`consume_state_token` (terminal only), so a state survives many polls
but is single-use at the end
- `device_code` added to `CredentialsType`; credential manager falls
back to the device registry for refresh

**Blocks** (`blocks/stripe_link/`)
- List Payment Methods, Create Spend Request, Retrieve Spend Request
- Get User Info, Get Shipping Address — an agent that can pay but cannot
say who it is or where to ship cannot finish a checkout

**Frontend**
- `DeviceAuthConnectButton` + `useDeviceAuthConnect`, shown on a new
"Device auth" tab. The code phrase and verification URL render inline in
the connect dialog and it polls for completion — no redirect.

## Verified against a real Link account

Not mocked. Device auth → approval on a phone → credential stored and
encrypted → block resolves it → authenticated call to `api.link.com`:

- a real virtual card provisioned and retrieved (16-digit PAN, CVC,
expiry, `valid_until`), live mode
- payment methods, user info and shipping address all returned real data
- `authorization_pending` polling, and the `scopes[0].split(" ")`
un-flattening of Link's space-delimited scope string

Live testing found a bug nothing else could: the list block called
`/payment_methods`, which 404s. The real resource is `/payment-details`,
with the list nested under a `payment_details` key. The skeleton had
been written from the CLI's *command* names rather than its HTTP
surface, so the mocks encoded the same wrong assumption. Fixtures now
carry the real wire shape.

## Security notes

- The initiate response deliberately omits `device_code`. It is the
secret used to poll; the poll endpoint takes only `state_token` and
reads the device code from server-side state, so the browser never needs
it.
- `context` on a spend request now enforces `min_length=100` rather than
only documenting it — that string is what the user reads when deciding
whether to approve a charge.
- `amount` is capped at 50000 (`ge=1, le=50000`).
- `card_number` and `card_cvc` are emitted as plain block outputs. That
is inherent to the feature, but reviewers should be aware anything wired
downstream receives them.

## Known limitations

- `/sources`, `/transactions` and `/balances` return 403
`feature_unavailable`. I tested whether RFC 9396 `authorization_details`
were the cause by comparing two grants, one with the source actions and
one without — both still 403. It is an account entitlement, not
something we can fix in code.
- The approval sheet shows a placeholder icon. The logo lives on
`merchant_information.icon_url`, resolved server-side by Stripe, with no
input field in the SDK.
- `line_items`, `totals`, `metadata` and the Shared Payment Token flow
are not here yet, and `requires_action` (e.g. 3DS) is not handled — the
status block treats every non-approved status as terminal. Both are
follow-ups, stacked on this PR (#14063).
- Every client of `@stripe/link-cli` shares one hardcoded public client
ID (`lwlpk_…`). Our own would be a conversation with Stripe.

## Testing

- `integrations/oauth/device_base_test.py` — refresh-skew window,
no-expiry case, foreign-provider guard, scope defaulting
- `integrations/oauth/stripe_link_test.py` — response mapping, optional
`interval`, each of the four RFC 8628 400-codes, `slow_down` backoff,
loud failure on an unrecognised response, refresh-token rotation,
revoke, and that `_get_oauth_handler` resolves the *device* registry
- 5 blocks under the standard runner
- 30 tests; `tsc` clean; `poetry run lint` and `pyright` clean; block
docs in sync

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Touches authentication, credential storage/refresh/revoke, and
payment-adjacent data (virtual cards, PANs/CVCs on self-hosted). A bug
here can leak tokens, leave live grants, or persist cardholder data.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **OAuth 2.0 Device Code Grant (RFC 8628)** as a platform auth
method, with **Stripe Link** as the first provider, so users approve
access on another device and agents can request spend credentials from a
Link wallet.
> 
> **Auth.** New `BaseDeviceAuthHandler` plus `DEVICE_HANDLERS_BY_NAME`,
with `POST /{provider}/device-auth/initiate` and `/poll`. The device
code stays server-side; the browser only sees `state_token` and the user
code. State tokens can be **peeked** across polls and **consumed once**
on a terminal result to avoid duplicate credentials. Redis throttling
(fail-open) protects the shared public client ID. Refresh now resolves
device handlers and **serializes** providers that rotate refresh tokens.
Credential delete uses the device registry so tokens are actually
revoked.
> 
> **Stripe Link blocks.** List payment methods, create/poll spend
requests, retrieve a virtual card (self-hosted only), plus user info and
shipping address. Cloud disables the card create/retrieve path so
PANs/CVCs are not stored in execution records; list/status stay
available and strip extra payment fields.
> 
> **Frontend.** Connect UI for `device_code` (builder modal,
integrations panel, copilot onboarding) with inline code + poll loop.
`device_code` shadows `oauth2` in the connect picker so these providers
are not sent down the authorization-code path.
> 
> Also fixes All Quiet webhook timestamps so epoch millis are not parsed
as ISO basic dates (intermittent 403s).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit
401f045a0fd016b5545a9795bd8313fe03164fce. Bugbot is set up for automated
code reviews on this repo. Configure
[here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

commits.commit_title: fix(infra): honor the batch-deploy bot's !deploy past the preview-dispatcher gate (#13655)
commits.commit_message:
fix(infra): honor the batch-deploy bot's !deploy past the preview-dispatcher gate (#13655)

### Why / What / How

**Why:** batched previews never deploy.
`platform-dev-deploy-event-dispatcher.yml` only honors
`!deploy`/`!undeploy` from `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`. The
**batch-deploy bot** (`autogpt-batch-bot[bot]`) comments via its GitHub
App installation identity, whose `author_association` is **`NONE`**, so
its `!deploy` on the rollup PR is rejected — the whole "deploy the batch
once" payoff is blocked.

Live proof on the current `orgs` rollup
([#13651](https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT/pull/13651)):
the bot posted `!deploy` ~14×, every one got "❌ Permission denied", no
preview ever ran.

**What:** allowlist trusted bot logins by login in **both** permission
checks — the comment handler (gate #1) and the auto-redeploy scan (gate
#2).

```js
const BOT_ALLOWLIST = ['autogpt-batch-bot[bot]'];
// gate #1:  … || BOT_ALLOWLIST.includes(commentUser)
// gate #2:  if (!allowed.includes(comment.author_association) && !BOT_ALLOWLIST.includes(comment.user.login)) return;
```

**Why it's safe:** the batch-deploy bot only posts `!deploy` on **rollup
PRs it authored**, which target isolated per-PR preview envs (namespace
`pr-<n>`, own schema) — exactly the "test the combined batch in one
preview" behavior the batch bot is designed for. Human
`OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR` gating is unchanged.

### ⚠️ Deployment note
This dispatcher runs from the **default branch (`master`)**, so — like
the batch bot itself — **it only takes effect once it reaches `master`**
(via the normal dev→master release), not on merge to `dev`.

### Testing
YAML validated; `comment.user.login` confirmed present (comments come
from `listComments`). Full verification is post-merge-to-master: the
bot's `!deploy` on a rollup PR should then deploy instead of "Permission
denied". Interim stopgap: a member can `!deploy` the rollup manually.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Expands who can trigger dev preview deploy/undeploy (trusted bot login
only), but scope is narrow and CI-only; wrong allowlist entry could let
a bot arm auto-redeploy.

commits.commit_title: fix(backend): aggregate sub-graph credentials in copilot run/trigger tools (#14076)
commits.commit_message:
fix(backend): aggregate sub-graph credentials in copilot run/trigger tools (#14076)

### Why / What / How

**Why:** Running an orchestrator agent through AutoPilot fails: the
agent starts, then every sub-agent dies on missing required credentials,
with no setup card offered beforehand. Reproduced on Dev in copilot
session `5ad245eb-f94f-4977-a24c-8c21b6cd70b1`.

Credential requirements are aggregated over a graph **and its
sub-graphs** (`GraphModel.aggregate_credentials_inputs()` iterates
`[self] + self.sub_graphs`), so the result depends entirely on whether
the graph was loaded with `include_subgraphs=True`. `run_agent` and
`setup_agent_webhook_trigger` both loaded graphs without it, so they
only ever saw top-level nodes.

For an orchestrator — AgentInput/AgentOutput plus a few
`AgentExecutorBlock`s, i.e. **no credential fields of its own** — that
means:

1. `graph.regular_credentials_inputs` is `{}`, so
`match_user_credentials_to_graph` short-circuits and never even reads
the user's credentials
2. no missing credentials → no setup card → straight to execute
3. `add_graph_execution` receives an empty credentials map, and
parent-level validation only walks top-level nodes, so the run starts
happily
4. each `AgentExecutorBlock` then starts its child with an empty input
mask → every sub-agent fails validation

The `_handle_graph_validation_race` safety net does not catch this,
because the parent's own validation passes — the failure only lands once
the children start.

Running the same agent from the Library UI works, because `GET
/graphs/{id}` builds `credentials_input_schema` with
`include_subgraphs=True` and the frontend sends the full map. This is
copilot-only.

**What:** Load sub-graphs on every copilot path that derives credentials
from a graph it loaded itself.

**How:** `include_subgraphs=True` on the three `get_graph` calls
(run_agent library + preset paths, webhook trigger tool). The
marketplace path needed more: `store_db.get_available_graph` never
loaded sub-graphs at all, so it gained an opt-in `include_subgraphs`
parameter (default `False`, so the one other caller is unchanged) which
`fetch_graph_from_store_slug` passes.

Also checked and found clean: `agent_search` (loads with
`for_export=True`, which implies sub-graphs, and strips credentials
anyway), `manage_presets` (no graph load — it carries
`preset.credentials` forward), `find_library_agent` (no credential
handling), `agent_generator` and `agent_output` (read no credentials).
Outside copilot, `library/db.py` already passes `include_subgraphs=True`
and `library/model.py` only populates `credentials_input_schema` when
sub-graphs were loaded.

### Changes 🏗️

- `copilot/tools/run_agent.py` — `include_subgraphs=True` on the
library-agent and preset graph loads
- `copilot/tools/setup_agent_webhook_trigger.py` — same on its graph
load; without it a trigger is registered with a preset that fails on
every firing
- `api/features/store/db.py` — `get_available_graph` gained an opt-in
`include_subgraphs` (default `False`)
- `copilot/tools/utils.py` — `fetch_graph_from_store_slug` requests
sub-graphs
- `copilot/tools/_test_data.py` — new `setup_subagent_test_data`
fixture: orchestrator parent wrapping a Firecrawl sub-graph, for a user
without Firecrawl credentials, registered in both the library and the
store. Extracted `_build_firecrawl_graph` so this and the existing
Firecrawl fixture share one definition.
- `copilot/tools/run_agent_test.py` — two tests asserting the setup card
lists the sub-agent's `firecrawl` credential, one per run path
- `copilot/tools/setup_agent_webhook_trigger_test.py` — test asserting
the graph is loaded with sub-graphs (that file is mock-based, so the
load kwargs are what can be pinned); `_patches` gained an optional
`graph_db_mock`

### Checklist 📋

#### For code changes:
- [x] I have clearly listed my changes in the PR description
- [x] I have made a test plan
- [x] I have tested my changes according to the test plan:
- [x] New tests fail without the fix and pass with it. Pre-fix, both
`run_agent` tests fail *by starting a real run* — the orchestrator graph
accumulated 5 `AgentGraphExecution` rows across pre-fix runs while the
top-level-credentials Firecrawl agent has 0. Post-fix the count stays
put: no run is started. The trigger test fails pre-fix with `KeyError:
'include_subgraphs'`.
- [x] `run_agent_test.py`, `utils_test.py`,
`setup_agent_webhook_trigger_test.py`: 64 passed
- [x] `store/db_test.py`, `store/routes_test.py`: 54 passed (covers the
`get_available_graph` signature change)
- [ ] Not verified locally — 4 tests that start real executions
(`test_run_agent`, `test_run_agent_with_llm_credentials`,
`test_run_agent_with_use_defaults`,
`test_run_preset_executes_with_merged_inputs`) block on a RabbitMQ
reconnect loop in my local env; leaving these to CI. The last one covers
the preset path this PR changes.
- [ ] Manual: run an orchestrator agent via AutoPilot on Dev and confirm
the credentials card lists the sub-agents' providers before the run
starts

> [!NOTE]
> Presets and schedules created by copilot for orchestrator agents
before this fix have an empty/partial credentials map persisted
(`preset.credentials` is used verbatim on re-run), so they keep failing
until re-saved.
