fix: backport security and correctness fixes to 1.11.6 (#14876)

* fix(api): run the caller-aware component policy on the vertex build seam (#14808)

* fix(api): run the caller-aware component policy on the vertex build seam

POST /api/v1/build/{flow_id}/vertices/{vertex_id} compiled the graph persisted on
the flow row and executed one vertex from it, applying only the caller-agnostic
global validator. The stored graph is caller-controlled -- any user who can write
a flow can persist Python through the ordinary flow API -- so with
custom_component_admin_only on, a non-admin was refused everywhere else and
executed their own source here.

Reproduced over real HTTP on an isolated instance, as two real principals, with a
marker in the component's own return value:

  seam             admin                  non-admin
  build/{id}/flow  200                    400 refused
  build/{id}/vert  200 EXECUTED           200 EXECUTED   <- the bypass

After the fix the non-admin is refused 400 on both seams and the admin still runs
their own code, so the gate substitutes rather than blanket-refusing.

The seam now runs prepare_flow_build_for_user on the stored data, mapping its
outcomes exactly as the whole-flow build does: 400 for a policy rejection, 503
when the policy cannot be evaluated. When the policy returns a sanitized copy the
graph is rebuilt from it rather than reused from cache -- cache keys carry no
policy generation, so a graph compiled while the policy was off still embeds the
caller's own source. That mirrors the guard already in endpoints.py for the
advanced-run cache.

Not claimed: the ticket also reports a 500 (AttributeError) instead of a clean 400
when ALLOW_CUSTOM_COMPONENTS=false. That needs a node whose type matches a
registry component so the substitution lands before the failure; the probe shape
used here is refused earlier, so it was never reproduced and this change is not
asserted to fix it.

Tests: 6 new, five of which fail against the vulnerable code -- policy denial,
caller-awareness, building from the sanitized copy, fail-closed on both
undecidable-policy paths, plus the control that a permissive policy still builds
normally. A refusal for everyone would be a denial of service, not a fix.

Fixes LE-2356

* [autofix.ci] apply automated fixes

* fix(api): close the same policy gap on the vertices-order route

Self-review follow-up on the LE-2356 fix.

B1 -- the sibling seam had the same hole. retrieve_vertices_order takes the same
owner-only stored graph and, when no inline data is supplied, called
build_graph_from_db with no caller-aware policy, then seeded the shared
flow-keyed cache with the result. Fixing only build_vertex left the ticket's
class of defect half open on the route next door. Both stored-graph branches now
go through one _trusted_stored_graph helper, so the exception mapping cannot
drift between them (this also folds in R1 from the review, since the helper would
otherwise have been a third copy).

Adding that call exposed a defect the change itself introduced:
retrieve_vertices_order wraps its body in `except Exception` and re-raises as 500,
so the helper's HTTPException(400) surfaced as an internal server error -- and the
INLINE branch, which mapped its own CustomComponentValidationError correctly
before, regressed the same way. HTTPException is a control-flow signal and now
propagates unwrapped, after the failure telemetry is still recorded. The new
order-route test is what caught it.

I1 -- the denial tests all monkeypatched prepare_flow_build_for_user, so they
proved the wiring, not the security property: the policy could stop refusing and
every one of them would stay green. Added end-to-end tests that flip the real
custom_component_admin_only setting and persist genuinely caller-authored source,
covering both seams and both principals -- a non-admin is refused 400 with no
marker in the body, a superuser is not.

Discrimination measured against release-1.12.0 rather than assumed: the order case
fails there, the build case does not (in this test environment the registry hashes
are warm and the global validator already refuses that payload), so for the build
route the discriminating evidence remains the mocked tests plus the live HTTP
probe. That caveat is recorded in the test docstring rather than left implied.

api/v1 suite: 2018 passed, 11 skipped.

* fix(api): keep vertex build state across policy calls

The admin-only policy returns a sanitized copy on EVERY request from a
non-superuser, not only when the cached compilation predates the policy. This
seam is incremental -- called once per vertex, carrying built state in the flow's
graph cache between calls -- so rebuilding on that condition discarded the
previous vertex's result and the next one reported its upstream as "Component
Chat Input has not been built yet".

Reported by QA against this PR and reproduced here: admin propagates, non-admin
loses state, and with the policy off the same non-admin propagates. Caller- and
policy-dependent, so not a fixture defect.

The condition is now "did the cached compilation come from this copy?", compared
through raw_graph_data. That still rebuilds the case the guard exists for -- a
graph compiled while the policy was off carries different node source -- and
stops rebuilding per request. raw_graph_data is part of Graph.__getstate__; a
marker attribute would be dropped there and would reintroduce this bug on
Redis-backed caches only, which is the kind of environment-dependent failure
worth avoiding. The comparison fails safe: anything unexpected rebuilds.

The reporter's other point is fixed too: initialize_run() was skipped on this
path. build_and_cache_graph_from_data does not initialize, unlike
build_graph_from_db, so the rebuilt graph was left uninitialized.

3 new tests -- the permitted non-admin, the superuser control, and the policy-off
counter-proof. The first fails against this PR's previous head. 20 tests pass
across the route's three suites.

test_should_build_from_the_sanitized_copy_not_the_stored_bytes also changed: its
MagicMock exposed neither a string run_id nor a dict raw_graph_data, which the
seam now reads. That was fixture thinness, not a production defect.

A custom_component/update response issued before the tool actions
editor closed was applied over the edits it predates, reverting the
action slug, description and approval_actions - and the debounced
autosave persisted the loss. The next request was then built from the
clobbered store, so the backend faithfully echoed the pre-edit
tools_metadata even though field_value carried the edits.

keepUserEdits now also preserves a field's value when the store
diverged from the values the last applied response wrote. Baselining
on the last applied response rather than on the request snapshot keeps
concurrent refreshes working: several mount refreshes share one
snapshot, so the first response to land would otherwise look like a
local edit and suppress the others.

* fix(mcp): keep advertising inputs for flows that declared no allowlist (#14855)

#14837 gated the MCP tools/list schema on api_editable, the Inspector's
per-field "API" toggle. That flag defaults to False, is written only by two
frontend controls, is set by no component and no backend code, and has no
backfill migration. A flow nobody hand-toggled therefore advertised an input
schema containing nothing but the injected session_id.

This was not confined to legacy flows. All 23 shipped starter projects that
carry an input node store input_value with no api_editable key at all — the
templates hold 161 occurrences of "api_editable": false and zero of true — so
the first flow a new user creates from the template picker was published on
the project MCP server with no callable input.

The failure was silent at both ends. handle_call_tool pops input_value before
the tweak filter runs and forwards it as SimplifiedAPIRequest.input_value, so
the runtime still accepted the message the schema no longer declared: the call
returned isError: false with empty content and the flow ran on input_value="".

Two changes, both applied to json_schema_from_flow and to
get_flow_input_tweaks so the advertised schema and the call-time filter cannot
drift apart:

_input_nodes_declare_api_allowlist makes the allowlist a per-flow opt-in,
mirroring the reasoning already recorded for the deployment tweak policy in
lfx/utils/flow_validation.py: a flow whose author toggled at least one field
has declared an allowlist, so the untoggled fields close; a flow with no
toggles has declared nothing and keeps its previous contract. Toggling still
narrows the schema, which is what the ticket asked for — it just no longer
empties the schema of every flow nobody prepared. Scoped to input nodes, since
those are the only fields MCP can advertise; a toggle on an Agent is an
API-snippet concern and must not reshape the MCP contract.

input_value is exempt from the allowlist the same way the call path already
exempts it, so the advertised contract matches the one served.

The type-mapping half of #14837 is unchanged, as is the A2A card, which reads
this schema with require_api_editable=False since #14843.

A file-system level test walks the shipped starter projects and asserts each
one with an input node advertises more than session_id, so a template can
never again ship publishing an uncallable tool.

* fix(amazon): send Top K only to providers with it (#14758)

* fix(amazon): send Top K only to providers with it

Bedrock Converse defined a Top K input that build_model never read, so
the value the user set was silently dropped - temperature, max_tokens
and top_p were all wired into init_params, top_k was not.

Wiring it into additionalModelRequestFields is necessary but not
sufficient on its own: the input defaults to 250 and every saved flow
persists that value, so an ungated send reaches models that document no
top_k at all. Meta Llama takes prompt/temperature/top_p/max_gen_len,
Amazon Titan and AI21 have no top_k, and Cohere spells it "k" - that is
23 of the 44 models in the dropdown, and Converse rejects the whole call
when additionalModelRequestFields carries a field the model does not
support. Scope the send to the providers that document the parameter;
the others can still opt in through Additional Model Fields.

* fix(agui): key tool and content dedup by ordinal (#14759)

* fix(agui): key tool and content dedup by ordinal

AG-UI dedup derived a tool call's id from its absolute position in
content_blocks, assuming that list is append-only. Message.text's setter
breaks the assumption: it drops every TextContent block and appends one
consolidated block at the end, so any block that had narration text
ahead of it shifts index. ChatOutput.message_response() triggers exactly
that on an Agent message that already finished streaming, then re-emits
it, and the shifted blocks read as brand new - re-firing a full
TOOL_CALL_START/ARGS/END/RESULT quartet under a fresh id, with the same
name, input and output, and ~zero duration.

Key off content["id"] when a producer stamped one, else off the leaf's
rank among the leaves of its own kind in the traversal. Only TextContent
blocks move, so that rank survives the reindexing. Ranking also keeps
two identical tool calls distinct, which a content fingerprint would
have collapsed.

Custom content blocks (json/code/media/error) were keyed the same way
and duplicate for the same reason, so they get the same treatment.

* fix(agui): separate id and ordinal key namespaces

A message can mix producer-stamped and unstamped leaves, and both keys
were minted into one namespace. [tool(id="1"), tool(id=None)] mapped
both onto m:tool:1, so the second call's whole lifecycle was dropped;
the same collision on custom content made two blocks overwrite each
other's fingerprint and re-emit on every re-fire. Mint stamped ids
under :id: and ordinals under :ord: so they cannot meet.

Also covers grouped leaves, whose nested tool_use / custom content the
traversal ordinal already handled but no test exercised.

* fix(datastax): stop batch_size from breaking Cassandra ingest (#14795)

* fix(datastax): stop batch_size from breaking Cassandra ingest

CassandraVectorStoreComponent.build_vector_store called
Cassandra.from_documents(..., batch_size=self.batch_size). from_documents does
not declare batch_size, so it landed in **kwargs and was splatted into cls(...)
-- Cassandra.__init__, which in langchain-community 0.4.2 accepts only
embedding, session, keyspace, table_name, ttl_seconds, body_index_options,
setup_mode and metadata_indexing. Anything wired to Ingest Data therefore died
with:

    Cassandra.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'batch_size'

The search-only path was unaffected because it constructs Cassandra(...)
directly and never passes batch_size, which is why disconnecting the Ingest
Data edge made the same flow build.

batch_size is not junk to drop: it is a real parameter of Cassandra.add_texts
(default 16), which add_documents forwards to. The store is now constructed
explicitly and the documents are added with
add_documents(documents=..., batch_size=...), so the exposed component field
keeps its meaning instead of being silently ignored.

setup_mode is deliberately NOT introduced on this path. from_documents never
forwarded it either, so the constructor default (SYNC) preserves today's
behaviour. Passing SetupMode.ASYNC here would hand cassio async_setup=True and
an un-awaited coroutine as the vector dimension while add_texts stays
synchronous -- trading one crash for another. The ingest branch ignoring the
user's Setup Mode is a real but separate defect, and it affects the
search-only branch too.

The component lives in the lfx-datastax bundle on this branch;
src/lfx/src/lfx/components/cassandra is only a compatibility shim.

Reproduced before the fix and verified after, against the installed
langchain-community 0.4.2: with the bug, 1/5/40-document ingests all raise the
TypeError; with the fix they build a real Cassandra store and issue one row
write per document. 9 new tests, 8 of which fail against the old code; 104
datastax bundle tests pass.

Co-Authored-By: andifilhohub <andersonfilho.contato@outlook.com>

* fix(datastax): address review on the Cassandra batch_size fix

Review by @viktoravelino on #14795. All four reproduced before fixing.

1. CI blocker. The 0.1.6 bump reached pyproject/extension.json/uv.lock but not
   the bundle profile or its lock, so bundle_profiles.json still requested
   >=0.1.5 and enterprise-hardened.lock.json still pinned ==0.1.5. Confirmed
   the three failures in scripts/ci/test_bundle_profiles.py, bumped the range
   and recompiled the lock with manage_bundle_profiles.py; the same three now
   pass and the release-plan gate still reports ready.

2. batch_size reached add_texts unvalidated. add_texts slices with
   range(0, len(texts), batch_size), and IntInput coerces a cleared advanced
   field to 0. Reproduced against the real implementation: 0 raised
   "range() arg 3 must not be zero" and -1 returned normally having written
   ZERO rows while logging "Adding 5 documents" -- a silent data-loss path
   worse than the crash. Clamped to max(int(self.batch_size or
   DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE), 1), with the input's default and the guard sharing one
   constant so they cannot drift.

3. Setup Mode OFF is now honoured on the ingest path. The reviewer is right
   that OFF is safe with a synchronous add_documents and that it is the value
   that matters: it drives skip_provisioning, so forcing SYNC re-ran the table
   DDL on every ingest for a pre-provisioned table or a role without CREATE.
   Only ASYNC still degrades to SYNC, for the async_setup reason. The test now
   pins the real invariant per value (Sync->SYNC, Async->SYNC, Off->OFF)
   instead of asserting SYNC for all three.

4. The two Cassandra(...) calls collapsed into one construction followed by a
   conditional add_documents, which is what makes (3) a one-liner.

Test coverage follows the review: batch_size=0 added to the real-implementation
parametrization (the previous 16/2 values could not fail, since put_async runs
once per document regardless of batch size), plus cleared-field and negative
cases. 14 Cassandra tests, 258 across the datastax bundle and the CI scripts.

* chore(ci): recompile the bundle profile lock after the merge

Merging release-1.12.0 brought in #14784, which bumped lfx-amazon and touched
the same bundle_profiles.json and enterprise-hardened.lock.json this branch
already edited for lfx-datastax 0.1.6. Git merged the profile text cleanly, but
the lock carries a profile_digest over the whole contract -- it has to be
RECOMPILED, not merged, so it kept the pre-merge digest and
test_reviewed_profiles_and_locks_are_current failed on the merge commit.

Regenerated with manage_bundle_profiles.py compile; the digest is the only

scripts/ci/test_bundle_profiles.py is back to 14 passed.

* fix(schema): stop coded driver errors collapsing to a bare code

Reported on LE-2352 by QA: a Cassandra Table Name typed with "-" instead of "_"
produced only "Flow build failed. Code: 8192" in the editor, while the real
cause sat in the logs. Noted there as the same shape as an earlier "code 13"
report, so this is not Cassandra-specific.

_coded_exception_message only read args[0]. Reason-coded Langflow errors such as
ModelProviderPolicyError populate it, but driver and SDK exceptions do not: a
cassandra.protocol.SyntaxException carries the protocol status on .code, an
EMPTY args, and the human text on .message / __str__. Since the branch is
selected by hasattr(exception, "code"), it short-circuited past the .message and
.detail fallbacks further down and rendered the number alone.

It now falls back to .message (the SDK convention) and then to __str__, so any
coded exception that has text surfaces it. An exception with a code and genuinely
no message still renders code-only -- the existing test for that shape is
unchanged and still passes.

Reproduced and verified against a REAL Astra database, not a stub. Same flow, same
hyphenated table name:

  before  Code: 8192
  after   line 1:53 mismatched input '-' expecting '(' (... IF NOT EXISTS
          default_keyspace.cassandra[-]...)

The markdown path keeps the code as context alongside the message.

Note on sequencing: reaching the CQL error at all requires the batch_size fix
from #14795, which is why QA only saw this after validating that PR. The
component fix was applied to the working tree for the verification run above and
is NOT part of this branch -- this change is confined to lfx/schema/message.py.

Tests: 2 new, both failing against the current code; 345 lfx schema tests and 90
backend message tests pass.

* fix(store): stop a Langflow Store outage from breaking the app (#14803)

api.langflow.store began serving a certificate for
*.<id>.us-east-1.cs.amazonlightsail.com instead of its own hostname, so every
TLS connection to it fails verification. Verified directly against the live
host, outside CI. Two independent defects turned that third-party outage into a
Langflow outage:

1. The visual editor asked for store tags on every boot. AppInitPage calls
   useGetTagsQuery unconditionally, on every route, even though

fix(agent): let structured output hold more than one record (#14839)

* fix(agent): let structured output hold more than one record

Asking an agent for "a list of South American countries and their capitals"
returned all twelve as text and exactly one as structured output. The model was
not truncating: json_response handed the provider a schema in which every field
was a scalar, so one record was all it could express.

The Agent and the standalone Structured Output component read the SAME schema
table and built different models from it:

    Structured Output   ->  {objects: [ {country, capital}, ... ]}
    Agent.json_response ->  {country, capital}

structured_output.py:159 wraps the record model in a list container; the
orchestrator did not. The Agent also contradicted itself, since its default
format instructions tell the model to "Extract ALL relevant instances that match
the schema" while the schema forbade a second one.

json_response now wraps the record model the same way. The record model is kept
separately for validation, and the prompt fallback accepts the envelope, a bare
record or a bare array, because models answer with all three.

Back-compat is preserved by _wrap_payload, which already unwraps a single-item
list: one record still surfaces flat, so downstream components reading fields off
the payload are unaffected. Several records surface under "results", the key this
seam already used.

Verified against the reporter's own flow, on a server sharing that database, with
a real model and the schema exactly as saved (two str fields, multiple=false):

    before  1 country   ['Argentina']
    after   12 countries ['Argentina', 'Bolívia', 'Brasil', 'Chile', ...]

schema actually offered to the provider, the fallback path, and the single-record
back-compat control. 60 structured-output tests, 237 models_and_agents tests and
33 standalone-component tests pass.

commits.commit_title: refactor(sandbox): make LANGFLOW_SANDBOX_BACKEND a registry (#14694)
commits.commit_message:
refactor(sandbox): make LANGFLOW_SANDBOX_BACKEND a registry (#14694)

* feat(sandbox): vendor-neutral backend registry + CreateOS

Splits lfx/utils/sandbox.py (1297 lines) into a package and gives a backend a
protocol to implement instead of a branch inside run_code_in_sandbox:

- base.py: result and error types, operator settings, code composition, and
  the SandboxBackend protocol
- registry.py: name to factory, and the single source of accepted backend
  names
- exec_sandbox.py: the QEMU backend, moved unchanged
- createos.py: a new "createos" backend, one Firecracker microVM per
  execution on the CreateOS control plane, so the Langflow host needs no
  hypervisor of its own

The backend declares its capabilities; the dispatcher decides whether they
satisfy the operator's settings, so a backend cannot grant itself an
exemption from LANGFLOW_SANDBOX_ALLOW_NETWORK or
LANGFLOW_SANDBOX_ALLOWED_DOMAINS. This also closes a real trap: the
dispatcher and validate_sandbox_backend each carried their own
hand-maintained allowlist, so a backend added to one and missed in the other
raised at startup. Both now read known_sandbox_backends().

Out-of-tree backends register through the lfx.sandbox_backends entry point,
gated by LANGFLOW_SANDBOX_BACKEND_PLUGINS (empty by default, so no
third-party code is imported without the operator naming it). A capability
declaration is configuration metadata, not evidence of enforcement, so
loading a plugin is a deployment decision, not an application default.

Adds an optional session and artifact surface for backends that report
support: one guest reused per (flow, user), and files the code wrote
returned with the result. Both are off by default and need the operator's
setting AND the backend's capability. exec-sandbox reports neither, so its
behaviour is unchanged.

CreateOS-specific behaviour, in one vendor-confined module:

- Runs the program over a streaming exec connection rather than a buffered
  one, because the exec endpoint has no server-side timeout and the stream
  is the only documented kill path (the server heartbeats every 5s and kills
  the guest command within about 5s of a client disconnect). A timeout taints
  the session guest: closing the connection is not proof the guest command
  stopped, so a timed-out guest is destroyed rather than reused.
- Sessions are owned by the control plane, not by one worker. A sandbox name
  is unique per account, so creating under a name derived from the session
  token is a compare-and-swap between workers/replicas: the first wins,
  every other adopts. The guest is not paused between executions (measured
  live: pause 16.2s, resume 12.7s, vs ~1.0s to create a fresh VM). Because a
  session guest can be shared, each execution uploads its program under its
  own name and the carried-state file is written atomically.
- Session state survives a fresh interpreter by pickling the top-level
  namespace on exit and restoring it on the next run. Each value is
  serialized separately so one unpicklable value (e.g. a user-defined
  function, which cannot load in a new interpreter) costs only itself
  rather than erasing the whole namespace.
- Artifact collection tars /workspace/artifacts, streams the download with a
  hard byte cap applied before the bytes are resident, and caps the member
  count so many empty files can't cost unbounded work.
- Declares 169.254.0.0/16 as an egress exception: the host always accepts
  link-local before its final DROP, whatever the policy says, so the
  dispatcher logs the hole instead of leaving an operator to find it.

Verified by the lfx unit suite (sandbox tests: 245) and repeated live test
matrices against api.sb.createos.sh covering streamed output,
stdout/stderr separation, unicode, 20k lines, timeout kill with partial
output preserved, a 95s quiet program, session state and cross-user
isolation, artifact collection and its caps, cross-worker session adoption,
and a VM leak check on every run. Docs site builds clean.

This is deliberately NOT the upstream PR. A vendor-named backend calling a
vendor URL is exactly the shape the agreed upstream design (protocol-first,
no vendor in tree) rules out -- see the createos.py module docstring. The
protocol/registry/exec-sandbox portion here also still carries session and
artifact surface that nothing upstream implements, so it is not yet the
narrow slice PR 1 needs either; that still has to be extracted separately
and rebased onto release-1.12.0.

Docs: docs/docs/Deployment/sandbox-backends.mdx is the new operator page for
the vendor-neutral layer -- the registry, the built-in backends, how a
backend's declared capabilities are matched against operator settings, and
the opt-in entry-point plugin path. The CreateOS page and the sandbox
environment variables now link to it, and CreateOS reads as one registered
backend rather than a second hard-coded one. The internal docs/createos
working notes are untracked and gitignored; they were never part of the
docs site.

Refs #12029, #14623

* fix(sandbox): close three CreateOS session and artifact defects

Three review findings, each reproduced by a test that fails without its
fix.

1. The idle reaper could destroy a guest mid-execution. `last_used` was
   stamped only on completion and the cached-guest path never refreshed
   it, so the only timestamp on record while a session ran was its
   PREVIOUS completion. Any other session entering an execution reaped on
   that stale reading and issued DELETE against a running guest; the exec
   stream then died as an infrastructure error and the session state the
   operator opted into was thrown away. Reachable on DEFAULT settings
   (300s timeout inside a 600s idle window) whenever two flows run
   concurrently. Now stamped on acquire as well as completion, and the
   reaper skips any session whose per-session lock is held, destroying
   under that lock after re-reading the timestamp. The caller's own
   session is exempt from the probe (a threading.Lock is not reentrant,
   and the caller holds it) so a session can still expire for the flow
   that owns it.

2. A reused or adopted session guest was never checked against current
   policy. `_assert_policy_applied` runs only at creation, and a session
   guest deliberately outlives the process under a stable name, so
   tightening LANGFLOW_SANDBOX_ALLOW_NETWORK (or narrowing the allowlist,
   or raising the memory floor) and restarting inside the auto-pause
   window adopted the guest built under the OLD policy and ran user code
   in it.

   Re-verifying on adoption is impossible: GET /v1/sandboxes/{id} omits
   egress entirely, and GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/egress returns [] for a
   sandbox created with real rules -- reproduced live, while running, on
   rules the create response had just echoed correctly. There is no
   endpoint that reports a live guest's egress at all.

   So the policy is folded into the session identity instead: the guest
   name derives from (session token, egress, memory), and a changed
   setting derives a different name that cannot match the old guest. The
   stale guest is orphaned to the reaper and auto-pause rather than
   inherited. Verified live: unchanged policy still reuses its guest and
   carries state; a tightened policy gets a fresh one with no leftovers.

3. A malformed artifact archive escaped as an uncaught traceback,
   contradicting the documented "never fatal" contract. tarfile reports
   corruption outside the OSError tree (TarError derives from Exception;
   a truncated gzip raises EOFError), neither of which the handler named,
   so a corrupt tarball replaced a good execution result with a raw
   traceback in the component. Both are now caught.

Also corrects the Python REPL tool's comment, which claimed artifacts are
not collected there. Collection is driven by the operator setting inside
the backend, not by the caller, so with LANGFLOW_SANDBOX_COLLECT_ARTIFACTS
enabled the tool does pay for collection and then discards the files --
wasteful, not unsafe. A per-call opt-out belongs in the backend protocol
and is left as follow-up.

Verified: 234 sandbox tests pass; each fix confirmed load-bearing by
reverting it and watching the new test fail. Full lfx suite shows an
IDENTICAL 17-failure set before and after these changes (all pre-existing,
in docling/extension/helpers, none sandbox-related). Live matrix against
api.sb.createos.sh passes with no leaked sandboxes. ruff clean.

* fix(sandbox): close 13 registry, policy, and untrusted-input defects

Findings from the CodeRabbit review on PR #14694. Each was checked against
the code before being accepted, and each fix was reverted once to confirm
its test fails without it.

Registry lock discipline:
* The module mutex was never replaced after a fork, and the fork hook read
  the registry before anything else. An inherited-locked mutex has no owner
  in the child, so the child blocked inside the hook itself, where the
  surrounding suppress() cannot help. Adds reset_registry_after_fork() and
  calls it first.
* resolve_sandbox_backend built the instance while holding that mutex. A
  factory that called back into the registry deadlocked permanently, and a
  factory that probed hardware blocked the settings validator for its whole
  duration. The build now happens outside the lock.
* The entry-point load latch was set before loading ran, so a concurrent
  reader saw a partial backend list and startup failed with
  "sandbox_backend must be one of". A dedicated reentrant load lock is now
  held across the whole load.
* A plugin entry point named "none" raised ValueError out of the settings
  validator and Langflow did not start, against what _load_entry_points
  documents. Registration failures are now logged and skipped.
* Plugin names kept their case while the settings validator lowercases, so
  an uppercase plugin registered and could never be selected. Names are now
  lowercased at registration.
* get_sandbox_backend() answered "none" when the settings service failed to
  build, which sent user code to in-process exec on a deployment that had
  asked for a sandbox. It now falls back to the environment, so an
  unresolvable name fails closed instead of running unsandboxed.

Policy gates:
* Capabilities.isolation defaulted to "hardware-virtualized", the one value
  the strongest gate accepts, so a backend that never named its isolation
  cleared that gate by omission. Now defaults to "none" like every other
  field. The in-tree backends already declare theirs.
* Session reuse was gated on "not off", so an unrecognized mode granted
  reuse. Now allowlisted against the modes that actually reuse.
* sandbox_session_idle_seconds and sandbox_max_artifact_bytes were
  unbounded ints and accepted zero and negatives. Both are guards, and the
  artifact cap bounds host memory. Both now carry Field bounds.

Untrusted values:
* int() on the control plane's mem_mib raised outside the
  SandboxUnavailableError tree, so the caller's teardown handler did not
  run and the VM leaked. An unreadable grant is now a failed verification.
* int() on the guest agent's exit_code frame raised unmapped, and
  _run_in_session drops a guest only for SandboxExecutionError, so the
  session kept pointing at a guest in unknown state. Now mapped.
* A corrupt session state file dropped every variable with nothing on
  stderr, against the promise stated in the same module.
* Built-in backend registration raised on importlib.reload. Now suppressed.

Docs record that a backend can declare a timeout cap below the 1-300 range.

Two findings were checked and rejected. SandboxUnavailableError subclasses
SandboxExecutionError, so the _with_artifacts and _log_metrics handlers
already catch it, and the _find_session_vm and _is_running handlers fail
toward a fresh guest, which is more isolation rather than less.

Tests: 22 added. lfx unit suite 7530 -> 7552 passed, zero failures before
and after.

* fix(sandbox): close 7 more control-plane, lifecycle, and test defects

Second CodeRabbit pass on PR #14694. Every finding was checked against the
code first, and every fix was reverted once to confirm its test fails.

Control-plane values, continuing the sweep the first pass left incomplete:
* _assert_policy_applied called sorted(map(str, echoed)) on the egress echo.
  A non-iterable value raised TypeError outside the mapped error tree, which
  skipped the caller's teardown handler and leaked the VM. An echo this code
  cannot read is now a policy mismatch.
* _catalog called int(shape["mem_mib"]) inside a comprehension, so one bad
  entry escaped _shape_for as a raw traceback. Unreadable entries are now
  skipped and logged.

Lifecycle:
* _catalog held self._lock across the /v1/shapes request, which carries a 60s
  budget. That mutex also guards every session operation, so a slow catalog
  fetch stalled unrelated flows for the whole budget. The fetch now happens
  outside the lock and the result is stored under it, matching what
  resolve_sandbox_backend already does.
* _session_locks grew without bound. _drop_session removed the _sessions
  entry and left the lock, and the identity encodes the policy as well as the
  flow and the user, so a long-running worker accumulated one permanent entry
  per tenant and per policy change. The lock is now dropped with the session.
* resolve_sandbox_backend discarded the instance that lost the setdefault
  race without shutting it down. That instance is not in _instances, so
  live_sandbox_backends() never returns it and shutdown_sandbox() cannot
  reach it; a factory that acquired a loop thread leaked it for the process
  lifetime.
* The DNS resolver rule was appended unconditionally, so an operator who
  already listed it sent it twice. _assert_policy_applied compares sorted
  lists, so a control plane storing a deduplicated set produced a length
  mismatch and refused the run with a message the operator could not act on.
* _stream_exec computed _exec_deadline twice, once for the loop and once for
  the transport. Now computed once and clamped at zero for the transport.
* The plugin allowlist was matched verbatim while registration lowercases, so
  an operator spelling the case differently got a silent skip and a startup
  failure reporting the backend as unknown. Both sides now lowercase.

Tests:
* The reap-guard concurrency test asserted inside a worker thread, where an
  AssertionError never reaches pytest. Any failure there also surfaced as the
  reaper assertion failing for the wrong reason. The outcome is now captured
  and re-raised on the main thread.
* The reload test left the module's attributes rebound, which breaks
  test_a_plugin_cannot_take_over_a_builtin_name under any reordering. It now
  restores them. Confirmed by running the two in that order.

Docs record the generated program path rather than /workspace/main.py,
capitalize Component, and split one long security paragraph.

One finding was checked and rejected: _run_in_session catching
SandboxExecutionError already covers SandboxUnavailableError, because the
latter subclasses the former. A test now asserts that relationship so the
handler cannot be silently narrowed. This repeats a rejection from the first
pass.

The vendor-scope finding on docs/docs/Deployment/sandbox-createos.mdx is left
for the author to answer; it is a scope decision, not a defect.

Tests: 11 added. lfx unit suite 7552 -> 7563 passed, zero failures.

* fix(sandbox): refuse a declared egress hole instead of logging it

Blocker from review. createos declared supports_deny_all_egress=True while
also declaring 169.254.0.0/16 in egress_exceptions. The dispatcher read only
the first field, so LANGFLOW_SANDBOX_ALLOW_NETWORK=false passed the gate and
the exception produced a one-line warning. That is fail-open in the one place
the design claims every branch fails closed.

The hole is not theoretical. This module's own docstring records a live test:
a guest reached 169.254.169.254:80 and got HTTP 200 under the default
deny-all policy, while a public address on the same policy was blocked. That
range carries the VM metadata service.

egress_exceptions is now a decision rather than an honesty field. When the
operator restricts egress, a backend that declares any exception is refused,
and the message names both the destinations and the way to accept them.

The refusal covers a domain allowlist as well as a denied network. The
reported case was ALLOW_NETWORK=false, but an allowlist is equally a
restriction and the exception sits outside it, so gating on only one half
would leave the same hole reachable by the other configuration.

LANGFLOW_SANDBOX_ACCEPT_EGRESS_EXCEPTIONS (default false) is the opt-out.
Without it createos would be unusable under any restricted policy, which is
the configuration the documentation recommends. Default false keeps the
refusal, so accepting the range is a deliberate act that is recorded in
configuration rather than discovered in a log.

Every existing createos test failed when this landed -- 86 of them -- because
each one ran under a restricted policy that is now correctly refused. Nothing
in the suite had objected to that policy before. The helper now opts in
explicitly, and the gate has its own tests.

Docs state the refusal in the CreateOS warning callout, in the backend
matching rules, and in the environment variable table.

Tests: 6 added, plus the new field registered in the settings composition
guard. lfx unit suite 7563 -> 7569 passed, zero failures.

* chore(sandbox): regenerate the component index

The Python Interpreter and Python REPL sources changed in this branch, so
their code_hash entries and the index sha256 no longer matched. The CI job
rebuilds the index and hands it to autofix-ci, which cannot write to this
pull request, so the check failed instead of correcting itself.

Rebuilt with `LFX_DEV=1 make build_component_index`, the same command the
workflow runs. The resulting sha256 matches what CI computed:
c36a84a074391d0d0a93efaeb0ad0546fd3267829d7480d0a789d22645497df8

The diff touches only the two components this branch edits.

* docs(sandbox): document every public and test symbol

CodeRabbit reported 40.66% docstring coverage against an 80% threshold.
Add docstrings to the 269 undocumented classes, methods, and functions in
the changed files. Coverage is now 100% (interrogate).

No behavior change. Two redundant 'pass' statements were removed where a
docstring became the method body.

* fix(sandbox): close six defects the maintainer named

Scope served sessions to the end user, and run anonymous served calls
cold. On the serving plane every request runs as one shared service
account, so (flow, user) named ONE guest for every caller of a
deployment and session reuse handed each caller the last one's
/workspace and state pickle. SessionKey now carries the
gateway-authenticated end user; a served request without one gets no
session at all, because the only key left is the shared account.

Keep CreateOS guests process-owned, give replacements fresh names, and
bind rootfs into identity. Adoption let a second worker execute in a
guest whose lock, idle reaper, and teardown all live in another
process. A guest now belongs to the process that created it, and its
name is fresh random hex per create -- a stable name would collide with
the `destroying` predecessor a replacement is racing. The rootfs joins
the identity so an image change cannot inherit the old image's
filesystem or its state pickle.

Declare the unrestricted DNS resolver path. A domain allowlist is
enforced on the destination address, so the resolver it opens answers
for any name and the query itself carries data out. It is now an
egress exception, refused unless the operator accepts it, rather than a
note in a comment.

Cap combined stdout/stderr at 8 MiB. The guest decided how much worker
memory one execution cost; it no longer does. Truncation shortens the
text and leaves the exit code alone.

Enforce the configured execution deadline and skip artifacts/metrics
after a timeout. The loop deadline was timeout PLUS the transport
grace, so the configured value was never the real one; the two are now
separate, and the transport budget is only longer so the deadline fires
first. After a timeout nothing else runs against a guest whose program
was very likely not stopped -- teardown starts immediately.

Reject duplicate allowlisted plugin names before importing either. Two
distributions can publish one entry-point name, and the allowlist names
a backend, not a distribution. The old loop imported both and let the
second overwrite the first.

commits.commit_title: fix(assistant): keep in-scope builds from stalling (#14792)
commits.commit_message:
fix(assistant): keep in-scope builds from stalling (#14792)

* fix(assistant): keep in-scope builds from stalling

LE-2323 — the injection guardrail interrupted an in-scope build with
"I'm sorry, but I can't process that request...". Reproduced live on
/api/v1/agentic/assist/stream: the GenerateComponent tool re-entered
execute_flow_with_validation, which re-ran sanitize_input on the spec the
assistant's OWN agent had written. A spec for a guardrail component names
the attacks it must catch ("...ignore previous instructions, reveal system
prompts..."), so the regex fired on the assistant's words and surfaced as a
validation_failed error while the agent kept working in the background —
matching the customer's report exactly.

The user turn is already checked at the door, so the nested call now passes
trusted_source=True: injection patterns are skipped for assistant-authored
text, content safety and normalization still run. Two patterns were also
narrowed, since they rejected ordinary requests from a real user: "act as"
is now anchored to the model as the subject ("a component that will act as
an orchestrator" is not a hijack), and the extraction pattern requires the
assistant's own directives as the target ("show instructions on how to fix
each finding" is a component description).

LE-2324 — exhausting the step budget was a full stop. The terminal error
branch returned without draining flow events, so a turn that had already
called build_flow/add_component threw that canvas away; the token-loop drain
cannot cover it because no token follows the tool call that dies on the
ceiling. It now drains first, emits each pending update as flow_update, and
appends PARTIAL_WORK_KEPT_SUFFIX so the stop reads as resumable. With no
partial work the message is unchanged.

The budget is also tunable per deployment via LANGFLOW_ASSISTANT_ITERATIONS
(precedence: per-request /iterations N > env > pinned default, clamped to
[1, 200]), resolved once in assistant_iterations_default() so both the JSON
and the Python assistant flow read it. The pinned default is untouched, so
the tripwire test still guards what ships out of the box.

Validated live: the LE-2323 prompt now builds with zero sanitization blocks;
LANGFLOW_ASSISTANT_ITERATIONS=64 reached the Agent as max_iterations 64; the
customer's multi-stage prompt at iterations=14 emitted 8 flow_update events
plus the suffix, and at iterations=8 (ceiling hit mid-build_flow, nothing
built) stayed a plain error. 1721 agentic unit tests pass.

Fixes LE-2323
Fixes LE-2324

* fix(assistant): address review on the partial-flow rescue

Review by @erichare on #14792. All three findings reproduced before fixing.

Blocking — the rescue never reached the canvas. The error branch yielded the
drained events raw, bypassing _reconcile_flow_updates, which is the only place
that strips the internal `flow_ran` signal and stamps `auto_apply`. Three
consequences: `flow_ran` leaked to a frontend that has no reducer for it; a
`flow_ran`-only batch tripped the "kept" suffix with nothing kept; and an
untagged `set_flow` landed as a proposal that the error branch of
assistant-message-body never rendered, so the flow was neither applied nor
offerable while the message claimed it was on the canvas.

The rescue now goes through the reconciler with the carried state already in
scope. Rather than forcing auto_apply, the consent gate is preserved: a flow
the agent already RAN is applied (the run happened, hiding it is
contradictory), anything else stays a proposal — the canvas is not replaced
without consent on a turn that failed, and the error event carries no
restore_version_id, so an unasked-for replacement would have no revert either.
The suffix follows that decision instead of asserting one outcome, and the
frontend renders the stranded proposal card alongside the error text so the
offer is reachable.

Non-blocking — the regex narrowing lost real coverage. My claim that it "only
reduces false positives" was wrong: enumerating hijack shapes let seven
previously-blocked strings through, including "I want you to act as a DAN"
(the modal alternation omitted the bare infinitive), "Please act as", "Now,
act as", and it dropped bare "print system prompt" by requiring a possessive.
Inverted: "act as" blocks by default as it originally did, and one carve-out
exempts the relative clause that names a component's role ("a Prompt Template
that will act as a bridge"). That direction can only reduce false positives,
never lose coverage. Only bare "instructions" needs a possessive now, so
"show instructions on how to fix each finding" still passes.

Non-blocking — LANGFLOW_ASSISTANT_ITERATIONS added to the operator env-var
table next to LANGFLOW_ASSISTANT_HISTORY_TURNS.

Verified sound with no change needed, per the review: trusted_source skips the
injection regexes only, and the unconditional inject_iterations_into_flow is a
no-op by default.

Tests: 10 new backend cases (4 for the rescue, 13 parametrized for the regex)
and 2 frontend cases, each failing against the pre-fix code. 1737 agentic
tests and 630 assistant-panel frontend tests pass; ruff and biome clean.

commits.commit_title: fix(mcp): keep advertising inputs for flows that declared no allowlist (#14855)
commits.commit_message:
fix(mcp): keep advertising inputs for flows that declared no allowlist (#14855)

#14837 gated the MCP tools/list schema on api_editable, the Inspector's
per-field "API" toggle. That flag defaults to False, is written only by two
frontend controls, is set by no component and no backend code, and has no
backfill migration. A flow nobody hand-toggled therefore advertised an input
schema containing nothing but the injected session_id.

This was not confined to legacy flows. All 23 shipped starter projects that
carry an input node store input_value with no api_editable key at all — the
templates hold 161 occurrences of "api_editable": false and zero of true — so
the first flow a new user creates from the template picker was published on
the project MCP server with no callable input.

The failure was silent at both ends. handle_call_tool pops input_value before
the tweak filter runs and forwards it as SimplifiedAPIRequest.input_value, so
the runtime still accepted the message the schema no longer declared: the call
returned isError: false with empty content and the flow ran on input_value="".

Two changes, both applied to json_schema_from_flow and to
get_flow_input_tweaks so the advertised schema and the call-time filter cannot
drift apart:

_input_nodes_declare_api_allowlist makes the allowlist a per-flow opt-in,
mirroring the reasoning already recorded for the deployment tweak policy in
lfx/utils/flow_validation.py: a flow whose author toggled at least one field
has declared an allowlist, so the untoggled fields close; a flow with no
toggles has declared nothing and keeps its previous contract. Toggling still
narrows the schema, which is what the ticket asked for — it just no longer
empties the schema of every flow nobody prepared. Scoped to input nodes, since
those are the only fields MCP can advertise; a toggle on an Agent is an
API-snippet concern and must not reshape the MCP contract.

input_value is exempt from the allowlist the same way the call path already
exempts it, so the advertised contract matches the one served.

The type-mapping half of #14837 is unchanged, as is the A2A card, which reads
this schema with require_api_editable=False since #14843.

A file-system level test walks the shipped starter projects and asserts each
one with an input node advertises more than session_id, so a template can
never again ship publishing an uncallable tool.

commits.commit_title: fix(frontend): translate the keys missing from every non-English locale (#14834)
commits.commit_message:
fix(frontend): translate the keys missing from every non-English locale (#14834)

Seven keys shipped in en.json only, so de, es, fr, ja, pt and zh-Hans fell
back to English mid-screen. `i18n.ts` sets `fallbackLng: "en"`, so no raw key
was ever exposed — the strings simply rendered in English inside otherwise
translated dialogs, most visibly the Vector Database field and its description
in Create Memory.

Missing everywhere: memory.backendLabel, memory.dbProviderLabel,
memory.dbProviderDescription, memory.dbProviderNotConfigured,
model.unavailable, model.unavailableTitle, shortcuts.modifierOnly.

model.unavailableTitle is also an aria-label, so screen-reader users on a
translated UI were read English, and shortcuts.modifierOnly is a validation
message on a different settings page — hence all seven rather than only the
four on the Memory Base dialog.

The dialog close control was a separate defect on the same surface: its
tooltip and sr-only label were hardcoded English literals rather than i18n
keys, so no locale could translate them, in every dialog in the product. The
visually hidden fallback DialogTitle next to them had the same problem. Both
now read from new common.close / common.dialog keys.

A locale-parity test keeps this from recurring: every locale must carry every
English key, and every translation must keep the interpolation placeholders of
the string it translates.

commits.commit_title: fix(frontend): date the UI in the language it is showing (#14836)
commits.commit_message:
fix(frontend): date the UI in the language it is showing (#14836)

The unsaved-changes modal translated its "Last saved:" label and then printed
the timestamp as 8/27, 4:45:21 PM in every language, because the call site
passed a hardcoded "en-US" to toLocaleString. A reader of 27/08, 16:45:21 gets
a different date out of the same string.

The same hardcoding sat in the header's saved tooltip, the version sidebar, the
deployments version panel and the trace date labels; the memory helpers passed
`undefined`, which follows the browser rather than the language the user chose
in Langflow. All of them now resolve the locale through `uiLocale()`, which
reads i18n's active language and falls back to the runtime's own locale before
i18n has resolved one — never to a language nobody picked.

The trace helper built its Intl formatter once at module load, so it would have
frozen whichever language the app started in; it now formats per call.

Left alone: the voice assistant's session names, which are stored data rather
than a rendered label, and would change what past sessions are called.

commits.commit_title: fix(frontend): fit the canvas once the whole graph is measured (#14832)
commits.commit_message:
fix(frontend): fit the canvas once the whole graph is measured (#14832)

* fix(frontend): fit the canvas once the whole graph is measured

Opening a flow framed the canvas around a subset of its nodes, leaving the
rest outside the viewport until the user pressed Zoom to Fit.

ReactFlow resolves a queued fitView on the first updateNodeInternals batch,
and getFitViewNodes drops any node without measured.width/height from the
bounding box — position included. Langflow's nodes measure across several
ResizeObserver batches, so every fit request site was computing over whichever
nodes happened to land first, and none of them re-ran.

Fits are now request-driven and deferred until `useNodesInitialized` reports
the graph fully measured, through a single `requestFitView` on the flow store:

- opening or switching a flow implies a request, so in-app navigation is
  covered as well (`useLoadFlowForRoute` skips loading a flow the store
  already holds, so it never reached `useApplyFlowToCanvas`)
- the welcome overlay's template hook hands over its `onFitted` callback
  instead of fitting inside two rAFs, and asks for a second fit once the
  overlay uncovers the canvas and the sidebar narrows it again
- a canvas resize shortly after a fit re-frames the graph, so the viewport
  matches the size the canvas settles at

Fit options (min/max zoom and padding) move into a shared module so the
initial fit and the Zoom to Fit control cannot drift apart — opening a flow
now lands on exactly the viewport the shortcut produces.

* fix(frontend): fit only when a flow asks for it

The deferred fit answered any moment the graph became measured, not just the
one it was asked for, which moved the canvas in two cases it had no business
touching:

- A flow that opens empty leaves the request pending, so the first component
  the user drops measures a graph and gets framed — the canvas jumps out from
  under the cursor mid-edit. Five Playwright shards caught this as a pointer
  interception: the specs build flows by dropping components at fixed
  coordinates, and the re-frame moved the ones dropped afterwards on top of
  their targets. `loop-component.spec.ts` reproduces it locally against the
  branch and passes on the base commit.
- The flow-events settle refresh re-applies the graph to a canvas the user is
  already working in. It also carried a fitView of its own with the padding
  literal duplicated a fourth time.

Fits are now requested explicitly and only where framing is the point: a flow
that arrives with a graph, a restored version, an applied template. Applying a
flow takes a `fitView` option so a background refresh can reload the graph
without re-framing it, and an empty flow requests nothing at all.

The resize correction no longer leans on a wall clock. It fits again at most
once per request, and only while the viewport is still exactly where the fit
put it — once the user has panned or zoomed, the framing is theirs and a later
resize leaves it alone. That also removes the race in the template path, where
uncovering the canvas queued a second fit against the pre-close width and
relied on the timing window to correct it; the template now hands over its
callback and lets the correction do its work.

commits.commit_title: fix(api): run the caller-aware component policy on the vertex build seam (#14808)
commits.commit_message:
fix(api): run the caller-aware component policy on the vertex build seam (#14808)

* fix(api): run the caller-aware component policy on the vertex build seam

POST /api/v1/build/{flow_id}/vertices/{vertex_id} compiled the graph persisted on
the flow row and executed one vertex from it, applying only the caller-agnostic
global validator. The stored graph is caller-controlled -- any user who can write
a flow can persist Python through the ordinary flow API -- so with
custom_component_admin_only on, a non-admin was refused everywhere else and
executed their own source here.

Reproduced over real HTTP on an isolated instance, as two real principals, with a
marker in the component's own return value:

  seam             admin                  non-admin
  build/{id}/flow  200                    400 refused
  build/{id}/vert  200 EXECUTED           200 EXECUTED   <- the bypass

After the fix the non-admin is refused 400 on both seams and the admin still runs
their own code, so the gate substitutes rather than blanket-refusing.

The seam now runs prepare_flow_build_for_user on the stored data, mapping its
outcomes exactly as the whole-flow build does: 400 for a policy rejection, 503
when the policy cannot be evaluated. When the policy returns a sanitized copy the
graph is rebuilt from it rather than reused from cache -- cache keys carry no
policy generation, so a graph compiled while the policy was off still embeds the
caller's own source. That mirrors the guard already in endpoints.py for the
advanced-run cache.

Not claimed: the ticket also reports a 500 (AttributeError) instead of a clean 400
when ALLOW_CUSTOM_COMPONENTS=false. That needs a node whose type matches a
registry component so the substitution lands before the failure; the probe shape
used here is refused earlier, so it was never reproduced and this change is not
asserted to fix it.

Tests: 6 new, five of which fail against the vulnerable code -- policy denial,
caller-awareness, building from the sanitized copy, fail-closed on both
undecidable-policy paths, plus the control that a permissive policy still builds
normally. A refusal for everyone would be a denial of service, not a fix.

Fixes LE-2356

* [autofix.ci] apply automated fixes

* fix(api): close the same policy gap on the vertices-order route

Self-review follow-up on the LE-2356 fix.

B1 -- the sibling seam had the same hole. retrieve_vertices_order takes the same
owner-only stored graph and, when no inline data is supplied, called
build_graph_from_db with no caller-aware policy, then seeded the shared
flow-keyed cache with the result. Fixing only build_vertex left the ticket's
class of defect half open on the route next door. Both stored-graph branches now
go through one _trusted_stored_graph helper, so the exception mapping cannot
drift between them (this also folds in R1 from the review, since the helper would
otherwise have been a third copy).

Adding that call exposed a defect the change itself introduced:
retrieve_vertices_order wraps its body in `except Exception` and re-raises as 500,
so the helper's HTTPException(400) surfaced as an internal server error -- and the
INLINE branch, which mapped its own CustomComponentValidationError correctly
before, regressed the same way. HTTPException is a control-flow signal and now
propagates unwrapped, after the failure telemetry is still recorded. The new
order-route test is what caught it.

I1 -- the denial tests all monkeypatched prepare_flow_build_for_user, so they
proved the wiring, not the security property: the policy could stop refusing and
every one of them would stay green. Added end-to-end tests that flip the real
custom_component_admin_only setting and persist genuinely caller-authored source,
covering both seams and both principals -- a non-admin is refused 400 with no
marker in the body, a superuser is not.

Discrimination measured against release-1.12.0 rather than assumed: the order case
fails there, the build case does not (in this test environment the registry hashes
are warm and the global validator already refuses that payload), so for the build
route the discriminating evidence remains the mocked tests plus the live HTTP
probe. That caveat is recorded in the test docstring rather than left implied.

api/v1 suite: 2018 passed, 11 skipped.

* fix(api): keep vertex build state across policy calls

The admin-only policy returns a sanitized copy on EVERY request from a
non-superuser, not only when the cached compilation predates the policy. This
seam is incremental -- called once per vertex, carrying built state in the flow's
graph cache between calls -- so rebuilding on that condition discarded the
previous vertex's result and the next one reported its upstream as "Component
Chat Input has not been built yet".

Reported by QA against this PR and reproduced here: admin propagates, non-admin
loses state, and with the policy off the same non-admin propagates. Caller- and
policy-dependent, so not a fixture defect.

The condition is now "did the cached compilation come from this copy?", compared
through raw_graph_data. That still rebuilds the case the guard exists for -- a
graph compiled while the policy was off carries different node source -- and
stops rebuilding per request. raw_graph_data is part of Graph.__getstate__; a
marker attribute would be dropped there and would reintroduce this bug on
Redis-backed caches only, which is the kind of environment-dependent failure
worth avoiding. The comparison fails safe: anything unexpected rebuilds.

The reporter's other point is fixed too: initialize_run() was skipped on this
path. build_and_cache_graph_from_data does not initialize, unlike

commits.commit_message:
fix(ollama): keep one unreachable model from emptying the picker (#14817)

* fix(ollama): keep one unreachable model from emptying the picker

get_model / get_models enumerate every model from /api/tags and call /api/show on
each to read its capabilities. Both called raise_for_status() inside that loop, so
the FIRST model the daemon refuses aborted the enumeration and the dropdown came
back empty.

Reproduced on a real Ollama install: a cloud model the daemon is not signed in for
answers 410 Gone on /api/show while every local model answers 200.

    glm-5:cloud                -> 410
    qwen2.5:1.5b               -> 200
    llama3.2:latest            -> 200
    nomic-embed-text:latest    -> 200
    gpt-oss:20b                -> 200

With glm-5:cloud first in /api/tags, the installed nomic-embed-text:latest was
never reached and the editor showed "Error while updating the Component". The loop
now logs and skips a model it cannot inspect.

The leaked message was a second defect in the same handler: httpx.HTTPStatusError
is NOT a subclass of httpx.RequestError, so a non-2xx escaped the except that was
meant to translate failures into "Could not get model names from Ollama." and the
raw httpx text reached the UI. Widened to httpx.HTTPError, which covers both.

Verified against the same live daemon: the picker now returns
['nomic-embed-text:latest'] with the 410 model still installed and listed.

commits.commit_title: fix(datastax): stop batch_size from breaking Cassandra ingest (#14795)
commits.commit_message:
fix(datastax): stop batch_size from breaking Cassandra ingest (#14795)

* fix(datastax): stop batch_size from breaking Cassandra ingest

CassandraVectorStoreComponent.build_vector_store called
Cassandra.from_documents(..., batch_size=self.batch_size). from_documents does
not declare batch_size, so it landed in **kwargs and was splatted into cls(...)
-- Cassandra.__init__, which in langchain-community 0.4.2 accepts only
embedding, session, keyspace, table_name, ttl_seconds, body_index_options,
setup_mode and metadata_indexing. Anything wired to Ingest Data therefore died
with:

    Cassandra.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'batch_size'

The search-only path was unaffected because it constructs Cassandra(...)
directly and never passes batch_size, which is why disconnecting the Ingest
Data edge made the same flow build.

batch_size is not junk to drop: it is a real parameter of Cassandra.add_texts
(default 16), which add_documents forwards to. The store is now constructed
explicitly and the documents are added with
add_documents(documents=..., batch_size=...), so the exposed component field
keeps its meaning instead of being silently ignored.

setup_mode is deliberately NOT introduced on this path. from_documents never
forwarded it either, so the constructor default (SYNC) preserves today's
behaviour. Passing SetupMode.ASYNC here would hand cassio async_setup=True and
an un-awaited coroutine as the vector dimension while add_texts stays
synchronous -- trading one crash for another. The ingest branch ignoring the
user's Setup Mode is a real but separate defect, and it affects the
search-only branch too.

The component lives in the lfx-datastax bundle on this branch;
src/lfx/src/lfx/components/cassandra is only a compatibility shim.

Reproduced before the fix and verified after, against the installed
langchain-community 0.4.2: with the bug, 1/5/40-document ingests all raise the
TypeError; with the fix they build a real Cassandra store and issue one row
write per document. 9 new tests, 8 of which fail against the old code; 104
datastax bundle tests pass.

Fixes #6255
Fixes LE-2352
Supersedes #14573 for the release-1.12.0 line, whose patch targets a path that
no longer holds this component.

Co-Authored-By: andifilhohub <andersonfilho.contato@outlook.com>

* fix(datastax): address review on the Cassandra batch_size fix

Review by @viktoravelino on #14795. All four reproduced before fixing.

1. CI blocker. The 0.1.6 bump reached pyproject/extension.json/uv.lock but not
   the bundle profile or its lock, so bundle_profiles.json still requested
   >=0.1.5 and enterprise-hardened.lock.json still pinned ==0.1.5. Confirmed
   the three failures in scripts/ci/test_bundle_profiles.py, bumped the range
   and recompiled the lock with manage_bundle_profiles.py; the same three now
   pass and the release-plan gate still reports ready.

2. batch_size reached add_texts unvalidated. add_texts slices with
   range(0, len(texts), batch_size), and IntInput coerces a cleared advanced
   field to 0. Reproduced against the real implementation: 0 raised
   "range() arg 3 must not be zero" and -1 returned normally having written
   ZERO rows while logging "Adding 5 documents" -- a silent data-loss path
   worse than the crash. Clamped to max(int(self.batch_size or
   DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE), 1), with the input's default and the guard sharing one
   constant so they cannot drift.

3. Setup Mode OFF is now honoured on the ingest path. The reviewer is right
   that OFF is safe with a synchronous add_documents and that it is the value
   that matters: it drives skip_provisioning, so forcing SYNC re-ran the table
   DDL on every ingest for a pre-provisioned table or a role without CREATE.
   Only ASYNC still degrades to SYNC, for the async_setup reason. The test now
   pins the real invariant per value (Sync->SYNC, Async->SYNC, Off->OFF)
   instead of asserting SYNC for all three.

4. The two Cassandra(...) calls collapsed into one construction followed by a
   conditional add_documents, which is what makes (3) a one-liner.

Test coverage follows the review: batch_size=0 added to the real-implementation
parametrization (the previous 16/2 values could not fail, since put_async runs
once per document regardless of batch size), plus cleared-field and negative
cases. 14 Cassandra tests, 258 across the datastax bundle and the CI scripts.

Co-Authored-By: andifilhohub <andersonfilho.contato@outlook.com>

* chore(ci): recompile the bundle profile lock after the merge

Merging release-1.12.0 brought in #14784, which bumped lfx-amazon and touched
the same bundle_profiles.json and enterprise-hardened.lock.json this branch
already edited for lfx-datastax 0.1.6. Git merged the profile text cleanly, but
the lock carries a profile_digest over the whole contract -- it has to be
RECOMPILED, not merged, so it kept the pre-merge digest and
test_reviewed_profiles_and_locks_are_current failed on the merge commit.

Regenerated with manage_bundle_profiles.py compile; the digest is the only
change. Reproduced the CI failure locally on the merged tree first, and
scripts/ci/test_bundle_profiles.py is back to 14 passed.

* fix(schema): stop coded driver errors collapsing to a bare code

Reported on LE-2352 by QA: a Cassandra Table Name typed with "-" instead of "_"
produced only "Flow build failed. Code: 8192" in the editor, while the real
cause sat in the logs. Noted there as the same shape as an earlier "code 13"
report, so this is not Cassandra-specific.

_coded_exception_message only read args[0]. Reason-coded Langflow errors such as
ModelProviderPolicyError populate it, but driver and SDK exceptions do not: a
cassandra.protocol.SyntaxException carries the protocol status on .code, an
EMPTY args, and the human text on .message / __str__. Since the branch is
selected by hasattr(exception, "code"), it short-circuited past the .message and
.detail fallbacks further down and rendered the number alone.

It now falls back to .message (the SDK convention) and then to __str__, so any
coded exception that has text surfaces it. An exception with a code and genuinely
no message still renders code-only -- the existing test for that shape is
unchanged and still passes.

Reproduced and verified against a REAL Astra database, not a stub. Same flow, same
hyphenated table name:

  before  Code: 8192
  after   line 1:53 mismatched input '-' expecting '(' (... IF NOT EXISTS
          default_keyspace.cassandra[-]...)

The markdown path keeps the code as context alongside the message.

Note on sequencing: reaching the CQL error at all requires the batch_size fix
from #14795, which is why QA only saw this after validating that PR. The
component fix was applied to the working tree for the verification run above and
is NOT part of this branch -- this change is confined to lfx/schema/message.py.

Tests: 2 new, both failing against the current code; 345 lfx schema tests and 90
backend message tests pass.

commits.commit_title: fix(frontend): refetch flow list when upload lands mid first load (#14826)
commits.commit_message:
fix(frontend): refetch flow list when upload lands mid first load (#14826)

A flow created while the paginated project query is still loading its first
page never appeared in the list. TanStack's cancelRefetch fast path only
cancels and restarts an in-flight request once the query holds data, so with
data still undefined the mutation's refetch resolved with the request issued
before the upload, and nothing refetched afterwards.

Add refetchQueriesFresh, which awaits a cold in-flight fetch before refetching,
and use it in usePostAddFlow. The call stays fire-and-forget: TanStack
dispatches the mutation success only after onSettled settles, so awaiting it
would delay every addFlow caller, including the navigation to the new flow.

This is what failed outdated-actions.spec.ts on the Windows nightly, where the
first project page takes ~900ms and overlaps the drop. Also drop the hardcoded
5s expect timeouts in that spec so the platform-aware default applies.

commits.commit_title: fix(store): stop a Langflow Store outage from breaking the app (#14803)
commits.commit_message:
fix(store): stop a Langflow Store outage from breaking the app (#14803)

api.langflow.store began serving a certificate for
*.<id>.us-east-1.cs.amazonlightsail.com instead of its own hostname, so every
TLS connection to it fails verification. Verified directly against the live
host, outside CI. Two independent defects turned that third-party outage into a
Langflow outage:

1. The visual editor asked for store tags on every boot. AppInitPage calls
   useGetTagsQuery unconditionally, on every route, even though
   ENABLE_LANGFLOW_STORE is false and the store's only consumer (ShareModal)
   already gates itself on hasStore, which is ENABLE_LANGFLOW_STORE && ... .
   Nothing could read those tags; the request was pure cost and pure risk. It
   is now gated inside the hook rather than at the call site, so no caller can
   reintroduce it, and an explicit enabled: false still wins.

2. GET /api/v1/store/tags answered 500 for an unreachable upstream. store.py
   funnels everything into a bare `except Exception` -> 500, so a third-party
   service being down read as a fault of this server. httpx surfaces the TLS
   failure as ConnectError (a TransportError); that now degrades to an empty
   tag list with a warning, since tags only decorate a filter. Errors that are
   genuinely ours still return 500 and stay loud.

Either fix alone closes the CI wipeout, but each covers a different failure:
(1) is what a deployment with the store off should always have done, (2) is
what protects deployments that keep the store on.

Blast radius: the Playwright fixture fails any test that sees an unexpected
server error, so a page load producing a 500 wiped whole shards -- unrelated
suites (a11y, api-keys) failed with nothing but store SSL errors in the report.

Tests: 6 backend (parametrized over the exact SSL message, connect/read
timeouts and a protocol error, plus the must-stay-500 and happy paths) and 3
frontend, each verified failing against the pre-fix code. 21 store backend
tests and 20 frontend tests pass; ruff and biome clean on the touched files.

commits.commit_title: fix(observability): start every request task from a clean context (#14769)
commits.commit_message:
fix(observability): start every request task from a clean context (#14769)

* fix(observability): start every request task from a clean context

Roughly half of HTTP server spans in a browser page load were emitted as
INTERNAL children of an unrelated, already-finished request instead of as
SERVER roots, merging unrelated requests into one trace.

When a request arrives on a connection while another is still in flight,
uvicorn queues it and later starts it from inside the finishing request's
task (httptools_impl on_response_complete -> _start_asgi_task).
create_task copies the context, so the new request begins with the
previous request's ended server span still current, and OpenTelemetry's
ASGI middleware faithfully reports that as nesting.

Nothing fails to detach: the originating request detaches correctly in
its own task, but the copied context keeps the ended span. This is
uvicorn's documented CPython #140947 case, and uvicorn already ships the
opt-out. Set it on both launch paths.

Measured with a probe on the ASGI span-kind decision, one browser page
load: 32 requests with 4 demoted before, 36 requests with 0 demoted
after. Sequential curl never reproduced it, which is why this needed a
real page load to see.

* fix: require uvicorn context reset support

commits.commit_message:
fix: detect Google retired-model 404 for fallback (#14778)

* fix: detect Google retired-model 404 for fallback

Google retires a model for newly issued API keys while still listing it, so
the name resolves everywhere and only the call fails:

    This model models/gemini-2.5-pro is no longer available to new users.
    Please update your code to use models/gemini-3.1-pro-preview

None of _MODEL_UNAVAILABLE_MARKERS matched that phrasing, so the assistant's
model-fallback chain never ran and the turn ended on a terminal "Model not
available. Please select a different model." — which came from the looser
heuristic in extract_friendly_error, making it look like the fallback had
been consulted and given up. The provider offered ten other callable models.

Add the marker so the existing chain fires, and fix two things it exposed:

- ASSISTANT_PREFERRED_MODELS listed gemini-1.5-pro as Google's second
  preference, but that name is deprecated and _catalog_model_names filters
  deprecated models out, so it could never be selected. The list looked like
  it had a fallback and did not. Replace it with gemini-3.1-pro-preview.
- get_provider_model_candidates followed catalog order after the default,
  which leads with small flash SKUs. Order it through _preferred_first so a
  blocked default drops to the next curated preference instead of a weaker
  model.

The default stays gemini-2.5-pro: it works for every key that has access
today, and a key that doesn't is now rescued by the fallback.

Fixes LE-2310.

commits.commit_title: docs: custom components in publicly shared flows (#14773)
commits.commit_message:
docs: custom components in publicly shared flows (#14773)

* docs: custom components in publicly shared flows

The unauthenticated public flow build path substitutes the server's own
component code and refuses any node whose type it doesn't recognize, so a
Shareable Playground can't run a flow containing a custom component. The
opt-out for that, LANGFLOW_ALLOW_PUBLIC_CUSTOM_COMPONENTS, has existed since
1.10.1 but was never documented, and the visitor-facing error says only
"This flow cannot be executed."

Document the default behavior, the error and the log line it writes, the
environment variable, how it combines with LANGFLOW_ALLOW_CUSTOM_COMPONENTS,
and why it shouldn't be enabled on a multi-tenant deployment.

* docs: document installing the component on the server

Review feedback. A custom component added through LANGFLOW_COMPONENTS_PATH is
part of the server's template set, so public flow builds substitute the
server's copy and the flow runs with the default policy intact. Verified
against the flow from issue #14729: with only LANGFLOW_COMPONENTS_PATH set and
LANGFLOW_ALLOW_PUBLIC_CUSTOM_COMPONENTS left at its default, both
/api/v1/build_public_tmp and /api/v2/workflows/public return 200 and the flow
reaches RUN_FINISHED.

Lead with that instead of the environment variable, stop claiming every custom
component lacks a server copy, qualify the authenticated paths as holding while
LANGFLOW_ALLOW_CUSTOM_COMPONENTS is true, and move the trust warning into a
warning admonition.
