commits.commit_message:
fix(web): stop asserting unknown project facts while entering a project (#7428)

* fix(web): stop asserting unknown project facts while entering a project

Entering a personal project cold showed two statements that were not true yet.

The read-only banner rendered on viewerOnly, which is fail-closed and also
covers the window where ownership is simply unproven. So your own project told
you it was someone else's shared project for as long as the workspace context
took to resolve. The gate stays -- controls should be disabled until proven --
but the banner asserts a reason, so it now waits for isSharedNonOwner, whose
docblock already promises positive evidence and never mere !isOwner during the
status-unknown window.

The design-files empty state has the same shape: zero files before the first
authoritative read is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty project, and its
CTAs create NEW content. The panel already draws this distinction for a team
mirror that is still downloading; a local list that has not returned yet now
gets it too, keyed on the files snapshot generation, which advances only on an
accepted list (a transport failure deliberately does not advance it).

Measured in Chrome against a personal project with one artifact: the read-only
banner appeared at 4.8s and the empty state was rendered then removed; both are
now absent for the whole entry. Neither change touches what is disabled -- only
what the UI claims while it does not know.

* fix(daemon): keep one preview scope per project so a refetch is byte-identical

The web client builds its srcDoc preview from GET /raw/<file>?odPreviewBridge=…,
and that route minted a fresh preview scope on every request, injecting it as
<base href="…/preview/<uuid>/">. So the same artifact served different bytes on
every read: any refetch produced a different srcDoc string, React assigned it,
and the iframe reloaded -- the artifact visibly vanished and came back.

Measured on a team-workspace entry before this change: the srcDoc was rebuilt
1-4 times per entry depending on timing (one run wrote an empty document in
between), each rebuild carrying a different base href.

Preview reads now acquire the live scope for that exact (project, workspace),
renewing its TTL, and only mint when none exists. The grant is identical -- same
project, same member, same TTL bound -- only its name is now stable.

Deliberately not folded into mint(): export flows mint a scope and revoke it
when the render finishes, and sharing an id with a live preview would revoke the
preview out from under it. acquire() is a separate entry point used only by the
preview read.

Verified two ways. Unit: two reads of one artifact return the same base href;
swapping acquire back to mint turns it red. Browser: recording a team-workspace
entry and measuring frames where the preview goes blank after content had
appeared -- 2 such episodes before (one lasting 74ms), 0 after.

* fix(web): say the file list is loading instead of showing nothing

Suppressing the empty-state CTAs removed a false claim but left the panel blank
until content arrived, which reads as stuck rather than busy -- a worse first
impression than the wrong copy it replaced.

The unknown window now renders the same pill the team-mirror sync uses, with the
existing common.loading copy, so the slot always says which of the three states
it is in: loading, syncing, or genuinely empty. No new copy, no new i18n keys.

This is a consolation, not a cure: the real cost is how long the list takes to
arrive. That is tracked separately -- the project-files read is keyed on the
workspace identity, and workspaceType inside that key is echoed straight back
from the request's own x-od-workspace-type header, so a stale header during
entry changes the key and defeats the request sharing that exists to prevent
exactly these duplicate reads.

* perf(web): single-flight the design-system catalog read

Entering a project mounts several independent catalog readers in the same
tick. `fetchDesignSystemsResult` fetched `/api/design-systems` directly, so
three concurrent readers meant three requests — while the team-index step in
the very same function was already coalesced. The catalog read was the half
that got missed.

Identical concurrent reads are not merely redundant here. The daemon answers
them serially, so each duplicate holds one of the browser's ~6 per-host
connections for seconds. Measured entering a real project, three catalog
reads took 1.8s / 3.1s / 3.7s while this project's own `/files` read — 17ms
when uncontended — waited 1.2s for a connection.

Route it through the same `coalescedGet` the team index uses, partitioned by
workspace identity and by the caller-supplied team witness. Two invariants
are preserved deliberately:

- A forced read (`forceTeamMaterialization`, fired BY a mutation) evicts any
  in-flight snapshot instead of joining it, exactly as the team index does
  one function above. A mutation must observe its own effect.
- `coalescedGet` declines to cache a rejection, but this reader reports
  failure as a resolved `{ ok: false }`, so that is evicted explicitly rather
  than shared for the rest of the window.

Measured entering the same project, three runs before and three after:

  design-systems requests   4 / 4 / 4      ->  2 / 2 / 2
  slowest of those          3678/5056/5318 ->  1501/745/1769 ms
  requests over 1s          37 / 53 / 27   ->  16 / 7 / 9

Total request count moved too but its ranges overlap across runs, so no
claim is made there. The remaining 2 reads are the two identity generations
of entry (provisional, then resolved); collapsing those is a separate change.

Red spec first: the burst assertion failed with "expected 3 to be 1" before
the fix. The forced-read guard was green before and after — it locks in the
invariant rather than reporting a defect.

* fix(daemon): never let a live preview adopt a one-shot preview scope

Review caught a real defect in this branch's own `acquire`. It searched every
registry entry by (project, workspace), and entries carried no record of who
minted them or why. A screenshot/PDF export mints a scope for the same tuple
and `revoke`s it in its `finally`, so a preview that acquired the export's
entry would lose its `<base href>` the moment that export finished -- blanking
the artifact, which is the exact symptom this area exists to prevent.

The comment above `acquire` claimed the mint/acquire split already prevented
this. It did not: the split only stopped `mint` from handing out a shared id,
while `acquire` remained free to find an export's entry.

Mark the lifetime on the entry instead. `mint` creates one-shot scopes whose
owner revokes them; `acquire` creates and matches only reusable scopes, which
are released by expiry alone. The public surface is unchanged -- both go
through one internal `create`.

Red spec first, at the HTTP boundary: `preview-url` mints exactly the way an
export does, so it stands in for one without needing a renderer. Before the
fix the bridged raw read handed back the *same UUID* that mint had just
issued:

  expected 'e60f3014-…-642f00aeadc2' not to be 'e60f3014-…-642f00aeadc2'

* fix(web): stop the remaining surfaces claiming an unproven share

Browser verification of the earlier banner fix showed the claim was shortened,
not removed. Measured entering an OWNED personal project, three runs each:

  main            "这是共享项目…" shown ~4.1s
  banner fix only shown ~1.0s, 3 of 3 runs
  this commit     not shown, 3 of 3 runs

The banner was only one of three surfaces deriving the claim from
`projectMutationReadOnly` (= `viewerOnly || materializationPending`), which is
fail-closed and therefore also true while ownership is merely unknown. The
chat composer placeholder and the project title tooltip each re-derived it,
so gating the banner alone left the same false sentence on screen.

Give the reason one name. `projectReadOnlyClaim` returns undefined while the
share is unproven, and all three surfaces read that one value. Disabling still
comes from the fail-closed flag — only the CLAIM waits for evidence.

This is the same defect class as the hook-level fixes in
use-project-collab.context-seed and use-project-collab.created-by-viewer; it
survived them because these three sites bypass the hook's guard and read the
flag directly.

* fix: restore the fixes d61be13806 reverted by accident

d61be13806 was meant to carry one web change. It also silently reverted the
daemon preview-scope fix, the design-files loading placeholder, and the
file-workspace banner gate — every fix this PR had landed so far.

Cause: verifying the branch in a browser meant swapping files to their
origin/main content and back. `git checkout origin/main -- <paths>` does not
only change the working tree, it STAGES those paths. Restoring the working
tree afterwards left the index still holding main's content, and `git commit`
commits the index, not the working tree. The check I ran before committing
(`git diff HEAD -- apps/daemon`) compares the working tree, so it reported
clean while the index was not. `git status` did say `MM`; I read the second M
and not the first.

This commit restores all five files to their state at the merge commit
0f923028c4, verified marker by marker rather than by eye:

  daemon acquire / reusable scope entries        present
  server-context acquire on the deps interface   present
  design-files loading placeholder + gate        present
  file-workspace banner requires a reason        present

No behavior is intended to change relative to 0f923028c4 plus d61be13806's
ProjectView work; this only undoes collateral damage.

* fix(daemon): keep the whole bridged document stable, not just the scope id

Review caught that this branch's preview-scope reuse does not actually stop
the flicker it was written for. `acquire` renewed `entry.expiresAt` on every
call, and that expiry is serialized into the bridge script of the very
document the scope is injected into (`buildPreviewBaseHrefBridge` JSON-encodes
`{href, expiresAt}`). So two repeated reads returned the same scope id and the
same `<base href>` while the full body still differed — React reassigns
`srcDoc`, the iframe reloads, and the artifact blinks exactly as before.

Stop renewing on acquire. Lifetime extension already has its own path: the
client renews explicitly via `x-od-preview-scope-renewal`, and that response
is not a document, so extending there changes no served bytes.

The existing spec could not see this: it compared only the `<base href>`. It
now compares the complete returned document, which is what `srcDoc` actually
receives — any byte that moves per request reloads the iframe just as surely
as a fresh scope id would.

Verified end to end against a running daemon, three repeated reads of one
artifact:

  before  6ccf51baf7238d5c / 3a7c49a353b5efdd / 0e02c96c1da882f4
  after   dfd91bb06572dd65 / dfd91bb06572dd65 / dfd91bb06572dd65

Not verified: a browser-level before/after on the srcDoc transport. Every
"before" attempt resolved to the URL-load path instead, where changing bytes
at a stable `src` does not reload the iframe at all, so the two runs were not
comparable. The HTTP-level evidence above measures the defect itself.

* docs(daemon): say that acquire reuses a scope without renewing it

Both docblocks still described the behaviour the previous commit deliberately
removed. The dependency contract in server-context.ts promised a renewed TTL,
and the summary above the implementation said the same, so a future consumer
could reasonably assume repeated acquisition keeps a scope alive -- or make
the implementation match the comment and reintroduce the byte instability
that reloads the iframe.

Both now state that acquire reuses without renewing, that ttlMs applies only
when it has to create a new reusable scope, and that keeping an in-use scope
alive is renew's job.

* fix(daemon): freeze the expiry a preview document reports

The previous commit stopped `acquire` from renewing, but left the other half:
the explicit `renew` endpoint still moves `entry.expiresAt`, and the next
bridged read serializes that new value. Review measured it — `read -> renew ->
read` kept the same scope and the same length, changed the embedded expiry,
and produced one additional iframe `load` in Electron. The client renews on a
timer for as long as a preview is open, so this is the steady state, not an
edge case.

Split the two meanings the field was carrying. `expiresAt` stays the live
lifetime that renewal extends, and JSON responses keep reading it.
`documentExpiresAt` is frozen when the scope is created and is what a served
body embeds, so nothing a renewal does can change the bytes of a document.

The host does not lose anything: it uses the embedded value only to seed its
first renewal, and every renewal after that is scheduled from the renew
response (FileViewer keeps the returned expiry, it does not re-read the
document for it).

Red spec first: `keeps the bridged document identical across an explicit
renewal` failed on two byte-different bodies. Mutation-checked by pointing the

commits.commit_title: fix(web): scope the reference-project picker to the caller workspace (#7701)
commits.commit_message:
fix(web): scope the reference-project picker to the caller workspace (#7701)

ProjectReferenceModal already carried a workspaceContext and already forwarded
it to getProjectDetail on confirm, but the catalog read called listProjects with
no context. Without one, listProjects falls back to the unscoped
GET /api/projects, which serves listUnboundProjects -- a LEFT JOIN that excludes
every workspace-bound project by construction. A signed-in member therefore saw
"No other projects yet" while Home listed those same projects.

Pass the context through with workspaceView 'all', matching the two sibling
pickers in TasksView and RoutinesSection. The effect is keyed on
workspaceIdentityCacheKey rather than the context object so a switch of
workspace or caller authority re-reads the catalog while an equivalent
re-created object does not spin the request.

The pre-existing assertion pinned the buggy call shape as a contract, so it is
updated rather than deleted. HomeView.context-picker's fetch mocks answered only
the unscoped route while rendering with an active workspace; they now answer the
workspace-scoped route the picker really uses.

Co-authored-by: Cheems <94773058+itscheems@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.commit_title: fix(dsh): support DeepSeek Harness 0.1.2-rc.1, now npm's latest (#7825)
commits.commit_message:
fix(dsh): support DeepSeek Harness 0.1.2-rc.1, now npm's latest (#7825)

`@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.2-rc.1` was published on 2026-09-03 and holds npm's
`latest` dist-tag, so it is what a user who installs without naming a version
receives. Both of our authorities rejected that line:

  - the agent def did not accept `0.1.2-rc.1`, so Settings labelled the user's
    CLI untested;
  - `packages/dsh-runtime`'s peer ranges evaluated to false for it, because
    semver admits a prerelease only against a comparator sharing its exact
    major.minor.patch and carrying a prerelease of its own — so the companion
    component could not resolve at all. That half is silent, which makes it the
    worse one.

Move the installers to `0.1.2-rc.1` with a resolution cutoff between its publish
time and any successor, add the `0.1.2-rc.N` alternative to the accepted line,
and add the matching comparator to all five dsh peers. All five, because a
single updated peer would otherwise vouch for the other four.

The Alpine fallback in install-dsh.sh named `0.1.0-rc.6` — two patch lines stale,
because nothing pointed at it when the pin moved. It now interpolates
$DSH_VERSION.

Both test files previously pinned the broken state, asserting `0.1.2-rc.1` was
rejected; they now assert the invariant and went red before any source change.
`0.2.0-rc.1` stays refused by both authorities so the widening cannot decay into
accepting everything.

`packages/dsh-runtime`'s dependencies and devDependencies stay at `0.1.1-rc.2`
on purpose: bumping them resolves a mixed-generation tree (dsh-scope and
dsh-settings stay on 0.1.0-rc.6) and wants a cordis bump too. See the PR body.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01B8MaA1ABkvbnfaYUKw3UH3

commits.commit_title: fix(ci): make the DSH upstream drift card readable (#7824)
commits.commit_message:
fix(ci): make the DSH upstream drift card readable (#7824)

The maintainer who received this alert could not tell what it was. The
headline jumped straight to a verdict, so nothing said an upstream release
had been detected or where the message came from; the body opened with
semver theory; the blocking branch never mentioned the version we pin,
making the most urgent card the least informative one; and nothing said
when upstream shipped, so there was no way to tell a release from this
morning apart from one that had been sitting for a fortnight.

The headline now names the check and only the check — severity travels in
the header template, which Feishu renders before any text. The first
sentence is three facts with no reasoning attached: what upstream
released, when, and what we still pin, on both severities. The
consequence follows, and the semver rationale is compressed into a
parenthetical behind it. The three-file checklist is untouched.

Reading the publish date means asking npm for the full packument: the
compact one (`application/vnd.npm.install-v1+json`) carries no `time` map
at all. `readPublishedAt` degrades to null for every shape short of that,
because the date is one sentence of context on an alert whose entire
reason to exist is being sent.

Also replaces a self-check assertion that could never fail:
`String(card.header).length === 0` is "[object Object]".length whatever
the card says. It now reads the fields a human reads.

commits.commit_title: fix(daemon): state the skill read-only boundary instead of letting agents guess (#7720)
commits.commit_message:
fix(daemon): state the skill read-only boundary instead of letting agents guess (#7720)

* fix(daemon): state the skill read-only boundary instead of letting agents guess

A user asked the agent to update one of his own skills. Every write to the
skill directory came back `Operation not permitted` — by design:
`resolveChatExtraAllowedDirs` keeps skill roots out of the writable
allowlist, and Codex is given no skill directory at all because it treats
`--add-dir` as write access (#622).

Nothing in the composed system prompt said so. With no stated boundary and
no stated exit, the agent invented one: it told the user to open Open
Design's settings and add the directory to a "文件系统 / 工作区 / 可写目录 /
writable roots" option. No such setting exists — not for writable roots, not
for a sandbox mode, not for an approval policy. The user went looking for
it, could not find it, and filed a diagnostics bundle (0.21.0, packaged
stable).

Adds an `## Editing skills` section that states the boundary and its
symptom, names the real edit surface (the Integration view's Skills tab —
NOT a "Settings > Skills" page, which does not exist), and forbids inventing
a settings path to explain the failure. The missing settings are worded as a
statement about the current build rather than a refusal, so contributors do
not read it as "we will never build this"; a controlled skill-write path is
still on the table.

Gated on `executionProfile === 'filesystem'`. Deliberately NOT gated on
`isSlimCore` — slim is the production default, so that gate would ship this
to nobody — nor on an active skill, since "update my skill" arrives on turns
where no skill is bound. Ask mode and API/BYOK mode have no file tools and
so cannot hit the boundary; the matrix snapshot pins that (18 of 20
scenarios receive it, `ask-mode-full-context` and `api-mode-byok` do not).

Red spec: tests/skill-write-guidance.test.ts, 5/5 red on this branch with
the `parts.push` removed, and 1/5 red (the wording guard alone) when
"does not currently expose" is rewritten to an absolute "we do not support".
Assertions are scoped to the extracted section rather than the whole prompt:
an earlier draft asserted /today/i document-wide and passed with no
implementation at all.

Note: like any prompt change this shifts the stable-prompt hash once, so
existing conversations take a single `stable-prompt-changed` cache miss on
first turn after upgrade.

Tested: pnpm --filter @open-design/daemon exec vitest run tests/skill-write-guidance.test.ts tests/system-prompt-template.test.ts tests/prompt-templates.test.ts tests/intent-signal-stable-prompt-cache.test.ts tests/official-system-prompt.test.ts tests/prompt-telemetry.test.ts tests/prompts tests/chat-route.test.ts (20 files, 355 tests)
Tested: pnpm --filter @open-design/daemon build
Tested: pnpm guard
Tested: pnpm typecheck
Not-tested: live packaged client — prompt-only change, no runtime surface

* fix(daemon): name the staged .od-skills copy as a non-persisting write

The boundary section told agents that writing a skill returns `Operation
not permitted`. That is true for the real skill root, and false for the
one skill path the prompt stack actually advertises:
`withSkillRootPreamble` names `<cwd>/.od-skills/<folder>/` as the primary
**Skill root**, and it sits inside the agent's writable project cwd. A
`Write`/`Edit`/`Bash` against `.od-skills/<id>/SKILL.md` therefore
succeeds, reads as an install, and is discarded when `stageActiveSkill`
re-stages the copy on the next turn — the same misdirection the section
was written to stop, minus the error that would have stopped it.

The handover line made that landing spot likely rather than incidental:
"write the proposed `SKILL.md` into the project folder" pointed at a
folder that already contains a directory labelled the skill root.

So: name the staged copy and say a write there does not persist, and
send the proposal to a new `.md` file in the project folder, explicitly
not under `.od-skills/`. The two new assertions are section-scoped and
go red against the previous wording — `/operation not permitted/` could
not, because on this path nothing is denied.

* fix(od-next): state the same skill read-only boundary on the strategy path

`server.ts` picks one composer per run:

    const prompt = odNextStrategyRecipe
      ? composeOdNextStrategyCorePromptV2(odNextStrategyRecipe)
      : composeSystemPrompt(systemPromptInputs);

so everything the previous commit added lives on the classic branch only.
When the OD Next strategy is assigned, `composeSystemPrompt` is never
called and there is no always-resident block underneath — the boundary
section disappears wholesale, and the reported failure comes back.

OD Next is not a path where this is hypothetical. It is the path with the
sharper version of the same trap: `materializeFrozenSkillPackage` writes
the frozen Skill package into `<cwd>/.od-skills/`, and the strategy prompt
hands the agent those exact roots — `materializedRoot` in the Skill roster
(`renderFrozenSkillRosterContext`) and `Frozen side-file root:` in each
Skill body (`resolveFrozenSkillBundleBodies`). Writable directory,
advertised path, no stated boundary, and a write there additionally breaks
the frozen identity the daemon verifies.

So the same four statements land in the core strategy prompt's
`## Agent and runtime boundaries`: the boundary, the materialized roots
that accept a write without persisting it, the real Skills-tab exit, and
the prohibition on inventing a sandbox / writable-roots / approval-policy
setting.

`assets.core.version` moves 2.1.0 -> 2.2.0 with the text. Package identity
is content-hashed from these bytes at apply time
(`buildStrategyPackageIdentity`), and `plugins-strategy-recipe.test.ts`
copies the real bundled folder, so that suite exercises identity against
the edited asset rather than a fixture.

The new assertions are scoped to the section (`.od-skills` also appears in
the task-profile assets, so a document-wide match could not go red) and
whitespace-normalized, since the asset is hard-wrapped prose. Five of the
six go red against the previous content; the sixth is labelled in-file as a
locator check that stays green on `main` by design.

commits.commit_title: test(desktop): give Electron probes a CI-sized timeout (#7774)
commits.commit_message:
test(desktop): give Electron probes a CI-sized timeout (#7774)

* test(desktop): give Electron probes a CI-sized timeout

The PPTX layered-background and base-href tests each spawn a throwaway
Electron process (xvfb-run on Linux) and gave it 10-20s. A cold Electron
start on a busy GitHub runner regularly exceeds that, and execFile then
reports a bare "Command failed: xvfb-run … electron …" with no stderr —
which is how an unrelated PR turns red on one probe (see #7772, four
consecutive runs, and #7768 on the same case) while the file passes locally.

Both files now share one probe budget (60s) and one per-test budget (90s)
behind named constants instead of scattered literals. A probe that really
hangs still fails, just later.

* test(desktop): run the PNG paint probe sandbox-less and surface its output

The paint probe was the one Electron spawn in the file without
--no-sandbox --disable-gpu, and the only one that rethrew a failed spawn
without the child's stdout/stderr. On the CI runner that combination is a
probe that exits before app.whenReady() with a bare "Command failed" —
the failure #7774's first run still showed with the larger budget. Align
it with the other probes and attach the child's output on failure so the
next flake, if any, says why.

commits.commit_title: feat(web): add recent projects and run status to the entry rail (#7730)
commits.commit_message:
feat(web): add recent projects and run status to the entry rail (#7730)

* feat(contracts,daemon): report awaiting-input projects on the runs list

`ChatRunStatus` cannot express "waiting on the user": the run that asked a
`<question-form>` reports `succeeded` and exits while the project stays
blocked, so a client folding `GET /api/runs` into a per-project status shows
such a project as finished. Ship `awaitingInputProjectIds` beside the runs,
composed from the same `listProjectsAwaitingInput` read `GET /api/projects`
uses and intersected with the projects the returned runs already reveal, so
the field can never widen what a caller may see.

Ported 1:1 from upstream #7635 for OPEND-2553 (PR-A).

* feat(web): derive per-project run status from the runs feed

`Project.status` only arrives on the unscoped `GET /api/projects`, so a
workspace-scoped session cannot read it. Add the pure fold
(`foldRunsToProjectStatuses`) that mirrors the daemon's composition, the
per-project `listRunsForProject` read plus `useProjectRunStatuses` hook that
keeps it live off `RUNS_CHANGED_EVENT`, the one glyph per status
(`ProjectRunStatusIcon` over the SiriOrb), and the two conversation reducers
(`latestUserPromptText`, `runProgressSteps`) the Design Files empty state
will read.

No visual change on its own. Ported 1:1 from upstream #7635 for OPEND-2553
(PR-A).

* feat(web): list recent projects in the entry nav rail

Adds the 最近浏览过 disclosure under 插件 in the signed-in rail: the head of
the same recent catalog 全部项目 shows, newest first, capped at eight rows.
Each row leads with the project's live run status (running / needs input /
completed / failed) from the runs feed, opens through the shell's pull-first
opener, floats a cover preview beside the rail on hover, and carries a ⋮ menu
with rename, whole-project export and a two-step delete. An acknowledged ✓ is
spent by opening the project and re-raised by the next run.

The Home page's recent-projects grid stays; this only adds the rail entry.
Row geometry, easing and colours are pinned to the Demo (upstream #7635) by
`tests/styles/entry-rail-recent.test.ts`. OPEND-2553 (PR-A).

* fix(web): acknowledge the rail ✓ per finished run

The 最近浏览过 rows spent a project's ✓ by remembering the PROJECT id and only
forgot it after observing a live queued/running status. The section polls
only while it is open, so a run that started and finished while it was
collapsed was never observed: on re-expanding, the stale acknowledgement
still matched and the new completion's ✓ never showed. (The Demo, #7635,
carries the same defect; this deliberately diverges from it.)

Acknowledge by run identity instead. `foldRunsToProjectRunSummaries` reports
the newest terminal run's id beside each project's status (the status-only
fold is derived from it and unchanged for its callers), `useProjectRunSummaries`
exposes it live, and the rail stores `{ projectId: acknowledgedRunId }`: a ✓
is acknowledged for one specific finished run, and a newer finished run is a
new notice. The reset-on-running effect is gone. A store in the old array
shape reads as nothing acknowledged, so at worst one already-seen ✓ shows
once more.

Red spec: tests/components/EntryNavRail.recent-section.test.tsx
"re-raises the ✓ for a newer finished run even when its running phase was
never seen". OPEND-2553 (PR-A).

The Home recent-projects specs keep main's shape (PR-C owns that move). Refs OPEND-2553.

commits.commit_title: feat(agentic_rag): add tool playbook, clarify tool specs, stop wasted… (#19459)
commits.commit_message:
feat(agentic_rag): add tool playbook, clarify tool specs, stop wasted… (#19459)

## Summary
- rag/prompts/action_run.md: add a TOOL PLAYBOOK section covering
combination chains, convergence rules, and a tool-status -> next-action
table, so the model emits a state patch instead of re-searching an
exhausted direction.
- rag/advanced_rag/harness/action_session.py: rewrite the 7 tool specs
into an explicit WHEN TO CALL / DO NOT CALL / ARGUMENTS / OUTPUT / IF IT
FAILS contract, and cap the shared evidence pool at _EVIDENCE_POOL_CAP
(60, mirrors _SCA_VIEW_CAP) so a saturated session stops admitting
chunks the SCA view can no longer read.
- rag/advanced_rag/agentic_rag_graph.py: short-circuit _route_sca to
finalize once the evidence pool reaches the SCA view cap, since another
research round cannot flip the sufficiency verdict.
- test/unit_test/rag/advanced_rag/test_action_session_schema.py: cover
the action-session tool-spec schema.

Co-authored-by: Hermes Agent <hermes-agent@localhost>

commits.commit_title: fix(market): stop advertising country stock indexes Yahoo cannot serve (#8092)
commits.commit_message:
fix(market): stop advertising country stock indexes Yahoo cannot serve (#8092)

* fix(market): stop advertising country stock indexes Yahoo cannot serve

Eight of the 45 countries in marketCountryStockIndexes have returned
available:false since the enum was created because Yahoo Finance serves no
daily closes for their symbols (#6240). Every seeder run fetched all eight
and logged eight failures, and every RPC request for one of them spent a
Redis read and a Yahoo request to learn nothing.

Re-probed on 2026-09-13 through the same chart endpoint the seeder uses:

- PT: ^PSI20 is dead but PSI20.LS (Euronext Lisbon) returns 24 closes over
  the month. Symbol swapped.
- RU, PL, EG, CL, PE, CZ, HU: no serviceable Yahoo symbol found. IMOEX.ME
  has had no data since 2022; WIG20.WA and ^IPSA carry a single close over
  three months; the exchange-suffixed variants for Prague, Budapest and
  Cairo do not exist.

Those seven stay in the public enum so the OpenAPI contract and existing
callers are unchanged, but each entry now carries an `unavailable` block
with the check date and reason. The handler answers available:false for a
flagged country without a Redis read or a Yahoo request, and the registry
excludes flagged countries from the seed work-list (38 seeded instead of 45
attempted). The health floor of 30 is unaffected.

scripts/audit-country-stock-index-symbols.mjs probes every declared symbol
through fetchYahooJson and exits non-zero when a serviceable entry is dead
or a flagged entry has come back, so a flag can be lifted on evidence. It is
network-bound and not part of test:data; its decision table is unit-tested.

* fix(market): keep failed audit probes out of flag verdicts and register the audit source

A Yahoo 429 or retries-exhausted probe was classified as a verdict on the symbol: a flagged country read 'flagged-still-dead' (exit 0) and a live one 'dead-but-serviceable' (flag it). Probe failures are now 'probe-error', never feed the flag verdicts, and exit 2 so a rate-limited run reads as inconclusive. main() loads .env.local like the seeder so fetchYahooJson can use the PROXY_URL fallback, the verdict follows buildCountryStockIndexSnapshot rather than a copied close count, the stagger matches the seeder's 200 ms, and direct execution uses pathToFileURL.

Also registers scripts/audit-country-stock-index-symbols.mjs in the source-attribution ledger (generated with the trusted origin/main scripts/source-attribution.mjs --write; its absence failed docs-stats and every unit shard), derives the health floor test's bound from the seedable registry instead of the 2026-08-05 literal 37, and updates the health, seeder, handler and test comments that still said every enum country is seeded.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01WxfoAwNX4jSHJmgq9HnmrV

* fix(market): route the audit entrypoint through the shared main-module helper

tests/main-module-gates.test.mjs rejects an inline import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href guard in new CLIs because it silently exits 0 when the checkout is reached through a symlink; use scripts/lib/main-module.mjs isMainModule like the other audit scripts. The source-attribution scanner no longer classifies the audit script as a Yahoo consumer after this edit, so the ledger reference added in the previous commit is removed again (trusted origin/main scripts/source-attribution.mjs --write reproduces the base manifest and --check passes).

commits.commit_title: fix(usni): map every published Fleet Tracker heading to real coordinates (#8091)
commits.commit_message:
fix(usni): map every published Fleet Tracker heading to real coordinates (#8091)

* fix(usni): map every published Fleet Tracker heading to real coordinates

The USNI Fleet Tracker parser and the client each carried their own region
coordinate table, and neither covered the headings USNI actually publishes.
Of the 91 distinct <h2> headings in the last 46 posts (2025-11-24 to
2026-09-08), 44 resolved nowhere on the client. An unmapped heading is not
dropped: getUSNIRegionApproxCoords falls through to a hash of the heading
text, so "Manila, Philippines" rendered at 59S 59W and "Norway" in the
Indian Ocean. "Sasebo, Japan" resolved to Yokosuka because the client took
the first containing key rather than the longest, and "Portsmouth, England"
resolved to the Maine shipyard.

- Extend both tables to every heading observed in the corpus, plus the
  straits, operating areas and ports named in #7548.
- Make both lookups identical: exact key, then the longest key contained in
  the heading, then each comma-separated segment of a "City, Country"
  heading (city before country).
- Keep genuinely unknown headings unresolved so the parser still emits its
  "Unknown region" warning and the client still logs the gap.
- Add tests/dom/usni-region-coords-parity.test.mts, which pins the two
  tables byte-identical, checks every published heading resolves the same on
  both sides, and asserts the specific-key preference. It lives in the DOM
  Vitest project because src/config/military.ts reads import.meta.env at
  module scope, which the tsx node:test runner cannot provide.

Addresses the unmapped-region half of #7548. The Open-Meteo 429 half was
already fixed by moving the climate fetch to the Railway seeder.

* fix(usni): resolve City, Country headings to the city even when the country key is longer

The comma-segment pass ran after the whole-heading longest-key search, and every segment is a substring of the heading, so it could never return a match. 'In Kure, Japan' therefore landed on Japan (Yokosuka, ~650 km away) and 'In Wellington, New Zealand' on the New Zealand centroid while the parity tests stayed green. Both lookups now take a comma-spanning key first ('Portsmouth, England'), then the first segment that names a known place, then the longest contained key. Pins Kure, Wellington, 'Near Portsmouth, England' and the Sea of Japan tie heading on both sides, corrects the 'byte-identical' parity comments (the test compares values), and restores the port provenance notes the table reorder dropped.

The rule is not that the monitor should be as tolerant as the proxy. It is
that the monitor's PASS/FAIL must not be stricter than what the proxy can
actually serve, while its REPORTING stays finer. So the boundary is copied
from api/mcp-proxy.ts rather than invented:

  307/308 to a resolvable https target   follow one hop, judge the resolved

  301/302/303                            finding — these permit a rewrite to

  second hop, http:// Location,          finding
  missing or unparseable Location

redirect: 'manual' stays, which is what keeps the hop visible: a vendor
re-plumbing behind a stable front door now reads as drift in the report
rather than as an outage or as silence.

commits.commit_title: fix(mcp): survive a vendor moving a published MCP endpoint (#8085)
commits.commit_message:
fix(mcp): survive a vendor moving a published MCP endpoint (#8085)

* fix(mcp): survive a vendor moving a published MCP endpoint

The shipped "Weather Forensics" preset died when the vendor moved
/mcp/free behind a permanent redirect. `redirect: 'manual'` turned that
308 into "Initialize failed: HTTP 308" for every caller — 53 events
across 5 users, and no automated signal: the presets suite checks a
static BANNED_URLS list, which cannot notice a live URL starting to
redirect, and the live connectivity suite is opt-in and never runs in CI.

Manual redirect handling is load-bearing, not an oversight: the Edge
runtime cannot pin a TLS connection to a vetted address, so every
dispatch re-resolves the host through assertServerUrlSafe. Letting
fetch() follow a redirect on its own would hand an upstream a way to
bounce the proxy onto an internal address without that re-check.

So postJson now follows at most ONE hop, by hand, under four bounds:

  - only 307/308, which preserve method and body — 301/302/303 permit a
    rewrite to GET, which would silently turn a tools/call into a
    bodyless GET
  - the Location must be https; assertServerUrlSafe vets the host but
    not the scheme, and validateServerUrl never sees a redirect target
  - the target clears the same SSRF guard as the original serverUrl
  - a cross-origin hop keeps only Content-Type/Accept/User-Agent

That last bound is why this is an allowlist. The upstream chooses the
redirect target, and the proxy is carrying caller credentials — the
Alpha Vantage, Datadog and Slack presets all send a Bearer token, and
Mcp-Session-Id is a credential minted by the previous origin. A denylist
of sensitive header names is the trampoline that cannot match a spelling
it has not seen.

The preset itself now points at the settled address so each call skips
the extra round trip; the hop above means that is no longer a one-way
door if the vendor moves again.

Each of the seven new tests was verified to fail against a mutant: the
three positive cases against the follow disabled, and the four refusal
cases against a permissive follow (2 hops / 302 accepted / https check
removed / revalidation skipped on the hop). Disabling the feature
satisfies the refusal tests vacuously, so that mutation alone would have
proved nothing about them.

Fixes WORLDMONITOR-128

* test(mcp-proxy): route the redirect stubs on parsed origin, not a URL prefix

CodeQL flagged the new fixtures for incomplete URL substring sanitization.
The finding is about test routing rather than a security control, but it is
fair on its own terms: startsWith('https://mcp.old.example.com') also matches
https://mcp.old.example.com.attacker.test, so the stub modelled the upstream
LESS precisely than the code it exercises, which compares url.origin.

Comparing parsed origin / host / protocol makes the fixture match the
production rule and clears the alert without a suppression.

Re-verified against the permissive mutant (2 hops / 302 accepted / https
check removed): all three refusal cases still go red, so the rewrite did not
soften them.

* fix(review): preserve redirected MCP sessions and DNS deadlines

* fix(mcp): track the vendor published endpoint, not its backend

Reverts the Weather Forensics preset to https://weatherforensics.dev/mcp/free.

The catalog records the address a vendor documents for public use, never one
found by resolving a redirect. That 308 is the vendor's own indirection layer,
and pinning past it removes exactly the capability this PR's one-hop follow was
added to absorb.

The failure modes are not symmetric, which is what decides it. A published
domain that moves again still redirects, and the proxy now survives that. A
retired backend just stops resolving: a run.app hostname is derived from
project number and region, so a project or region move breaks it with no hop
to catch it. The measured cost of not pinning is one ~0.4s round trip per 60s
poll cycle, not per RPC, because the post-redirect session URL is threaded into
follow-up calls.

All 22 catalog entries now use vendor-controlled domains again; the pin was the
only entry on cloud infrastructure.

Also adds the missing static URL assertion. This preset was the one that went
dark and the only open endpoint with no URL check in the default CI run — the
live suite is opt-in, so a silent re-point was invisible to normal CI. That is
the gap that let the original breakage ship.

commits.commit_title: fix(gateway): name the internal-MCP 401 in telemetry, not to the caller (#8086)
commits.commit_message:
fix(gateway): name the internal-MCP 401 in telemetry, not to the caller (#8086)

* fix(gateway): name the internal-MCP 401 in telemetry, not to the caller

A signed MCP tool call fails with 401 a handful of times a month. Sentry
shows it on list-global-tenders because that tool raises on a bad
response; the same failure also lands on get-country-risk and
get-bootstrap-data, where it is swallowed and returns empty. Axiom
records auth_kind=anon on all of them, so the gateway saw no identity.

Which of four things happened was unknowable. The verify block collapses
a stale timestamp, a malformed signature envelope, a missing user-id and
a failed HMAC compare into one opaque 401, and the replay branch adds a
fifth. That opacity is deliberate and correct — a caller who can tell
those apart has a forgery oracle — but it also meant nobody could
reproduce the failure, so there was no honest fix to make yet.

So this changes only what the server records. verifyInternalMcpRequest
grows a Detailed variant returning which check failed; the original
keeps its null-on-failure contract and every existing caller. The
gateway maps that onto RequestReason members split out of auth_401, the
way replay_cache_unavailable and hmac_secret_unconfigured already were.

The caller-facing half is unchanged and now harder to break: every
rejection returns one Response built in one function, so a future branch
cannot quietly introduce a distinguishable reply. A test asserts all
five modes match on status, body, content-type and header set, and it
was verified to fail against a variant that adds a single header to the
replay path — the tempting shape of exactly this bug. The reason tests
were separately verified against a variant that collapses every reason
back to auth_401.

No behavior changed: the timestamp window, the replay TTL, and every
auth decision are untouched. This buys the evidence to fix the real
cause, which is still unknown.

Refs WORLDMONITOR-XZ

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_012nVNfJrGEQwfhB3keoy73H

* test(gateway): follow the internal-MCP reason split in the config-telemetry pair

This case exists to contrast with the one above it: secret missing is a
deploy incident (hmac_secret_unconfigured, 500), secret present with a
bad signature is the caller's failure (401). Splitting the internal-MCP
rejections by failing check changed the literal, not that distinction.

Asserts both halves now — that the reason is the specific failing check,
and that it is still not the config reason — so the contrast the pair is
built around cannot quietly erode.

commits.commit_title: fix(mcp): group internal-MCP 401s as one issue instead of one per route (#8090)
commits.commit_message:
fix(mcp): group internal-MCP 401s as one issue instead of one per route (#8090)

* fix(mcp): group internal-MCP 401s as one issue instead of one per route

The intermittent signed-MCP 401 has been open since at least July and has
never been root-caused. Chasing it turned up why: it cannot accumulate.

mcpErrorFingerprint keys on [step, toolName, endpoint:status]. That split
exists for good reason — it broke up the T8 catch-all so a 5xx spike in
one tool could not hide behind auth drift in another. But a 401 on this
hop is not a property of the tool. The edge signs an HMAC of the outbound
request and the gateway verifies it; a rejection belongs to that shared
mechanism, whichever tool happened to be calling.

So each affected route opened its own issue, each holding a handful of
events, each small enough to read as noise:

  WORLDMONITOR-XZ  list-global-tenders          4 events  open
  WORLDMONITOR-WZ  summarize-article            8 events  resolved
  WORLDMONITOR-WN  get-country-intel-brief      1 event   resolved
  WORLDMONITOR-VK  deduct-situation             3 events  resolved

Three were closed. Gateway telemetry shows 401s on two further routes
(get-country-risk, get-bootstrap-data) with no Sentry issue at all. One
bug, six routes, ~0.2% of signed calls, presenting as a trickle of
unrelated trivia — so it kept getting resolved instead of investigated.

A 401 now fingerprints on the failure mode alone. Every other status
keeps the per-tool split, and 403 explicitly stays on that path: it is a
real per-endpoint entitlement answer, not the shared hop.

This opens a fresh group rather than merging the old ones — a changed
fingerprint always does. The gain is forward-looking: the next occurrence
lands somewhere that accumulates.

Verified each new assertion against a mutant with the carve-out disabled;
all five coalescing tests go red. The pre-existing "different tools stay
separate" case moved off 401 to 502 so it still tests what it was written
to test.

* fix(forecasts): cap shared forecast-id similarity at eight ids

forecastIds now carries complete membership, so the 0.5-per-shared-id
term in computeSituationSimilarity was unbounded (a 31-member state could
score 15.5 from ids alone). Continuity matching in state-unit, situation,
and report continuity picks the highest-scoring prior cluster above 4,
so large clusters would win on size over region and actor evidence.

meets the threshold, as it could before, but never outweighs a shared
region plus actor (5). Prior world states saved with 12- or 16-id samples
reach the same cap, so the first run after deploy scores like later runs.

commits.commit_title: fix(umami): fit the storage growth trend and keep its history out of the evicted cache (#8097)
commits.commit_message:
fix(umami): fit the storage growth trend and keep its history out of the evicted cache (#8097)

* fix(umami): fit the storage growth trend and keep its history out of the evicted cache

The Umami Storage Monitor failed critical on 2026-09-13 with "1.530 GiB/day,
projected headroom 8.1 days". Two defects produced that number.

Railway refreshes the volume's currentSizeMB only every ~6 hours, and the
monitor sloped the current reading against the newest sample at least 24
hours old. One +1,078 MB refresh at 06:47 UTC therefore set the whole rate.
Growth is now a least-squares fit over a 3-day window, projected once the
samples span 2 days. On the observed refresh staircase that reads ~740
MB/day and 17 days of headroom: still a warning, no longer critical.

The sample history lived in the Actions cache, which sits at its 10 GB
repository limit. GitHub evicted every copy on 2026-09-12 ("Cache not found
for input keys"), so the trend restarted from a single sample. The history
now travels as the umami-storage-state artifact, restored from the newest of
this workflow's recent runs on the same branch.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XvdUXHJMPbq3btQnX8W2uq

* fix(umami): make the storage history artifact rerun-safe and encode the branch filter

Review of #8097:

- A re-run keeps github.run_id, and upload-artifact v6 rejects a second
  artifact with the same name in one run. The save step now sets
  overwrite: true, so a re-run replaces the first attempt's history instead
  of failing and dropping its sample.
- The restore step interpolated BRANCH into the runs endpoint URL. A branch
  name containing `&` would add its own query parameter and could restore
  another branch's history. The branch is now a gh api GET field, which gh
  encodes: `main&per_page=1` matches zero runs instead of main's.

commits.commit_title: fix(checkout): retry Cloudflare origin transients and stop dropping checkout timeouts (#8069)
commits.commit_message:
fix(checkout): retry Cloudflare origin transients and stop dropping checkout timeouts (#8069)

* fix(checkout): retry the Cloudflare origin-reachability 5xx family (WORLDMONITOR-Q4)

The 2026-09-12 Q4 event was a bare 520 on POST /api/create-checkout. The
retry shipped in #5374 covers 502/503/504 only, so Cloudflare's own spelling
of the same transient-origin condition was handed straight back to the user
with no second attempt.

Widen RETRYABLE_CHECKOUT_STATUSES to 520-525 (origin unreachable, handshake
failed, or timed out). 526 (invalid origin certificate) and 530 (wrapped
origin DNS/Worker error) stay out: neither clears in 1.5s, so retrying them
only delays the failure copy.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0186VfYQfATeancuREBhRvU4

* fix(sentry): stop dropping checkout timeouts as zero-frame noise (WORLDMONITOR-Q4)

The checkout transport times out at 15s and reportCheckoutError captures the
rejection, but the event never reached Sentry. `AbortSignal.timeout` mints its
DOMException at the timer boundary, so the stack is the header line alone
(verified in Chromium 141: `stack === 'TimeoutError: signal timed out'`) and
the parser extracts zero frames. The zero-frame gate then dropped it as
extension noise, because the only exemption was the panel dispatch tag added
in #7552. A terminal, revenue-losing failure was invisible, and the Q4 event
count understated the real rate.

Key the exemption on `kind` PRESENCE rather than on a list of kind names.
`kind` is set only by first-party capture call sites (pending-panel-data.ts,
wm-session.ts, checkout.ts) and can never be set by the SDK, an extension, or
an injected script, so the tag is an enforced invariant instead of a name
treadmill. Tag every checkout report with it.

Both halves are locked: tests/sentry-beforesend.test.mjs proves the gate lets
a kind-tagged zero-frame timeout through while the untagged counter-fixture
stays suppressed, and tests/checkout-report-error.test.mts proves the emit
side still sets the tag and the gate still keys on presence.

Also corrects the rationale in pro-test/src/sentry-filter-policy.ts, which
claimed the dashboard mints its timeout DOMException in first-party code with
caller frames. That is true only of the pre-Baseline-2024 fallback path, and
believing it is what let this hide.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0186VfYQfATeancuREBhRvU4

* fix(checkout): classify the idempotency conflict and tighten the Q4 proofs

Review of the previous two commits turned up one defect the change itself
introduced, plus three weak proofs.

The defect: the retry replays with the SAME Idempotency-Key, so when it races
a still-running first attempt the edge answers 409 `idempotency_conflict`
(api/_idempotency.js). `statusToCode` had no branch for that envelope, so it
fell through the generic 4xx arm to `invalid_product` — telling the buyer
"That product isn't available" AND switching the retry affordance off. That
turned a recoverable race into a terminal dead end, and widening the retry set
made the race likelier, because 520 and 524 are emitted precisely when the
origin DID receive the request. Now classified `service_unavailable`.

Proofs, after an independent pass showed each could pass while broken:
- The emit-side lock only proved the tag block exists in the file. Deleting
  the second argument of `captureException(caught, payload)` left it green
  while production lost the exemption. Now both capture calls are pinned.
- The gate-side lock was a regex over sentry-init.ts source. Six behaviour-
  preserving spellings of the same condition all reddened it; a false red on a
  correct refactor is what teaches the next author to delete the assertion.
  Replaced with behavioural fixtures over six `kind` values, one of which
  (`kind_presence_probe`) belongs to no call site — a gate narrowed back to a
  name list fails there and only there.
- Every fixture assigned `event.tags` by hand, assuming the SDK applies capture
  payload tags before beforeSend. Now driven end to end through the real
  public API against a stub transport, with the untagged counter-fixture
  asserting suppression. Verified in @sentry/browser 10.46.0, and the
  assumption is now a test rather than a belief.

Also: 524 leaves the retry set. Cloudflare emits it at its 100s origin
deadline and CHECKOUT_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS aborts this client ~85s earlier, so
it can never reach the browser here. The `kind` census in the gate comment was
wrong at three sites; there are six, and the old gate was silently dropping
csp_violation, variant_theme_load_failed and wm_session_dead the same way it
dropped checkout. The transport header no longer states the edge dedupe as
unconditional: every Upstash failure arm disables it. The pro-test filter
policy no longer cites checkout.ts as a live timeout reporter, because that
catch logs to console and returns without capturing.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0186VfYQfATeancuREBhRvU4

* fix(sentry): exempt owned reports on every zero-frame branch, not just timeouts

A second review round found the previous fix was half-done in two directions.

Safari was never fixed. WebKit words an AbortSignal.timeout rejection
`AbortError: Fetch is aborted` (WORLDMONITOR-10F, documented in
services/timeout-signal.ts), and that phrase sat in `ignoreErrors`. The SDK
applies ignoreErrors as an event processor inside prepareEvent, so it runs
BEFORE beforeSend and is blind to both frames and tags — no `kind` tag could
ever rescue it. The previous commit restored checkout visibility on Chromium
only. The pattern moves into the zero-frame block, where it keeps the identical
suppression for unowned events and can now be claimed by a first-party report.

The exemption also guarded one operand of a twelve-way OR instead of the chain.
The same transport's double-network-failure path arrives as a zero-frame
`Failed to fetch`, which stayed suppressed even when checkout had reported it —
the same terminal, revenue-losing class the fix exists to surface. The guard is
hoisted. Every current `kind` setter is a first-party capture, so this
un-suppresses owned failures and nothing else; the untagged counter-fixtures
assert the suppression still holds on each branch.

Proof work from the same round:
- The kind tag moves into a `buildCheckoutReportTags` helper in the pure policy
  module. The old source regex matched the literal anywhere in checkout.ts,
  including inside `extra`, so relocating the key one field over would leave
  every test green while beforeSend — which reads only `tags.kind` — went
  blind. Tests now assert the real returned object, and the beforeSend suite
  builds its fixture from the shipped helper instead of a hand copy.
- The widened gate rests on nothing setting `kind` on a global scope. A source
  scan now pins that, with a population check so a silently broken scan cannot
  pass as a clean one.

Extracting the helper broke two esbuild-stubbed suites that had their own
copy of the policy module. Caught only by running every suite that reads these
files together; the per-file runs stayed green.

* fix(pro): report the checkout failures this surface inherited but never surfaced

The retry widening reached /pro, the reporting did not. pro-test shares
checkout-transport.ts byte-for-byte with the dashboard, enforced by
tests/marketing-mirror-parity.test.mts, so the marketing bundle already
replays the same Idempotency-Key and races its own first attempt. It just had
nowhere to put the result: the error chain names 429 and the two 409 envelopes
and falls off the end into a bare `return false`, and the outer catch logged to
the console. A 409 idempotency_conflict, a 52x that survived the retry, and
every transport timeout all produced the same thing on the pricing page — the
interstitial unmounts, no toast, no event. Three reviewers reached that
independently, and it means the previous commits raised the rate of a silent
failure on the surface where the paid funnel starts.

Both paths now capture, tagged `kind: 'checkout_request_failed'` so a
zero-frame rejection is claimed as a first-party report wherever it is
filtered. User-facing copy on that arm is still missing and is not addressed
here.

Two harness gaps from the same round:

The zero-frame guard tested truthiness, so `kind: ''` read as absent and was
suppressed — confirmed by replaying the previous gate against that event. No
call site can emit an empty kind today, but `kind: someVar` is one refactor
away and the failure would be silent. It now tests presence.

The ignoreErrors mirror in tests checked only the bare message value, while
production also matches `${type}: ${value}` and drops on either. An entry
anchored as `TimeoutError:` would therefore drop a first-party failure in
production with the suite green — the same layer that hid the Safari case
until this round.

* docs(solutions): a suppression layer above beforeSend cannot see your ownership tag

Captures the WORLDMONITOR-Q4 learning while the evidence is fresh.

The reusable part is not the checkout fix but the layering: ignoreErrors is
installed as an SDK event processor and runs inside prepareEvent, so it fires
before beforeSend and is blind to tags and frames alike. Any message listed
there is unrescuable, which is why the first fix restored Chromium only and
left WebKit silent.

Also records the three things that made the proofs real: the Chromium probe
establishing that AbortSignal.timeout yields a header-only stack, replaying
each new fixture against the previous gate to show it was not vacuous (which
surfaced three other first-party report classes the gate had been eating), and
why an emit-side source regex cannot tell tags from extra.

Adds an Ownership Tag entry to CONCEPTS.md next to Trampoline Frame, its
coherence neighbour: both are about a suppression gate needing an enforced
invariant rather than a maintained census of names.

* docs(solutions): keep the template-literal example out of MDX's way

tests/mdx-lint.test.mjs rejects a bare curly expression outside code, because
Mintlify parses it as JSX. A double-backtick inline span is not recognised as
code by that linter, so the template literal I used to show Sentry's two
candidate message spellings read as a bare expression and reddened
unit-shard (2).

Moved the example into a fenced block, which the linter does recognise.

The gate lives in the data test suite, not in `npm run docs:check` or
markdownlint, so a docs-only change passes both of those and still fails CI.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0186VfYQfATeancuREBhRvU4

* fix(sentry): move network-worded suppression late enough to read the ownership tag

The ownership tag only works if every layer that can drop the event runs after
the gate reading it. Two layers did not.

On the marketing surface, MARKETING_IGNORE_ERRORS held Safari's `Load failed`,
Chromium's `Failed to fetch` and Firefox's `NetworkError`. The checkout capture
added in the previous commit produces exactly those wordings, so it was inert
for every network failure — the most common way that path fails — while the
timeout case it was written for worked. The retry widening shipped to this same
bundle made those wordings more reachable, so the net effect was to raise the
rate of an unreported failure on the page where the paid funnel starts.

On the dashboard, `Load failed` was still in ignoreErrors, so the zero-frame
exemption was fixing WebKit in name only.

A probe against the pre-fix lists bounds it:

  Load failed (both forms)  dashboard: dropped   marketing: dropped
  Failed to fetch           dashboard: reached   marketing: dropped
  NetworkError ...          dashboard: reached   marketing: dropped

Both relocations keep their reach exactly — same wordings, same TypeError
constraint, no frame gate — so ordinary noise volume is unchanged and the only
verdict that flips is an event a first-party call site claimed. The type check
is load-bearing for that: ignoreErrors matched both the bare value and the
`"<type>: <value>"` spelling, so testing the message alone would have quietly
started suppressing a non-TypeError carrying the same words.

The end-to-end fixtures now install the real ignoreErrors array via
eventFiltersIntegration. Building that client with `integrations: []` proved
delivery through half the stack and would have reported green through exactly
this bug.

KTD5 pinned the Safari blind spot and said it existed so whoever narrowed the
entry would see what changed. It now pins the new contract instead: unowned
events dropped as before, including with a first-party frame, and one verdict
changed.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0186VfYQfATeancuREBhRvU4

* fix(checkout): honour the wait the idempotency conflict already tells us

CodeRabbit review on #8069.

The edge sends `Retry-After: 2` with the 409 conflict because it knows how long
the first attempt may still hold the processing marker, and checkout.ts already
forwards the header to the classifier. It was then dropped: retryAfterSeconds
was populated only for `rate_limited`, so the caller had nothing to set a
cooldown from and an immediate re-click went straight back into the same lock.
The Cloudflare 52x widening is what makes that race reachable, since those
statuses mean the origin did receive the request.

Three sites now key on the server-specified wait rather than on one code: the
classifier populates it for the conflict, the caller sets its cooldown from it,
and the error surface keeps the buyer where they are instead of redirecting to
/pro while their own checkout session is still being created.

Declined the suggested mechanism. The review asked for the response to be
classified `rate_limited` while retaining service-unavailable messaging, and
those cannot both hold — copy is derived from the code, so reusing
`rate_limited` would tell a buyer they are rate limited when they are not. That
is the same false-message defect as the `invalid_product` branch this
classifier already had to fix. Keying copy on the code and the wait on the
header satisfies every requirement in the comment without it.

Honouring the wait then exposed a second-order version of the same bug, one
click later. The pre-flight gate explains an active cooldown by synthesizing an
error, and it synthesized a 429 unconditionally — correct while only a 429
could set the cooldown, but it would have greeted a conflict-blocked click with
"rate limited" anyway. The cooldown now records its cause and the gate replays
the matching error. The first draft of the test missed this because it read the
toast only after the initial call; it now reads it after the blocked click too.

Not changed: the conflict still reports at error level. Demoting it needs its
own CheckoutErrorCode, and the race is rare enough that the extra code is not
yet worth it.

fix(economic): isolate World Bank query cache identities (#8050)

## Problem and change
Omitted-country World Bank requests fetched the curated country list but
shared a Redis key with explicit `country_code=all`. Either request
could populate the other's response for 24 hours.

Use a `v2` cache namespace and a distinct `__default__` sentinel.
Canonicalize known ISO2/ISO3 aliases while preserving all two-letter
country filters, bound raw country input and indicator syntax, cap
lookback at the existing relay's 30-year ceiling, and encode both
outbound path components. Include the effective lookback and calendar
year in the cache key.

Preserve generic indicator codes (the tech display catalogue is not an
exhaustive allowlist), explicit `all`, curated defaults, the five-year
default, response shape, first-party session access and existing 30/min
fail-closed policy. No gateway, proto, generated code, relay, seeder or
unrelated World Bank changes.

## Verification
- Before: 21 failed / 19 passed; reproduced both directions of
default/all cache contamination and invalid-input I/O.
- After: 50 focused tests pass with real handler/shared cache and
synthetic Redis/provider transport, including a
generated-route/gateway/session test.
- 83 existing rate-limit, query-contract and Tech Readiness tests pass.
- API typecheck, rate-policy audit and diff check pass.
- Full sequential exact-head review at
`0147e2ece8058acbff3f5671535042fc71ff8dc1`: no actionable findings.
External cross-model review excluded by the existing automatic-approval
restriction on unpublished security-diff transfer.
- No live Redis/World Bank acceptance probe. Generic valid indicators
and country combinations remain numerous; this change does not add a
global cache quota.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation
Owner: deploying operator. During the first 24 hours after an authorized
release, inspect `economic:worldbank:v2` cache/upstream telemetry and
`/api/economic/v1/list-world-bank-indicators` error rates. Verify
omitted-country and explicit `all` responses have their correct scope on
cold and warm reads. Normal supported requests should retain 200
responses, with independent default/all cache entries. Investigate
unexpected empty responses or provider 4xx increases; revert this commit
if supported callers regress. No cache purge or migration is required;
old keys expire naturally.

fix(aviation): bound and rate-limit aircraft identifier lookups (#8047)

## Summary

Aircraft identifier searches now reject malformed or oversized input
before cache and provider work. Equivalent ICAO and callsign inputs
share normalized cache keys, and callsign substring searches remain
supported. Identifier lookups have a fail-closed 30/minute budget;
bbox-only map requests retain their existing gateway limit and provider
behavior.

Cloud and Docker requests use the shared trusted-IP limiter, including
requests admitted by internal MCP authentication. Missing or failed
limiter storage returns 503 with a degraded marker and retry delay;
exhausted quota returns 429 with the scoped policy, remaining count and
retry delay. The authenticated native sidecar uses a bounded
process-local window. These are admission limits, not a global provider
spending cap.

Related: DeepSec finding 10.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Affected areas

- [x] API endpoints (`/api/*`)
- [x] Desktop app (Tauri)

## Validation

- 88 focused tests passed: input rejection before I/O, canonical cache
reuse, actual configured limiter budget and client IP, distinct-key
exhaustion, Redis outage, verified MCP admission, bbox global budget,
authoritative empty results and provider recovery.
- 96 existing Redis caching tests passed, including all aircraft
provider-priority and deadline tests.
- API TypeScript check and Convex call audit passed.
- Native proof uses the actual localhost HTTP server, transport token
authentication and generated gateway. It verifies useful OpenSky data,
one cached provider request, 30 allowed requests, denial and recovery at
the window boundary.
- Full ce-code-review completed sequentially on the committed diff with
no actionable findings. The optional cross-model CLI returned no usable
output.

External providers and Redis were mocked. No live provider billing,
deployed behavior, or production acceptance is claimed. After a
separately authorized deployment, verify valid searches and rejection
responses, monitor limiter degradation, and confirm bbox/map
availability. Rate-limit documentation now records the identifier scope
and error headers; no UI or generated files changed.

## Checklist

- [x] No API keys or secrets committed
- [x] TypeScript API compiles without errors
- [ ] Live dashboard variant verification (not performed; backend
fixture proof above)

Documentation claims were checked against the handler and HTTP fixtures.
No screenshots are needed because no UI changed.

## Summary
Normalize webcam viewport inputs before reading or writing the response
cache and before GEOSEARCH. Malformed and non-finite values now return
the existing structured 400 response without Redis access. Finite zoom
maps to integer 0–22 while preserving the current clustering thresholds;
coordinates clamp to globe bounds before the existing quantization.

The supported global map establishes the maximum box: 360 degrees
longitude by 180 degrees latitude. Normal integer cache identities,
quantized superset queries, antimeridian splits, seeded camera
keys/metadata, the 2,000-result query cap and one-hour response TTL stay
unchanged. No image proxy, gateway, shared Redis helper, entitlement,
rate-policy, proto or generated-client changes.

transport tests. Before the fix, 22 of the first 24 witnesses failed;
the two normal-query characterizations passed.

aliases, extreme coordinate combinations, full-globe cache equivalence,

around all clustering thresholds.

verify ordinary regional/global/antimeridian requests, clustering and
cache reuse, then check that invalid numeric inputs return 400 before
Redis access. Monitor unexpected webcam 400/5xx responses and Redis
GEOSEARCH errors. Roll back the scoped change if valid map behavior
regresses. No deployment or production acceptance is claimed.

commits.commit_message:
fix(aviation): keep bootstrap publication out of delay requests (#8027)

## Summary
Airport-delay requests no longer publish `aviation:delays-bootstrap:v2`.
The handler previously replaced the shared producer snapshot after every
request, including when source reads missed, returned errors or timed
out. Those responses could contain UNKNOWN rows and missing
international coverage, and the write refreshed the shared TTL without
updating seed metadata.

The seeder remains responsible for bootstrap publication and its
metadata. The RPC keeps its existing alert response and coverage
behavior. Removed the coverage variable used only by the deleted write.

Related: DeepSec finding 5. Finding 6 (international raw-key mismatch)
remains separate and unchanged. No shared rate, gateway or bootstrap
registry changes.

## Validation
- Synthetic producer payload passed through the real handler and public
bootstrap reader reproduces the overwrite before the fix.
- Healthy reads, cache misses, HTTP 503 and actual 1.5-second read
timeouts now preserve the shared payload, TTL and metadata while
returning the expected RPC statuses.
- 67 focused aviation, bootstrap and China-coverage regressions passed;
API typecheck and diff check passed.
- Sequential ce-code-review completed with no actionable findings. Mock
command/origin assertions remain observable even when the handler
catches errors.
- No production provider calls or load tests. The overwrite is
confirmed; inducing Redis degradation through request volume was not
demonstrated. The scheduled publisher and full CII score computation
were source-traced, not executed.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation
Owner: repository operator. After authorized API deployment, observe one
natural aviation seed cycle and verify bootstrap and seed-meta freshness
advance together. Confirm that ordinary delay RPC traffic no longer
refreshes the aggregate key, and that map hydration and China-corridor
coverage retain the producer data. Monitor UNKNOWN response rates
separately from shared snapshot freshness. If freshness stops advancing,
inspect the scheduled publisher rather than restoring request-driven
writes. No deployment or live acceptance was performed here.

fix(shipping): bound pinned webhook response resources (#8020)

A callback could keep the pinned Shipping v2 delivery request open by
trickling response bytes, or grow memory through an unbounded response
body. The native HTTPS path now discards unused body chunks, rejects
responses over 1 MiB, and applies a 10-second hard request deadline in
addition to the socket inactivity timer. Failures destroy the request
and response; completion clears the deadline.

The public status result is unchanged. Removing unused `Response`
construction also handles normal 204/304 responses. DNS pinning and Node
TLS defaults remain intact. A native Node 24.20 local HTTPS probe
returned 302 after exactly one request, disproving automatic redirect
following; no redundant redirect policy was added.

Validation: both size/time regressions failed before the fix. All 58
focused delivery, handler, SSRF, and OpenAPI tests passed, as did API
typecheck. Tests cover active dribbles, missing headers, aborts, exact
size limit, deadline cleanup, and IPv4/IPv6/mapped pins. Sequential
review covered `4ed3768c81021d3c3c2dd0b07ba5456de941282f`.

fix(aviation): bound cached fare search inputs and request quota (#8017)

## Summary

Fare searches now reject malformed airport codes, dates, cabin classes,
currencies and markets before constructing Travelpayouts cache keys or
making provider requests. Invalid live search inputs return HTTP400
instead of being treated as upstream failures. Equivalent valid input
uses normalized cache keys; existing defaults and day/month/latest
search behavior remain supported.

The route also gets a fail-closed 30/min endpoint policy. The command
bar issues one request per user search; this budget permits interactive
changes while leaving headroom below the provider's shared 300-600/min
quotas. Existing gateway attribution stays intact: verified paid users
use principal buckets, enterprise keys retain IP/account controls, and
verified internalMCP retains its upstream quota enforcement. This is not
a global provider-token budget. Per-search billing was not verified and
is not claimed as the impact.

## Validation

- 18 of 20 initial boundary checks failed before the repair. The final
21 boundary checks and existing focused suites total 104 passing tests.
- Real generated RPC/gateway/auth/handler/cache behavior with mocked
external transports verifies anonymous denial, validated-key access,
malformed input 400, missing rate storage 503, and request 31 returning
429 without another provider call.
- Equivalent input/defaults reuse cache; real day/month date validation
rejects rollover dates. Previous cache-key variation and
degraded-response suites pass.
- 109 gateway tests and415 server tests pass. API typecheck, rate-policy
guard and EdgeVM currency-enumeration smoke pass.
- Sequential same-agent code review found no actionable issue; no
independent corroboration claimed. Redis quota replies are mocked, not
real Lua execution. No production or paid-provider probes.

Provider contract references: [cached data
API](https://support.travelpayouts.com/hc/en-us/articles/203956163-Aviasales-Data-API),
[request
quotas](https://support.travelpayouts.com/hc/en-us/articles/4402565416594-API-rate-limits).

## Integration

Independent addition to `server/_shared/rate-limit.ts` overlaps the file
changed by unmerged PR8009. This branch starts from main and does not
include its crypto policy or generic test-fixture changes. Refresh main
and recheck both policies after integration.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

Owner: deploying maintainer, first 24 hours after an authorized
deployment. Monitor fare-search 400/429/503 rates, cache hit rate, and
Travelpayouts 429/error volume. Valid command-bar searches must retain
indicative results or their existing explicit degraded state. In a
synthetic environment, malformed inputs must create no
fare-cache/provider work and an unavailable limiter must return 503
before provider access. Unexpected rejection of documented valid inputs
or sustained quota failures blocks acceptance; correct the focused
validation/policy issue without lifting all rate control. No deployment
is part of this PR delivery.

work.

cached repeat requests, API typecheck and the rate-policy guard passed.

fix(mnd): preserve proxy failure phase and status (#8067)

## Summary

MND request diagnostics now distinguish a proxy connection, CONNECT
reply, target TLS handshake, response headers, and response body
failure. Previously, the buffered proxy helper could receive HTTP 200
and then lose the status when the body reset. The adapter logged
`response_headers` with `httpStatus: null`.

The helper adds non-enumerable phase/status metadata to the same error
object. The adapter copies only allowlisted phases and numeric statuses,
with CONNECT status separate from target HTTP status. Unknown errors
remain `unknown`; immutable errors and primitive abort reasons keep
their original identity. Raw errors, credentials, proxy URLs, headers,
and response bodies are not added to diagnostics. Error codes, transport
selection, retry counts, deadlines, and source success clocks are
unchanged.

## Validation

- Seven new diagnostic assertions failed before the repair while the
prior 178 checks passed. After repair, 185 focused checks pass across
the MND adapter, real proxy helper, and source fallback suites.
- Another 295 affected-caller checks pass, including FRED, sanctions,
PortWatch, weather, Open-Meteo, China macro, electricity, valuations,
FATF, GDELT unrest, and OpenSky proxy contracts.
- Covers HTTP 200 followed by body reset, observed
connection/CONNECT/TLS phases, target header failure, unknown or hostile
metadata, CONNECT/origin status separation, secret exclusion, and
unchanged rejection identity/code.
- Biome and all repository pre-push gates pass. Sequential
ce-simplify-code and ce-code-review found no actionable findings; no
external review automation was invoked.

All behavior evidence above uses controlled local fixtures. This is a
diagnostic correction, not proof of live transport recovery.

## Post-deployment verification

Deployment requires separate authorization. After deployment, inspect a
naturally occurring MND failure for an observed phase and separate
CONNECT/target statuses. An HTTP-200 body failure should retain
`response_body` and `200`; unknown errors must remain unknown. Verify
request limits and source success clocks remain unchanged. Do not run a
seeder or generate paid probes for this verification.
