docs(references): fix dead heading anchors in the reference docs (#20418)

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

Four in-page links under `docs/references/` point at heading anchors
that no longer match their headings, so they resolve to nothing:

- `docs/references/lan-transfer/README.md:21` — the TOC entry for
section 4 links to `#4-message-format-specification`, but the heading is
`## 4. Message Format Specification (Mixed Protocol)`, whose GitHub
anchor is `#4-message-format-specification-mixed-protocol`.
- `docs/references/lan-transfer/README.md:27` — the TOC entry for
section 10 links to `#10-mobile-implementation-guide`, but the heading
is `## 10. Mobile Implementation Guide (v1)`, anchor
`#10-mobile-implementation-guide-v1`.
- `docs/references/window-manager/window-manager-api-reference.md:147`
and `:152` — two links to
`./window-manager-platform.md#platform-quirks`, but that heading is now
`## OS Quirks`, anchor `#os-quirks`.

Nothing catches this today: `scripts/check-doc-links.ts:65` strips the
fragment (`rawLink.split('#')[0]`) and only asserts that the target file
exists, and `:61` skips anchor-only links entirely.

After this PR:

All four links resolve. The two `lan-transfer` TOC entries now carry the
same parenthetical qualifiers as their headings, matching the convention
already used by entry 2 of that same TOC (`2. [Service Discovery
(Bonjour/mDNS)](#2-service-discovery-bonjourmdns)`). The two
`window-manager` links now read `[OS
Quirks](.../window-manager-platform.md#os-quirks)`.

A repo-wide scan of every `](...#fragment)` link across all 415 tracked
markdown files now reports zero unresolved anchors inside `docs/`.

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

`docs/references/` is the developer-facing entry point for the LAN
transfer protocol and for the window manager. A dead anchor is invisible
in CI but user-visible: clicking a table-of-contents entry does nothing,
and anyone following a cross-reference lands at the top of the wrong
page.

The window-manager drift is confirmed by history rather than guessed:
commit `62d39d41f7` (`refactor(window-manager): split metadata into
windowOptions/behavior/quirks`, 2026-04-19) renamed `## Platform Quirks`
to `## OS Quirks` in `window-manager-platform.md` **and modified
`window-manager-api-reference.md` in the same commit** — yet the two
inbound anchors were left behind, so those links have been broken since
that day. The `lan-transfer` drift is older still: the TOC already
omitted the qualifiers before the file was moved to
`docs/references/lan-transfer/README.md` in #18848.

The following tradeoffs were made:

Fixing the links instead of renaming the headings back. The headings are
the source of truth, and the stale side is unambiguously the link — no
content depends on the old anchor names.

The following alternatives were considered:

Adding an anchor check to `check-doc-links.ts`. Deliberately not done
here, to keep this PR documentation-only and because a naive anchor
check can false-positive on headings whose slugs are generated outside
this repo. Happy to open that separately if the maintainers want it.

Links to places where the discussion took place: N/A

### Breaking changes

None — documentation only.

### Special notes for your reviewer

**Scope, and what was deliberately left out.** The same scan turns up
three more dead anchors that this PR does not touch, to keep the change
inside `docs/`:

- `CLAUDE.md:168` and `CONTRIBUTING.md:67` — both files are currently
modified by open PRs, so editing them would create avoidable overlap.
- `src/shared/data/presets/README.md:14` — lives under `src/`, so it is
kept out to leave this PR in the docs lane.

Happy to send any of these as a follow-up once the in-flight PRs land.

**Why the other doc gates are unaffected.** Both files are inside the
`docs/` scan set, so here is the per-gate reasoning:

- `docs:check-links` — the edited links still point at files that exist;
only the fragments changed, and fragments are stripped before the
existence check.
- `docs:check-frontmatter` / `docs:check-structure` — no frontmatter key
and no reference domain was changed.
- `docs:check-index` — only validates the generated `docs/README.md`;
the two pages edited here are hand-written and not part of that
generated index.
- `oxfmt` does not format markdown (`.oxfmtrc.json` → `ignorePatterns`
includes `**/*.md`).

No line endings were touched either — `git diff` shows exactly four
changed lines, with no file rewritten end to end.

commits.commit_message:
docs(migrations): correct the stale package manager in the migrations README (#20410)

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

`migrations/README.md` told contributors to generate migrations with a
yarn command:

> - To generate migrations, use the command `yarn run
db:migrations:generate`

That command belongs to the toolchain this repository no longer uses.
The move from yarn to pnpm
landed in #12260 (`refactor/switch-yarn-to-pnpm`, merged 2026-01-05, 58
files) — it rewrote the
install and run instructions in `CLAUDE.md`,
`docs/en/guides/development.md`,
`docs/zh/guides/development.md` and the package READMEs, but it never
touched `migrations/README.md`.
The file has been pointing at yarn ever since.

Anyone who follows it today is told to use a package manager this repo
has not declared for eight
months. The current state of the repository says pnpm on every axis:

- `package.json` declares `"packageManager": "pnpm@11.8.0+sha512.…"`,
and `engines` pins Node.
- The only lockfiles and workspace/config files present are
`pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`
  and `.npmrc`. There is no `yarn.lock`.
- A repo-wide search finds no `yarn` invocation in
`.github/workflows/**` or `scripts/**`.

After this PR:

The bullet reads the command that actually works:

> - To generate migrations, use the command `pnpm
db:migrations:generate`

`db:migrations:generate` is a real root script (`package.json`), and
`pnpm <script>` is the form the
rest of this repo's Markdown already uses — the string `pnpm run `
appears in zero Markdown files
here, so the fix follows the existing convention rather than introducing
a new one.

The rest of the file is byte-for-byte unchanged. Net `+1 / -1`.

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The migrations README is the entry point for anyone adding a schema
change, and it is the one file in
`migrations/` a contributor is expected to read. Sending them to a
package manager that the repo does
not declare is a documentation defect with a one-token fix, so the
change is deliberately narrowed to
that token.

This is the leftover of a completed migration rather than a deliberate
choice: #12260 swept 58 files
including every other developer-facing command reference, and
`migrations/README.md` simply was not in
its list. The same file's sibling facts (the driver, the ORM,
`migrations/sqlite-drizzle` as generated
output) were re-verified while preparing this PR and are all still
accurate, so nothing else needed to
change.

The following tradeoffs were made:

Replacing the whole command text (`yarn run db:migrations:generate` →
`pnpm db:migrations:generate`)
rather than only the executable (`yarn` → `pnpm`, keeping `run`).
Keeping `run` would work, but it
would be the only `pnpm run …` in the repository's Markdown; matching
the surrounding convention keeps
the corpus internally consistent, which is the point of the fix.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Rewriting the bullet into a longer "how to regenerate the schema"
paragraph. Rejected: that is a
  content change, not a correction, and it would balloon a one-line fix.
- Leaving the file alone because yarn still exists as a tool. Rejected:
the README's job is to state
how *this* repository is operated; `package.json` pins pnpm via
`packageManager`, so yarn is not an
  equivalent path here.

Links to places where the discussion took place:

- https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/pull/12260 —
`refactor/switch-yarn-to-pnpm` (merged
  2026-01-05), the migration that missed this file

### Breaking changes

None. Documentation only: no code, dependency, API, or user-visible
behavior change.

### Special notes for your reviewer

- Scope: 1 file, `+1 / -1`, one bullet. No new dependencies, no
refactor.
- The two other Markdown occurrences of yarn were deliberately left
alone, because both live in
`src/renderer/routes/`, which open PR #19104 (`feat(navigation): add
configurable sidebar and tab
  layouts`) is actively editing: `src/renderer/routes/README.md:24` and
`src/renderer/routes/README.zh-CN.md:24` ("After running `yarn dev`").
Both are the same class of
leftover and are one-word fixes — I would rather land this file cleanly
than create overlap on a
directory another PR owns. Happy to send them as a follow-up once #19104
is in, or to fold them in
  here if you prefer; say the word.
- Every other `yarn` hit in the repo was checked and is correct as
written: `.gitignore` /
`.gitattributes` / `oxfmt` / `oxlint` / `eslint` ignore patterns and
`.vscode` settings, the yarn
command *detectors* in `src/main/ai/toolApproval/dependencyGuard.ts` and
`packages/dsh-bridge/src/policy.ts`, a vendored patch under `patches/`,
and a lockfile name used as
an example in `resources/**/hooks-patterns.md`. None of those are
instructions to a contributor.
- Conflict check: `migrations/README.md` is touched by none of the
currently open PRs (451 sampled),
none of the recently merged PRs (60 sampled, 839 distinct files), and
none of my previous PRs here —
#19237, #20295, #20305, #20409. Zero overlap. (Open PRs do add files
under
  `migrations/sqlite-drizzle/`, but not this README.)
- No gate covers this file, verified rather than assumed:
`scripts/check-doc-links.ts` scans `docs`,
`src`, `packages`, `.agents` plus root-level Markdown (`migrations/` is
not in that list, and this
file contains no links anyway); `scripts/verify-doc-frontmatter.ts`
scans `docs/references` and
`docs/contrib`; `scripts/gen-doc-index.ts` only writes `docs/README.md`;
and `.oxfmtrc.json` ignores
both `**/*.md` and `migrations/**`. So no formatter or doc gate applies
to this edit.
- No test added: the change is Markdown-only and no test asserts on
documentation prose.
- Local verification: `git diff` reviewed line by line — exactly 1 file,
`+1 / -1`, line endings
unchanged (LF), and the 27 unrelated paths that a checkout glitch
removed from my working tree were
restored before staging, so the index contains this file and nothing
else.
- Local limitation, stated plainly: I could not run `pnpm docs:check` or
the test suite here — this
environment has no reachable npm registry, so pnpm's dependency status
check aborts before any check
starts. The failure is the network, not this change. Also note that
running
`pnpm db:migrations:generate` itself is deliberately *not* part of the
verification: it writes new
files into `migrations/sqlite-drizzle/`. The script's existence and name
were verified against
  `package.json` instead.

fix(mcp-runtime): clamp oversized tool-result images before they reach agents (#20348)

<!-- Template from
https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md?-->
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:
1. Consider creating this PR as draft:
https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

> ### Branch strategy
>
> - Active development targets `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR: an MCP tool-result image was forwarded to the model
untouched, so a full-page browser screenshot (e.g. 2004×18538 px) hit
DeepSeek's 8192 px per-edge limit and the whole turn failed with a
misleading `unsupported image format` 400 — in Cherry chat, pi, and dsh
(whose `read_image` re-inlines the file it saved).

After this PR: `McpRuntimeService.callToolByServer` clamps every
tool-result image to a 2000 px longest edge before any consumer sees it
(Cherry chat via `mcpTools`, pi / dsh / claude via
`createMcpBridgeServer`), preserving format and mime type. In-bounds
images are only header-probed, never decoded or re-encoded; an
undecodable image degrades to a text block instead of failing the call;
error results are left untouched.

<!-- (optional, in `fixes #<issue number>(, fixes #<issue_number>, ...)`
format, will close the issue(s) when PR gets merged)*: -->

Fixes #

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

Every vision provider downscales far below 2000 px on its own (Anthropic
1568, DeepSeek ~1300-equivalent), so the clamp loses nothing the model
would have seen while removing a hard reject. The MCP client boundary is
the only single point all model-bound consumers share, and it is
independent of whether the agent runtime routes through the local
gateway or directly to the provider.

The following tradeoffs were made: one constant edge cap for all
providers instead of per-model limits (noted as the upgrade path); no
byte budget on top of the dimension clamp, since bytes are not what
providers reject and the cost side has not been measured.

The following alternatives were considered: clamping in each runtime's

docs(main): drop the stale bootstrap.ts cleanup note from core README (#20409)

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

`src/main/core/README.md` §"Startup phases" ended with a note about a
file that no longer exists:

> The legacy file `src/main/bootstrap.ts` predates this vocabulary and
is no longer imported anywhere.
> It will be removed in a follow-up cleanup PR.

That promise is stale. `src/main/bootstrap.ts` **was** removed — commit
`a917ecd6a1`
("refactor(cleanup): remove deprecated bootstrap and init files",
2026-04-08) deleted it together with
`src/main/utils/init.ts`, migrating their responsibilities to
`resolveUserDataLocation()` in
`src/main/core/preboot/userDataLocation.ts`. The paragraph was added one
day earlier by `ed694a19cf`,
so it has been stating a pending cleanup for roughly five months after
the cleanup actually landed.
A reader following it today finds no such file and no pending work.

After this PR:

The two-sentence note is gone. The surrounding section is untouched: the
three-phase table, the
explicit statement that `bootstrap` means only `application.bootstrap()`
in this codebase, and the
clarification that lifecycle stages run inside the bootstrap phase all
remain, so the terminology the
paragraph existed to disambiguate is still documented. Net `-3` lines,
no additions.

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

This is the leftover of a completed cleanup rather than a deliberate
note. `a917ecd6a1` touched exactly
three files — `src/main/bootstrap.ts`, `src/main/utils/init.ts` and
`src/main/ipc.ts` — and did not
update this README, which is how the future-tense promise survived the
deletion it was announcing.

The following tradeoffs were made:

Deletion rather than rewriting it into the past tense ("was removed in
a917ecd6a1"). The paragraph's
only job was to flag a legacy file that was still present and about to
go; once the file is gone there
is nothing left for it to say, and a commit hash in prose ages badly.
Deletion also matches how this
repo handled the equivalent stale paragraph in
`packages/ui/docs/design-token-system.md`, which
`82d06345b8` removed outright when the command it documented was
deleted.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Keep it as a past-tense history note. Rejected above — but if
reviewers would rather preserve the
"bootstrap used to mean a file too" nuance, I am happy to restore it in
the past tense; the deletion
  is easy to convert.
- Leave it. Rejected: it reads as an open TODO and points contributors
at a file that does not exist.

Links to places where the discussion took place:

- `ed694a19cf` — docs(main): mark bootstrap.ts and config.ts as
v2-deprecated legacy (added the note)
- `a917ecd6a1` — refactor(cleanup): remove deprecated bootstrap and init
files (fulfilled it)

### Breaking changes

None. Documentation only: no code, dependency, API, or behavior change.

### Special notes for your reviewer

- Scope: 1 file, `-3 / +0`. No new dependencies, no refactor.
- Confirmed this is the **only** stale reference: a repo-wide search for
`main/bootstrap.ts` across
Markdown returns this single hit. `src/main/utils/init.ts`, the other
file deleted by `a917ecd6a1`,
  is not referenced from any doc, so there is nothing else to clean up.
- Conflict check: `src/main/core/README.md` appears in none of the
recently merged PRs (50 sampled),
none of the currently open PRs (100 sampled), and none of my previous
PRs in this repo — #19237
  (`docs/contrib/development.md`), #20295 (`CONTRIBUTING.md`) and #20305
(`packages/ui/docs/design-token-system.md`). Zero overlap with all
three.
- No test added: the change is Markdown-only and no test asserts on
documentation prose.
- Local verification: `git diff` reviewed line by line (1 file, `-3`, LF
endings unchanged); the
  repo-wide reference search above re-run after the edit.
- Local limitation, stated plainly: I could not run `pnpm docs:check` or
the test suite here. This
environment has no reachable npm registry, so pnpm's dependency status
check aborts before any test
or doc check starts — the failure is the network, not this change. I am
relying on CI for those
  gates and will re-run them if anything comes back red.

### Checklist

- [x] Branch: This PR targets `main`
- [x] PR: The PR description is expressive enough and will help future
contributors
- [x] Code: kept to the minimum deletion that removes the stale promise
- [x] Refactor: left the surrounding section as found; only the stale
paragraph is gone
- [x] Upgrade: no upgrade impact — documentation only
- [x] Documentation: this PR *is* a documentation fix; no user-guide
(docs.cherry-ai.com) update needed
- [x] Self-review: reviewed my own diff (`git diff`) line by line before
requesting review


> ### Branch strategy
>
> - Active development targets `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR: Cherry embeds DSH 0.1.0-rc.7 through the demo executable
and agent spine, uses older session/question/command APIs, and queues
tool-approval rejection feedback for a later turn.

After this PR: Cherry embeds DSH 0.1.2-rc.1 through its own runtime
entry and explicit Cordis composition. It adopts the updated SDK APIs,
denies tool calls without a verified workspace, and delivers rejection
reasons before the next model step in the current turn. Full Access
bash/pwsh schemas omit escalation parameters; a facts-based tool guard
returns corrective errors for stale or malformed requests without
forcing a blocked turn. The unused SDK umbrella dependency is excluded,
and runtime shutdown has bounded resource cleanup. The shared sandbox
loads Windows ACL only on Windows, and the packaged external runtime
includes its Win32-process dependency.

<!-- (optional, in `fixes #<issue number>(, fixes #<issue_number>, ...)`
format, will close the issue(s) when PR gets merged)*: -->

Fixes: N/A. Related: #19801; this PR does not implement same-mode
escalation as a no-op.

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made: Cherry owns the runtime composition
to preserve workspace, tool-policy, skill-discovery, and credential
boundaries. A version-specific pnpm override removes the SDK umbrella
dependency because every Cherry launch supplies `dshBin`; remove it when
upstream makes that dependency optional or a peer. Session-aware schema
projection remains a temporary workaround until upstream supports it.

The following alternatives were considered: A version-only upgrade
leaves removed runtime entries and incompatible APIs. Regex-based
escalation counters and `agent/pre-step` rejection were removed after
review because parallel calls could terminate the turn before feedback
reached the model. Tool arguments are not rewritten, permissions are not
relaxed, and no general retry limit is imposed.

Links to places where the discussion took place:
https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/pull/20214 and
https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/19801 <!-- optional:
slack, other GH issue, mailinglist, ... -->

### Breaking changes

<!-- optional -->

If this PR introduces breaking changes, please describe the changes and
the impact on users.

No intentional configuration migration. Approval rejection reasons now
reach the current turn. Full Access agents must remove redundant
escalation parameters before a shell command can run; this is not
automatic approval or an infinite-retry circuit breaker. Historical rc.7
session-log compatibility and rollback safety remain unverified.
User-facing behavior is documented in
`v2-refactor-temp/docs/breaking-changes/2026-09-09-dsh-full-access-shell-validation.md`.

### Special notes for your reviewer

<!-- optional -->

Packaging follow-up (2026-09-11, commit `76a06f91c5`), validated after
fast-forwarding to the remote branch at `1e28ff3df7`:

- The bundled shared sandbox entry imports Windows ACL only on Windows.
macOS/Linux never resolve the ACL or Win32-process package through this
entry. The version-specific build transform fails if the SDK import
shape changes; remove it after upstream provides platform-safe loading.
- Unpack `@deepseek-ai/dsh-win32-process` alongside the external ACL
runner. Missing Windows ACL dependencies still fail startup; confinement
is never silently disabled.
- Bridge build passed (111 runtime files). Bridge tests: 71 passed. Main
DSH plus packaging tests: 177 passed (169 main, 8 packaging). `pnpm
lint`, including typechecking, i18n and Oxfmt, passed with existing
unrelated warnings. `pnpm docs:check` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Packaging regressions cover fresh-process macOS/Linux platform
simulation, Windows dependency resolution constrained to unpacked paths,
runner availability, and fail-closed missing dependencies. Windows
imports use the real installed packages. These are not macOS/Linux
native sandbox or installed-application tests; those checks remain
pending.
- Only the existing packaging test file was extended; no temporary test
sources or data are included.

Previous baseline validation on Windows after resolving conflicts with
`origin/main` at `33f827b80f` and syncing the subsequent non-DSH fixes
at `0e0e53ebf8`:

- `pnpm install --lockfile-only --ignore-scripts --offline` and `pnpm
install --frozen-lockfile --offline --ignore-scripts`: passed; lifecycle
scripts were not run.
- `pnpm --filter @cherrystudio/dsh-bridge build` and `pnpm --filter
@cherrystudio/dsh-bridge exec tsc --noEmit`: passed; 114 runtime bundle
files.
- `pnpm --filter @cherrystudio/dsh-bridge test`: 71 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project main
src/main/ai/runtime/dsh/__tests__`: 168 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project scripts
scripts/__tests__/dsh-runtime-packaging.test.ts`: 5 tests passed.
- `pnpm lint`: passed after resolving the DSH conflicts, including
typechecking and formatting; 45 existing unrelated ESLint warnings.
- After syncing main's subsequent local-model and Mistral fixes, their
three test files passed (30 tests), and `pnpm typecheck:node` passed
again.
- `pnpm docs:check` and `git diff --check`: passed.

Merge resolution preserves main's durable approval/question sequence
correlation, autonomous-turn origin classification, and Ultra reasoning
support while using the new SDK's `snapshotEvents`, `ToolCallId`, and
`SessionSeq` APIs. The old rc.7 compatibility patch is replaced by a
minimal rc.1 Ultra-level patch; native developer-role support remains
unpatched. The lockfile was regenerated by pnpm instead of choosing one
side wholesale.

Earlier one-off real-SDK subprocess probes verified current-turn
approval feedback, non-empty skill activation, and
malformed/parallel/repeated Full Access escalation requests. At the
author's request, the two generated fixtures were removed after
verification and are no longer part of the runnable suite. The current
168 main tests cover retained stream/trace, autonomous-turn, approval
correlation, provider/header/Ultra configuration, and bundling
contracts; the 71 bridge tests and 5 packaging tests also pass. Reusable
testing documentation now distinguishes retained automated coverage from
manual approval/sandbox checks.

Outstanding review items: DSH-specific `minimumReleaseAgeExclude`
entries were not expanded; main's existing provider-utils exemption
update was retained. Additional persistent DSH exemptions still await
explicit approval. Previously published Windows portability changes have
not been split out by rewriting commit history. Upstream
optional-dependency/session-aware-schema changes remain external
follow-ups.

Manual real-provider/UI testing, historical-log migration, installed-app
packaging, and native sandbox behavior on macOS/Linux remain pending.
The full application build from the initial upgrade was not rerun for
these review fixes. This PR remains open and non-draft at the author's
request; readiness does not imply these checks are complete.

`docs/references/testing/dsh-runtime-upgrade.md`.

feat(messages): add select-all to multi-select (#20257)

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

Multi-select mode (message export) only allows ticking messages one by
one or drag-marquee. Selecting "everything except a few messages" in a
long topic required ticking every message manually.

After this PR:

A tri-state **Checkbox** sits to the left of the "Selected N messages"
count in the bottom action bar:

- unchecked / indeterminate → click selects every selectable message in
the topic
- checked → click clears the selection
- disabled when the topic has no selectable messages

Select-all is data-driven off the message list (safe under list
virtualization) and tri-state semantics mirror the existing
`useHistoryRecordsController` pattern.

Fixes #20190

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

- **Select-all = active branch chain.** The selectable set excludes (a)
context-boundary divider messages (no checkbox rendered, mirroring
`MessageFrame`'s early return) and (b) non-active siblings of
multi-model groups, whose columns are hidden by the fold layout's
`[&.fold]:hidden` CSS in multi-select mode. This keeps the selection
consistent with what the user can actually see and tick, consistent with
marquee behavior.
- **Known behavior note:** current main defaults multi-model layout to
**horizontal**, where non-active sibling columns *are* visible and
individually checkable — in such topics "select all" intentionally
covers the active branch chain only, so the count may be lower than the
visible checkboxes. If multi-select ever unhides fold columns, the
sibling-exclusion predicate must be removed (annotated at both sites).
Broader multi-model / multi-branch export semantics are being handled
separately.

The following alternatives were considered:

- DOM-based selectable detection (rejected: the list is virtualized, DOM
is partial).
- `Cmd/Ctrl+A` shortcut (deferred; not in this PR).
- Forcing fold columns to expand in multi-select mode (deferred; changes
the multi-select interaction model).

### Breaking changes

None.

### Special notes for your reviewer

- Export/copy/delete paths are untouched — select-all just feeds the
existing `ensureSelection` pipeline, so output is byte-identical to
manually ticking the same set.
- Streaming messages behave exactly as with manual ticking (checkable;
delete stays blocked via the existing `generating` availability gate).
- Verified: 47 unit tests (controller + popup + agent adapter + topic
messages), tri-state flow / fold-layout count consistency / clipboard
parity / topic-switch reset via CDP on a real Electron instance.
- Commit 2 aligns the new tests with
`docs/references/testing/frontend-testing.md` (assert prop passthrough
instead of stand-in-reimplemented behavior; `userEvent` over
`fireEvent`).
- **Select-all loads the full topic first** (commit 5): topic history is
cursor-paginated (`limit` in `useTopicMessages`), so a naive select-all
would silently miss unloaded pages — and their parts are not resident,
so exports would be empty. Toggling select-all while older pages remain
now kicks off auto-pagination to the end (same pattern as `useTopics({
loadAll: true })`), shows a loading state on the checkbox, and applies
the selection once every page is resident. Applies to both home topics
and agent sessions.

### What this PR does

Before this PR: log files could only be pruned by winston's own rotation
caps (30 days for `app.*.log`, 60 days for `app-error.*.log`), with no
way for a user to clear them or to choose how long they are kept.

After this PR: Settings → Data gains a "Keep logs for" setting (7 / 14 /
30 / 90 days, default 30) enforced by a new `LogRetentionService` that
sweeps at startup, every 12 hours, and whenever the setting changes; the
cache cleanup dialog gains an "Old logs" group for clearing rotated logs
on demand. Both paths skip the files the rotating transports still hold
open, so today's logs survive.

<!-- (optional, in `fixes #<issue number>(, fixes #<issue_number>, ...)`
format, will close the issue(s) when PR gets merged)*: -->

Fixes #

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

- Retention is enforced by the sweep, not by winston's `maxFiles`:
`LoggerService` is constructed before the preference layer exists, so
the transports cannot read the setting. Their `maxFiles` is raised to
the longest selectable window (90 days) and kept purely as a backstop.
- Files carrying today's date stamp are never deleted — removing an open
rotating file silently drops the rest of the day's logs on POSIX and
fails outright on Windows.
- Undated leftovers (e.g. a stray `app.log`) are removed only by the
manual sweep, since there is no age to weigh against a retention window.
- `app.logs` is added to the cleanup helper's trusted roots because on
macOS the logs directory lives outside userData; without it every log
target would be rejected as an unsafe symlinked path.
- The retention sweep runs through `CacheCleanupService`'s existing
mutex, so it can never race a manual cleanup.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Recreating the winston transports when retention changes, letting the
library own pruning: rejected because a change would only take effect at
the next rotation, and the setting would silently do nothing until then.
- Capping the selectable retention at 30 days to avoid touching
`LoggerService`: rejected because picking 90 days would then be a
control that does not work.

Error logs (`app-error.*.log`) were kept for 60 days regardless of

commits.commit_title: fix(agent-runtime): honor per-server MCP timeout in Pi and dsh runtimes (#20297)
commits.commit_message:
fix(agent-runtime): honor per-server MCP timeout in Pi and dsh runtimes (#20297)

## Problem

In Agent mode with the Pi or dsh runtime, every MCP tool call to a
user-configured server is aborted after exactly 60 seconds — the
per-server **timeout** setting and **Long Running Mode** are silently
ignored (#20266).

## Root cause

The two session runtimes build in-memory MCP clients per session over
the runtime-neutral bridge. Their `client.callTool(...)` passed only the
abort signal, so the SDK fell back to `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MSEC`
(60s) and aborted before `McpRuntimeService` — which already applies the
configured policy and relays progress — could finish.

## Design (ownership model — reworked per @EurFelux's review)

One set of user settings must correspond to one timeout owner. The first
iteration of this PR mirrored the per-server policy onto the forwarding
clients; the review correctly identified that as two independent,
mutually interfering timers: the mirror would come from the **session
snapshot** while `McpRuntimeService` reads **live config on every
call**, so e.g. raising the timeout mid-session would still abort at the
stale snapshot value.

The forwarding layer now interprets no server timeout policy at all:

- Both forwarding clients pass `{ signal, timeout:
MCP_FORWARDING_TIMEOUT_MS }` — the constant is the setTimeout-safe
maximum standing in for "no budget" (the SDK offers no way to disable
its request timer). They forward cancellation and results; that's their
whole job.
- `McpRuntimeService` is the single owner of timeout and
progress-renewal semantics (per-server `timeout`,
`resetTimeoutOnProgress` + 10-min `maxTotalTimeout` under Long Running
Mode), reading live config per call.
- `resolveMcpRequestOptions` is extracted as the one derivation of SDK
`RequestOptions` from per-server config, consumed by `McpRuntimeService`
(also a dedupe of the previously inline policy).
- No `AgentMcpServer` shape changes, no claudeCode changes — the earlier
config channel and whitelist hardening became unnecessary and were
dropped.

If a runtime ever needs an overall execution budget, it should be
designed as its own semantically explicit policy, not by re-interpreting
server settings at the forwarding layer.

## Test plan

Behavior tests run the **real SDK client over InMemoryTransport under
fake timers**, asserting call outcomes (never the RequestOptions shape —
per the review, an options check with the implementation's own constant
cannot catch a regression to the 60s default):

- [x] `McpRuntimeService.timeoutPolicy.test.ts` (new): terminates at the
per-server timeout; a long-running call survives past the per-progress
window via progress notifications; progress cannot extend past the
10-minute `maxTotalTimeout`
- [x] Pi bridge: a 65s tool call completes (fires red if the forwarding
client ever falls back to the SDK's 60s default); abort forwarding on a
slow call
- [x] dsh bridge: a signal-less 65s call completes; existing real-chain
cancellation test retained
- [x] Unit tests for `resolveMcpRequestOptions` derivation (4)
- [x] Mutation-checked: reverting the forwarding options to a bare
signal, or dropping the policy spread in `McpRuntimeService`, turns the
corresponding tests red
- [x] Full affected suites: 1551 passed (ai/mcp + pi + dsh +
claudeCode); `typecheck:node`, eslint `--no-cache`, oxlint, biome clean

Fixes: #20266

commits.commit_message:
fix(shortcuts): report conflicts between main and renderer keybindings (#20339)

> ### Branch strategy
>
> - Active development targets `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

The shortcut conflict check in `findKeybindingConflicts` skipped any
pair whose `scope` differed (`main` vs `renderer`). A renderer shortcut
such as **New Topic** could be bound to `Cmd+=` while **Zoom In** (a
main-scope shortcut) still owned it, and Settings saved it without a
warning. At runtime the main process handles the key in
`before-input-event` and calls `preventDefault`, so the page never
receives the `keydown` and the renderer command never fires.

After this PR:

Conflict detection no longer treats scope as a separator. Recording,
toggling on, or bulk-enabling a shortcut that collides with a main-scope
binding (primary or `additionalBindings`) now shows the existing
conflict toast/label. Platform and `when` filtering are unchanged.
Runtime dispatch is untouched.

Fixes: N/A

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

Every `CommandScope` value currently routes through the same window
input path: non-global main bindings run in `before-input-event` on the
main window and attached webviews, global ones go through
`globalShortcut`, and both are consumed before the renderer's `keydown`
listener. There is no case where two bindings on the same keys stay
independent because they run in different processes, so the scope gate
was a wrong premise rather than a missing rule.

The following tradeoffs were made:

Users who already saved a cross-process duplicate under the old check
will now see the conflict warning when they re-enable either command and
must change one binding first. Existing bindings keep working at
runtime.

The following alternatives were considered:

Introducing an explicit "input surface" attribute per command was
considered and rejected: every command would carry the same value today,
so it would only rename the fact the removed check got wrong. Sub
windows also mount the renderer dispatcher while the main-process
interceptor is only attached to the main window; the fix over-reports
there, which is the safe direction.

Links to places where the discussion took place: N/A

### Breaking changes

None.

### Special notes for your reviewer

The regression test uses the real registry (`app.zoom.in` defaults) so
it fails on the previous code for both the primary `Cmd+=` and the
additional `Cmd+Shift+=` binding. Default bindings were checked across
darwin/win32/linux and contain no cross-command duplicates, so removing
the scope gate does not surface conflicts in a fresh install.

`typescript/no-unnecessary-type-assertion` was parked at `off` in the

`tsc@7` still requires. The **88 files** containing those carry a
file-level `// oxlint-disable typescript/no-unnecessary-type-assertion`
with a rationale, so the rule is enforced everywhere else without
breaking type-checking.

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

This is the exit layer for the backlog #17720 deferred. The clean
removals (~400 files) are the point — new unnecessary assertions will
now be caught at `error`.

The ~130 false positives are real: removing them produces 186 `tsc@7`

The following tradeoffs were made:

- **88 files opt out of the rule** (40 tests + a set of production
files). This is a deliberate, documented consequence of the tsgolint/tsc
inference gap, not a code problem. If tsgolint tightens this sub-check
upstream, these disables can be removed.

- Leaving the rule at `off` was rejected because it forgoes catching the
~1350 genuinely-unnecessary assertions and never converges the backlog.
- Per-line `oxlint-disable-next-line` on ~130 sites was rejected as

commits.commit_message:
chore(build-toolchain): drop @electron-toolkit/tsconfig (#17744)

<!-- Template from
https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md?-->
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! -->

> ### 🚨 Branch strategy — read before opening this PR
>
> This active-development toolchain change targets the preceding Vite 8
branch and ultimately `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

`tsconfig.node.json` and `tsconfig.web.json` extended
`@electron-toolkit/tsconfig`. That base config sets `moduleResolution:
"node"` (conflicting with this stack's bundler/TS7 direction) and
`noImplicitAny: false` alongside `strict: true`. Both project configs
already re-declared `moduleResolution: "bundler"`, so the base's
`"node"` was silently masked rather than removed.

After this PR:

The `@electron-toolkit/tsconfig` dependency is removed. Both project
configs inline the compiler options they were inheriting and are now
self-contained: `moduleResolution: "bundler"` is the only declared value
(no masked `"node"`), and there is no hidden base layer. Type-check
behavior is otherwise unchanged.

<!-- No linked issue. -->

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The base config introduced two footguns that were invisible at the call
site: a `moduleResolution: "node"` that only worked because both configs
happened to override it, and `noImplicitAny: false` masking `strict`.
Inlining the options makes the real configuration explicit and removes
the `"node"` value entirely, so the resolution mode can no longer
regress if an override is dropped.

The following tradeoffs were made:

- `noImplicitAny: false` is kept explicit rather than dropped. Enabling
it (via `strict`) surfaces ~277 implicit-any errors across main +
renderer; fixing those is out of scope for a dependency-removal layer
and is left for a dedicated follow-up. Keeping it explicit preserves
current type-check behavior exactly.
- The inlined options mirror the previous effective configuration (base
+ per-config overrides), so no type-check result changes in this PR.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Keeping `@electron-toolkit/tsconfig` was rejected because it hides the
resolution mode and the `noImplicitAny` opt-out behind an external base.
- Flipping `noImplicitAny` in the same layer was rejected because ~277
pre-existing implicit-any sites would turn a config cleanup into a broad
code change.

Links to places where the discussion took place:
https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/pull/17719#pullrequestreview-4838129638

uiContract parser stack branch and ultimately `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

The application used the `rolldown-vite` alias, the React SWC plugin,
electron-vite 5, Vitest 3, and configuration keys inherited from
Rollup/esbuild paths.

After this PR:

The stack uses official `vite@8.2.0`, `electron-vite@6.0.0-beta.1`, and
`@vitejs/plugin-react@6.0.5`, so React transformation follows Vite 8's
Oxc path. Compatible React, Tailwind, and TanStack Router plugins are
upgraded, and Vitest plus its companion packages move to Vitest 4. Build
configuration uses `rolldownOptions`, native main/preload dependencies
remain external, and the package hook forces `better-sqlite3` to rebuild
from source for the exact Electron platform/architecture ABI before
files are copied.

<!-- No linked issue. -->

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

Vite 8 makes Rolldown the official production bundler and uses Oxc in
the default React integration. The electron-vite beta supplies the Vite
8 peer range. Keeping native dependencies external preserves Electron
runtime loading, while an explicit source rebuild prevents pnpm from
retaining a host-Node prebuild in packaged output.

The following tradeoffs were made:

- This layer uses an electron-vite beta because it is the available
release line with Vite 8 support.
- `better-sqlite3` packaging takes a source rebuild to guarantee the
target Electron ABI.
- Vite's config-loader compatibility warnings remain advisory and can be
handled separately from this dependency migration.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Keeping `@vitejs/plugin-react-swc` was rejected because it replaces
Vite 8's development Oxc transform with SWC.
- Adding Rolldown as a direct dependency was rejected because Vite 8
already owns it.
- Bundling native modules was rejected because main/preload must load
their platform binaries at runtime.

https://github.com/alex8088/electron-vite/issues/894

No user-facing API, IPC, or data-structure changes. Internal build and

focused 6-test fixture and was exercised by the complete unpacked
package build. A final repeat of `pnpm build:check` was stopped at the

tsgolint stack branch and ultimately `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

Formatting was provided by Biome across root scripts, workspaces,
generators, pre-commit hooks, and editor configuration.

After this PR:

Oxfmt replaces Biome in every active formatting entry point — root
scripts, `packages/aiCore`, `packages/extension-table-plus`,
`packages/provider-registry`'s catalog generator, pre-commit hooks, and
editor configuration — and the `@biomejs/biome` dependency is dropped
from every workspace. The configuration enables import, `package.json`,
and Tailwind class sorting, with stylesheet handling for both the
renderer and `packages/ui`.

The ignore set is **not** a 1:1 carry-over from Biome; it shifts in both
directions:

- **Newly formatted** (previously outside Biome's scope): `.github/**`,
`.vscode/**`, `.zed/**`, `*.yml`/`*.yaml`, `*.mjs`/`*.cjs`, and every
`package.json`.
- **Newly excluded** (previously formatted by Biome): `patches/**`,
`**/vendor/**`, `coverage/**`, and `migrations/**`. Excluding
`migrations/**` means drizzle snapshots are no longer reformatted after
generation; this is tracked as a separate follow-up.
- `packages/provider-registry/data/*.json` is formatted by Oxfmt
(byte-identical to the previous Biome output), making Oxfmt the single
formatting authority for the generated catalog.

Build output (`dist/**`, `out/**`, `build/**`), generated files, and
`v2-refactor-temp/**` remain excluded. All other tracked source/config
files are reformatted once.

<!-- No linked issue. -->

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

Using Oxfmt consolidates formatting on the Oxc toolchain and removes the
duplicate Biome dependency. A dedicated formatting baseline isolates
mechanical changes from later semantic lint/parser/build layers.

The following tradeoffs were made:

- Oxfmt does not implement arbitrary JSON key ordering; stable generated
ordering remains the responsibility of each generator.
- The migration intentionally creates a large mechanical diff.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Maintaining both Biome and Oxfmt was rejected because it would leave
conflicting formatting authorities.
- Building a custom general-purpose JSON sorter was rejected because
Oxfmt does not promise that behavior and generators are the correct
source of stable order.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

The repository used an older Oxlint/tsgolint integration
(`oxlint@^1.56`, `oxlint-tsgolint@^0.17`).

After this PR:

Oxlint is upgraded to `1.76.0` and `oxlint-tsgolint` to `7.0.2001`, with
`options.typeAware: true` retained and `--deny-warnings` kept in
`test:lint`. tsgolint 7's stronger type-aware checks flag a batch of
`await` on synchronous (better-sqlite3) calls; those are cleaned up. Two
rules that the upgrade newly surfaces are parked at `off` and handled
outside this layer (see below); no rule-severity policy is changed here.

<!-- No linked issue. -->

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The newer tsgolint package is the type-aware lint companion for the
TypeScript 7 layer. This PR is scoped to the upgrade itself and the
cleanups the upgrade forces; unrelated rule changes are kept out.

- **`await`-on-sync cleanups (upgrade-forced):** the type-aware pass
correctly flags `await` / `Promise.all(...)` wrapping synchronous
data-layer calls (`getById`, `list`, `enqueue`, … all return
non-Promises per the better-sqlite3 convention in CLAUDE.md). These are
unwrapped to plain synchronous calls.
- **`typescript/no-unnecessary-type-assertion` → `off` (backlog):**
tsgolint 7 adds a new "receiver accepts the original type" sub-check
that surfaces a repository-wide backlog invisible under 0.17 — **1508
diagnostics across 488 files**, of which **1181 (78%) are in test
files** and **1417 (94%) come from the new sub-check**. This is not
appropriate to fix in an upgrade PR, so the rule is parked at `off` with
a `// TODO` and a dedicated migration is tracked in **#17746** (the rule
auto-fixes with `oxlint --fix`; the exit layer restores it to `error`).
- **`typescript/no-useless-default-assignment` → `off` (split out):**
oxlint 1.76 enables this rule by default; it is unrelated to the
upgrade. The rule and its 17 source fixes are moved to a dedicated PR,
so this layer stays a pure upgrade.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Promoting the warn-tier rules to `error` and dropping
`--deny-warnings` was reverted: with the backlog parked at `off`, the
warn tier carries nothing, so the refactor was net-neutral and off-topic
for an upgrade.
- Fixing the 1508-item backlog inline was rejected as far too broad for

chore(typescript): adopt TypeScript 7 (#17719)

<!-- Template from
https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md?-->
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! -->

> ### 🚨 Branch strategy — read before opening this PR
>
> This active-development toolchain change targets `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

Cherry Studio used `@typescript/native-preview` through the `tsgo`
executable, while Compiler API consumers and type-check entry points did
not have a stable split between TypeScript 7 and the compatibility
compiler.

After this PR:

All repository type-check entry points run the native `tsc` from
`typescript@7.0.2`. `typescript` remains aliased to
`@typescript/typescript6@6.0.2` only for Compiler API tooling that is
not yet TypeScript 7 compatible. Unsupported `baseUrl` settings are
removed, workspace manifests are aligned, and the affected side-effect
imports and RichEditor option inference are corrected.

<!-- No linked issue. -->

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

TypeScript 7 provides the native compiler performance path. The single
hard blocker to running everything on it is ESLint's TypeScript parser:
`@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree` still requires the Compiler API —
its latest release (8.65.0) peer-depends on `typescript <6.1.0` and
calls `ts.createSourceFile` — while `typescript@7.0.2`'s main entry only
exports `{ version, versionMajorMinor }`. Separating the command-line
compiler (`tsc` from TS7) from the Compiler API compatibility package
(`@typescript/typescript6`) lets type checking move to TS7 now without
rewriting that tooling in this layer.

Retaining `@typescript/typescript6` is deliberately not open-ended. Its
real consumer surface is narrow: ESLint's parser is the only hard
constraint; the two remaining non-production scripts can move to
`ts-morph`, and Storybook's `react-docgen-typescript` never executes
because `storybook@10` defaults to the babel `react-docgen`. ESLint is
removed in layer 4 (#17722), which clears the hard blocker. **Exit
condition:** once the two scripts migrate to `ts-morph`, a follow-up
layer drops the `typescript` → `@typescript/typescript6` alias — this
dual-compiler state ends there rather than persisting.

The following tradeoffs were made:

- The repository temporarily carries TypeScript 7 for type checking and
TypeScript 6 for Compiler API compatibility, until the exit layer above;
the only hard consumer is ESLint's parser, which is removed in #17722.
- Existing command names such as `pnpm typecheck` remain unchanged.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Keeping `@typescript/native-preview` was rejected because the stable
TypeScript 7 package now supplies the native compiler.
- Migrating every Compiler API consumer in the same layer was rejected
because it would make the compiler upgrade unnecessarily broad.

docs(contributing): restore the missing DCO sign-off example (#20295)

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

The "Contributor Compliance with Project Terms" section of
`CONTRIBUTING.md` promises an example and then never shows it. It reads
*"A signed commit is one where the commit message includes the
following:"*, and the next non-empty line moves on to a different topic
(the `git commit --signoff` command). The `Signed-off-by:` trailer the
sentence introduces is missing, so the sentence dangles and contributors
are asked to certify their commits without ever being shown the exact
trailer format. `Signed-off-by` currently does not appear in any
Markdown file in the repository.

After this PR:

The promised fenced example is restored immediately under that sentence,
so the paragraph introduces the trailer, shows it, and only then
explains how to generate it:

```
Signed-off-by: Your Name <your.email@example.com>
```

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

This is a regression from the guide's translation, not a gap that was
never filled:

- `a5f8ac8587` ("feat: add English contributor guide and update issue
templates", #5300) introduced this section in Chinese **with** the
fenced block `Signed-off-by: Your Name <your.email@example.com>`.
- `2807e71f1a` ("docs: contributor guide"), committed ten minutes later,
replaced the Chinese sentence with the English one that is still in the
file today and removed the fenced block along with it.

Both can be verified locally with `git show 2807e71f1a --
CONTRIBUTING.md` and `git log -S'Signed-off-by:' -- CONTRIBUTING.md`,
which lists exactly these two commits and nothing since.

The restored line is byte-for-byte the example this project already
shipped in `a5f8ac8587`, so no new wording is invented. It also lines up
with the upstream guide this documentation is derived from
(`kubevirt/kubevirt`, credited in this repository's PR template), where
the same sentence is likewise followed by a `Signed-off-by:` block.

The following tradeoffs were made: the change is confined to restoring
the lost block. The surrounding sentences, the existing `--signoff`
command example, and the heading are left untouched so the diff stays
trivially reviewable.

The following alternatives were considered: rewording the sentence to
drop its promise instead of restoring the example. That was rejected
because signing off is a real requirement for every contributor here, so
showing the exact trailer is more useful than deleting the reference to
it.

commits.commit_title: fix(mistral-ocr): inline separated tables into converted markdown (#20137)
commits.commit_message:
fix(mistral-ocr): inline separated tables into converted markdown (#20137)

> ### Branch strategy
>
> - Active development targets `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

The Mistral document-to-markdown handler requested tables in a separate
format (`tableFormat: 'html'`), but the response schema only declared
`pages[].markdown`, so `pages[].tables` was stripped at parse time and
the builder joined page markdown alone. Every table in an imported PDF
reached the knowledge base as a bare `tbl-N` placeholder while the
processing task still reported success. Numbers inside tables were not
searchable.

After this PR:

Each page's `tables[]` entries are substituted back at their `[id](id)`
placeholder before the markdown is persisted; a table whose placeholder
is missing is appended to its page so its content is never lost. The
handler now requests `tableFormat: 'markdown'`, so tables arrive as pipe
tables, which the knowledge `MarkdownReader` passes through untouched.
The image-to-text builder applies the same inlining so it cannot
silently drop separated tables either.

Fixes N/A (no linked issue)

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The substitution follows Mistral's documented contract: with a non-null
`table_format` the page markdown carries `[tbl-N.md](tbl-N.md)`
placeholders and the table bodies live in `pages[].tables[]`, and the
caller is expected to map them back. The SDK offers no helper for this.
A function replacer is used for the substitution because a plain string
replacement would expand `$&`-style patterns inside table content.

The following tradeoffs were made:

- Markdown tables instead of HTML: the knowledge ingestion reader
contains HTML-tag stripping code (currently a no-op due to an upstream
bug in `@vectorstores/readers`), so HTML tables would be one upstream
fix away from collapsing into concatenated cell text. Pipe tables are
immune to that and chunk one row per line. The cost is that merged cells
are flattened; before this PR nothing from the table was indexed at all.
- Missing-placeholder fallback appends the table rather than failing:
the defect being fixed was silent data loss behind a green task, so
degrading to "present but not positioned" is preferable to either
dropping it or failing the whole conversion.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Dropping `tableFormat` entirely so the API inlines tables itself:
simplest, but leaves the code with no protection if separated tables are
ever requested again.
- Keeping `tableFormat: 'html'` with substitution: preserves merged
cells but depends on the reader's HTML stripping staying broken.

Links to places where the discussion took place: N/A

### Breaking changes

None.

### Special notes for your reviewer

- PDFs already imported through Mistral keep their previously persisted
markdown until the knowledge item is re-indexed; nothing migrates
automatically.
- The five assertions removed from the two test files only recorded mock
call arguments (signed-URL and delete pass-throughs, the `fs.readFile`
call, the progress sequence). The remaining assertions cover the
outbound request shape, cleanup on success/failure/abort, and output
content.
- Placeholder and id shape for markdown mode (`tbl-N.md`) was confirmed
against publicly saved Mistral OCR responses; the official docs only
show the `.html` variant.

commits.commit_title: fix(export): await the Notion body write and report its failure (#20268)
commits.commit_message:
fix(export): await the Notion body write and report its failure (#20268)

> ### Branch strategy
>
> - Active development targets `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

`notion-helper`'s `appendBlocks` never rejects. On failure it resolves
with `apiResponses: null` and an `error` string. `executeNotionExport`
handed that promise to the loading toast and never awaited it, so the
export returned `true`, showed the success toast, and released the
export mutex while the body was still being written. A failed body write
was reported as a successful export, and a second export could start
mid-write.

After this PR:

- The body write is awaited and the export mutex is held until it
settles.
- The resolved failure shape (`apiResponses: null` or an `error` field)
is treated as an error: the export returns `false`, logs the library
message, and shows the existing generic export error toast.
- Both loading toasts ("Preparing" and "Exporting") get a fixed key and
close themselves when their promise settles, following the pattern
already used by the topic and session image export toasts. One result
toast is shown per export instead of the auto-transitioned duplicate.

Fixes # N/A

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

- The library's raw error message is only logged, not shown. The user
sees the existing generic `message.error.notion.export` toast, which
keeps the failure UI consistent with the page-creation failure path.
- Static toast keys are used because `executeNotionExport` is already
guarded by the single export-in-progress mutex, so two Notion exports
never overlap.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Wrapping `appendBlocks` in a `.then` that throws on the failure shape
and passing that promise to the loading toast. This surfaced the failure
but produced two error toasts (the auto-transitioned loading toast plus
the generic one), so it was replaced with the close-on-settle pattern.
- Letting the loading toast auto-transition to success. Its title cannot
change, so the user would see "Exporting to Notion ..." with a check
mark instead of the real success message.

commits.commit_title: feat(agent-session): label runtime-started turns with their origin (#18770)
commits.commit_message:
feat(agent-session): label runtime-started turns with their origin (#18770)

> ### Branch strategy
>
> - Active development targets `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR: after a DSH host turn finished ("Processed"), the
`goal-round-driver` could start another round with no user input, and
the transcript showed a second assistant message with nothing above it
and nothing to say why. Claude Code had the same gap when background
work woke the main agent. And if the user replied right after the turn
ended while a round was queued, the round's content streamed into the
user's response and the user's actual reply was dropped.

After this PR: a runtime-started assistant turn carries a header badge
naming why it exists — **Goal round N** (dsh) or **Continued after
background work** (Claude Code) — while the session is open. The round
itself is shown, not hidden. A user prompt that races a queued round
gets its own turn and its own reply.

Fixes #18755

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The reporter's complaint was "it started a new answer **without any
prompt**" — the surprise, not the visibility. They described exactly
what the second bubble did, so hiding it (the earlier revisions of this
PR) would have removed real work from the transcript while it kept
running in the child: files still written, tokens still spent, and the
round still in the model's context on resume. `main`'s behaviour of
showing the bubble was closer to right; what it lacked was an
explanation.

The explanation is available on both runtimes that open such turns:

- dsh: `turn/start` carries only `{ turn }`, but the entering
`user/message` batch that the agent loop appends right after
`step/start` (before the model call) is tagged by its producer — `{
kind: 'user' }` by our bridge for a host prompt, `{ kind: 'goal', round
}` by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal-round-driver` for a continuation.
- Claude Code: parentless content with no open turn is the SDK waking
the main agent after background work (`streamAdapter.ts`, already
translated to `autonomous-turn-state`).

So the change is made at the runtime-neutral seam,
`autonomous-turn-state: started`, which now carries an
`AutonomousTurnOrigin`. The state machine keeps it on the
`autonomous-turn` execution, `startReceiveOnlyTurn` publishes it to the
shared cache per assistant message, and the renderer reads it next to
the live flow parts it already reads from the same cache.

**The race** (third commit) was found by running the branch against a
live dsh session, not by the unit tests: the user replies ~1 s after a
turn ends while a goal round is queued. dsh accepts the prompt, then
runs the round first. Two independent defects in `main`:

1. The adapter's `beginTurn()` claimed the round's turn when the round's
`turn/start` had already arrived — the round's content streamed into the
prompt's response with no badge.
2. `AgentSessionRuntimeService` ignored `autonomous-turn-state: started`
whenever the host turn was live *and admitted*. On dsh, admitted means
"accepted into the inbox", not "running", so even a correctly classified
round streamed into the prompt's turn, and the prompt's own reply —
arriving after that turn was closed — was dropped (`Agent SDK usage lost
its active turn`, `Ignoring invalid transition runtime-terminal`).

`beginTurn()` now leaves a classified or open runtime turn alone. The
service defers an admitted turn the same way it already deferred an
unadmitted one, keeping its admission so the relaunch does not re-send
the prompt, and buffering content the runtime produces for it before its
stream reopens (replayed by `flush-transition`, after the `start`
chunk).

The following tradeoffs were made:

- **Not persisted.** The origin is live session status in the shared
cache, like the api-retry state, and is gone after a restart — rounds
from before a restart show as plain assistant messages again. Persisting
it would have cost a column and a migration for an after-the-fact label;
the goal state itself (round N of M, "goal in progress", a stop control)
is the right durable home and is a follow-up.
- **Closed origin set with two members**, each with a producer today. A
new runtime with a new reason adds a member and an i18n key.
- **`@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal` becomes a dependency** purely to load its
`MessageSourceMap` merge — the same reason `dsh-compaction-basic` /
`dsh-llm-retry` / `dsh-plan-mode` are already declared for this file.
Removing the import turns `source.kind === 'goal'` into a compile error.
- **Transcript order follows execution order.** When a prompt is
deferred behind a round, its row lands after the round's rows, which is
when dsh actually answered it.

The following alternatives were considered:

- **Suppress the round** (this PR's earlier revisions, 500 ms grace
window → per-turn latch → turn-id isolation → arrival-time heuristic →
event-time comparison). Each revision was reopened by a new
interleaving, ending at a tie between two equal millisecond timestamps
from two processes — a point with no ordering information. Rejected on
both grounds: underdetermined, and it hides real work.
- **Persist the origin on the message** (column + migration). Rejected
as disproportionate for a label; see tradeoffs.
- **Infer "unprompted" from transcript adjacency** (assistant after
assistant). Gives no reason or round number, pages are newest-first so
the previous message may be on another page, and steer continuation rows
are also assistant-after-assistant.

Links to places where the discussion took place: review history on this
PR;
https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/pull/18770#issuecomment-5582161992

### Breaking changes

None.

### Special notes for your reviewer

The branch was rebased onto `main` and replaced (force-push): the
earlier suppression revisions are superseded, not amended. Three
commits: the runtime/main/shared contract, the renderer badge, then the
race fix. `pi` and `aiSdk` never emit `autonomous-turn-state`, so they
are untouched.

Verified live against a dsh session (`deepseek-v4-flash`) in an isolated
profile — the model armed the goal itself via `create_goal`, i.e. the
reporter's path:

- three rounds, each badged `目标推进 · 第 N 轮`, content streamed, goal
completed;
- a user reply sent ~1 s after the host turn ended, with a round queued:
before the third commit the round's content landed under the user's
prompt and the user's reply was lost; after it, the rounds are badged
and the reply has its own turn.

Tests (state the bug each catches):

- dsh adapter — goal round after a host turn opens as an autonomous turn
tagged `{ goal-round, round }` and its content still streams; a round
racing a fresh host prompt (either ordering: prompt first, or round's
`turn/start` first) opens its own turn and the prompt's content lands in
the prompt's turn; non-goal sources are tagged `background-work`; a host
batch with injected context ahead of the prompt still classifies as host
(`claim()` returns `[injected…, prompt]`); mid-turn input cannot
reclassify an open round.
- Claude Code adapter — the wake carries `background-work`.
- State machine — `started(origin)` lands on the execution; an admitted
deferred turn stays admitted across the relaunch and its early content
is replayed by `flush-transition`.
- `AgentSessionRuntimeService` — publishes the origin under the
assistant message's key; an admitted host turn is deferred behind a goal
round and resumed without re-sending, with the buffered reply delivered.
The old test asserting the guard ("ignores a receive-only signal while
an admitted turn is live") pinned the defect and is removed.
- `useAgentSessionParts` — a cache value becomes `metadata.turnOrigin`;
`MessageHeader` — renders the badge for a goal round, nothing for a
prompted turn.

`src/main/ai` + `src/main/data` full sweep passes. tsgo (node + web),
oxlint, biome, eslint, `i18n:check`, `docs:check` clean.

Out of scope, for a follow-up: consume `goal/change` so the session can
show "goal in progress · round N/M" with a stop control instead of
"Processed", and decide whether a goal the model arms itself via
`tool-goal` should require confirmation.

```release-note
Agent sessions now label a reply the agent started on its own — "Goal round N" for a DSH goal continuation, or "Continued after background work" — instead of showing an unexplained new message. A message sent while a DSH goal round is starting no longer has the round's output attributed to it, and its own reply is no longer lost.
```

commits.commit_title: fix(obsidian-export): serialize note front matter as YAML (#20260)
commits.commit_message:
fix(obsidian-export): serialize note front matter as YAML (#20260)

> ### Branch strategy
>
> - Active development targets `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

The Obsidian export dialog built the note's front matter by string
interpolation. A title containing `: ` (for example `Meeting: sprint
planning`) produced invalid YAML, a title starting with `#` turned into
a YAML comment and the title was lost, and the tags field was written as
one raw string instead of a list.

After this PR:

Front matter properties are serialized with the `yaml` package, one line
per property, so any title round-trips intact. The tags input is
normalized into a YAML list: comma-separated values, bracketed lists
(`[work, notes]`, `["work", "notes"]`, `['work', 'notes']`) and an empty
list are all accepted, and a leading `#` is dropped because Obsidian
rewrites tag properties without it.

<!-- (optional, in `fixes #<issue number>(, fixes #<issue_number>, ...)`
format, will close the issue(s) when PR gets merged)*: -->

Fixes # N/A

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

- Serialize with the `yaml` package (already a renderer dependency)
instead of hand-escaping values, and pass `lineWidth: 0` so long titles
are not folded across lines.
- Export tags as a YAML list because the Obsidian Properties
documentation requires the `tags` property to be a list.
- Drop a leading `#` from tag values; Obsidian deprecated `#tag` in
properties and rewrites it to `tag`.
- The comma separator regex is taken from Obsidian Web Clipper's
`multitext` parsing (MIT), credited in a code comment.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Wrapping each value with `JSON.stringify`: fixes the quoting but keeps
tags as a single string.
- Porting the Web Clipper parser verbatim: it only accepts the strict
JSON form, so `[work, notes]` would export as two bracketed tags.

## 中文

### 改动

提示词润色此前会一直等待 `ai.text.generate` 返回。请求卡住时，界面只能持续显示
loading，用户无法取消，也没有截止时间。

本 PR增加 request-scoped cancellation 和 60 秒 deadline：

- `ai.text.generate` 可选携带 request ID；
- 新增对应的 `ai.text.abort`；
- Main IPC 用 `AbortController` 把取消信号传入现有 `AiService.generateText()`；

- 已取消、已超时或过期的响应不会覆盖当前提示词；
- 不使用 cancellation 的现有调用保持原有请求形状。

ID / abort 配对。

`fetchGenerate()` 在注册 abort listener 后再次检查
`signal.aborted`，避免注册窗口中的取消被漏掉；abort handler 只会执行一次。

#20161 还包含显示润色模型和设置入口等产品项，因此本 PR不关闭整个 issue。

Before this PR:

- The message debug panel (Call Chain) truncated `ai.turn` Outputs at
~8k chars (`MAX_CONTENT_CHARS = 8 * KB` in `turnSpanAttributes.ts`), so
long streaming responses could not be fully inspected.
- Opening Raw Data (or any tab) with a large payload synchronously ran
`JSON.stringify` + full Shiki highlighting in `SpanDetail`, freezing the
UI.

After this PR:

- `ai.turn` Outputs are captured up to 512 KB (aligned with the HTTP
trace body cap); inputs stay capped at 8 KB. ~8k-char responses are
preserved in full.
- `SpanDetail` renders payloads over 100k chars as a plain-text
(highlight-free) virtualized preview with Expand/Collapse and
full-content Download; Copy always copies the full content. Large
strings skip `JSON.parse` + pretty-print via a fast path.

<!-- (optional, in `fixes #<issue number>(, fixes #<issue_number>, ...)`
format, will close the issue(s) when PR gets merged)*: -->

Fixes #19564

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

- Output cap raised to 512 KB rather than removed, so a pathological
single turn still cannot blow the trace store / IPC payload on its own
(bounded by the existing 64 MB store budget with eviction).
- Large payloads render unhighlighted instead of
paginated/virtual-highlighted: minimal change that removes the freeze
vector (Shiki tokenization), while `CodeViewer` virtualization keeps
even full 1 MB+ text smooth.
- Preview is 100k chars to match the existing `ErrorDetailModal`
truncation convention; full content stays one click away (Expand) or one
Download away.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Removing the output cap entirely (rejected: unbounded per-turn
IPC/store growth).
- Paginated virtual list for raw data (rejected: more work for marginal
gain over highlight-free virtualized rows).

perf(knowledge): lazy-load management dialogs and item detail panels (#19728)

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

`KnowledgePageDialogSection` statically imported all six management
dialogs (AddKnowledgeItemDialog, CreateKnowledgeBaseDialog,
CreateKnowledgeGroupDialog, KnowledgeBaseNameDialog,
RenameKnowledgeGroupDialog, RestoreKnowledgeBaseDialog — roughly a
thousand lines incl. model selects) and `KnowledgePageDetailSection`
statically imported the chunk/note item detail panels. Visiting the
Knowledge page pulled all of it into the page graph even though none of
it is rendered until a dialog opens or an item is selected.

After this PR:

Both groups use module-level `lazy(() => import(...))` with the
conditional mounts that already existed (`{open ? <Dialog/> : null}`,
`selectedItemId ? <panel/> : ...`), each wrapped in `<Suspense
fallback={null}>` exactly like the already-lazy RagConfig/RecallTest
drawers in the same file. A dialog module now loads the first time its
open state activates; the chunk/note detail panels load the first time
an item is opened in the matching view. Open state stays in
`KnowledgePageProvider`; close callbacks and all existing loading
fallbacks are untouched. The two rename dialogs share
`KnowledgeEntityNameDialog`, which the bundler extracts into a shared
chunk — no extra indirection module needed.

Fixes #19671

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

- One shared `<Suspense>` wraps all six dialogs instead of one per
branch. Dialogs are modal and never co-open, so a suspending sibling
cannot unmount a rendered one in practice; per-branch wrappers would add
churn for a theoretical case.
- The new contract tests sit at the top of the describe block: `vi.mock`
factories run once per module per file, so only the first test to open
each dialog/panel can observe the module load. A comment in the test
file documents this ordering constraint.

The following alternatives were considered:

- A shared re-export module so the two rename dialogs share one explicit
chunk — rejected: they are thin wrappers over
`KnowledgeEntityNameDialog` already, and build-time shared-dependency
extraction achieves the same with zero machinery.
- Lazy-loading `DataSourcePanel` as well — rejected: it is the default
view once a base is selected, so laziness would only move the cost to
base selection and add a blank frame; the issue only asks for the
optional dialogs and item detail panels.

### Breaking changes

tests for those flows pass with their post-click assertions converted to
`findBy` (the dialog render is now asynchronous on first open).

modules + three positive) use module-load recorders in the existing
`vi.mock` factories, following the file's `mockRagConfigPanelModuleLoad`
precedent, and use `userEvent` per the frontend testing guidelines.

drivable.
