commits.commit_title: refactor(ai-request): split the AI request pipeline by modality and carry the conversation on chat requests (#20224)
commits.commit_message:
refactor(ai-request): split the AI request pipeline by modality and carry the conversation on chat requests (#20224)

> ### Branch strategy
>
> - Active development targets `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

The AI layer ran chat, embedding, rerank and image requests through one
undifferentiated pipeline (`AiBaseRequest` → `buildAgentParamsFor` →
`buildAgentParams` → `resolveProviderAiSdkConfig`), with no type that
says "this is a chat request". A chat-only need therefore had no legal
home: OpenCode Go/Zen's mandatory `x-opencode-session` header was set
from an optional `sessionId` on the provider config that only the chat
path supplied, so model health checks, context compaction, image jobs
and gateway calls reached OpenCode without it. `chatId` doubled as
stream key, topic id and provider affinity key, and `streamPrompt`
rewrote it for gateway streams.

After this PR:

The modality axis exists end to end:

- **Types** — `AiRequest` is the transport base (model, credential,
request options). `AiChatRequest` adds `conversation: ConversationRef {
id, topicId? }` and the turn-shaping fields only chat uses
(`mcpToolIds`, `reasoningEffort`, `serviceTier`, `fastMode`,
`knowledgeBaseIds`, `contextOwner`, `callOverrides`). `AiStreamRequest`
and `AiGenerateRequest` extend it; embedding, rerank and image requests
extend `AiRequest` and have no conversation. The IPC schemas split the
same way (`aiRequestShape` / `aiChatRequestShape`).
- **Pipeline** — `src/main/ai/provider/sdkConfig.ts` is the
modality-agnostic transport core (`resolveSdkConfig`: provider config +
wire model id + `providerOptions` namespace). `buildAgentParams` is
chat-only and layers tools, prompt, context and fallbacks on top.
`AiService.embedMany` / `rerank` / `generateImage` call the core
directly instead of the chat pipeline.
- **Provider** — builders never read request context.
`buildOpenCodeGoConfig` only declares `ProviderConfig.conversationHeader
= 'x-opencode-session'` (unless the user configured the header
explicitly); `buildAgentOptions` fills it from
`request.conversation.id`, and caller-supplied headers win.
- **Callers** state the conversation where the request is born: the
three chat context providers and agent-session runtime turns pass the
topic (raw agent session id as the conversation), `streamPrompt` passes
the stream id or the trusted agent session, `TopicNamingService` its
topic, `checkModel`'s text probe one id per probe, and the
`ai.text.generate` handler one id per renderer call. `chatId` is no
longer rewritten for gateway streams.

Fixes #

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The root cause is structural, not a missing parameter: different kinds
of requests shared one pipeline that could not tell them apart, so any
chat-specific requirement pushed into it had to become either optional
(silently absent on every path but the one that added it) or fabricated
for callers that have no conversation at all. Giving the pipeline a
modality axis lets the requirement live where it is meaningful and
nowhere else.

The following tradeoffs were made:

- `conversation` is required on `AiChatRequest` and absent from the
other request types. There is no optional context parameter and no
fallback anywhere below the caller; `ProviderConfig.conversationHeader?`
is provider capability metadata ("absent" is a real value), not request
context.
- Callers without a topic (health probes, renderer one-shot
`ai.text.generate`) mint one id per call at the call site. That is the
caller stating its unit of work, not a default inside shared code.
- `resolveSdkConfig` moved to `provider/` so the transport core no
longer lives inside the chat params module; `SdkConfig` is re-exported
from `params/scope.ts` for existing importers.
- `chatId` stays on `AiStreamRequest` as the stream manager's topic key;
`ConversationRef.topicId` carries the same value below the pipeline
boundary. Collapsing the two is left for a follow-up.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Keeping `sessionId` optional on the provider config and passing it
from more call sites — rejected; every future path would still have to
remember.
- Making a required identity on the shared base and stamping it inside
`AiService` — rejected; the verbs do not own that fact, and non-chat
callers would have to invent one.
- A `randomUUID()` fallback inside the OpenCode builder — rejected; a
builder must not invent a conversation.
- A provider-keyed header table in `buildAgentParams` — rejected; a
second per-provider dispatch next to the existing builder table.

Links to places where the discussion took place: #18184 introduced the
optional `sessionId`.

### Breaking changes

None for users. Main-internal API: `AiBaseRequest` is replaced by
`AiRequest` / `AiChatRequest`; `AsInProcess` no longer carries chat-only
sinks (`AsInProcessChat` does); `AiStreamRequest` and
`AiGenerateRequest` require `conversation`; `AiGenerateRequest.chatId`
is removed; `ProviderToAiSdkConfigOptions.sessionId` is removed.

### Special notes for your reviewer

- Deleted the two behavior-pinning tests that asserted `sessionId`
forwarding, and replaced them with contracts: the OpenCode builder
declares (and does not declare when the user configured the header),
`buildAgentParams` fills the declared header from the conversation with
caller headers winning, and the stream manager's conversation decisions
(`AiStreamManager.test`).
- `AiService.test` now spies `resolveTransportFor` for embedding /
rerank / image tests instead of the chat pipeline.
- `docs/references/ai/provider-resolution.md` and `params-pipeline.md`
describe the transport core, the chat-only pipeline and the "builders
declare, the chat pipeline fulfils" rule.
- Verified locally: `tsgo` main project clean; vitest over
`src/main/ai`, `features/apiGateway`, `features/knowledge`,
`shared/ipc`, the IPC `ai` handler and `TopicNamingService` (428 files /
6388 tests green); eslint, biome and `oxlint --deny-warnings` on changed
files; `pnpm docs:check`.
- Follow-up (separate PR): split `checkModel`'s probe dispatch into a
per-modality table and move the image job branch out of `AiService`.

feat(provider-registry): add DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Expires-On model (#20234)

### What this PR does

Before this PR: the DeepSeek catalog exposes `deepseek-v4-flash`,
`deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`, and `deepseek-v4-pro`, but not the
`deepseek-v4.1-flash-expires-on-0910` variant.

After this PR: adds `deepseek-v4.1-flash-expires-on-0910` as a vision
model (text + image input) to the DeepSeek creator, so it appears in the
model catalog. It mirrors the existing `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`
entry (same `deepseek-flash` family, peak pricing, and effort reasoning
controls).

Fixes #

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The new variant is a text + image model, so it is modeled after the
existing V4 Flash Vision Exp entry rather than the text-only
`deepseek-v4-flash`. Since it is an experimental/expiring SKU not
present in models.dev/OpenRouter, it is declared by hand in
`src/creators/deepseek.ts` with full metadata.

The following tradeoffs were made:

- The registry id is canonicalized at build/runtime
(`deepseek-v4.1-flash-expires-on-0910` →
`deepseek-v4-1-flash-expires-on`; the dot becomes a hyphen and the
trailing `-0910` is stripped as a date suffix). The display `name` keeps
the original `DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Expires-On-0910`.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Adding `imagePixelBudget` / `imageMaxBytes` as new schema fields. Not
done: neither field exists anywhere in the registry schema
(`ModelConfigSchema`) or the runtime `Model` type, and `metadata` is
reset to `{}` by the generator. Vision support is instead expressed
through `inputModalities: ['text', 'image']` plus the
`image-recognition` capability.
- Adding a provider override in `src/providers/deepseek.ts` so the model
is served by the DeepSeek endpoint. Out of scope for this change (the
attached file was the creator only); can be added separately with an
`apiModelId` mapping back to the dotted wire id.

After this PR:

- Read the operating system's machine ID through pinned
`systeminformation`, normalize it, and produce an application-specific
digest without transmitting the raw ID.
- Submit `machine_code` during cloud login and include
`Cherry-Machine-Code` in signature v2 for every signed request,
including refresh.

The server must recognize the same computer after local credentials are
cleared, without confusing signing-key identity with machine identity.

OS-provided machine IDs can change after OS reinstallation or be
duplicated by cloning. The digest is cached only in memory, not copied

introduced.

The following alternatives were considered:

Public-key hashes alone do not survive key regeneration. Moving
credential files does not identify the computer. Deriving signing

commits.commit_title: feat(image-export): pixel-faithful message image export via Chromium compositor (#20089)
commits.commit_message:
feat(image-export): pixel-faithful message image export via Chromium compositor (#20089)

## Motivation

"Save as image" / "Copy as image" for messages goes through
`html-to-image`'s DOM-clone pipeline (clone → inline computed styles →
serialize into SVG `foreignObject` → re-rasterize). That is a second
rendering pipeline, structurally unable to match what the page shows:

- fallback-font metrics re-lay-out text inside frozen width/height boxes
→ clipped overflows (the reason `captureScrollable` waits on
`document.fonts.ready` before cloning)
- clipped scroll containers need the `data-image-capturing` CSS to
unclip table viewports
- remote images hitting CORS collapse to the transparent placeholder
- `pixelRatio: window.devicePixelRatio` cannot actually sharpen the
output: the SVG is rasterized at 1× intrinsic size, so the ratio mostly
upscales

These are patched one by one today; the pipeline ceiling stays "very
close".

## Approach

Rasterize through Chromium's own compositor — CDP
`Page.captureScreenshot` with `captureBeyondViewport` (the mechanism
Puppeteer and DevTools' "capture node screenshot" use). The compositor
outputs what the page actually renders: same fonts, same layout, same
effects, including content scrolled out of view.
`webContents.capturePage` cannot do this (clips to the visible viewport
— electron#17834).

- **`window.capture_screenshot` IPC route** (`window` domain: acts on
the caller's own window via `WindowManager`, per the domain's scope
guard). Input: `clip` in page-space CSS px + `scale`, zod-validated.
- **`captureScreenshotViaCdp`** (`src/main/utils/cdpScreenshot.ts`):
stateless attach → capture → detach per request; if a session is already
attached it is reused but never detached. Deliberately not shared with
the browser MCP controller's CDP usage — that one is a session-style
attach with `Page`/`Runtime` domains enabled and tab lifecycle
management; this path needs none of that and must not depend on the MCP
feature.
- **Clip recipe** mirrors DevTools: element rect relative to
`document.documentElement` rect, sized by `scrollWidth/Height` so
capture-only CSS expansion (wide tables) stays inside.
- **Renderer**: `captureScrollableImage` is native-first; the
html-to-image pipeline remains as automatic fallback for attach
conflicts, oversized clips (> 16384 composited px) and IPC failures —
behavior never gets worse than today.
- **Scale**: CDP `clip.scale` multiplies on top of the device scale
factor; passing `1` yields exactly on-screen pixel density.
- During capture the element is temporarily expanded (`overflow:
visible; height: auto`) so clipped scroll content is rendered for the
compositor — the real-DOM equivalent of the style override the clone
path applies — then inline styles and `scrollTop` are restored.

## Verification

- Unit: 19 main-side (6 new for `cdpScreenshot`, 3 for the handler) and
full renderer suite 10998 passed; 6 new renderer cases cover native
success, fallback, oversize skip, style/marker restoration and the blob
path.
- `pnpm lint` (format + typecheck + i18n:check) clean.
- End-to-end probe on Electron 41.8.0 with a 500 px-tall window vs 921
px of content: CDP output 2992×3684 px contains the out-of-viewport tail
marker (verified at pixel level), while a `capturePage` control image
only covers 368 CSS px — the old limitation, and the new path covering
it.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

- The daily / weekdays / weekly schedule presets accept a single time of
day. Running the same task at, say, 09:00 and 18:00 requires duplicate
tasks, or asking the agent to author a cron expression — which the
settings form then displays as an uneditable "Custom schedule"
placeholder.
- Editing such an agent-authored multi-time task offers no way to see or
adjust its times from the UI.

After this PR:

- The time control of the daily / weekdays / weekly presets accepts
multiple hours with a shared minute (multi-select combobox), persisted
as a cron hour list such as `0 9,18 * * *` — a shape the croner-based
scheduler and the agent-facing `cron` tool already support end to end.
- Multi-time cron expressions project back into the preset controls when
editing: an agent-authored task like `30 9,18 * * *` now opens as
"Daily, hours 09 + 18, minute 30" instead of a read-only custom label,

expression) is unchanged; the presets remain a bidirectional projection

format" architecture used by n8n's Schedule Trigger and Home Assistant's

- All times of one preset share a single minute. Cron fields are
independent, so per-entry minutes would cross-product into extra firings

minute keeps the preset honest about what the underlying cron can

- Raw cron authoring stays out of the form, respecting the deliberate
simplification in #17332.

- Re-adding a raw cron expression input — previously rejected in #17332

- Multiple triggers per schedule row (systemd `OnCalendar=` lines / Home

scheduler schema changes and overlaps with the in-flight interval

commits.commit_message:
fix(registry-sync): restore catalog publishing and refresh older schema dirs (#20208)

<!-- Template from
https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md?-->
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:
1. Consider creating this PR as draft:
https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

> ### Branch strategy
>
> - Active development targets `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

Two defects kept the provider-registry catalog from reaching users.
First, `Sync provider-registry data` has failed on every run since
#20056 bumped the schema to v2: the frozen `compat/v2-validator.mjs`
externalizes `semver` (reached through `registry-loader.ts`), so the
workflow's bare `node` invocation died with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and
`v2/` was never published. Second, the workflow only ever refreshes the
*current* `v{N}/` dir, so the moment the schema bumped, every shipped
client on schema v1 (2.0.9–2.0.12) silently stopped receiving catalog
updates, with no recovery date.

After this PR:

The job installs `semver` into the checkout before running any baseline,
so the publish job works again without touching the immutable v2 bundle;
the baseline generator now inlines every dependency and asserts the
emitted bundle imports only `node:` builtins, so v3 onward will not need
that step. Every published `v{N}/` is refreshed rather than just the
current one: an older dir gets the catalog down-converted against its
own frozen validator, dropping only the values that schema cannot
represent — the same degradation `schemas/forwardCompat.ts` performs
inside a v2+ client, moved to publish time for clients too old to do it
themselves. Verified end to end against the real catalog and the real
published `v1/manifest.json`: both dirs are accepted by their own frozen
validator, `v2/` is byte-identical to source, and `v1/` keeps all 1442
overrides with only the unknown `ultra` effort removed, so 2.0.9–2.0.12
users get `gpt-6-astra` without waiting for a release.

<!-- (optional, in `fixes #<issue number>(, fixes #<issue_number>, ...)`
format, will close the issue(s) when PR gets merged)*: -->

Fixes # N/A

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The frozen validator is the only authority on what a given schema
version can parse, so it is used as the oracle: prune the array element
each reported `issue.path` points at, revalidate, repeat. A break that
is not an array element (a renamed or retyped field) cannot be pruned,
and that version simply stops being refreshed instead of failing the run
— the v1 stream then ends on its own, with no manual policy to maintain.
An older dir keeps the `minAppVersion` recorded in its already-published
manifest, so no new source of truth is introduced.

The following tradeoffs were made:

- The v1 stream keeps its published semantic floor of `2.0.9`, so
2.0.9–2.0.12 can receive rows whose newest semantics their runtime
renders imperfectly (Astra's tiered pricing, for example). This was
chosen over an indefinite update freeze for every currently released
user.
- The `semver` install stays in the workflow for as long as v2 is
published, because a frozen baseline cannot be repaired in place. It is
scoped to a scratch prefix and copied in as a single package, so it
never reifies this repo's dependency tree.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Regenerating `compat/v2-validator.mjs` so it is dependency-free —
implemented first, then reverted: `compat:policy` compares baselines
byte-for-byte against the base ref and rejects any modification, and
that guard is right even though `v2/` has never been published.
- Leaving `v1/` frozen and relying on shipping 2.0.13 — rejected because
it strands every currently released user with no recovery date.

commits.commit_title: fix(agent-task): keep run log session link for failed and cancelled runs (#20200)
commits.commit_message:
fix(agent-task): keep run log session link for failed and cancelled runs (#20200)

> ### Branch strategy
>
> - Active development targets `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

The task run log resolved its "view session" link from
`job.output.sessionId`. `JobManager.finalizeJob` only persists `output`
on success, so a fire that had already produced a reply or tool calls
and then errored, timed out, or was cancelled lost the link. The "view
session" button disappeared from that row and refreshing could not bring
it back, even though the session itself still existed.

After this PR:

`runAgentTask` writes the link to `job.metadata.sessionId` through
`ctx.patchMetadata` before `startAgentSessionRun`, and re-patches it
when an ownership race forces a rebind onto a replacement session.
`AgentTaskService.toTaskRunLogEntity` reads the link from metadata.
Failed, timed-out, and cancelled runs keep their "view session" button.
`sessionId` is removed from `AgentTaskOutput`, so metadata is the source
for new runs; the read mapper falls back to `output.sessionId` only for
older v2 rows that have no metadata link.

Fixes #

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

`ctx.patchMetadata` is the job runtime's existing mechanism for
persisting handler state independently of the terminal outcome (the
cross-restart hand-off pattern in
`docs/references/job-and-scheduler/handler-authoring.md`). The link is
written before the run starts, so every path that can end the run
afterwards leaves it intact. The terminal write in
`JobService.setTerminalTx` never touches the metadata column.

The following tradeoffs were made:

- Existing v2 rows retain their session links through a read-only
fallback to `output.sessionId` when the metadata link is absent. New
runs write only metadata, and metadata takes precedence after a session
rebind. No migration or dual write is needed.
- Because the link now lands before the run starts, in-flight and
cancel-requested rows also show the "view session" button. Sticky
sessions were already user-reachable mid-run, so this adds no new
hazard.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Continue writing `sessionId` in `AgentTaskOutput`. Rejected: new runs
need only the metadata link. Supporting existing persisted output in the
read mapper preserves prior logs without introducing dual writes.
- Store the link on the session row instead. Rejected: job rows are
GC'd, so a session-to-job reference would dangle; the link is a
job-owned audit trail, which is what the job row already modelled.

### Breaking changes

None. `TaskRunLogEntity.sessionId` and the DataApi endpoint are
unchanged.

### Special notes for your reviewer

The focused AgentTaskService suite passes all 35 tests. The
compatibility regression fails before the correction and passes
afterwards: old successful rows retain their output-only session link,
while metadata wins when both locations are present. Existing
failed/cancelled-run metadata coverage remains passing.

`pnpm lint` passes, including type checks, i18n validation, and
formatting.

commits.commit_message:
fix(provider): omit app attribution for custom providers (#19531)

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

Every model-provider request merged Cherry Studio's `HTTP-Referer` and
`X-Title` attribution headers, including requests sent to user-created
OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Some third-party hosts interpret those
browser-style headers as CSRF metadata; the endpoint reported in #18362
rejects the otherwise valid request with `403 CSRF_INVALID`.

After this PR:

- automatic app attribution is limited to canonical bundled and managed
providers;
- fully custom providers and custom preset clones no longer receive
automatic attribution;
- authentication and user-configured `extraHeaders` are preserved,
including explicitly configured `HTTP-Referer` or `X-Title` values;
- the same policy is applied to chat requests, model listing, Vertex
model discovery, Ollama probes, and direct Claude Agent SDK routes.

Fixes #18362

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

Provider provenance is a stable boundary that distinguishes
Cherry-managed rows from user-created endpoints without maintaining a
fragile hostname allowlist. It also preserves the existing behavior for
ordinary registry providers, grouped registry providers, and the managed
CherryAI provider.

The following tradeoffs were made:

- A user-created clone of a bundled provider does not inherit automatic
attribution. Users who need it can add the headers explicitly through
`extraHeaders`.
- Editing the endpoint of the canonical bundled provider still retains
its existing attribution behavior; this PR targets the reported
user-created-provider flow.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Removing attribution globally would risk regressions for providers
that rely on it.
- Matching known hosts would be brittle for proxies, regional domains,
and future endpoint changes.

Links to places where the discussion took place: #18362

### Special notes for your reviewer

The request-boundary regression runs through `providerToAiSdkConfig`,
`createExecutor`, and the AI SDK model's `doGenerate` call. It verifies
that the final wire request keeps Bearer authentication and explicit
user headers while omitting only automatic attribution for a custom
provider.

commits.commit_title: fix(word-export): render indented code, ordered lists, images and strikethrough (#20197)
commits.commit_message:
fix(word-export): render indented code, ordered lists, images and strikethrough (#20197)

> ### Branch strategy
>
> - Active development targets `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

The markdown-to-docx converter in `ExportService` handles block and
inline tokens through a `switch` with no `default` branch, so any
markdown-it token it does not name is dropped silently while the export
still reports success. Four kinds of content were affected:

- Four-space-indented code (`code_block`) lost its whole body; only
fenced code was rendered.
- Ordered lists came out as unindented `•` bullets, and a nested ordered
list did not push the indent level.
- Images vanished together with their alt text.
- `~~strikethrough~~` lost its formatting.

The code box also opened and closed with an empty line, because every
line was preceded by a line break and the trailing newline of the block
was kept.

After this PR:

- `code_block` shares the fenced-code handler, so indented code renders
as the same Consolas shaded box.
- Ordered lists are numbered from their `start` value and indent
correctly when nested (a `listCounters` stack replaces the bullet-only
`listLevel` counter).
- Image alt text is exported as plain text, built per token type so
multi-line alt keeps its word boundaries.
- Struck text carries `strike` in the docx run.
- Code boxes no longer have a leading or trailing blank line (fenced and
indented alike).
- Headings render their inline markdown (image alt text, strikethrough,
bold, links, inline code) through the same run path as paragraphs
instead of exporting the raw source. Runs omit off flags rather than
writing them as `false`, which would override the heading styles
(Heading 4 is italic by default).
- A list item whose first block is a code fence, a blockquote or a
nested list keeps its number or bullet; the block is rendered below the
marker. Fenced and indented code blocks inherit the active list and
quote indentation, including mixed nested lists.

Fixes # N/A

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

Users writing notes in source mode with indented code, numbered lists,
images, or strikethrough got a Word file that looked complete but
silently omitted content. The fix keeps the existing token-switch
structure and adds the missing cases in place, matching how the
neighbouring handlers are written.

The following tradeoffs were made:

- Line breaks inside image alt text become a space rather than `\n`:
`\n` inside a `<w:t>` element is not rendered as a break by Word, and
this converter already emits a space for soft breaks in prose.
- Inline code inside alt text keeps its words. markdown-it skips
`code_inline` when rendering an HTML `alt` attribute, but in Word the
alt text is the only visible placeholder for the image, so dropping
words would leave the description incomplete.

> ### Branch strategy

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

Cherry Studio did not catalog GPT-6 Astra or apply its model-specific
context, reasoning, pricing, and request-parameter contracts. OpenAI API
and ChatGPT OAuth/Codex also require different Astra capabilities and
token limits.

After this PR:

Cherry Studio supports `gpt-6-astra` end to end:

- OpenAI API: 1,050,000-token context, 922,000-token maximum input,
128,000-token maximum output, reasoning through `max`, Responses API,
native web search, and Astra-compatible request filtering.
- ChatGPT OAuth/OpenAI Codex: 272,000-token context, 144,000-token
maximum input, inherited 128,000-token maximum output, `low` as the
default reasoning effort, Codex-only `ultra`, and Fast mode. Existing
Codex SKUs retain their own upstream reasoning ladders and defaults.
- Official long-context pricing above 272,000 input tokens is
represented in the provider catalog, propagated into runtime usage
accounting, and synchronized to OpenClaw's whole-request tier format
when the installed OpenClaw schema supports it.
- Provider registry schema v2 adds tiered pricing and `ultra`, tolerates
unknown list vocabulary at the smallest droppable unit, ships a frozen
compatibility validator, and requires Cherry Studio 2.0.13 or later.
- DeepSeek raw reasoning replay remains preserved when Responses
requests use `store: false`.
- Endpoint selection remains provider-owned: OpenAI and ChatGPT Codex
use Responses, while Chat-only providers do not inherit an incompatible
model-level endpoint.
- Model display resolves `gpt-6-astra` to OpenAI's official Astra icon
from
https://developers.openai.com/images/api/models/icons/gpt-6-astra.png,
while dated and later GPT-6 Astra SKUs inherit the same model contract.

<!-- (optional, in `fixes #<issue number>(, fixes #<issue_number>, ...)`
format, will close the issue(s) when PR gets merged)*: -->

Fixes #20144

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

GPT-6 Astra has provider-specific limits and rejects parameters accepted
by older OpenAI models. The provider catalog, shared reasoning
vocabulary, renderer controls, runtime model injection, usage
accounting, and patched SDK transport therefore need to agree on the
same contract.

The following tradeoffs were made:

- Keep `@ai-sdk/openai` on the latest AI SDK 6-compatible release,
`3.0.109`, and narrowly patch the missing Astra behavior instead of
taking a repository-wide AI SDK 7 migration.
- Scope `ultra` to the exact `gpt-6-astra` Codex path. Standard OpenAI
API metadata intentionally ends at `max`.
- Version the provider registry schema because tiered pricing and
`ultra` change the catalog contract. The frozen v1 validator remains
unchanged, while v2 validates increasing tier thresholds and a single
currency across base and tier prices.
- Preserve independent model-limit inheritance so the Codex override
narrows context and input limits without dropping Astra's 128,000-token
output limit.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Upgrading directly to `@ai-sdk/openai@4.x`, rejected because it moves
to AI SDK 7 / `LanguageModelV4` and requires a repository-wide major
migration outside this PR.
- Advertising `ultra` for standard OpenAI API, rejected because the
supported contract is Codex-only.
- Treating long-context pricing as a flat price, rejected because it
would undercount usage above the official 272,000-token threshold.
- Relying only on remote model discovery, rejected because it would omit
documented token limits, reasoning controls, request compatibility,
native-tool eligibility, and deterministic offline catalog behavior.

commits.commit_title: Fix video_understand sampling only the opening seconds of a clip
commits.commit_message:
Fix video_understand sampling only the opening seconds of a clip

_extract_video_frames built `-vf thumbnail=N -frames:v N` when no explicit
frame_indices were given. That reads as even sampling and is not: thumbnail=N
selects the most representative frame out of each consecutive N-frame BATCH, so
paired with -frames:v N it stops once N frames have been emitted and never
looks at the rest of the video.

Reproduced against a four-second fixture, solid red for 2s then solid blue
for 2s:

  ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -frames:v 4 -vf "thumbnail=4" out_%04d.png
  -> frame_0001 (254,0,0)  frame_0002 (254,0,0)
     frame_0003 (254,0,0)  frame_0004 (254,0,0)

Every sample lands in the first half. The blue half of the clip is invisible,
and because the failure produces four perfectly valid frames the caption pass
has no way to know: it described the clip as one in which nothing changes.

Sampling is now timestamp-driven. Duration comes from ffprobe and one frame is
taken at duration*(i+0.5)/n — inside each slice rather than on its edge, so a
cut landing exactly on a boundary does not sample the frame before or after it
depending on rounding. -ss goes ahead of -i to seek by keyframe, which is fast
and accurate enough for sampling that was never frame-exact.

Same fixture, after:

  frame 0 (254,0,0)  frame 1 (254,0,0)  frame 2 (0,0,255)  frame 3 (0,0,255)

Three behaviours preserved deliberately:

  * The explicit frame_indices branch is untouched. It was already correct.
  * No duration — a stream, or no ffprobe on PATH — falls back to an even pass
    over the file rather than returning an empty list.
  * A zero or negative duration is treated as unknown, since it would otherwise
    divide the sampler by zero.

Also drops probe_cmd, which was assigned and never used.

tests/tools/test_video_understand_sampling.py adds 9 cases with subprocess.run
faked, so they assert the commands built rather than one ffmpeg build's output,
and fail if `thumbnail=` returns. tests/tools/ is 490 passed, 1 skipped.

commits.commit_title: test(stock-sources): pin the search transport-error contract
commits.commit_message:
test(stock-sources): pin the search transport-error contract

A parametrized pair over `all_sources()`, so the contract is asserted for
every registered adapter rather than the eight that happened to be wrong,
and a new source cannot quietly reintroduce the bug.

  - a failing transport propagates out of `search()`
  - a genuine 200 carrying no results still returns `[]`

Both halves matter. Fixing only the first would let an adapter "pass" by
raising on everything, which breaks the empty-result case the corpus
builder relies on.

Eight of the propagation cases fail against the unfixed adapters. Three
-- archive_org, wikimedia and pond5_pd -- still swallow errors through a
different shape (a query cascade that continues past a failed strategy,
and an API failure that falls through to the web fallback) and are marked
`xfail(strict=True)` pending the follow-up. That records them as known
defects instead of encoding the bug as expected behavior, and fails the
suite the moment one is fixed and left in the map.

`requests` and `bs4` are stubbed via `sys.modules`, following the
fake-requests pattern in test_atlas_video.py. bs4 is stubbed because it is
an optional dependency that the scraping adapters import at the top of
`search()` -- left alone, those five would fail on the import rather than
on the request wherever bs4 is not installed, and pass for the wrong
reason.

Refs #511

commits.commit_title: fix(stock-sources): raise transport errors instead of reporting no results
commits.commit_message:
fix(stock-sources): raise transport errors instead of reporting no results

Eight adapters -- dareful, esa, jaxa, loc, mixkit, nara, noaa, videvo --
wrapped their search request in `except Exception`, logged a warning and
returned `[]`. That is indistinguishable from a source that genuinely
matched nothing, so `direct_clip_search` reports `success: True,
clips_downloaded: 0, errors: []` for a run in which every request failed.

`base.StockSource.search` already documents the rule they violate:
"Network errors should be raised -- the corpus builder catches and logs
per-source so one flaky API doesn't poison the whole run." Both callers
already do exactly that: `direct_clip_search` and `corpus_builder` catch
per source and record `{phase, source, query, error}` before continuing,
so the plumbing to receive the truth is already in place.

Each adapter now re-raises after logging. The warning is kept -- it names
the source in the adapter's own words, which the caller's generic record
does not.

Behavior change: a run where every source failed previously reported
success with zero clips and will now surface the errors.

Refs #511

fix(remotion-composer): resolve videoSrc through resolveAsset in TalkingHead

TalkingHead passes videoSrc straight to OffthreadVideo, so relative asset
paths (e.g. "clips/source.mp4" under public/) fail to load at render time.
Every other composition that accepts a video source (TitledVideo, Explainer,
CinematicRenderer) already routes it through resolveAsset; this brings
TalkingHead in line with them.

videoSrc before (load failure) and after (renders) this change.

commits.commit_title: feat(remotion-composer): CJK-aware captions and caption styling props
commits.commit_message:
feat(remotion-composer): CJK-aware captions and caption styling props

CaptionOverlay assumes space-delimited text: it hardcodes a " " between
words and lets lines wrap anywhere inside a word. For CJK captions this
produces spurious inter-word spaces (Japanese does not use them) and
mid-word line breaks, including punctuation stranded at line starts.

Changes:
- CaptionOverlay: new wordSeparator prop (default " " keeps current
  behavior; CJK callers pass ""). Each word renders as an unbreakable
  inline block so lines wrap only at word boundaries - visually unchanged
  for space-delimited text, fixes mid-word breaks for CJK.
- WordCaption: optional pageBreakAfter flag; buildPages flushes the page
  early when set, so pages can align with sentence/scene boundaries
  instead of splitting a clause across pages.
- TalkingHead: exposes captionColor / captionBackgroundColor (previously
  hardcoded inline), captionFontFamily, and captionWordSeparator, all
  defaulting to the current values.

Tested by rendering TalkingHead stills with Japanese captions before and
after (screenshots in PR), and with default props to confirm the
space-delimited rendering is unchanged. Used in production for Japanese
vertical ad videos.

commits.commit_title: Add contract tests for chart text colour on dark themes
commits.commit_message:
Add contract tests for chart text colour on dark themes

Follows the existing source-assertion style in this file. Both tests fail
against the pre-fix Explainer and pass after it:

- charts must receive textColor={textColor}, or their labels render
  dark-on-dark (the components default textColor to #1F2937)
- ComparisonCard must get a themed cardBackgroundColor, or its labels
  render light-on-light (the component hardcodes #F3F4F6)

commits.commit_title: Fix: forward theme text colour to chart scenes and theme the comparison card
commits.commit_message:
Fix: forward theme text colour to chart scenes and theme the comparison card

Chart scenes are unreadable on any dark theme. BarChart, LineChart,
PieChart and KPIGrid all default `textColor` to #1F2937 (near-black),
but Explainer only ever passed them `backgroundColor` - so on a dark
theme every title, axis label, category label and value renders
dark-on-dark.

ComparisonCard has the mirror-image bug: it *does* receive the theme's
`textColor`, but hardcodes `cardBackgroundColor = "#F3F4F6"`, painting
light text onto a light card.

Forward `textColor` to the four chart components, and give
ComparisonCard `cut.cardBackgroundColor || theme.surfaceColor` so its
surface follows the theme. Adds `cardBackgroundColor?: string` to the
Cut interface for a per-cut override.

Verified by re-rendering a 7-scene explainer on a dark theme: chart
title, y-axis scale, category labels and per-bar values are all legible,
and the comparison card labels now show on a themed surface.

commits.commit_title: fix(playbook_loader): load generated playbooks from styles/custom/
commits.commit_message:
fix(playbook_loader): load generated playbooks from styles/custom/

lib/playbook_generator.save_playbook() writes generated playbooks to
styles/custom/, and the skills tell agents to save them there
(skills/meta/capability-extension.md, the animation and explainer
proposal directors). But this loader globs only the styles/ root, and it
is the loader tools/video/video_compose.py imports — so every generated
playbook was invisible at render time. The only way to make one work was
to hand-copy it up one directory, which is why custom playbooks end up
duplicated in both places.

Search styles/custom/ as a fallback in load_playbook() and merge it into
list_playbooks(), matching the semantics lib/playbook_generator.py
already uses: a preset wins when both exist, and the listing is deduped.
The not-found error now names both directories it searched instead of
just the last path it tried.

commits.commit_message:
【安全修复 GHSA-4c6j-45p9-rhrw】填值规则管理接口缺少权限校验

/sys/fillRule 的 list、queryById、exportXls、importExcel 四个接口缺少 @RequiresRoles({"admin"})，
任意登录用户（含零角色新注册账号）可导出全部填值规则（ruleCode/ruleClass/ruleParams）并新增规则记录。
补齐 admin 角色限制，与 add/edit/delete/testFillRule 保持一致；
executeRuleByCode 供 Online 表单调用，按公告建议不加限制。

commits.commit_title: --author:JEECG--date:20260713--for:【vite8】消除 dev server 启动时两条 WARN（esbuildOptions 废弃、esbuild/oxc 同时设置）
commits.commit_message:
--author:JEECG--date:20260713--for:【vite8】消除 dev server 启动时两条 WARN（esbuildOptions 废弃、esbuild/oxc 同时设置）

按 Vite 8 Rolldown/Oxc 的迁移规范，把两处已废弃的 esbuild 配置迁到新写法：

1. optimizeDeps.esbuildOptions.target: 'es2020' → optimizeDeps.rolldownOptions.transform.target: 'es2020'
   （消除 esbuildOptions deprecated 警告）

2. 顶层 esbuild: { drop: isBuild ? ['console', 'debugger'] : [] } + build.minify: 'esbuild'
   → 删除 esbuild 块，build.minify: true 改用 Oxc minifier，
   drop 功能迁移到 build.rollupOptions.output.minify: { compress: { drop: ['console', 'debugger'] } }
   （消除 esbuild/oxc 同时设置的警告，并保留生产构建删除 console.debugger 的能力）

commits.commit_title: feat(tg): collapse context compaction notices into one edited message
commits.commit_message:
feat(tg): collapse context compaction notices into one edited message

Context compaction previously posted two separate chat messages: a
'Compressing context…' notice when compaction started and a follow-up
'Context compacted.' once it finished.

The Telegram channel now collapses this into a single message: the
started phase posts the notice and remembers its message id, and a
terminal phase (succeeded/failed/cancelled) edits that same message in
place instead of posting another. If the edit fails, a fresh message
keeps the outcome visible. Notices are keyed by compaction id and
bounded, so concurrent or abandoned compactions cannot leak state.

commits.commit_title: fix(discord): update the compaction notice in place instead of sending a second message
commits.commit_message:
fix(discord): update the compaction notice in place instead of sending a second message

Automatic compaction delivered two standalone Discord messages,
"Compressing context…" and "Context compacted.", even with
sendProgress off. The lifecycle itself is information the user should
keep seeing (it changes the context of every later turn), so the
dispatcher keeps delivering both events to every channel; the noise is
a presentation problem of the Discord adapter.

The Discord client now remembers the message it sent for a compaction's
"started" event, keyed by compaction_id, and edits that message with the
outcome when it arrives, so one compaction is one message. Without a
stored notice (restart, or the edit being refused) the outcome is sent
as before. The earlier dispatcher-level filtering is dropped, and the
manager test pins that both lifecycle events reach a channel whose
progress messages are off.

Fixes #5719

commits.commit_title: fix(channels): keep the compaction outcome visible, gate only the start notice
commits.commit_message:
fix(channels): keep the compaction outcome visible, gate only the start notice

Rework after review: compaction changes the context of every later turn,
so its outcome (compacted / failed / cancelled) is always delivered,
whether the user or the scheduler started it. Only the transient
"Compressing context…" start notice follows the channel's send_progress
setting, so a channel with progress off receives one notice per
compaction instead of two. The manual flag is gone.

commits.commit_title: fix(channels): make automatic compaction notices follow send_progress
commits.commit_message:
fix(channels): make automatic compaction notices follow send_progress

Idle auto-compaction emitted "Compressing context…" / "Context compacted."
as standalone messages even when the channel had sendProgress: false, so
routine maintenance kept interrupting Discord chats after scheduled turns.

Gate ContextCompactionEvent notices in the outbound dispatch loop on the
channel's send_progress like other progress text. Two cases stay visible
regardless of the setting: a user-requested /compact (the event now
carries manual=True, set by cmd_compact through compact_idle_session)
and a failed compaction.

Fixes #5719

The Telegram channel forwards slash commands through an allowlist regex
that must mirror the builtin command router. /compact and
/evaluator-prompt were missing from it, and messages starting with '/'
never reach the generic text handler, so both commands were silently
dropped: pressing /compact did nothing at all.

Add both commands to the allowlist, register /compact in the Telegram
command menu, and pin the router/regex pairing in the existing regex
test.

commits.commit_title: feat(exec): add a macOS Seatbelt sandbox backend
commits.commit_message:
feat(exec): add a macOS Seatbelt sandbox backend

`tools.exec.sandbox` only supported bubblewrap, which depends on Linux
kernel namespaces, so macOS had no process-level isolation for shell
commands: SECURITY.md told macOS users the sandbox was simply
unavailable.

Add a `seatbelt` backend that generates an SBPL profile for
sandbox-exec(1) with the same policy bwrap applies. The workspace is
read-write, the media directory is read-only, the workspace's parent is
unreadable so config.json and its API keys stay hidden, and everything
else is denied by default.

Two macOS details the profile has to get right, both found by running
the generated command rather than by reading the SBPL reference:

- sh(1) reads `/` while resolving a path, and `(subpath "/usr")` does
  not cover the root itself. Without `(literal "/")` every wrapped
  command aborts during shell startup.
- Denying the parent directory also blocks traversal into the
  workspace, so commands fail with ENOTDIR before they run. The
  ancestors of every allowed path are therefore re-allowed for
  `file-read-metadata` only: they stay searchable, but the config
  directory still cannot be listed or read.

Paths are SBPL-escaped so a quote or backslash in a workspace path
cannot terminate a literal early and widen the rules that follow it.

Network access stays unrestricted to match bwrap, which does not pass
`--unshare-net`. Windows keeps its existing warn-and-run-unsandboxed
path, and selecting `seatbelt` on Linux fails loudly on the missing
sandbox-exec(1) exactly as selecting `bwrap` does on macOS today.

Verified on macOS 26.6.2 against the real sandbox-exec(1): workspace
writes, media reads and /tmp scratch succeed, while writing media,
reading config.json, listing the config directory, writing outside the
workspace and reading ~/.ssh are all denied.

Refs #1448
Refs #2569

commits.commit_title: test(mcp): keep reconnect fixture idle across SDK versions
commits.commit_message:
test(mcp): keep reconnect fixture idle across SDK versions

MCP SDK 1.30 treats an open GET notification stream as an in-flight request, so the real-server fixture no longer expires its session and the shutdown regression waits forever for a reconnect that never starts.

Decline the optional notification stream with the protocol-defined HTTP 405 response while retaining real POST, DELETE, lifespan, idle expiry and reconnect handling. Assert that successful recovery replaces the tool wrapper so the first regression cannot pass without reconnecting.

Reproduced the failure with SDK 1.30 before the repair. Both 1.29 and 1.30 now pass, including five repeated 1.30 runs and 141 related MCP tests. Runtime code and timeout limits are unchanged.

NAN-104 requires terminal chat and browser attachment without granting a client ownership of Desktop's gateway. Resolve bounded short-lived credentials over authenticated current-user IPC, pin both Desktop and gateway identities, and reject replacement instances or incompatible clients before any mutation.

Reuse the existing TUI artifact resolver behind a narrow Desktop-only entrypoint, keep credentials out of argv/environment/files, and preserve Python-mode reconnect and gateway leases. commits.commit_message:
fix(cli): protect Windows browser credential handoff [skip ci]

Windows browser dispatch can expose bootstrap credentials through BROWSER or native handler command arguments. Send the URL to an isolated helper over stdin and open an owner-only ACL-protected redirect file instead, with no raw-URL fallback.

Keep file ownership and bounded cleanup independent of CLI exit, reject unsafe storage, and cover shared callers, native API contracts, error paths and lifecycle regressions. Document the intentional Windows compatibility tightening; native Windows browser and ACL verification remains pending.

Cover encoding, native failures, resource cleanup and Desktop dispatch with regression tests. Preserve existing browser behavior and leave TUI and non-macOS handoff changes outside this scoped repair.

commits.commit_title: fix(linkai): recurse into _send when retrying a failed midjourney reply
commits.commit_message:
fix(linkai): recurse into _send when retrying a failed midjourney reply

The plugin's _send is a copy of ChatChannel._send, which retries a failed
send twice with a 3s/6s backoff by recursing into itself
(channel/chat_channel.py:447). This copy forwarded the retry counter to
channel.send instead:

    channel.send(reply, context, retry_cnt + 1)

Every channel declares send(self, reply, context) (channel/channel.py:133,
and the same two-argument signature in all 14 channel implementations), so
the extra positional argument made the retry raise

    TypeError: send() takes 3 positional arguments but 4 were given

Because that is raised inside the except block it escapes _send instead of
being retried, so the reply is never delivered and the exception kills the
task-polling thread that _process_success_task runs on. Forwarding the
counter to _send restores the retry and its bound.

commits.commit_title: fix(linkai): classify media urls from the parsed url path
commits.commit_message:
fix(linkai): classify media urls from the parsed url path

_send_image decided the reply type from the complete raw url, and
_download_file derived the saved file name the same way. Both read the
whole string instead of the parsed path, so:

- a media url carrying query parameters was not matched at all --
  ".../clip.mp4?token=abc" fell through to IMAGE_URL, so returned videos
  and documents were sent as images
- extension matching was case-sensitive -- ".../clip.MP4" was sent as an
  image
- ".../download?name=report.pdf" matched ".pdf" but produced the local
  file name "download?name=report.pdf"; "?" is not a legal file name
  character on Windows, so open() raised OSError [Errno 22] and the file
  was silently dropped

Parse the url once and match on its path instead. The same pattern was
applied to the keyword plugin in #3061.

commits.commit_title: fix(voice): decode silk into its own wav before re-encoding to mp3
commits.commit_message:
fix(voice): decode silk into its own wav before re-encoding to mp3

any_to_mp3 decoded silk onto any_path -- the caller's own voice file -- and
then repointed any_path at mp3_path, which had not been written yet. Every
silk conversion therefore failed with FileNotFoundError, and the file the
caller fell back to had already been replaced by wav bytes.

This is reachable: the WeChat channel saves inbound voice as .silk, and both
the DashScope and ZhipuAI ASR paths route .silk/.slk through any_to_mp3, so
those voice messages never transcribe and the cached audio is left corrupt.

Decode into a sibling .wav instead, re-encode from it, and remove it in a
finally. The .wav name matters: pydub reads a file with the stdlib wave module
when the path ends in .wav, and only reaches for ffprobe otherwise.

commits.commit_title: fix(translate): report the api error when every baidu retry fails
commits.commit_message:
fix(translate): report the api error when every baidu retry fails

translate() retries the transient error codes 52001/52002 up to three
times. When the third attempt fails too the loop exits on an exhausted
retry counter, and the code then read result["trans_result"] from an
error payload that has no such field, so callers saw a bare
KeyError: 'trans_result' instead of the reason the request failed.

Raise the api error message on that path, so an exhausted retry reports
what actually went wrong. The other branches are unchanged.

commits.commit_title: feat(web): edit a provider's model catalog from the console
commits.commit_message:
feat(web): edit a provider's model catalog from the console

The backend has carried a per-provider model catalog for a while — entries
with capability tags, a context window and a max output budget — and the
models API already returns both what is saved (catalog) and the vendor's
presets typed with their real capabilities (seed). Nothing rendered them, so
the only way to use the feature was hand-editing config.json.

Add an editor to both provider modals, collapsed under an "Advanced" heading
since it is opt-in: a catalog REPLACES a vendor's preset model list, so the
section stays shut until the user has a reason to open it.

- rows for each entry: name, capability chips, context window, max output
- "restore presets" seeds the draft from the vendor's preset models, so
  editing an override starts from the real values instead of a blank row
- embedding / image / asr / tts entries have no text budget, so their window
  and output inputs are hidden — and cleared if the tags change — rather than
  inviting numbers that mean nothing
- the row list scrolls on its own and each modal is height-capped, so a long
  catalog cannot push the save button off screen
- saved as a separate request, and only when the draft differs from what is
  stored: writing it on every credentials save would silently wipe a list the
  user never opened

Tests: 21 covering the seed/catalog fields the editor reads, the save
handler it posts to, and the normalization rules it relies on.

fix(baidu): reply with an error instead of crashing on image-create

BaiduWenxinBot inherits the bare Bot base class, which defines no
create_img(). The IMAGE_CREATE branch called self.create_img(query, 0)
anyway, so an image-create prefix raised AttributeError inside the
channel worker. The worker logs and swallows that exception, so the
user got no reply at all and only a traceback reached the log:

    models/baidu/baidu_wenxin.py:69, in reply
        ok, retstring = self.create_img(query, 0)
    AttributeError: 'BaiduWenxinBot' object has no attribute 'create_img'

branch now answers with the same "unsupported type" error the other
text-only bots return.

commits.commit_title: fix(desktop): always show the built-in default Agent on the team page
commits.commit_message:
fix(desktop): always show the built-in default Agent on the team page

The desktop team page could come up empty - not even the built-in CowAgent
card - so users thought their Agent was gone. The Agent was fine (its
persona lives in ~/cow/AGENT.md and it kept chatting); only the roster list
failed to render.

Two causes, both fixed:

1. Frontend (the actual trigger): on a cold start the local WSGI backend can
   be momentarily busy (an SSE stream or a concurrent poll holding threads),
   and a plain fetch then throws a bare TypeError. getAgents() went through
   the no-retry request() path (postFormData already retries the same hiccup
   for uploads), and agentStore.refresh() treated that failure as a valid
   empty roster and cleared the list. Creating an Agent still worked because
   that POST ran once the backend was idle and then refreshed - which is why
   "create works but the list is empty" looked contradictory.
   Now the roster fetch retries a few times on the transient network error
   (a real HTTP status like 401/404 stays final), and the page is never
   stranded on an empty roster: keep the last good roster, otherwise fall
   back to the same synthesized default the backend uses (id=default,
   name=CowAgent) so the built-in Agent - and its brand logo - is always
   shown.

2. Backend hardening: a config.json saved with a UTF-8 BOM (e.g. edited with
   Windows Notepad / PowerShell) made AgentAdminService._load() raise
   "Unexpected UTF-8 BOM", which surfaced as a failed /api/agents snapshot.
   commit a9dfc54c fixed the main config and web-console read paths but
   missed the roster paths; read config.json/team.json with utf-8-sig at
   agent/admin.py and agent/team.py (write-back stays plain utf-8 so the BOM
   is stripped on the next save).

Single- and multi-Agent installs and legacy backends without /api/agents are
unaffected.

Co-authored-by: cowagent <cow@cowagent.ai>

commits.commit_title: fix(models): resolve custom credentials from the routed provider, not global
commits.commit_message:
fix(models): resolve custom credentials from the routed provider, not global

When a turn is routed to a provider other than the globally configured one
— an engaged chat fallback, or a session /model override — the bot was rebuilt
with the right type, but its credentials still came from conf()["bot_type"].

The failure is silent until the two providers differ: the routed provider's
model id was sent to the primary provider's api_base, and the vendor answered

    404 {"error": {"message": "model is not found", "code": "5"}}

so the fallback (or the session override) could never take over. Reproduced
with the global bot_type on one custom vendor and the fallback link on another;
the same request succeeds once it reaches the right endpoint.

Thread the resolved provider down to the bot:

  * resolve_custom_credentials() takes an optional bot_type (None keeps the
    historical global read, so every existing caller is unaffected)
  * create_bot() gains credential_bot_type for the same purpose
  * ChatGPTBot remembers the type it was built for and uses it in __init__,
    get_api_config() and the vision path
  * AgentLLMModel.bot() passes the type it already resolved

The resolved type is identical to the global one whenever nothing is
overridden, so behavior only changes in the case that was broken.

commits.commit_title: fix(web): resolve live ChannelManager for console channel startup
commits.commit_message:
fix(web): resolve live ChannelManager for console channel startup

The console could not start a channel configured from the UI: saving a
channel whose credentials had just been filled in (e.g. a QQ bot with a
valid AppID/AppSecret) returned success, then logged

    [WebChannel] ChannelManager not available, cannot start 'qq'

and never started it, so the platform showed the bot as disconnected.

commit 87706bee (the fix for #3120) moved the manager out of app.py's
module globals into common.channel_registry, because `python app.py`
makes `__main__` a distinct module object from a later `import app`, and
reading `_channel_mgr` off `__main__` could silently yield None. That
migration missed channel/web/web_channel.py, which still looked the
manager up with

    getattr(sys.modules['__main__'], '_channel_mgr', None)

`_channel_mgr` no longer exists anywhere, so every console-side lookup
returned None: connect, disconnect, restart-on-save, the WeChat login
status badge, and channel-instance binding were all affected.

Resolve the manager through common.channel_registry at every one of those
call sites, via a small `_live_channel_manager()` helper, and add
regression tests that fail against the previous lookup.

commits.commit_title: fix(tools): report byte truncation when the kept line is partial
commits.commit_message:
fix(tools): report byte truncation when the kept line is partial

`truncate_tail` relabels the cut as "lines" after the loop whenever the kept
output fills `max_lines`, which also fires in the single-over-long-line case:
the loop breaks on the byte limit, keeps a partial line and reports
`last_line_partial=True` and `output_bytes == max_bytes`, but `truncated_by`
comes back as "lines".

With `max_lines` > 1 the same input reports "bytes", so the field was
inconsistent, and callers branch on it — agent/tools/bash/bash.py tells the
model "showing lines X-Y" for output that was actually cut mid-line.

Skip the relabel when the last line is partial: the byte limit is what cut
the output in that case, however many lines it ends up filling.

commits.commit_message:
fix(skills): ignore empty b64_json/url when saving generated images

OpenAI-compatible image results were parsed with `if "b64_json" in item`,
a key-presence check. Some backends (e.g. Agnes) still send `b64_json` in
URL output mode with an empty string alongside a usable `url`, so the old
check decoded "" and wrote a 0-byte file — the script reported success and
the failure only surfaced when the client tried to send the empty image.

Parse on the value instead of the key, falling through to the other field,
and skip items that carry no payload at all so the caller raises instead of
handing back an empty file list.

Refs #3131

commits.commit_title: fix(models): error_generator closes over the deleted `except ... as e`
commits.commit_message:
fix(models): error_generator closes over the deleted `except ... as e`

Seven bots build the stream error generator inside `except Exception as e`
and reference `str(e)` from the generator body. Python 3 unbinds the except
target when the handler exits, so by the time the caller iterates the
returned generator the closure cell is empty and the first `next()` raises
NameError instead of yielding the error chunk.

Bind `error_msg = str(e)` inside the handler and yield that, matching the
seven bots that already do it this way (openai_compatible_bot, zhipuai,
gemini, dashscope, modelscope).

Signed-off-by: Anai Guo <antai12232931@outlook.com>

commits.commit_title: fix(chat): offer real models to the fallback picker, keep Save in step
commits.commit_message:
fix(chat): offer real models to the fallback picker, keep Save in step

Two console bugs found while configuring a chain by hand.

The fallback card built its model lists straight from PROVIDER_MODELS while
the primary card ran them through _apply_catalog, so the two pickers drifted
apart: a vendor whose models came from a catalog offered a dropdown on the
primary card but only "custom" + a typed name on the fallback one. Both cards
now share one path — the vendors' presets as the base, a catalog overriding
them — which is what _chat_provider_models' own docstring claimed already
happened. The presets have to stay as the base: the primary card is driven by
its separate `providers` list, but the fallback has no such layer, so starting
from an empty map emptied the picker for every vendor without a catalog.

Separately, Save disabled itself only when the enable toggle was flipped, so
its state went stale after any edit to the chain: enabling the fallback with
no links left it disabled, and adding a link never re-enabled it. The refresh
now runs at the end of every re-render, including the empty-chain branch that
returns early — removing the last link is exactly when it must flip back.

commits.commit_title: feat(chat): walk an ordered fallback chain instead of one backup model
commits.commit_message:
feat(chat): walk an ordered fallback chain instead of one backup model

The chat fallback could only ever hold a single backup model: once
fallback_available() saw a fallback engaged it returned False for the rest of
the turn, so max_switches was never actually reachable and a second backup
could not be configured at all.

Replace the single {provider, model, max_switches} entry with an ordered chain
of links. A failing link advances to the next one rather than ending the turn,
and the walk wraps around for a second pass so a transient failure (a rate
limit that has since cleared) does not cost the user the whole turn.

- config: chat_fallback is now {enabled, chain: [{provider, model}, ...]};
  _migrate_chat_fallback() folds a pre-chain entry into a one-link chain at
  load time, so existing configs keep working and max_switches is dropped
- model: fallback_available()/use_fallback() walk the chain by index;
  links duplicating the primary or an earlier link are skipped
- executor: a link gets one attempt rather than the primary's full retry
  budget, so a long chain cannot sleep past the web channel's SSE idle
  timeout; when the chain is spent the error names every model that was
  tried instead of only the last one
- a rate limit switches immediately when a backup is configured, and keeps
  waiting it out when there is none
- web console + desktop: edit the chain as a list with add/remove/reorder

Tests: 68 covering config migration, chain walking, the rate-limit fast path,
and the nested-run scope that keeps a sub agent from rewinding its parent.

fix: make channel disconnect stick and put WeChat channels first

Disconnecting a channel had no effect on both the web console and the
desktop app. In multi-Agent mode a legacy channel (enabled via config.json
channel_type) is folded into channel_instances by bootstrap_legacy_instances,
which runs on every team.json write. Removing the instance record alone was
immediately undone: the next write re-materialized it straight from
channel_type, so the card came right back.

- Prune the type from channel_type when disconnecting its last instance, so
  the bootstrap has nothing to recreate.
- Route disconnect/rename without an instance_id to the legacy per-type path
  instead of rejecting it with "instance_id is required".
- Surface disconnect failures on both clients (web toast, desktop status)
  and refresh the desktop list silently so it no longer jumps to the top.
- Show WeChat channels first in the connected list (stable sort).
- Add regression tests covering the dispatch routing and the bootstrap
  re-materialization bug.

commits.commit_message:
feat: add Keenable as a keyless web_search provider

Keenable (https://keenable.ai) is a web search API whose public endpoint
works without an API key, so web_search is now available on a fresh install
instead of being unregistered until a vendor key is configured. The
provider is appended last in PROVIDER_ORDER, so any provider the user has
configured still wins under the auto strategy.

- web_search.py: `keenable` backend. Without a key it calls
  POST /v1/search/public with an `X-Keenable-Title: cowagent` header; with
  `tools.web_search.keenable_api_key` / `KEENABLE_API_KEY` it calls
  /v1/search with `X-API-Key`. The key only lifts the per-IP rate limits.
  Maps `snippet` (falling back to `description`) and `published_at`;
  freshness tokens and `a..b` date ranges become published_after /
  published_before; `summary` asks for longer snippets. 401/429/other
  statuses map to `Error: ...` results like the other backends, and the
  keyless 429 points at the optional key.
- KEYLESS_PROVIDERS: providers that always count as configured.
- web console: keenable in the mirrored provider list, shown as configured
  with no key, optional key editable through the existing search key modal
  (zh / zh-Hant / en strings).
- docs (en / zh / ja): provider row, auto order, and the note that the tool
  is now always registered.
- tests: 10 new cases (key resolution, keyless availability and ordering,
  console sync, endpoint and header selection, count clamp, freshness
  mapping, error mapping) with requests stubbed.

commits.commit_title: [AIP-85] Add Dag importers to Task SDK in preparation for rewiring (#72369)
commits.commit_message:
[AIP-85] Add Dag importers to Task SDK in preparation for rewiring (#72369)

* feat: Restructure the AbstractDagImporter/DagImporterRegistry and move the /importers base classes into the task SDK

* fix: run the checks

* Decouple Dag importers from Dag bundles in Task SDK

Pass bundle name and path as primitive parameters to importer methods instead of
requiring a BaseDagBundle instance. This effort saves us from passing whole bundle object into the DagBag for the import_definition() method.

* Fix core Airflow import violations in shared libraries and Task SDK Dag importers

* Harden ZipImporter against path traversal. Remove core dependencies from Task SDK DAG importers and standardize exceptions. Clean up test boilerplate and redundant checks.

* Pass Dag bundles directly to Task SDK Dag importers

* Reimplement Zip import def to extract on-demand

* Simplify ZipImporter's get_source_code

The whole-zip-file concat logic is removed since we are not supposed to treat
the entire zip file as one dag source. Airflow's mental model is to treat a zip
more like a directory, and only one member in the zip is the source file of a
given dag. This tradition should be kept. Viewing an entire zip should instead
be handled as a feature on the dag bundle level.

* Improve Dag importer resilience, discovery filtering, and bytecode support

* Pass conf explicitly to might_contain_dag instead of frame introspection

Resolving which config module to read (airflow.configuration vs
airflow.sdk.configuration) by walking the call stack only worked by
coincidence, since every current caller's immediate frame already sits
in an airflow-prefixed module. It silently breaks for anything else in
the chain (tests, wrapped calls) and re-walks the stack on every file
scanned in safe mode. Every caller already has the right conf object
in scope, so require it explicitly instead.

commits.commit_title: Fix airflowctl connections test failing on stored connections (#73098)
commits.commit_message:
Fix airflowctl connections test failing on stored connections (#73098)

The API server fills the fields a test request leaves out from the stored
connection, and decides which fields the caller meant to override from the
keys present in the request body. Sending every unset field as an explicit
null therefore reads as "clear these", so a stored host or port counts as
changed and the request is refused; where it is not refused the stored
credentials are overwritten with nulls and a blank connection gets tested.

Nothing in the CLI can express an intentional null, so omitting them loses
no caller intent.

commits.commit_title: Keep polling DataFusion pipeline state when the run is not visible yet (#72406)
commits.commit_message:
Keep polling DataFusion pipeline state when the run is not visible yet (#72406)

#60688 changed `_check_response_status_and_data` to raise
`requests.exceptions.HTTPError` on a 404 instead of
`AirflowNotFoundException`, but the polling loop in
`DataFusionHook.wait_for_pipeline_state` was changed to catch `KeyError`
instead of `AirflowException`. The two no longer line up, so the 404 that
CDAP returns while a run is still being registered escapes the loop and
fails `CloudDataFusionStartPipelineOperator` immediately.

That 404 tolerance was added in #10031 for exactly this reason: right after
a pipeline is started, the run is not yet visible in the system.

Catch `HTTPError` alongside `KeyError` so the loop keeps polling. Only the
404 branch of `_check_response_status_and_data` raises `HTTPError` (any
other non-200 raises `RequestException`), so this stays narrow: real
failures still propagate.

commits.commit_title: Clarify that AccessView.JOBS is the Edge worker management permission (#72627)
commits.commit_message:
Clarify that AccessView.JOBS is the Edge worker management permission (#72627)

The Edge UI plugin docs say that "can read on Plugins" and "can read on
Jobs" let you view the UI and manage the workers, but they do not say how
the two permissions differ, and they do not mention what the default
Viewer role already holds.

Both gaps matter, because the endpoints and the navigation are gated
differently:

- The worker management endpoints under /edge_worker/ui/ check only
  AccessView.JOBS, and the check is not method-aware -- the same
  dependency guards the GET reads and the POST/PATCH/DELETE mutations.
- "can read on Plugins" only controls whether the plugin shows up in the
  UI navigation. It is not required in order to call the endpoints.

So "can read on Jobs" alone is enough to shut down, delete, re-queue and
retune Edge workers, whether or not the plugin is visible to that user.

That is intentional -- AccessView.JOBS is the management permission for
the plugin rather than a read-only grant -- but it reads as surprising
from the code alone, where a permission named "can read" guards mutating
routes. It is more surprising in a default Flask AppBuilder setup, where
the Viewer role includes (ACTION_CAN_READ, RESOURCE_JOB) but not the
Plugins read: such a user cannot see the Edge plugin and can still reach
its management endpoints.

Adds a warning to the UI plugin docs stating the intent, the split
between the two permissions, the consequence for the default Viewer role,
and the concrete action for deployments where Viewers must not manage
workers. Points at the existing "fine granular access control" entry in
architecture.rst rather than restating it.

Documentation only; no behaviour change.

commits.commit_title: Remove airflow info `--file-io` as `file.io` dropped anonymous uploads (#73054)
commits.commit_message:
Remove airflow info `--file-io` as `file.io` dropped anonymous uploads (#73054)

* Remove airflow info --file-io as file.io dropped anonymous uploads

The flag uploaded the info report to file.io and printed a shareable link.
file.io no longer accepts anonymous uploads: the apex host 301s to a static
site that answers only GET/HEAD/OPTIONS, and uploads from the site itself now
go through LimeWire's API behind an account. The documented anonymous POST
endpoint is not wired up any more, so the flag could not succeed.

It also failed badly rather than cleanly. The error body is HTML, so the
resp.json() call in the failure branch raised json.JSONDecodeError before the
intended FileIoException was reached. tenacity only retried FileIoException and
_send_report_to_fileio only caught it, so the command ended in an unhandled
traceback.

Nothing replaces it: sending the report to a third-party host that can vanish
the same way is what broke here. Redirect the output to a file instead. Note
that --file-io implied --anonymize, so pass --anonymize explicitly when sharing
a report.

Closes: #73045

* Add newsfragment and drop the console parameter left dead by the removal

The removal is user-visible CLI surface, so it needs a significant newsfragment;
without one it files under Uncategorized and nobody upgrading sees it. The
fragment carries the anonymization note, which matters because --file-io applied
--anonymize implicitly and plain `airflow info` prints connection passwords in
cleartext.

AirflowInfo.show() took a console argument only so render_text could hand it a
separate console. render_text is gone and nothing else ever passed it.

The flag test asserted only argparse's exit code, which is 2 for a typo'd flag
and a missing subcommand alike, so it did not distinguish "flag removed" from
"command removed". Pin the stderr message the way the pools --output test does.

commits.commit_title: Cover the bundled registry web fonts in the root LICENSE (#73065)
commits.commit_message:
Cover the bundled registry web fonts in the root LICENSE (#73065)

The source tarball is what a consumer of an Apache Airflow release reads for
licensing, and its root LICENSE was bare Apache-2.0 with no subcomponents
section. Since the provider registry landed it has also shipped two web fonts
that are not ours and not Apache-2.0: JetBrains Mono and Plus Jakarta Sans,
both under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, vendored as woff2 and loaded through
@font-face. The OFL requires the copyright notice and licence to travel with
the font, so redistributing them with no notice anywhere in the tree left the
tarball own licensing incomplete.

The licence texts are the ones published by each upstream project, at the
versions recorded in the woff2 name tables. They sit next to the component
they cover, matching how airflow-core and the fab and google providers keep
their third-party texts, and the root LICENSE gains the subcomponents section
that airflow-core/LICENSE already carries so the pointer is where a reader
looks first.

commits.commit_title: Make dependency review one repo-wide gate, not a per-SDK one (#73061)
commits.commit_message:
Make dependency review one repo-wide gate, not a per-SDK one (#73061)

`dependency-review-action` has no path or manifest input. Once it runs
it reviews the entire dependency graph diff of the PR, every lockfile
included - so a gate named after one SDK can only ever be lying about
what it covers.

That is not theoretical. apache/airflow#72946, a release sync PR that
changed 816 files and not one of them under `java-sdk/`, tripped the
Java SDK gate through the self-reference in its own `paths` filter
(v*-test and v*-stable keep different copies of every workflow file),
and the Java SDK gate then failed on a Python advisory in `uv.lock`.

Replace the two per-SDK review jobs with one `Dependency review`
workflow covering the manifests of every ecosystem in the repo:

* new `.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml`, triggered by any
  Python, JavaScript, Go or JVM manifest in the PR.
* `java-sdk-dependency-security.yml` keeps only the Gradle
  `dependency-submission` job, which really is Java-specific, and
  drops its `pull_request` trigger.
* `ts-sdk-dependency-review.yml` goes away - the generic gate already
  reviews `ts-sdk/package.json` and `ts-sdk/pnpm-lock.yaml`.

The check name contributors see, `Reject vulnerable dependency
changes`, is unchanged. The settings are the stricter of the two the
repo had: the ts-sdk gate ran at the action's default
`fail-on-scopes: runtime`, and now gets `runtime, development,
unknown` like the java one.

commits.commit_title: Fix StatsD not restarting when overrideMappings or cache.ttl changes (#72633)
commits.commit_message:
Fix StatsD not restarting when overrideMappings or cache.ttl changes (#72633)

* Fix StatsD not restarting when overrideMappings or cache.ttl changes

The checksum annotation that rolls the StatsD pod was only rendered when
extraMappings or podAnnotations was set, so changing overrideMappings or
cache.ttl updated the ConfigMap without restarting the pod and the
exporter silently kept the old mappings.

The checksum is also narrowed to the ConfigMap data so that chart version
bumps and other metadata-only changes no longer restart StatsD.

* Hash the whole StatsD ConfigMap document for the rollout checksum

Narrowing the checksum to the ConfigMap's .data made StatsD the only
component in the chart whose pods do not roll on a chart version bump.
Review preferred keeping the same full-document hash every other
component uses: a restart of the stateless StatsD exporter on upgrade
is cheap, and a change we would want to roll out for but did not
anticipate is not.

* Keep the podAnnotations block in its original form

The if-to-with rewrite was a cosmetic change unrelated to the rollout fix
and was flagged as unnecessary in review.

commits.commit_title: Fix airflow standalone announcing readiness before the API server is up (#73025)
commits.commit_message:
Fix airflow standalone announcing readiness before the API server is up (#73025)

The readiness banner is the signal developers wait on before opening the
browser, so it has to account for the component that serves it. The API
server is the slowest of the four to come up, and until it binds its port
the banner points users at a connection they cannot make.

The port check existed from the command's introduction and was lost as
collateral damage when the old webserver was removed: #46942 deleted the
attribute holding the port but left the call reading it, and the follow-up
hot-fix #47145 resolved the resulting AttributeError by deleting the call
rather than repointing it at the renamed config key. The probe and its
tests have been unreachable since.

Resolving the port once during startup, as the pre-#47145 code did, also
keeps a raising config lookup out of the poll loop, whose only handler is
KeyboardInterrupt and whose component shutdown sits after the try block.
