commits.commit_title: fix: forward compress_tool_results in LlamaOpenAI._format_message (#10031)
commits.commit_message:
fix: forward compress_tool_results in LlamaOpenAI._format_message (#10031)

## Summary

`LlamaOpenAI._format_message` had drifted from its base class, so every
run on this provider crashed.


[`OpenAIChat._format_all_messages`](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/main/libs/agno/agno/models/openai/chat.py#L390)
calls the method with the compression flag as a **positional** argument:

```python
return [self._format_message(m, compress_tool_results) for m in normalized]
```

but the override only accepted `(self, message)`, raising

```
TypeError: _format_message() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given
```

The model layer swallows this into the response, so the provider
returned the `TypeError` text as the assistant's answer rather than
failing loudly.

`LlamaOpenAI` was the last `OpenAIChat` subclass with a drifted
signature — deepseek, cerebras, openrouter, moonshot, watsonx, mimo,
ollama and huggingface already match the base class.

### Forwarding, not just accepting

The override now **forwards** the flag rather than only accepting it:

```python
return format_message(message, openai_like=True, compress_tool_results=compress_tool_results)
```

`agno.utils.models.llama.format_message` already accepts
`compress_tool_results` and uses it to select
`message.get_content(use_compressed_content=...)`. Taking the parameter
and dropping it would stop the crash but silently disable tool-result
compression for this provider — users would set
`compress_tool_results=True`, get no compression, and grow their context
with no error. Verified locally:

| flag | resulting content |
|---|---|
| `True` | `"SHORT"` (compressed) |
| `False` | full 200-char payload |

## Related

Fixes #9034 (the `TypeError` reported there).

- **#9898** (AIMLAPI) fixes the same class of bug for `AIMLAPI` and
includes a `llama_openai.py` change, but that version accepts
`compress_tool_results` without forwarding it, so compression stays
disabled. That PR also carries attribution headers and a default-model
change that need a separate business decision; this PR is only the crash
fix, so it can ship independently.
- **#9035** proposes the same fix for both files and was blocked on
`missing-tests` since July. Credit to @KhandelwalChirag for the
root-cause analysis on #9034.

## Summary

Hi! I'm Hugo from aimlapi.com — an AI aggregator that gives access to
1000+ models in one API, trusted by 400k+ users.

We're already available as a provider inside Agno — but right now the
integration is broken by a bug that crashes every run, so we went ahead

Along with it we added payment tracking to build our partnership: from
now on we offer a 50/50 revenue share on all traffic from the AI/ML API
integration. (P.S.: tracking starts as soon as this release goes live,
so no earnings will be lost during setup)

If you have any questions - happy to answer.

My contacts: hugo@aimlapi.com (email / Slack), Telegram: @hug0the

Fixes #9034

Agno already ships an `AIMLAPI` model class, but requests to aimlapi.com

base class passes `compress_tool_results` positionally, so the old

[fix] Preserve empty Anthropic tool arguments (#8970)

## Summary

Anthropic represents a zero-argument tool call with an empty input
object. The Claude adapter treated that object as falsy and omitted
`function.arguments`. Both streaming and non-streaming parsing now
serialize every Anthropic tool input, so empty input becomes `"{}"`.

Fixes #8971

## Where this appears

This matters when Agno conversation history is persisted and later
replayed through another provider, such as when an application switches
an existing conversation from Claude to an OpenAI model.

Before this fix, a zero-argument Claude tool call was stored without
`function.arguments`. OpenAI requires an arguments string on every
function-call item, so replaying that history fails before generation
with a missing `arguments` request error.


[mindroom-ai/mindroom#1546](https://github.com/mindroom-ai/mindroom/pull/1546)
is the complementary consumer-side fix: it normalizes already-persisted
histories at the OpenAI request boundary, and has been in production
since July 2026. This PR fixes the source so newly parsed Anthropic tool
calls are complete.

commits.commit_message:
[fix] agno 3.x: drop the caller-frame namespace pydantic keeps on cached tool wrappers (#9941)

## Summary

`validate_call` stores the caller's `f_locals` on the wrapper it builds,
and `Function` caches those wrappers for the life of the process. On
Python 3.13 `f_locals` is a frame proxy, so every cached tool kept the
frame that wrapped it alive, and with it the Agent, session and run
state on the stack at the time. pydantic builds the validators eagerly,
so the namespace is never used after the wrapper exists.

`_wrap_callable_uncached` now builds the wrapper (body moved unchanged
into `_validate_callable`) and sets `ns_resolver = None` on the
`ValidateCallWrapper` the returned function closes over, recursing once
for the async-generator shim. Duck-typed on `ns_resolver` and
`__pydantic_validator__`, no pydantic internals imported, so it is a
no-op on pydantic versions without the attribute.

Test: `tests/unit/tools/test_function_wrap_releases_frame.py`. A
sentinel in the wrapping frame becomes collectable (fails on `main`
under 3.13, trivially passes on 3.12), the resolver is `None`, argument
coercion still works; the async-generator shim is covered. Note: the
repo's dev environment is 3.12, so CI only sees the leak assertion bite
if a 3.13 job runs it.

Found while upgrading MindRoom to 3.0.5 (mindroom-ai/mindroom#1944),
where this is carried as a monkey patch.

Fixes #9940

## Summary

Moves reusable read-only page commands from Docs Agent into
`PageFileSystem(knowledge=...)`, with synchronous and asynchronous
execution. Applications keep their tool names/descriptions, prompts,
explicit pre-hook retrieval, rendering, citations and error wording.

The adapter uses public Knowledge APIs for lazy, revision-pinned page
reads, scoped metadata listings and bounded literal grep. Regex scans,
command workers and caches are bounded; cancellation retains capacity
until work finishes. Body caches are instance-scoped and validate
publication before reuse. Tool exposure is explicit through
`files.tools()`. Commands cannot execute a shell or write files; prompt
orchestration remains application-controlled.

Current head: `3adee8b487ba24cdfc479517daa460e1c66f61f9`, based on main
`229908e2155769cd63d1377bf0837c488ef90847` containing merged #9996. The
branch was rebased after that dependency merged; this review diff
contains only VFS work.

The opt-in toolkit removes the handwritten command wrapper:

```python
knowledge.setup()
files = PageFileSystem(knowledge=knowledge)
agent = Agent(tools=[files.tools()])
```

`files.tools(tool_name="query_docs_filesystem", description="...")`
customizes the model-visible tool. Sync and async Agent runs select
corresponding implementations under one tool name. Page errors become
`tool_error` results, while direct command methods still raise typed
PageError. Toolkit creation performs no setup, retrieval, or prompt
insertion. Custom product wrappers remain supported.

commits.commit_message:
feat: add coordinated pages and public docs serving (#9963)

## Summary

Add the page storage and public-serving functionality consumed by the
explicit Docs Agent migration in [product PR
#14](https://github.com/agno-agi/docs-agent/pull/14). Knowledge
atomically publishes catalog metadata, filesystem text and vectors,
preserves previous revisions on failed refresh, and exposes bounded
sync/async setup, source synchronization, search, read, list and grep
APIs. The `agno.knowledge.page` package contains `types.py`, private
discovery and coordination; existing public result imports remain
available through lightweight re-exports.

PublicSurface serves selected Agents, native stateless MCP and
authenticated durable sync Workflows with shared PostgreSQL quotas,
feedback identity, request/upload/output bounds, CORS, internal-service
authentication and signed-interface compatibility. Docs Agent owns its
prompt, explicit pre-hook, query alternatives, evidence rendering,
citations, tools, models and follow-ups.

## Documentation-only cleanup

Agno PR head `797e62685319e68d23c7f5457d86d970a07f710b` removes the new
changelog file and its cookbook link at the user's request. The
constructor behavior remains documented in the cookbook and this PR.
This Markdown-only commit leaves the complete framework Python package
and packaging configuration identical to the reviewed/tested runtime
`b14c5fa940a55bfd4ec259422ee24464bb612ef0`. Product
`490099fbf10aa6bdc3109808c5190ac92018d348` and both dependency pins
remain unchanged. Required format/validation and reference/diff checks
pass. Runtime tests, independent review and performance measurements
below retain their original runtime provenance. New framework-head CI
snapshot: pending ['supported-runtime-page-guards', 'style-check-agno
(3.10)', 'style-check-agnoctl (3.10)', 'style-check-cookbook (3.10)',
'tests (1/5)', 'tests (2/5)', 'tests (3/5)', 'tests (4/5)', 'tests
(5/5)'], failures []; REVIEW_REQUIRED.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Breaking change
- [x] Improvement

## Intentional 3.0 constructor cleanup

All Knowledge constructor arguments are now keyword-only, explicitly
approved for 3.0. Positional calls such as `Knowledge("docs")` must
become `Knowledge(name="docs")`. `content_db` is preferred; existing
`contents_db` keywords and attribute assignments remain supported
without warnings. Both names share one canonical dataclass field,
`contents_db`. Existing serialization/reconstruction/copy and
`dataclasses.replace(..., contents_db=...)` behavior remain. Replacement
via the new property alias is not required. Supplying both constructor
keywords requires the same object, including explicit None.

## Explicit search configuration

`Knowledge(page_search=PageSearchConfig(...))` provides typed
transaction-local planner controls. Unset scan preferences, costs,
worker counts and scan thresholds inherit PostgreSQL settings. Custom
plans default on to retain namespace partial-index eligibility and may
explicitly be unset. Page search honors the existing `PgVector` HNSW
`ef_search`; it no longer silently forces 200. Concurrent alternative
queries use zero nested PostgreSQL parallel workers. Setting names are
fixed and values are bound; there is no arbitrary SQL setting interface.
Docs Agent explicitly preserves its existing HNSW 200 and planner
choices. The cookbook retains HNSW 200 and omits optional planner
overrides.

## Reviewed blocker fixes

- Anonymous native Agent JSON previously returned HTTP 200 containing
status ERROR and nested model diagnostics. Replace the entire failed
envelope with safe `503 run_failed`, matching streaming error
protection. Successful outputs and authenticated operator workflow
diagnostics remain.
- Normalize concurrent-future/asyncio timeout types on supported Python
3.9/3.10, including the public page API and request-body boundary.
Cancellation is signaled and worker capacity remains held until actual
exit.
- Optional-query pool waits obey the existing optional deadline. New
optional connection handshakes are avoided; queries can fall back to the
parent's coherent snapshot. Exporting snapshots and admission survive
all child cleanup. This fixes public primary-result loss under
reproduced contention, but the performance limitation below remains.
- Initialized startup validates required tables, namespace binding,
generated column and indexes without taking the long sync writer lock.
First setup and necessary DDL remain serialized; readiness follows
successful validation. Missing indexes are repaired and incompatible
definitions rejected.

Retain the previously fixed output-header buffering, approved
search-only 24,000–32,000-byte allowance, completeness propagation and
public async deadline delivery. The optional `validate_discovery`
callback runs under the namespace lock before page work; Docs Agent
keeps its original shrink/force policy. No automatic context integration
is restored.

## Current cookbook update

Agent dependency callables now optionally receive `run_input` and
`session`, alongside `agent` and `run_context`. The public-pages
cookbook uses an explicit async `docs_context` dependency while keeping
the same search function and instructions placeholder.
`add_dependencies_to_context` already defaults to False and stays unset.
This remains application-controlled retrieval. Resolution runs before
pre-hooks, reuses successful values on model retries and emits no
pre-hook events; continuations receive original stored input, not added
instructions. Docs Agent product source keeps its existing explicit
pre-hook and retrieval policy.

The cookbook still omits optional planner overrides and retains
`HNSW(ef_search=200)`. Demo CLI and offline executable/recording-model
checks pass; no fresh live retrieval, provider, HTTP or MCP cookbook run
is claimed. Earlier live evidence retains its original executable hash.
`FileSystem(db=...)` and `PgVector(db=...)` remain separate follow-ups.

## Validation and paired heads

Agno PR head `797e62685319e68d23c7f5457d86d970a07f710b`; reviewed
runtime `b14c5fa940a55bfd4ec259422ee24464bb612ef0`; Docs Agent
`490099fbf10aa6bdc3109808c5190ac92018d348`. Both product dependency
files and the installed distribution pin
`b14c5fa940a55bfd4ec259422ee24464bb612ef0`. The product environment was
installed from that exact local Git commit with no dependency upgrades;
installed VCS metadata was verified. Both heads are pushed on the
existing `ab/docs-agent-v2` branches.

- Required framework `scripts/format.sh` and `scripts/validate.sh`: pass
(ruff, mypy on 1,043 framework and 21 CLI files, cookbook pattern
checks).
- Final framework run: **771 passed** (713 Agent/Team-dependency unit
cases plus 58 PostgreSQL page-storage cases). Command:
`AGNO_PAGE_TEST_DB_URL=<local admin URL> .venv/bin/python -m pytest
libs/agno/tests/unit/agent
libs/agno/tests/unit/team/test_dependencies_merge.py
libs/agno/tests/integration/knowledge/test_page_storage.py -q`.
PostgreSQL tests create/drop disposable databases.
- The 27 dependency cases include **17 added regressions**: sync/async
and stream/non-stream prompt/history/follow-up equality against a
pre-hook; input/session/agent/run-context injection; model retry reuse;
continuation by object/by ID; concurrent input isolation. They assert
actual public run behavior and model inputs/call counts.
- Cookbook `--help` and offline executable probe pass in `.venvs/demo`
with `PYTHONPATH=libs/agno`. Recording search/model checks cover
trimmed, blank, non-text and absent input, multi-turn context and
follow-ups. Probe:
`.context/docs-agent-v2/evaluation/dependency-inputs/cookbook_probe.py`.
The tracked TEST_LOG records its executable hash and limits.
- Required product format/validate scripts: pass, including mypy and
**256 tests**, with `DOCS_AGENT_TEST_DB_URL` set to the local PostgreSQL
admin URL. The composed chat/MCP/feedback/durable-sync test ran on a
disposable database. Product recording-model
prompt/pre-hook/tools/follow-up assertions pass on the exact installed
framework pin.
- `git diff --check` passes; no product source/policy changes. Logs and
pre-update handoff/PR snapshots are preserved in the dependency-inputs
evidence directory.

Earlier b12c2f881/33f3c456 validation and independent review retain
their original provenance. Their Python 3.10/local live-smoke claims are
not relabeled as new-head runs.

Runtime-head CI snapshot (before this Markdown-only follow-up): agno: 11
successful checks; pending ['tests (1/5)', 'tests (3/5)']; failures [];
REVIEW_REQUIRED. docs: 2 successful checks; pending []; failures [];
REVIEW_REQUIRED.

## Performance: accepted local trade-off and historical live uncertainty

On 2026-09-06 the user accepted the measured local latency trade-off for
simplicity in this iteration. Pool startup preparation and background
replenishment remain declined. This is an explicit local trade-off
decision, not evidence that the recorded regression disappeared or that
historical live latency/quality uncertainty has been resolved. Formal
review and explicit merge/deployment authorization remain required.

The fresh ordinary-startup replay matches **120/120 pairs across all 40
cases**, including **21 nonempty-tool pairs across seven cases**.
Model-request hashes, tool arguments/results, recorded answers and
follow-ups match. No clipping cases or failures are excluded. It uses
recorded embeddings/provider events and real PostgreSQL/product
rendering, so it measures local application work, not live provider
latency or newly judged quality.

Despite matching evidence, **the shipped ordinary-startup path
regresses**: baseline → candidate initial retrieval/render mean **63.103
→ 73.008 ms**, initial p95 **110.996 → 169.464 ms**, and completion p95
**174.240 → 249.423 ms**. Candidate initial SQL mean is 52.049ms and
page-loading mean 15.426ms. Faster medians alone do not establish
improvement; the user has separately accepted this measured local
trade-off.

A separately labeled full-cohort diagnostic prewarms the candidate's
existing bounded pool before serving: all 120 pairs still match, initial
mean **62.890 → 58.816 ms**, completion p95 **170.812 → 165.108 ms**.
This supports underfilled-pool serial fallback after the H-3 deadline
fix as the new local regression's cause. Prewarming is a harness
intervention, **not implemented startup behavior**. Startup-only
preparation is insufficient: the existing pool recycles connections
after 300 seconds, and optional checkout forbids replacement connections
as well as initially missing ones. The independent PostgreSQL probe and
owned-head reproduction prepare all eight slots and observe three query
connections before expiry, then distinct-connection counts
`[1,1,1,2,2,2,2,2,2,2]` across ten successful equal-result searches
after aging the records beyond the configured threshold. This exercises
real recycling without waiting five minutes or changing pool policy.
Primary traffic partially rebuilt the pool in this run; the evidence
does not establish permanently serial execution. On 2026-09-06 the user
explicitly deferred pool startup preparation and replenishment because
of the added complexity. Do not implement startup warming or substitute
a background pool-maintenance subsystem. Keep the completed correctness
fixes, existing connection behavior, capacity/deadlines and
snapshot/cancellation cleanup. Evaluate improvements elsewhere against
this unchanged configuration; no new implementation alternative is
authorized by this decision. The measured serial-fallback latency
trade-off remains explicit and is now accepted for this iteration;
historical live uncertainty and merge authorization are separate. The
worse ordinary-startup evidence remains the unchanged runtime result.

The independent warm-pool planner/HNSW experiment covers all 40 cases,
56 query groups × three repeats × nine randomized conditions (1,512
searches). Explicit Docs tuning: **168/168** payload matches, mean
42.435 ms / p95 77.528ms. Planner defaults with HNSW 200: **168/168**,
mean 66.245 ms / p95 117.973ms. Framework HNSW 5: only **54/168**
payload matches; 38/56 distinct query groups change. Custom-plan and
setup-cost effects are material here; this does not establish a benefit
for every individual override or live quality. Docs tuning remains
explicitly unchanged.

Historical live results at e27c299/e457cef remain first-answer p95
**6.613 → 9.265s**, completion p95 **11.883 → 15.170s**,
grounded-correct judge 52→51/80, citations 65→71/80 and one candidate
primary-embedding timeout. No fresh full-cohort live evaluation
disproves those results. The live cookbook smoke and recorded-response
equality do not replace that acceptance gate. Batch reads, overall
timeout/retry changes and agent-parameter tuning remain unimplemented.
**The measured local trade-off is accepted for this iteration; formal
review and explicit merge/deployment authorization remain required.**

## Deferred scope and review

Automatic reference/message/checkpoint orchestration,
Message.add_to_history, page expansion/guidance/tool rosters, AgentOS
URL derivation and public Team serving remain deferred. Recovery
branches preserve their implementation and corrected reference JSON.
Existing KnowledgeProtocol and non-page Agent/Team behavior remain.

Validated ingestion findings M-8 (failed first-source recovery), M-20
(targeted transport retries), M-23 (duplicate destination/title),
percent-escaped namespace indexing and other qualified findings remain
follow-ups. ASGI 2.4 SSE timeout compatibility is separate. No merge or
deployment; independent local review of this updated pair found no
high-confidence consequential findings; formal GitHub review and
explicit merge/deployment authorization remain required, and historical
live uncertainty is unchanged.

## Independent review

Independent read-only review is complete on Agno
b14c5fa940a55bfd4ec259422ee24464bb612ef0 / Docs Agent
490099fbf10aa6bdc3109808c5190ac92018d348, with no high-confidence
consequential findings in this bounded delta. From pinned source
archives, the reviewer passed 713 Agent/Team dependency unit tests, 256
product tests including composed disposable-PostgreSQL coverage, eight
extra structured-input/absent-original-input continuation cases across
all four run modes, 35 focused cases on Python 3.10, and the offline
executable cookbook probe. Installed framework metadata and the
pins-only product diff were independently verified. The reviewer did not
rerun unchanged page-storage tests, required format/validate scripts,
controlled replay or live providers; implementation validation is
separately listed above. This review confirms normal-run
prompt/history/follow-up equivalence, not pre-hook lifecycle
equivalence. Formal GitHub approval and explicit merge/deployment
authorization remain required. Historical performance evidence and the
accepted local trade-off remain unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Code complies with style guidelines
- [x] Ran required format/validation scripts

commits.commit_message:
chore: Release v3.0.6 (#9907)

# **Changelog**

## New Features

- **Stateless MCP
serving.** `MCPConfig(stateless=True)` serves `/mcp` without session
tracking, so any replica can answer any request and a multi-instance
deployment needs no session affinity. Costs server-initiated
notifications and SSE resumability, so it stays off by default.
- **`MCPTools(protocol_mode=...)`** selects which MCP protocol era to
negotiate. Defaults to `"legacy"`, preserving today's session-based
behaviour; `"auto"` negotiates the newest era both sides support
(sessionless from `2026-07-28`). Existing servers are unaffected — a
modern server still accepts the legacy handshake. Internally, MCP
clients are now built on `fastmcp.Client`.
- **AgentOS MCP Server Card** at `GET /mcp/server-card`, listing the
served tools and carrying a configurable name, version and instructions.
- `.zip` and `.eml` file uploads in AgentOS. See
[cookbook](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/main/cookbook/05_agent_os/04_run_lifecycle/unpack_archives.py).
- **`AuthorizationConfig.excluded_route_paths`** marks custom routes
public without disabling auth globally.
- **Bedrock**: pass your own async client to the model or embedder.

## **Bug Fixes**

- **Anthropic**: replay assistant turns verbatim so thinking blocks are
no longer rejected.
- **Gemini**: resolve image MIME type instead of
hard-coding `image/jpeg`.
- **RecursiveChunking**: stop emitting duplicate trailing chunks.
- **AG-UI**: send wire fields instead of `RunContext` to remote
entities.
- **AG-UI**: expose streamed run errors.
- Pin `tree-sitter-language-pack<1.16` to unblock the chonkie code
chunker.

Co-authored-by: Kaustubh <shuklakaustubh84@gmail.com>

commits.commit_title: feat: add stateless MCP transport and build MCP clients on `fastmcp.Client` (#9927)
commits.commit_message:
feat: add stateless MCP transport and build MCP clients on `fastmcp.Client` (#9927)

## Summary

Two related MCP changes, one on each side of the connection.
**Server side.** `MCPConfig(stateless=True)` serves `/mcp` without
session tracking, so every request gets its own transport and any
replica can answer any request. A multi-instance deployment then needs
no session affinity.
**Client side.** `MCPTools` hand-assembled every connection: an httpx
client, a transport, a `ClientSession`, and an explicit `initialize()`,
unwound by hand across three connect paths. That lifecycle is now owned
by `fastmcp.Client`, which handles all four steps, so
`_build_fastmcp_client()` replaces them for stdio, SSE and
streamable-http alike. The dead `_streamable_http_connection` helper
goes with them. Adds `MCPTools(protocol_mode=...)` to select which
protocol era to negotiate.
Also raises the fastmcp floor to **4.0.2** and aligns the three system
test pins with it.


## Design decisions

### Stateless is passed only when set
fastmcp reads `stateless_http=None` as "fall back to
`fastmcp.settings.stateless_http`". Always passing `False` would
silently override a user's global setting, so the flag reaches
`http_app()` only when `MCPConfig(stateless=True)` asks for it. The
parameter is also guarded on existing in the installed fastmcp, matching
the pattern already used for `host_origin_protection`.

### `fastmcp.Client` and not `mcp.Client`
The MCP SDK v2 ships its own `mcp.Client` that collapses the same four
step and it was the obvious first choice. It is unusable here: it has 16
constructor parameters and not one of them accepts HTTP headers or an
httpx client. Given a URL it builds the transport internally, so there
is no injection point and `MCPTools` depends on headers heavily.

 ### `protocol_mode`: the default is "legacy"   

fastmcp's `Client` defaults to `mode="auto"`, which negotiates the
newest era both sides support. Against a current server that is the
2026-07-28 revision, which is sessionless. That is a real behaviour
change for existing users, so `MCPTools` defaults to `"legacy"` instead
and keeps the session-based era (<= 2025-11-25) this toolkit has always
used.

- `"legacy"`: long-lived session, `is_alive()` pings the connection.
Required for a server that gates access in `on_initialize`, holds
per-session state.
- `"auto"`: newest mutual era. Requests are self-contained, so any
replica behind an ordinary load balancer can serve them.
 

### `terminate_on_close` needs its own transport       

`StreamableHTTPClientParams.terminate_on_close=False` means "do not send
a DELETE on close, so the server keeps my session for a later
reconnect".
The MCP SDK still supports it: `streamable_http_client(url,
http_client=..., terminate_on_close=...)`. fastmcp's
`StreamableHttpTransport` does not accept the parameter and calls the
SDK without it, so the SDK default (send DELETE) always wins.

### Backward compatibility
- The `MCPTools` constructor is unchanged. `url`, `command`,
`transport`, `server_params`, `headers`, `header_provider`,
`timeout_seconds` and `refresh_connection` all keep their meaning.
- `MCPTools(session=...)` still accepts a caller-supplied
`ClientSession` and uses it as before. `list_tools()` and the liveness
probe are normalised so both object types work.
- `protocol_mode` defaults to `"legacy"`, so the negotiated era does not
move.
- `terminate_on_close` behaves as it did for `None`, `False` and `True`.
- `MCPConfig.stateless` defaults to `False`, so server behaviour is
unchanged.

commits.commit_message:
feat: support .zip and .eml file uploads in AgentOS (#9193)

## Summary

Adds `.zip` and `.eml` to the set of file types AgentOS upload routers
accept. Previously these were rejected with "Unsupported file type"
(HTTP 400) because neither MIME type was present in
`DOCUMENT_MIME_TYPES`/`_DOCUMENT_EXTENSION_MIME`
(`libs/agno/agno/os/utils.py`) or `FileMedia.valid_mime_types()`
(`libs/agno/agno/media.py`).

- `.eml` (`message/rfc822`) is a standard email format, same use case as
the already-supported `.msg`.
- `.zip` (`application/zip`) is accepted as an opaque binary attachment
only — no server-side extraction or inspection of its contents.
Unpacking is left to the caller's own `pre_hooks`/workflow logic,
consistent with how other binary formats (`.doc`, `.ppt`, `.msg`) are
already passed through without being parsed by Agno itself.

Also updated `EXTENSION_CATEGORY` and `_DOCUMENT_EXTENSION_MIME` so
uploads with a missing/generic `content_type`
(`application/octet-stream` or empty) still resolve to the correct MIME
type from the filename extension, following the existing fallback
pattern used for `.md`/`.pptx`.

Closes #9191

feat: add AuthorizationConfig.excluded_route_paths for custom public routes (#9295)

## Summary

Add `AuthorizationConfig.excluded_route_paths` to allow custom routes to
bypass JWT authentication while keeping the rest of AgentOS protected.

### What it does

```python
AgentOS(
    authorization=True,
    authorization_config=AuthorizationConfig(
        verification_keys=[JWT_SECRET],
        excluded_route_paths=["/public/*"],
    ),
)
```

- Custom patterns use `fnmatch` syntax (`*` matches any characters
including `/`)
- Note: `/public/*` does not match bare `/public` — list both if needed
- Default exclusions (`/`, `/health`, `/info`, `/docs`, etc.) are always
preserved
- Custom paths are additive, not a replacement
- Merges with interface prefixes (Slack, etc.) and MCP OAuth paths

### Changes

**Code (`libs/agno/agno/os/app.py`)**
- Reads `excluded_route_paths` from config and merges with defaults
- Minimal change: adds `excluded_routes` variable and `+
excluded_routes` to concatenation

commits.commit_title: feat: MCP Server Card at /mcp/server-card (#9932)
commits.commit_message:
feat: MCP Server Card at /mcp/server-card (#9932)

## Summary

An MCP Server Card at `/mcp/server-card`, on by default, and a redirect
for people who open `/mcp` in a browser. Stacked on #9930 (base branch
`feat/mcp-server-identity`); retarget to `main` once that merges.

**The card** follows the MCP Server Card extension (SEP-2127,
experimental): `$schema`, a reverse-DNS `name` built from the request
host and the server name, `title`, `version`, `description` from the
AgentOS description, and one `remotes` entry with the endpoint URL.
Proxy headers (`X-Forwarded-Proto`, `X-Forwarded-Host`) are honoured, so
a deployment behind Railway or a load balancer reports its public URL.
When the server is gated, the remote declares the required
`Authorization` header. The card lists no tools; the extension leaves
those to `tools/list`.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://static.modelcontextprotocol.io/schemas/v1/server-card.schema.json",
  "name": "com.agno.docs/acme-support",
  "title": "Acme Support",
  "version": "1.4.0",
  "description": "AgentOS that describes its MCP server to connecting clients.",
  "remotes": [{"type": "streamable-http", "url": "https://docs.agno.com/mcp"}]
}
```

**The redirect.** A GET on `/mcp` whose `Accept` header lacks
`text/event-stream` gets a 302 to the card. MCP clients always send that
header on a GET, and the draft transport revision has no GET at all, so
only browsers and curl ever see the redirect. Today they see a JSON-RPC
406 error, or a 405 once the stateless transport lands.

**Public by design.** The card path is exempt from the AgentOS auth
middleware the same way the OAuth well-known routes are. Under
`mcp_auth` the fastmcp challenge guards only the MCP endpoint, so the
card is public there too. On a JWT-gated AgentOS the endpoint itself
stays behind auth; only the card is public.

**Off switch.** `MCPConfig(server_card=False)` removes the route and the
redirect.

**Why.** The docs site tells users to add `https://docs.agno.com/mcp`.
Pasting that into a browser today shows an error, and
`agno-agi/docs-agent` carries a hand-rolled manifest middleware to cover
it. With the card in the framework, docs-agent can delete that
middleware and any AgentOS gets discovery in the extension's shape and
location.

**Verified.**
- Eight unit tests in `tests/unit/os/test_mcp_server.py`: card contents,
proxy headers, the bearer hint on a gated server, the redirect and its
pass-through for MCP clients, the off switch, the auth exemption on an
authorized AgentOS, and the name derivation.
- Three mutation checks: removing the auth exemption fails the
public-card test, removing the redirect middleware fails the redirect
test, removing the route fails four card tests.
- 438 tests across the MCP, MCP auth, OAuth and JWT helper suites pass.
- Live: `cookbook/05_agent_os/14_mcp/server_identity.py` served with
fastmcp 4.0.2. A browser-style GET on `/mcp` answered 302; the card came
back with the extension's media type, CORS and cache headers; forwarded
headers produced the public URL; a GET with `Accept: text/event-stream`
was left to fastmcp. Recorded in the folder's TEST_LOG.

**Docs.** The MCPConfig option table on the docs MCP page has the
`server_card` row (docs repo, separate change).

commits.commit_title: fix: replay Anthropic assistant turns verbatim so thinking blocks are not rejected (#9924)
commits.commit_message:
fix: replay Anthropic assistant turns verbatim so thinking blocks are not rejected (#9924)

## Summary

Fixes #9923.

Claude signs `thinking` blocks and verifies the thinking sequence of an
assistant message when it is replayed. Agno rebuilt every assistant turn
from the convenience fields (`reasoning_content`, `content`,
`tool_calls`, `provider_data["signature"]`), which is lossy: only the
last thinking block and its signature survived a multi-thinking
response, blocks were emitted in a fixed order, and two consecutive
assistant messages were stitched into one message carrying two signed
thinking sequences. The API rejects those with `thinking or
redacted_thinking blocks in the latest assistant message cannot be
modified`, and because the session replays identically on every retry
the run stays stuck.

Changes:

- Store the ordered content blocks of every Claude response on the
assistant message as `provider_data["content_blocks"]`, from both the
non-streaming parse and the streaming `MessageStop` event. `content`,
`reasoning_content` and `tool_calls` keep working as derived views.
- Replay stored blocks verbatim from `format_messages`. A `tool_use`
block is replayed only when the message still carries the matching tool
call, so a tool call truncated by `max_tokens` (which never ran and has
no `tool_result`) is not sent back.
- When two consecutive assistant messages are merged into one API
message, drop the earlier message's `thinking` and `redacted_thinking`
blocks instead of stitching two signed sequences. Omitting thinking is
permitted outside a tool-use turn, and the earlier message in this
position never has a tool call to continue. This also heals sessions
that are already stuck.
- Omit the thinking block when the stored signature is missing instead
of raising a pydantic `ValidationError` from `ThinkingBlock` (hit when a
session carries `reasoning_content` from another provider).
- Messages without stored blocks (sessions written by earlier versions)
keep the existing rebuild path.
- Default `append_trailing_user_message` to True whenever thinking is
on. Prefill is rejected while thinking is on regardless of model, so
`continue_run` without input after a response truncated inside its
thinking failed with `The final block in an assistant message cannot be
thinking` on prefill-capable models such as Sonnet 4.5. With the
trailing user turn the truncated turn is a prior turn and the
continuation succeeds. The check also honours a thinking config supplied
through `request_params`, which is applied last and overrides the
`thinking` field.
- Replayed blocks are shallow-copied so request-time edits never reach
the stored session message.
- Azure Claude now runs the shared post-init. It defined its own without
calling the parent's, so the trailing-user-message auto-detection never
ran there, neither the existing prefill rule for 4.6 and later nor the
new thinking rule. Its structured-output overrides are kept.
- The legacy `redacted_reasoning_content` block type the parser accepts
from rehydrated events is normalized to `redacted_thinking` when stored
blocks are serialized, and replay goes through the same serializer so a
stored legacy type also replays as the canonical one.

Bedrock and Vertex AI Claude subclass the Anthropic model and share
`format_messages`, so all three are covered.

feat: name, version and instructions for the AgentOS MCP server (#9930)

## Summary

`MCPConfig` gains three fields that describe the AgentOS MCP server to
the clients that connect to it. All three go straight into the `FastMCP`
constructor and travel in the initialize response.

| Field | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | the AgentOS name | The server name a client shows in its
server list. |
| `version` | `AgentOS(version=...)` | `serverInfo.version`. With
neither set, the server keeps reporting fastmcp's own version, as it
does today. |
| `instructions` | `None` | Guidance for the calling model: what the
tools are for, which one to start with, and any conventions to follow.
Claude, Cursor and ChatGPT read it when they connect. |

```python
agent_os = AgentOS(
    name="Support AgentOS",
    version="1.4.0",
    agents=[support_agent],
    mcp=MCPConfig(
        name="Acme Support",
        version="1.4.0",
        instructions="This server answers questions about Acme products. Start with run_agent ...",
    ),
)
```

**Why.** A public MCP server has to say what it is and how to use it.
`AgentOS(version=...)` was accepted but never reached the MCP server,
and there was no way to set instructions at all. The docs MCP server in
`agno-agi/docs-agent` works around this today by wrapping
`agno.os.mcp.build_mcp_server` and writing to a private fastmcp
attribute. `instructions` is deliberately not derived from
`AgentOS(description=...)`: the description is written for humans, the
instructions are a prompt for the calling model, the same split
`as_tool(description=...)` already makes.

**Behaviour when unset is unchanged.** No name and no version anywhere
still gives a server called `AgentOS` reporting fastmcp's version; a
test pins that.

**Relation to #9927.** That PR adds `MCPConfig(stateless=True)` and
rebuilds the client side. This PR adds only the identity fields and
touches `config.py`, `os/mcp.py`, the MCP cookbook README and TEST_LOG
in different places, so the two can merge in either order. The second
one in will need a trivial rebase on the README table.

**Verified.**

defaults, the fastmcp fallback when nothing is set, `MCPConfig`

and instructions in both the legacy handshake and the 2026-07-28
negotiation. Entry added to the folder's TEST_LOG.

rows (docs repo, separate change).

commits.commit_message:
fix: stop RecursiveChunking from emitting duplicate trailing chunks (#9919)

## Summary

`RecursiveChunking.chunk()` had no exit for a chunk that reaches the end
of the content. After the last full chunk, `start` rewound by `overlap`,
so `start < len(content)` still held and the loop emitted a shorter
suffix of text an earlier chunk already held. It repeated until `start`
passed the end.

A 300 character document with `chunk_size=100` and `overlap=20` produced
6 chunks instead of 4. Chunks 5 and 6 sit inside chunk 4. Those
duplicates reach the vector store as separate documents, which inflates
the embedding cost and returns near-identical hits.

`FixedSizeChunking` already breaks out of its loop at
`libs/agno/agno/knowledge/chunking/fixed.py:52-54`:

```python
# Stop once a chunk reaches the end of the content
if end >= content_length:
    break
```

This adds the same guard to `recursive.py`.

(If applicable, issue number: #9918)

Fixes #9918

commits.commit_title: fix: send wire fields instead of RunContext to remote entities over AG-UI (#9909)
commits.commit_message:
fix: send wire fields instead of RunContext to remote entities over AG-UI (#9909)

## Summary

`test-agentos-system` fails on `release/v3.0.6` (#9907): the two AG-UI
remote streaming tests end in `RUN_ERROR` instead of `RUN_FINISHED`. The
failure is on `main`; the release PR only bumps the version.

### Where the value breaks

```
AG-UI client
   │  POST /agui
   ▼
run_entity (agui/router.py)
   │  entity.arun(..., run_id=..., run_context=RunContext(...))
   ▼
RemoteAgent.arun / RemoteTeam.arun          run_context, run_id land in **kwargs
   │  agentos_client.run_*_stream(**kwargs)
   ▼
AgentOSClient                               every kwarg becomes a form field
   │  data["run_context"] = str(RunContext(...))
   ▼
remote AgentOS  /agents/{id}/runs
   │  get_request_kwargs harvests unknown form fields
   ▼
Agent.arun(run_context="RunContext(run_id=...)")
   │  apply_to_context -> run_context.user_id
   ▼
AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'user_id'
   │  agent_response_streamer -> RunErrorEvent on a 200 SSE stream
   ▼
gateway AG-UI mapper -> RUN_ERROR
```

### Timeline

| When | Change | Effect on the remote AG-UI path |
|---|---|---|
| #8565 (Jul 8) | Router builds a `RunContext` for client tools and
passes it to every entity | Remote runs start failing on the remote
server; the `RunError` chunk is mapped to `RAW` and the stream still
ends in a synthesised `RUN_FINISHED`, so the system test keeps passing |
| #9487 (Sep 2) | `RunError` becomes a terminal AG-UI event | The same
failure now surfaces as `RUN_ERROR`; `release/v3.0.6` is the first
release run since the merge |

### Change

`run_entity`, fresh-run branch only:

```python
# before
response_stream = entity.arun(..., run_context=run_context, **run_kwargs)

# after
if isinstance(entity, (RemoteAgent, RemoteTeam)):
    run_kwargs["session_state"] = session_state
    run_kwargs["dependencies"] = ui_deps
    if client_tools:
        log_warning("AG-UI client tools are not forwarded to remote agents or teams")
else:
    run_kwargs["run_context"] = run_context
response_stream = entity.arun(..., **run_kwargs)
```

`session_state` and `dependencies` are declared on both remote `arun`
signatures and decoded by `get_request_kwargs` on the server. `run_id`
keeps flowing as a form field the server hands to `Agent.arun`, so the
remote run keeps the AG-UI run id like a local run does. The resume path
already rejects remote entities and is untouched.

| Path | Change |
|---|---|
| `libs/agno/agno/os/interfaces/agui/router.py` | Remote entities get
wire fields instead of `RunContext`; warning for client tools |
| `libs/agno/tests/unit/os/interfaces/test_agui_router.py` | Three
regression tests against real `RemoteAgent`/`RemoteTeam` with the
AgentOS client stubbed; all three fail without the fix |

### Verification

Against the `libs/agno/tests/system` Docker stack built from this
branch:

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/test_agui_routes.py` | 2 failed, 5 passed | 7 passed (run
twice) |
| Remote server log | `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute
'user_id'` per remote run | no tracebacks |
| AG-UI `context` reaches the remote agent | never | agent answers from
the context value |
| AG-UI `state` persists on the remote session | never | persisted |
| Remote run id equals the AG-UI run id | n/a | yes |

Unit: `tests/unit/os/interfaces/`, `tests/unit/app/test_agui_app.py`,
`tests/unit/team/test_remote_team.py` green. `ruff check`, `ruff format
--check` clean; `./scripts/validate.sh` output on this branch is
identical to the `origin/main` baseline (the 32 pre-existing mypy errors
in 8 files are unchanged; nothing new).

commits.commit_title: feat: migrate MCP client and AgentOS server to mcp 2.x (#9269)
commits.commit_message:
feat: migrate MCP client and AgentOS server to mcp 2.x (#9269)

## Summary

`mcp` 2.0.0 (released 2026-07-28) shipped breaking changes across the
client and server surface: it renamed `McpError` to `MCPError`, removed
`streamablehttp_client`, changed `ClientSession` timeouts to float
seconds, renamed `mcp.types` fields to snake_case, and dropped the
`timeout`/`sse_read_timeout`/`auth` kwargs from
`streamable_http_client`. Because the `mcp` extra declared an unbounded
`mcp>=1.9.2`, a fresh `pip install agno[mcp]` resolved to the
incompatible 2.0.0 and crashed on import (see #9267).

The blocker that made a quick "cap it" the only option has since
cleared: **fastmcp 4.0.0b1 now supports `mcp>=2.0.0,<3.0.0`**
(PrefectHQ/fastmcp #4655). So this PR does the full migration rather
than a temporary pin.

Changes:

- **Dependency floors** (`pyproject.toml`): `mcp = ["mcp>=2.0.0,<3.0.0",
"fastmcp>=4.0.0b1,<5"]` (pre-release fastmcp until stable 4.x ships).
Added `httpx[http2]>=0.28.1` floor — pre-release resolvers otherwise
pull `httpx 1.0` dev builds that drop `HTTPStatusError` and crash
`fastmcp.server.server` on import.
- **MCP client** (`utils/mcp.py`, `tools/mcp/mcp.py`,
`tools/mcp/multi_mcp.py`, `tools/mcp/params.py`): `McpError`→`MCPError`;
`streamablehttp_client`→`streamable_http_client` (now yields a 2-tuple);
`read_timeout_seconds` as float; snake_case attribute access
(`is_error`, `structured_content`, `mime_type`, `input_schema`);
`model_dump_json(by_alias=True)` for wire output;
`StreamableHTTPClientParams` timeouts as float seconds. A shared helper
`_streamable_http_connection()` maps the removed
`timeout`/`sse_read_timeout` kwargs onto an `httpx2.Timeout` via the
SDK's own `create_mcp_http_client` (the same pattern fastmcp 4 uses).
- **AgentOS auth** (`os/mcp_auth_builtin.py`): adapted to the v2
`OAuthClientInformationFull` — `client_id` is now a required `str`
(removed dead `None` guards),
`token_endpoint_auth_method`/`redirect_uris` are `Optional` (handled),
`model_dump_json(by_alias=True)` for stored client metadata.

fix: pin tree-sitter-language-pack<1.16 to unblock chonkie code chunker (#9901)

## Summary

CI unblock. `main` and every open PR have been red since 2026-09-01
16:52 UTC: 20 of 22 tests in
`libs/agno/tests/unit/knowledge/chunking/test_code_chunking.py` fail
with `AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'chunks'` (failing
run: https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/actions/runs/33556194573, last
green on `main`:
https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/actions/runs/33490379047). This should
merge ahead of feature work.

This repeats the #7869 / #7904 / #8012 cycle on the same package in the
same extra. #7869 pinned `tree-sitter-language-pack<1.8.0` in the
`chonkie` extra when tslp 1.8.0 removed a symbol chonkie imported; #7904
dropped the pin once chonkie migrated; #8012 raised the chonkie floor.

## Root cause

`tree-sitter-language-pack` 1.16.1 (PyPI, 2026-09-01) changed
`api.py::process()` from returning the native pyo3 `ProcessResult`
object to returning `options.ProcessResult`, which is a `TypedDict`, so
a plain `dict` at runtime. There is no alias, no `__getattr__`, no
deprecation path; `result.chunks` raises and only `result["chunks"]`
works. The change arrived in a generator regeneration commit
(xberg-io/tree-sitter-language-pack@18e2a6b2c, "chore(alef): bump pin to
0.72.0 and regenerate tree"); the 1.16.x release notes describe only the
regeneration and mention no API change, and tslp's own Python README
still documents attribute access.

chonkie's `CodeChunker._process_code` (`chonkie/chunker/code.py:172`)
does `return result.chunks`, so every code-chunking call fails. With
`language="auto"`, chonkie swallows the same error per language and
reports `ValueError: Could not auto-detect the language` instead (the
other 2 of the 20 failures).

## Why chonkie is not the culprit

chonkie did not change. Its newest release, 1.7.0, is from 2026-07-07.
Verified in three clean environments:

| chonkie | tree-sitter-language-pack | `test_code_chunking.py` |
|---|---|---|
| 1.7.0 (newest) | 1.16.1 (newest) | 20 failed, 2 passed |
| 1.6.7 (this repo's pinned minimum) | 1.16.1 | 20 failed, identical
traceback |
| 1.7.0 | 1.15.8 (previous PyPI release) | 22 passed |

Pinning or bumping chonkie would change nothing. The variable is the
transitive dependency one level below it. `chonkie[code]` floors tslp at
`>=1.8.0` with no ceiling, this repo declares tslp nowhere, and CI
installs `libs/agno[tests]` fresh on every run with no lock file, which
is why the break propagated within hours of the upload.

## The change

```toml
chonkie = [
    "chonkie[semantic,code]>=1.6.7",
    "tree-sitter-language-pack<1.16",  # 1.16.1 process() returns a dict; chonkie reads .chunks. Drop when xberg-io/tree-sitter-language-pack#183 or chonkie fixes that
]
```

No agno code changes: `CodeChunking.chunk()` reads `chunk.text` off the
list chonkie returns and never sees the dict. No tests added or modified
— the existing 22 are the contract, and they go 20 failed → 22 passed on
the dependency line alone.

`<1.16` rather than `!=1.16.1` because chonkie 1.x is frozen for fixes,
so an exclusion would need re-editing on every tslp release.

## Removal condition

tslp restoring attribute access (asked in
xberg-io/tree-sitter-language-pack#183). If the dict is intentional, the
pin stays until a chonkie release reads it, and removal looks like
#7904/#8012.

Upstream: xberg-io/tree-sitter-language-pack#183 · feyninc/chonkie#659
(filed for the record; no PR, 1.x is frozen)

## Verification

Clean resolve picks chonkie 1.7.0 + tslp 1.15.8, reproducible across two
fresh envs, package set differs by exactly one line.
`test_code_chunking.py` 22 passed · knowledge suite 816 passed, 13
skipped · full unit suite 19191 passed, 93 skipped (with
`tests/unit/models/xai_model` run separately: 132 passed, 1 skipped,
because under the full suite it hits a pre-existing GC-timing deadlock
in `models/xai/oauth.py` unrelated to this change) · resolves on Python
3.10 · ruff clean, mypy at pre-existing baseline.

commits.commit_message:
[fix] Resolve Gemini image MIME type instead of hard-coding image/jpeg (#9887)

## Summary

Gemini image inputs were always labelled `image/jpeg`, regardless of the
actual image format. `format_image_for_message()` in
`libs/agno/agno/utils/gemini.py` hard-coded `"mime_type": "image/jpeg"`
in all three branches (URL, filepath, raw bytes), so a PNG/WebP/GIF/HEIC
image was sent to the Gemini API declared as a JPEG. This can cause the
API to reject or misinterpret the image, and it silently discards an
explicitly supplied `Image.mime_type`.

This PR replaces the three hard-coded values with the existing helper
`agno.utils.media.resolve_image_mime_type()`, which is already used
elsewhere in the codebase and resolves in the documented priority order:
explicit `mime_type` > `format` field > file extension > magic bytes >
`image/jpeg` fallback. Behaviour for real JPEGs is unchanged, and the
fallback keeps the previous value when nothing can be determined, so
this is not a breaking change.

Issue number: #9885

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Improvement
- [ ] Model update
- [ ] Other:

---

## Changes

- `libs/agno/agno/utils/gemini.py`
- URL branch: resolve from the **downloaded bytes**
(`image_bytes=content_bytes`) plus any explicit `mime_type`/`format`.
The URL extension is deliberately *not* used here — the downloaded bytes
are authoritative, and a `.jpg` URL that actually serves WebP is
precisely the case this issue is about.
- Filepath branch: resolve from explicit `mime_type`/`format`, then the
file extension, then the file's magic bytes.
- Raw-bytes branch: resolve from explicit `mime_type`/`format`, then
magic bytes.
- `libs/agno/tests/unit/utils/test_gemini.py`: 7 new regression tests
covering URL/bytes/filepath resolution, explicit `mime_type` precedence,
the `format` field, JPEG stability, and the unknown-bytes fallback.
- `libs/agno/tests/unit/models/google/test_gemini.py`: **one existing
expectation changed.**
`test_format_messages_nests_tool_result_media_in_function_response`
builds `Image(content=b"image-bytes", mime_type="image/png")` but
asserted `"image/jpeg"` — i.e. the assertion encoded the bug being fixed
here. It now asserts `"image/png"`, matching the image the fixture
declares. Flagging this explicitly since changing an existing assertion
deserves a maintainer's eye.

## Testing

Commands actually run, in a clean `uv` venv with `uv pip install -e
libs/agno`:

- Reproduction script (no network; WebP/PNG/JPEG byte headers
constructed locally) covering URL, raw bytes, filepath, explicit
`mime_type`, and real JPEG.
  - Before: all 5 cases returned `image/jpeg`.
- After: `image/webp`, `image/webp`, `image/png`, `image/webp`,
`image/jpeg`.
- Sabotage check: with the fix reverted and the new tests kept, 5 of the
7 new tests fail; restoring the fix makes them pass. The tests genuinely
exercise the change.
- `ruff format --check` on the changed files → already formatted.
- `ruff check` on the changed files → all checks passed.
- `mypy --config-file libs/agno/pyproject.toml
libs/agno/agno/utils/gemini.py` (same config `./scripts/validate.sh`
uses) → 0 errors.
- `pytest libs/agno/tests/unit/utils/` → 488 passed, 1 skipped
(excluding `test_path_safety_consistency.py`, which needs the
`slack_sdk` extra that is not installed in my environment).
- `pytest libs/agno/tests/unit/models/google/` → 185 passed.

I did **not** run the entire `libs/agno/tests/unit` suite: it aborts
during collection on modules requiring optional vectordb/workflow extras
that I could not install here. Stating this rather than claiming a green
full suite. CI will cover the rest.

commits.commit_title: chore: Release v3.0.5 (#9888)
commits.commit_message:
chore: Release v3.0.5 (#9888)

# Changelog

## **Breaking Changes**

- **Embedding failures are surfaced, not masked.** Ingestion now reports
embedding failures instead of returning success. Content that previously
showed `completed` may now show `failed` or `partial` — those ingests
were always incomplete, they were only *reported* as successful.
The `ContentStatus` enum in the API (`/openapi.json`) gains `partial`,
changing
from `["processing","completed","failed"]` to `["processing","completed","partial","failed"]`.
No schema migration is required (the status column is
already `varchar`).
- **Embedders raise `EmbeddingError` instead of returning an empty
vector on failure.** Calling a vector DB's `search()` directly now
raises where it previously returned `[]`; `Knowledge.search()` is
unaffected and still returns no results.
- **AWS Bedrock embedding failures raise `EmbeddingError`,
not `ModelProviderError`.** Existing `except
ModelProviderError` handlers around Bedrock embedding will stop catching
— switch to `except EmbeddingError`.
- **`GET /knowledge/content/{id}/status` returns 404 for
missing/non-owned content** instead of 200 with `status: "failed"`.
- **`skip_if_exists=True` no longer skips content recorded
as `failed` or `partial`,** so incomplete content is re-embedded rather
than silently marked complete.

## **New Features**

- **`partial` content status**: new `ContentStatus.PARTIAL` for files
where some chunks embedded and others did not — searchable but
incomplete, so neither `completed` nor `failed`. (**#9814**)
- **Optional embedding retry during ingestion** (off by default): enable
with `Knowledge(max_embedding_retries=3, embedding_retry_backoff=1.0)`.
Authentication failures ignore both settings and fail on the first
attempt (the same credential is rejected every time). Note: each retry
re-embeds the whole document.
- **GandrTools**: new text-to-speech toolkit for the Gandr TTS API.
- **llmman model provider**: new model provider.

## **Improvements**

- **Actionable embedding failure messages**: failure messages now name
the chunk count, embedder, reason and recovery step, instead of "Could
not insert embedding".
- **Re-ingest no longer destroys searchable chunks**:
an `embed_before_replace` guard embeds documents before deleting
existing ones, so a failing re-ingest aborts before anything is removed
(previously a failed re-embed could leave a document with zero chunks).
- **`MCPTools` accepts static `headers=`**: connect-time auth headers
can be passed directly on the `url=` path for Streamable HTTP and SSE,
without constructing `StreamableHTTPClientParams`.

commits.commit_title: fix: surface embedding failures during knowledge ingestion (#9814)
commits.commit_message:
fix: surface embedding failures during knowledge ingestion (#9814)

## Summary

Ingestion reported completed for content that never embedded, so the
`knowledge_contents` row looked healthy while the agent could retrieve
nothing.
The root cause is in the embedders. Every one caught provider exceptions
and returned an empty vector:
 ```
def get_embedding(self, text: str) -> List[float]:
try:
response = self.response(text=text)
return response.data[0].embedding
except Exception as e:
log_warning(f"Failed to get embedding: {str(e)}")
return [] # <- rate limit, bad key, oversized chunk all land here
```                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  That [] flowed through `Document.embed()` into the vector store record. Nothing raised, so Knowledge fell through to content.status = ContentStatus.COMPLETED. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                             
  1. **Detection**. New **`EmbeddingError`** carries the provider, model, a classified reason and a recovery hint. All embedders raise it instead of returning [].                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  2. **Status**. New **`ContentStatus.PARTIAL`** for the case the customer called out: some chunks embedded, others did not. Searchable but incomplete, so neither completed nor failed.       
  
  3. **Recovery**. Failures are retried in place, before any status is written, while the chunk text is still in memory:                                                                                                                                                                                              
  
  **`Knowledge(vector_db=..., max_embedding_retries=3, embedding_retry_backoff=1.0)`** 
  
                                                                                                                 
  Authentication failures ignore both settings and fail on the first attempt, the same credential is rejected every time,   so retrying only delays the report.

embedder. Everything else in the file was already valid v3 and is

**Retired on Cerebras (5 files)**

`90_models/cerebras_openai/{basic,db,knowledge,structured_output,tool_use}.py`
— `llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct` was retired by Cerebras on

**Retired on Groq + unfetchable image (1 file)**

`meta-llama/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct` was shut down by Groq on
2026-07-17. Swapped to `qwen/qwen3.6-27b`, Groq's named replacement and
their only vision-capable model (Preview tier — no Production model
accepts images). The image URL also moves from Wikimedia to
`agno-public.s3.amazonaws.com/images/krakow_mariacki.jpg`: Wikimedia
returns 403 to Groq's server-side fetch (non-browser user agents are
blocked), so the file failed at runtime even with a working model. The

Groq `output_parse_failed` with the model's thinking text in

custom-tool-capable model (gpt-oss-20b: tool-call validation failures +
413 TPM cap; qwen3.6: silent stops; qwen3.8: 413 every run), and 15
across the documented mitigations via `request_params`
(`reasoning_format="hidden"`/`"parsed"` change nothing;
`service_tier="flex"` is a 400 on non-upgraded plans). Options are a
maintainer call: delete, rewrite around native reasoning, move to
another provider, or keep with the flakiness documented.
- `libs/agno/tests/integration/models/groq/test_multimodal.py` pins the
same retired Groq model. It's already skipped, and whether to un-skip it
against a Preview-tier model is a call for whoever owns the tests.

### Wider findings (not acted on here)

- ~25 other cookbook files pass `upload.wikimedia.org` image URLs; the
URL-form ones hand them to providers that fetch server-side, so the same
latent 403 exists across the repo. The `*_bytes.py` variants download
client-side and have a different failure surface.
- Groq's docs still list `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` and
`llama-3.1-8b-instant` as Production models; both return 404
`model_not_found` on a real call.
- Agno's `Groq` class exposes none of `reasoning_format`,
`include_reasoning`, `service_tier`, `disable_tool_validation` as
first-class fields — all four require `request_params={...}`.
- Suggested framework follow-up: the `Groq` class has no reasoning-token
handling in its streaming path, unlike `MiniMax`, which strips inline
`<think>` tags with a stateful filter and routes reasoning to the
Thinking panel. Adding the equivalent to `agno/models/groq/groq.py`
would fix `image_agent.py`'s streaming caveat, both
`10_reasoning/models/groq/` qwen cookbooks, and likely the finance
agent's silent stops. That's a `libs/` change, out of scope for this PR.

commits.commit_message:
feat: Add GandrTools text to speech toolkit for the Gandr TTS API (#9852)

This PR adds a Gandr text to speech toolkit, following the same
structure as the existing Cartesia and ElevenLabs toolkits.

Resolves #9853.

What changed:
- `libs/agno/agno/tools/gandr.py`: new `GandrTools` toolkit with a
`text_to_speech` tool. It mirrors `CartesiaTools`: constructor takes
`api_key` (falls back to the `GANDR_API_KEY` environment variable and
raises `ValueError` when missing), tools register via `enable_*` flags
plus `all`, and `text_to_speech` returns a `ToolResult` with an
`agno.media.Audio` artifact on success and an error string `ToolResult`
on failure.
- `cookbook/91_tools/gandr_tools.py`: runnable example mirroring
`cookbook/91_tools/cartesia_tools.py`: an Agent with `GandrTools()`,
then `write_audio_to_file` to save the result.
- `libs/agno/tests/unit/tools/test_gandr.py`: unit tests mirroring
`test_cartesia.py`: init with key, env var, overridden defaults, missing
key, feature registration, the text to speech happy path with request
argument assertions, parameter overrides, oversized input rejection, and
the error path. All network calls are mocked.

Implementation notes:
- The Gandr API is `POST https://tts.gandr.ai/v1/audio/speech` with a
Bearer key and an OpenAI compatible JSON body: `{"model": "tts-1",
"input": "...", "voice": "gandr-mia", "response_format": "mp3"}`. The
response body is the audio bytes.
- The toolkit calls it with `httpx`, which is already a core agno
dependency, so there is no new optional dependency and no `try/except
ImportError` block.
- Formats: mp3 (default), wav, and pcm. pcm is headerless signed 16 bit
little endian mono at 24000 Hz. The artifact `mime_type` is set per
format.
- Input is capped at 2000 characters per request; the toolkit validates
this client side and returns a clear error instead of making the
request.
- Voices: gandr-mia, gandr-ava, gandr-jenny, gandr-dane, gandr-leo,
gandr-lewis. The service supports 23 languages and every render is
watermarked.
- API keys are available at https://gandr.ai; the free tier is 50,000
tokens.

How to verify:
- `pytest libs/agno/tests/unit/tools/test_gandr.py -v` (no network, no
key needed).
- `GANDR_API_KEY=gnd_... python cookbook/91_tools/gandr_tools.py` writes
`tmp/greeting.mp3`.

Disclosure: I work on Gandr.


Addresses #9853.

commits.commit_title: chore: release 3.0.4 (#9862)
commits.commit_message:
chore: release 3.0.4 (#9862)

# Changelog

## Behavior Changes

- **`KnowledgeManagementTools` constructor flags renamed, `ingest_path`
now opt-in**: the 2.x-style `enable_ingest` / `enable_remove` flags are
replaced by flags named after the tools they register — `ingest_url`,
`ingest_path`, `ingest_text`, `remove_content` (the old names are no
longer recognised and are ignored if passed). `ingest_path` defaults to
off: it reads any path the server process can read, and under
`scope="shared"` what it loads becomes readable by every agent on that
knowledge base, so registering it is now an explicit choice.
`list_content` and `ingest_status` stay unflagged — they only read.
(#9861)
- **`agno.tools.knowledge_management` import path moved**:
`KnowledgeManagementTools` (introduced in 3.0.3) now lives at
`agno.tools.knowledge`; the old module path is gone. `from
agno.tools.file_generation import FileGenerationTools` keeps working
through a compatibility shim. (#9861)

## Improvements

- **`agno.tools.file` and `agno.tools.knowledge` are packages**:
`FileTools` and `FileGenerationTools` share `agno.tools.file`;
`KnowledgeTools` (read side) and `KnowledgeManagementTools` (write side)
share `agno.tools.knowledge`, following the `agno.tools.mcp` and
`agno.tools.finance` layout. Names resolve on first access, so importing
`FileTools` no longer pulls `reportlab` and `python-docx` in behind it —
measured at 44.8 ms with both installed, previously paid on every
`FilesystemContextProvider` import. (#9861)
- **AtomicMail reuses its auth handshake**: the resolved context
(capability JWT, API URL, account and inbox ids) is cached on the
instance until the token nears expiry, in both sync and async paths, and
keyed to the api_key it was minted from so re-registration is picked up
on the next call. Warm tool calls drop from ~35 s to 0.4–3 s. (#9825)
- **AtomicMail proof-of-work parallelised**: the scrypt nonce search
splits across a bounded thread pool — new `pow_workers` argument,
default `min(4, cpu_count())`, with `pow_workers=1` matching the old
sequential search exactly. Measured at difficulty 10: mean solve 25.9 s
→ 10.4 s on 4 workers. `pow_timeout` still bounds the search, and a
worker that finds a solution wins over a concurrent timeout. (#9825)

## Bug Fixes

- **AtomicMail `list_inbox` returned the agent's own sent mail**:
`send_email` files the outgoing message in the inbox mailbox with
`$draft` set, and `list_inbox` queried that mailbox unfiltered, so an
agent could not tell its own outgoing mail from a reply. The query now
filters `notKeyword: "$draft"`, the parser drops any `$draft` entry, and
a rejected query is reported as an error instead of an empty inbox.
(#9825)
- **Caller-supplied `requires_confirmation_tools` dropped the
`remove_content` gate**: `KnowledgeManagementTools` set its confirmation
list with `setdefault`, so passing your own list silently removed the
built-in confirmation requirement on `remove_content` — the one tool in
the kit that destroys data. The lists now union. (#9861)

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.commit_title: fix: AtomicMail list_inbox returns sent mail; reuse auth and parallelise proof-of-work (#9825)
commits.commit_message:
fix: AtomicMail list_inbox returns sent mail; reuse auth and parallelise proof-of-work (#9825)

## Summary

Follow-up to #9130 (AtomicMail toolkit). Three defects in
`AtomicMailTools`, one correctness and two latency, all verified live
before and after:

| # | defect | fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Sent mail reads back as received.** `send_email` files the
outgoing message in the inbox mailbox with `$draft` set and never clears
it; `list_inbox` queries that same mailbox with no keyword filter. An
agent cannot tell its own outgoing mail from a reply — live, one
`list_inbox` returned `count: 2` where one was our own sent message. |
`Email/query` now filters `notKeyword: "$draft"`, `Email/get` requests
`keywords`, and the parser drops any `$draft` entry. Live server honours
the filter: 4 messages, 2 of them `$draft`, filtered to exactly the
other 2. The list parser also now reports a rejected query (method-level
`["error", ...]`, e.g. `unsupportedFilter`) as an error instead of an
empty inbox — the guard the send parser already had. |
| 2 | **Every tool call re-runs the whole auth handshake.** challenge ->
proof-of-work -> session -> capability -> JMAP session -> mailbox
lookup, then one JMAP request. Four sequential `list_inbox` calls
measured 140s, of which the JMAP reads were ~1.3s. | The resolved
context (capability JWT, `apiUrl`, account id, inbox mailbox id) is
cached on the instance until the token nears its own `exp`, in both the
sync and async twins, and keyed to the api_key it was minted from, so a
forced re-registration (this instance, another instance, or another
process sharing the credentials dir) is picked up on the next call. Warm
calls now 0.4–3s. |
| 3 | **The proof-of-work solve is single-threaded.** `hashlib.scrypt`
releases the GIL, so the nonce search parallelises but ran on one
thread. | `_solve_pow` splits the nonce space across a bounded
`ThreadPoolExecutor` (`workers` threads search `start, start+workers,
...`; first valid digest wins, the rest stop). New `pow_workers` ctor
arg, default `min(4, cpu_count())`; `pow_workers=1` is byte-for-byte the
old sequential search. Live at difficulty 10: mean solve 25.9s -> 10.4s
on 4 workers (3.8x). |

### Where the time went, and goes

```
before (per tool call)                          after
────────────────────────                        ─────────────────────────────────────
POST /challenge                                 first call in a 90s window:
scrypt PoW solve      ~25s  (1 thread)            POST /challenge
POST /session                                     scrypt PoW solve   ~10s  (4 threads)
POST /capability                                  POST /session, /capability
GET  /.well-known/jmap                            GET  /.well-known/jmap, Mailbox/query
POST Mailbox/query                                -> context cached until exp - 30s
POST Email/query+get  ~0.3s                     every later call in the window:
                                                  POST Email/query+get  ~0.3-1s
```

### Item 1 on the wire

```diff
 ["Email/query", {
     "accountId": ...,
-    "filter": {"inMailbox": <inbox>},
+    "filter": {"inMailbox": <inbox>, "notKeyword": "$draft"},
     ...
 ["Email/get", {
-    "properties": ["id", "threadId", "receivedAt", "from", "to", "subject", "preview"],
+    "properties": ["id", "threadId", "receivedAt", "from", "to", "subject", "preview", "keywords"],
```

The result shape is unchanged (`keywords` is consumed by the parser, not
surfaced). The `list_inbox` docstring now says "emails received".

### Item 2 — the cache

Follows the one client-side token cache in the library, `tools/zoom.py`
(private attributes, check-then-refresh at the top of the accessor,
expiry set short of the real one). Lifetime is the capability JWT's own
`exp - iat` span (or `exp` against the local clock when the token
carries no `iat`) on a monotonic clock; a token without a numeric `exp`
is never cached; refresh happens 30s early so a request that starts just
inside the window cannot outlive the token. `credentials.json` is still
read on every call, as before; the cache is keyed to the api_key it
holds, so a swapped file means a fresh handshake, not a stale inbox.

Deliberately **not** in this PR: a 401-refresh retry path (a
conservative margin instead); `Toolkit(cache_results=...)` (a disk cache
under `gettempdir()` would serve a stale inbox); `connect()`/`close()`;
persisting the token; the shared clients in `utils/http.py` (see note
below).

### Item 3 — precedent

There is almost none under `tools/`: `ThreadPoolExecutor` appears once,
in `tools/exa.py`, as a `max_workers=1` timeout wrapper. Elsewhere in
the library it is the house pattern for fan-out (`workflow/parallel.py`,
`team/_task_tools.py`). The default is bounded at 4, not `cpu_count()`:
saturating every core with scrypt starves the host, the same class of
defect #9130 fixed with `asyncio.to_thread`. The async path already runs
the solve under `asyncio.to_thread`; the pool sits inside that, so the
event loop stays free. `pow_timeout` still bounds the search; the
deadline is checked by every worker, and because one worker can cross it
while another is mid-way through the winning hash, the pool waits for
every worker and a solution wins over a timeout.

### One observation from the live lane

With the handshake gone, warm calls issued back-to-back hit the API's
burst rate limit (`429 rate_limited … Retry after 3s`). The old 25s
handshake was spacing calls out. The toolkit returns it as the usual
`{"error": ...}` with the server's retry hint; no retry logic added.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Improvement

---

## Checklist

- [x] Code complies with style guidelines
- [x] Ran format/validation scripts (`./scripts/format.sh` and
`./scripts/validate.sh`) — mypy 26 errors before, 26 after, none in
`atomic_mail`
- [x] Self-review completed
- [x] Documentation updated (comments, docstrings)
- [ ] Examples and guides: Relevant cookbook examples have been included
or updated (if applicable) — no cookbook change; `pow_workers` is opt-in
with a safe default
- [x] Tested in clean environment
- [x] Tests added/updated (if applicable)

### Duplicate and AI-Generated PR Check

- [x] I have searched existing [open pull requests](../../pulls) and
confirmed that no other PR already addresses this issue
- [ ] If a similar PR exists, I have explained below why this PR is a
better approach
- [x] Check if this PR was entirely AI-generated (by Copilot, Claude
Code, Cursor, etc.) — written with Claude Code, reviewed and verified by
me

---

## Additional Notes

**Tests** (`libs/agno/tests/unit/tools/test_atomic_mail.py`, 33 -> 47,
all mocked). Each new test was written first and fails on `main` for the
defect it names:

| test | fails on main with |
|---|---|
| `test_list_inbox_query_excludes_drafts_on_the_wire` | `KeyError:
'notKeyword'` |
| `test_list_inbox_drops_draft_messages_from_result` | `count` 2 != 1 |
| `test_list_inbox_reuses_auth_within_token_window` (+ async twin) |
second call re-ran the handshake |
| `test_list_inbox_reauthenticates_after_token_expiry` | reuse inside
the window: `assert 2 == 1` handshakes |
| `test_forced_register_drops_cached_auth_of_replaced_inbox` | reuse
before the forced swap: `assert 2 == 1` handshakes |
| `test_cached_auth_is_dropped_when_credentials_change_on_disk` | reuse
proven, then the swapped key was ignored |
| `test_solve_pow_prefers_a_solution_over_a_concurrent_timeout` |
timeout raised over a valid proof |
| `test_capability_token_without_numeric_exp_is_not_cached` | (cannot
fail on main — main never reuses; red against the pre-fix version of
this diff, `TypeError`) |
| `test_list_inbox_reports_rejected_query_as_error` | `count: 0`
reported for a rejected query |
| `test_solve_pow_single_worker_matches_sequential_search` | `TypeError:
unexpected keyword 'workers'` |
| `test_solve_pow_parallel_returns_a_valid_proof` (recomputes scrypt for
the returned nonce) | same |
| `test_solve_pow_parallel_is_bounded_by_pow_timeout` | same |
| `test_pow_workers_defaults_bounded_and_reaches_the_solve` | no
`pow_workers` attribute |

None of the 33 existing tests changed.

**Verification beyond unit tests.** A local mock of `auth.atomicmail.ai`
+ `api.atomicmail.ai` that verifies the proof-of-work server-side:
register -> list -> send -> list, run twice per process, sync and async
on the same instance, with `pow_workers` 1 and 4 — two server-side PoW
verifications total (registration + the first read), every later call
served from the cache, `notKeyword` present on the wire, sent mail
excluded. The same mock driven through a real `Agent` (`run` and `arun`)
with a scripted offline model, since no shipped example calls these
tools through an agent. Live, against the registered inbox: the numbers
above (read-only), then one real send from the toolkit directly (cold
handshake 3.3s on 4 workers, then `list_inbox` 0.5s from the cache, our
own outgoing mail absent from the listing, the 2 received messages
present) and one agent-driven run with `OpenAIResponses(id="gpt-5.5")`:
`Agent.run` -> `list_inbox`, `Agent.arun` -> `send_email` on the same
toolkit instance, the send served from the context cached by the sync
read. Both mails were delivered to the recipient's mailbox.

**Shared HTTP clients.** The plan considered switching the six
`httpx.Client(...)`/`AsyncClient(...)` sites to `utils/http.py`'s
`get_default_sync_client()`/`get_default_async_client()`. Not done here:
no toolkit uses them today, and every existing network test mocks
`httpx.Client().__enter__`, so the swap would rewrite the mock in 25
tests for a ~0.3s-per-call TLS saving that is small next to the
handshake this PR removes. Happy to do it as a follow-up if wanted.

Co-authored-by: Ashpreet <ashpreetbedi@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.commit_title: refactor: agno.tools.file and agno.tools.knowledge as packages (#9861)
commits.commit_message:
refactor: agno.tools.file and agno.tools.knowledge as packages (#9861)

## Summary

Two toolkits that belong together now share one import path, and
`KnowledgeManagementTools` drops its 2.x-style `enable_*` flags.

```python
from agno.tools.file import FileGenerationTools
from agno.tools.knowledge import KnowledgeManagementTools
```

**Packages.** `agno/tools/file.py` and `agno/tools/knowledge.py` become
packages that hold their sibling toolkit, following `agno.tools.mcp` and
`agno.tools.finance`:

```
agno/tools/file/__init__.py        FileTools, FileGenerationTools
agno/tools/file/file.py            (was tools/file.py)
agno/tools/file/generation.py      (was tools/file_generation.py)

agno/tools/knowledge/__init__.py   KnowledgeTools, KnowledgeManagementTools
agno/tools/knowledge/knowledge.py  (was tools/knowledge.py)
agno/tools/knowledge/management.py (was tools/knowledge_management.py)
```

Names resolve on first access (PEP 562, the `agno/knowledge/__init__.py`
pattern), so importing `FileTools` no longer pulls `reportlab` and
`python-docx` in behind it — measured at **44.8 ms** with both
installed, and `agno.context.fs.FilesystemContextProvider` was paying it
on every import. A test pins the laziness out-of-process.

**Constructor flags.** `KnowledgeManagementTools` replaces
`enable_ingest` / `enable_remove` with flags named after the tools they
register:

```python
ingest_url: bool = True
ingest_path: bool = False
ingest_text: bool = True
remove_content: bool = True
```

`ingest_path` becomes opt-in. It reads any path the server process can
read, and under `scope="shared"` what it loads becomes readable by every
agent on that knowledge base — so the common case no longer needs to
remember to exclude it:

```python

KnowledgeManagementTools(knowledge=product_knowledge, exclude_tools=["ingest_path"])
