commits.commit_title: fix: cache tool schema derivation across runs (#9771)
commits.commit_message:
fix: cache tool schema derivation across runs (#9771)

## Summary

Agno rebuilt every tool's schema on every run: `parse_tools` re-ran
`inspect.signature`, `get_type_hints`, docstring parsing, JSON-schema
construction and pydantic `validate_call` for each registered tool on
each request, so an agent carrying tools paid ~190 us per tool per run
even when no tool was called. cProfile showed 93-95% of a mock-model
run's time going to schema construction at 10 tools, and cross-framework
benchmarking showed a 10-tool no-call run turning a 4.4x win over
LangGraph into a 5x loss.

This PR derives each tool's schema **once per callable** and hands every
run a cheap isolated copy:

- `Function.from_callable` caches a fully-built template per `(class,
callable identity, name, strict)` and returns an isolated per-run copy
of it on every call.
- `Function.process_entrypoint` fetches a cached `_EntrypointSchema`
record per `(entrypoint identity, strict, requires_user_input,
user_input_fields)` — the old inline introspection moved verbatim into
`_derive_entrypoint_schema` — and applies it to the live instance, so
instance-owned state (a user-authored `parameters` schema,
`description`, fresh `UserInputField`s) is still (re)built per run.
- `Function._wrap_callable` caches the `validate_call` wrapper per
callable; the wrapper holds no per-call state, so all runs share it.
This was the single largest cost (~60 us per tool per run).
- `Function._resolve_framework_params` and the `needs_media` signature
check (`entrypoint_accepts_media`) are cached per entrypoint.
- The agent and team parse loops use a new `Function._per_run_copy()`
instead of `model_copy(deep=True)`: same isolation contract (fresh
`parameters` and `user_input_schema`, everything else shared by
reference, all private attrs — subclass-declared ones included — reset
to class defaults, `_framework_params` copied), ~3x cheaper.

### Numbers (mock model, median of 200 runs; benchmark from the issue;
before/after interleaved in one load window)

| Agent `run()` | before | after | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| no tools | 54.5 us | 58.3 us | parity (within cross-run noise;
quiet-window rounds read 59.8 vs 59.1) |
| 1 raw callable | 264.6 us | 79.0 us | 3.3x |
| 10 raw callables | 1,926 us | 168 us | 11.5x |
| 50 raw callables | 9,416 us | 584 us | 16.1x |
| async, 10 tools | 1,892 us | 170 us | 11.1x |
| team, 10 tools (marginal over 0 tools) | ~184 us/tool | ~11 us/tool |
~17x |
| team, 0 tools | 564 us | 597 us | parity (within noise; quiet rounds
read 605.6 vs 605.4) |

Marginal cost per registered tool: ~190 us -> ~11 us. A 10-tool run is
now ~2.8x a 0-tool run (was ~35x). Independently reproduced by a
separate cross-framework benchmark harness (147.9 us at 10 tools on the
pre-review-fix commit; the 10-tool row flipped from a 5x loss to a 2.2x
win over LangGraph, with tool construction time unchanged — the cost was
removed, not relocated).

### What the cache keys on, and why it cannot go stale, leak, or pin
memory

- **Identity, not equality.** Keys hold the callable via
`_CallableIdentity` (hash by `id`, eq by `is`, strong reference). Two
callables that compare equal (bound methods of equal objects, instances
with custom `__eq__`) may dispatch to different objects, and the wrapped
entrypoint must call the exact object it was built from. A live entry's
strong reference pins the object, so its id cannot be reused for a wrong
hit (verified by an executed probe in review).
- **Closure-carrying callables never enter the caches**
(`_cache_stable`): a callable with a closure cell anywhere under its
`__wrapped__`/`partial` chain is usually a per-run factory product (team
`delegate_task`, knowledge/memory default tools close over the run's
output, session and agent). An identity-keyed cache can never hit those,
and caching them would pin the last ~N runs' full graphs in memory — the
adversarial review's highest-severity finding, verified with weakref
probes and fixed by the gate. Module functions, bound methods, `@tool`
wrappers — the long-lived tools — all cache. Gated tools behave exactly
as before this PR (weakref test pins that dropped closures are
collectable).
- **Failed derivations are never cached.** A derivation that fails (e.g.
a forward reference defined after the tool — notebook cell order, late
class registration) raises a carrier exception through `lru_cache`,
which never stores raising calls, so the failure replays and heals on
the next run exactly as the uncached code did. This also applies to the
framework-params injection guard, where freezing a partial result would
have left type-owned parameters unguarded for the process lifetime.
- **Bounded without a cliff.** All caches are `lru_cache(maxsize=4096)`
— sized after review measured that a cyclically-revisited working set
larger than the cache decays to 0% hits (not graceful degradation), and
a multi-agent server can exceed 512 distinct tools.
- **Everything else is read live.** Edits to `agent.tools`, a toolkit's
surface (`get_functions()` is read per run), `instructions`,
`description`, hooks, and skills flow into the next run. `strict`
(per-run `output_schema`), `name`, `requires_user_input`, and
`user_input_fields` are part of a key. `async_mode` selects different
source Function objects, keying them apart naturally.
- **Isolation.** The only structures downstream code writes into are the
`parameters` dict and the `UserInputField` objects inside
`user_input_schema` (the model layer writes the user's answers into
them). Both are freshly copied for every run — same contract as the
`model_copy(deep=True)` this replaces — and per-run private attrs
(`_run_context`, media, `_agent`, `_team`) are reset on copy. Verified
against a full map of every Function mutation site downstream of
`parse_tools` (models/base.py HITL writers, continue-run answer writers,
FunctionCall execution — which writes no Function field at all).

### Tests

New suite `libs/agno/tests/unit/tools/test_tool_schema_cache.py` (16
tests) pins:

- two sequential runs on one agent see their own `_run_context`/media,
with disjoint Function instances; run context does not leak across
users/sessions;
- **two concurrent `arun()` calls** on one agent with different
users/sessions/images do not cross-contaminate
(`test_concurrent_runs_do_not_cross_contaminate`);
- mutating `agent.tools` (append and replace) between runs changes the
tools the model sees; a toolkit surface change between runs is seen;
live source-Function edits flow through;
- `from_callable` copies are isolated and the cache keys on name and
strict; distinct callables with one name get distinct schemas;
- `user_input_schema` is fresh per run; parsed `parameters` mutations do
not reach the next run; stale per-run state on a source is not carried;
- **closure tools are not pinned** (weakref + gc assertion) and still
parse/run correctly without the cache;
- **a transient introspection failure heals on the next parse** on both
the `from_callable` and `process_entrypoint` paths.

Mutation-tested: 12 hand mutations (share the template, drop a key
component, skip a copy, skip the per-run reset, disable media detection,
re-freeze failures) — 10 killed by named tests, 2 proven equivalent (the
strict-mode `required` list a mutation would corrupt is unconditionally
rebuilt by `process_schema_for_strict`, in the pre-change code too).

Adversarial review: a 10-agent workflow (4 lenses: behaviour parity,
state isolation, staleness/invalidation, concurrency/lifecycle; every
non-low finding independently verified with executed probes). Confirmed
findings — closure pinning, frozen transient failures, the LRU cliff,
dict-subclass flattening in hand-authored schemas, a strict-path
`param.default ==` evaluation main never ran, subclass private attrs —
are all fixed in the third commit. Full unit suite differential vs
unmodified `main` in the same venv: identical failure lists (95
pre-existing environment failures / 371 pre-existing collection errors
from missing optional extras, byte-identical names on both sides), +16
passed = exactly the new tests.

commits.commit_title: [fix] Tolerate a tool schema without `properties` in strict mode (#9409) (#9578)
commits.commit_message:
[fix] Tolerate a tool schema without `properties` in strict mode (#9409) (#9578)

## Summary

Fixes #9409.

`Function.process_schema_for_strict` rebuilt `required` by reading
`self.parameters["properties"]` bare:

```python
self.parameters["required"] = [
    name
    for name in self.parameters["properties"]   # <- KeyError when the key is absent
    ...
]
```

Not every schema that reaches this method comes from `get_json_schema`.
`MCPTools` registers a server's schema verbatim
(`parameters=tool.inputSchema`, `libs/agno/agno/tools/mcp/mcp.py:773`),
and a real MCP server advertises an argument-free tool as `{"type":
"object"}` — no `properties` key at all. Under strict mode that raised
`KeyError: 'properties'`.

The failure mode is what makes it hard to diagnose: agent construction
and `MCPTools` registration both succeed, because
`Function(skip_entrypoint_processing=True)` only calls
`process_schema_for_strict()` from `process_entrypoint(strict=True)`.
What dies is every *run* of the agent, which returns `RunStatus.error`
with the one-word content `'properties'`.

This is the other half of the family #9371 already fixed on the
non-strict path (`user_properties = self.parameters.get("properties") or
{}`, `function.py:1275`).

## Fix

Normalise a missing or non-dict properties map to `{}` before the
rewrite, and store it back, so strict mode emits the same complete shape
the no-parameter default already uses (`function.py:798`): `properties:
{}`, `required: []`, `additionalProperties: false`.

## Verification

`process_schema_for_strict` extracted byte-for-byte from `main`
(`b889441`) and from the patched file, run against four schema shapes:

| schema | `main` | patched |
|---|---|---|
| `{"type": "object"}` (MCP no-arg tool) | ❌ `KeyError: 'properties'` |
✅ `{'type': 'object', 'additionalProperties': False, 'properties': {},
'required': []}` |
| `{"type": "object", "properties": None}` | ❌ `TypeError: 'NoneType'
object is not iterable` | ✅ same as above |
| normal schema with an injected `agent` param | ✅ `required: ['p1']` |
✅ `required: ['p1']` (identical) |
| `{"type": "object", "properties": {}, "required": []}` | ✅ | ✅
(identical) |

Both previously-passing shapes are byte-identical before and after, so
this is additive only.

The new regression test fails on `main` with `KeyError: 'properties'`
and passes with the patch.

commits.commit_title: fix: stop rebuilding session history on every conversation turn (#9775)
commits.commit_message:
fix: stop rebuilding session history on every conversation turn (#9775)

## Summary

Conversation cost was quadratic: on turn N the session store rebuilt all
N-1 prior runs from their dicts — twice. cProfile of a 100-turn
conversation showed 94% of run time in session-store round-tripping
(`get_session` deep-copied the whole stored session and re-ran
`RunOutput.from_dict`/`Message.from_dict` on every run; `upsert_session`
deep-copied and re-deserialized the entire stored history just to build
a return value the per-turn save path discards). Instrumented counts:
9,901 `RunOutput.from_dict` calls over a 100-turn conversation, ~99 per
turn at turn 100.

Four changes, in order:

1. **`InMemoryDb.upsert_session` returns the incoming session's runs** —
the SQL adapters' contract (verified by executed probe against SqliteDb:
fresh session row, caller's own runs attached by reference, stored
history untouched). The in-memory adapter alone rebuilt and deep-copied
the whole stored history for a return value; a full caller audit found
only two consumers of the deserialized return (both REST routes passing
`deserialize=True` explicitly, both unaffected).
2. **Bounded reads slice before copying** — `runs_limit` reads
deep-copied the full history first, then sliced.
3. **`InMemoryDb` serves agent-session history runs from a run-object
cache.** Objects are built once per stored run dict and shared by every
read; the invalidation token is the stored dict's identity —
`upsert_run` replaces the dict on every write (and now keeps its own
copy of incoming dicts, so a caller-held dict can never rewrite stored
state in place). The session row is rebuilt fresh per read; the stored
dicts stay canonical; nothing ever serializes the shared objects back.
4. **The same cache for SQLite and Postgres (sync + async), keyed for
SQL**: run rows are fetched as raw text (cast to `Text`, keeping the
JSON column's result processor out of the way) and the token is
`(hash(text), len(text))` per `run_id` — **a write from this or any
other process changes the text and misses the cache**, so cross-process
correctness holds by construction. Only fully-migrated agent sessions on
the full-history `deserialize=True` path use it; windowed reads,
legacy-blob sessions, and team/workflow sessions keep the rebuild path
unchanged.

### The isolation contract, and how it is preserved without the per-turn
deepcopy

Shared history run objects are **immutable by contract**. That contract
is enforced, not assumed:

- A full map of every session consumer/mutator (built for this change)
found exactly two agent-path sites that mutate a historical run in
place. Both now copy first:
`_mark_run_regenerated`/`_amark_run_regenerated` flip status on a
shallow copy and replace the session's list entry; continue-by-`run_id`
deep-copies the run it resumes at extraction (all three sites — sync,
async, async-stream). Fork already deep-copied; the model-bound history
path already copies per message (`copy_history_message`, #9700).
- Team and workflow sessions are deliberately excluded from the cache:
their save paths scrub member responses / media on loaded runs, and
hardening those is its own piece of work. They keep today's fresh-copies
behavior bit for bit.
- The stored dicts/rows remain canonical: caller mutation of returned
objects can never reach them (pinned by named tests), and
`deserialize=False` reads are unchanged (full deep copies).

### Numbers (mock model; InMemoryDb unless stated; medians)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| conversation, per-turn at turn 5 / 100 | 246 µs / 4,832 µs (**19.3x
growth**) | 180 µs / 208 µs (**1.2x growth**) |
| conversation, 100-turn total | 265 ms | 20.5 ms (**12.9x**) |
| conversation, 100-turn total (async) | ~equal to sync | 20.8 ms |
| `RunOutput.from_dict` calls per turn | ~N (99 at turn 100) | **1** |
| durable (SQLite), 50-turn total | 98.3 ms | 72.8 ms |
| durable (SQLite), per-turn read at turn 50 | 1,293 µs and growing |
263-344 µs, flat |
| single turn (fresh session, with db) | 174.7 µs | 152.3 µs |
| agent construction | 7.5 µs | 7.2 µs |

The durable row's remaining floor is the per-turn write pair
(`upsert_run` + session row update, ~0.9 ms, fsync-bound); its read side
no longer grows with history. Conversation and durable shared the same
root cause, so both land in this one PR.

### Correctness verification

- **History equality**: stored dicts and `get_messages()` output are
byte-identical to unmodified `main` after 5/25/100-turn conversations
(differential harness; only the auto-generated per-process agent name
differs). Also pinned in-suite: cached objects vs a fresh rebuild of the
stored dicts.
- **New suite** `libs/agno/tests/unit/db/test_run_object_cache.py` (22
tests): shared-object reads, per-run invalidation on
update/append/delete/recreate, caller-held-dict isolation, store
isolation under caller vandalism, **two concurrent `arun()` calls on one
session** (and on separate sessions), history equality, the hardened
regenerate and continue mutators, and the SQLite twin including **a
second adapter instance on the same file standing in for another
process**.
- **Mutation-tested**: 6 hand mutations (drop each invalidation token,
share the caller's dict, return the cached list itself, revert each
mutator hardening) — 6/6 killed by named tests.
- **Adversarial review**: a 17-agent workflow (4 lenses — missed
mutators, staleness/invalidation, behavior parity, concurrency/memory —
every non-low finding independently verified by executed probes; 13/13
confirmed) ran against the initial cache commits and earned its keep. It
found the immutability contract was enforced at only two mutator sites
while the boundaries feeding everything else still handed out shared
objects: background continue and the job-queue sweeper flip status on
`session.get_run` results, AG-UI/Slack resume writes HITL answers into
requirement objects from a session read, and
`continue_run(run_response=...)` truncates the caller's object — each
probe showed never-persisted state published to every reader of the
session (sticky when the follow-up persist fails). It also caught a
threaded-read crash in the InMemoryDb cache sweep and that the SQL
adapters never dropped a deleted session's cached objects. All of it is
fixed in the final commit: `AgentSession.get_run` and the last-run
getters return the caller's own copy (covering background continue, the
terminal handlers, the sweeper, and Slack in one move), AG-UI's
paused-run finder copies, the `run_response` branch copies like the
`run_id` branch, reads publish a fresh entry map instead of sweeping a
shared one, and `drop_session` is wired into both delete paths of all
four adapters. One reviewer re-ran its corruption probes against the
fixed tree and reported every leg negative.
- Full unit suite differential vs unmodified `main` in the same venv:
identical pre-existing failure lists, plus the new tests. Three
regenerate tests were updated to assert the durable outcome (the session
entry's status and the store) instead of write-through mutation of a
caller-held object — that write-through is exactly what the isolation
hardening removes.
- `./scripts/format.sh` and `./scripts/validate.sh` pass (mypy clean).

- [ ] If a similar PR exists, I have explained below why this PR is a

Code, Cursor, etc.)

---

## Additional Notes

**Contract change, deliberate and argued:** history run objects returned
by `get_session` (and the sessions built from them during a run) are now
shared between reads instead of freshly rebuilt. Library code honors
immutability (hardened as above). User code that mutates a returned
session's *historical* runs in place was silently tolerated before and
is unsupported now — such a mutation never reaches the stored dicts/rows
(still pinned by tests), but it can be visible to later reads in the
same process. The stored state remains the source of truth in every
case.

**Follow-ups (out of scope here):** team/workflow session reads keep the
rebuild path until their save-time scrub paths are hardened to
copy-first; session-row JSON fields are double-encoded in every SQL
adapter (dumps into a JSON column that dumps again — a storage-format
fix needing read-compat migration); SQLite's
`upsert_session(deserialize=False)` branch re-serializes all runs (only
REST-ish callers hit it); the non-SQL remote adapters (mongo, redis,
dynamo, …) keep the rebuild path and stay correct.

commits.commit_message:
fix: use httpx for location lookup instead of undeclared requests (#9793)

## Summary

`agno.utils.location` imported `requests`, which is not a declared
dependency of the core package. `add_location_to_context=True` loads the
helper while the system message is being built, so a core-only install
hit `ModuleNotFoundError` on the first run.

This switches the helper to `httpx` — already a core dependency
(`httpx[http2]`) — and adds coverage for the helper itself and for the
`Agent(add_location_to_context=True).get_system_message(...)` path.

Issue number: #9772

### Relationship to #9738

This supersedes #9738, which carries the same `requests` -> `httpx`
switch from @Elioooon (authorship preserved on the commit here). That PR
is from a fork with "Allow edits from maintainers" disabled, so it could
not be rebased or amended in place — its CI has been stuck on a
two-day-old base since Aug 24, with one shard failing on an unrelated
flaky test and `fail-fast: true` cancelling the other four.

One deliberate difference from #9738. That PR also narrowed the
exception clause:

```python
except (httpx.HTTPError, KeyError, ValueError) as e:
```

`get_location()` runs inline while a system message is assembled, and
its result only decorates that message, so any failure must come back as
an empty dict rather than reach the run. Three httpx exceptions do
**not** subclass `httpx.HTTPError`:

- `httpx.InvalidURL`
- `httpx.CookieConflict`
- `httpx.StreamError`

Under the narrowed clause each of those escapes `get_location()` and
breaks `get_system_message()` for every agent and team with
`add_location_to_context=True`. This PR keeps the broad `except
Exception` and adds a comment explaining why it is intentional rather
than an oversight.

### Tests

`libs/agno/tests/unit/utils/test_location.py` (13) and
`libs/agno/tests/unit/agent/test_location_context.py` (2). Beyond the
two happy-path tests from #9738:

| Test | Covers |
|---|---|
| `test_get_location_swallows_every_failure` | 8 parametrized failures,
incl. the three non-`HTTPError` httpx types |
| `test_get_location_returns_empty_dict_when_lookup_is_not_ok` | non-200
from the geolocation host |
| `test_get_location_survives_a_malformed_geolocation_payload` | 200
with none of the expected keys |
| `test_get_location_does_not_import_requests` | guards the actual
regression |
| `test_a_failed_lookup_drops_the_location_line_and_not_the_run` |
system message still builds when the lookup fails |

Verified against three versions of the helper:

- original `requests` version — 13 fail (the module cannot be mocked via
`httpx`)
- #9738's narrowed-clause version — 4 fail, all in
`test_get_location_swallows_every_failure`
- this PR — 15 pass

commits.commit_title: fix: make ScheduleManager cleanup tolerate partial copies (#9792)
commits.commit_message:
fix: make ScheduleManager cleanup tolerate partial copies (#9792)

## Summary

`ScheduleManager.close()` assumed `_pool` always exists. A failed
`deepcopy()` of a manager that owns a database engine can leave an
object that `__new__` allocated but whose `__init__` never populated.
When the collector reaches that half-built object it calls `__del__()`,
which calls `close()`, which raised `AttributeError` while reading
`_pool`.

`close()` now reads `_pool` through `getattr(..., None)`, treating a
missing pool the same as no pool having been created. Fully initialized
managers shut down and clear the pool exactly as before.

Issue number: #9614

### Relationship to #9787

This supersedes #9787, which carries the same one-line fix from
@Elioooon (authorship preserved on the commit here). That PR is from a
fork with "Allow edits from maintainers" disabled, so its test coverage
could not be extended in place. This PR keeps the fix and replaces the
single smoke test with a fuller set.

The original test was:

```python
def test_close_handles_partially_constructed_manager():
    manager = ScheduleManager.__new__(ScheduleManager)
    manager.close()
    manager.__del__()
```

It does fail without the fix, so it was a real regression test — but it
asserts nothing, and the explicit `manager.__del__()` call duplicates
the `close()` line above it while not testing the reported scenario. In
real use `__del__` runs under the garbage collector, which swallows
exceptions and routes them to `sys.unraisablehook`; a failure on that
path would print to stderr and still pass. It also never exercised the
`deepcopy` path that produces the half-built object in the first place.

`TestManagerCleanup` replaces it with five tests:

| Test | Covers |
|---|---|
| `test_close_on_manager_that_never_ran_init` | `close()` is quiet and
leaves `_pool` unset |
| `test_close_is_idempotent_on_partial_manager` | a second `close()` (as
`__del__` would make) stays quiet |
| `test_collecting_a_partial_manager_reports_nothing` | the real GC
path, via `sys.unraisablehook` |
| `test_failed_deepcopy_leaves_nothing_that_raises_on_collection` | the
reported trigger end to end |
| `test_close_still_shuts_down_a_real_pool` | the fix did not break
normal shutdown |

Each was run against both versions of `close()`. The first four fail
without the fix and pass with it; the fifth passes either way, which is
what makes it the guard against over-correcting.

## Summary

`cookbook/90_tools` and `cookbook/92_models` were renumbered to
`91_tools` and `90_models` by #6042 (2026-01-19), and #6515 (the v2.5

updated the references. 296 `cookbook/...` paths across the repo pointed
at directories and files that no longer exist, and nothing in CI checks
path references, so this went unnoticed for seven months.

This resolves every reference that has a live target, removes the
entries whose target no longer exists anywhere, and fixes one case that
was breaking at runtime rather than in docs.

### Runtime fix

`cookbook/frameworks/langgraph/langgraph_session_agentos.py` passed
`app="langgraph_tools_agentos:app"` to `agent_os.serve`. `AgentOS.serve`
hands a string straight to uvicorn, which imports that module — and

[fix] add PubMed request timeout (#9463)

Closes #9465

## Problem

`PubmedTools` makes two external NCBI E-utilities requests during
`search_pubmed()`, but neither request exposed or passed a tool-level
client timeout. A slow or stalled PubMed response can hold the tool call
longer than intended.

## Before / after

Before:
- `fetch_pubmed_ids()` called `httpx.get()` without a tool-level
timeout.
- `fetch_details()` called `httpx.get()` without a tool-level timeout.
- Callers could not configure the local HTTP timeout for these requests.

After:
- `PubmedTools` accepts a `timeout` constructor option, defaulting to 30
seconds.
- The new option is appended after the existing public constructor
parameters to preserve positional compatibility.
- Both PubMed HTTP requests pass `timeout=self.timeout` to
`httpx.get()`.
- Existing constructor behavior remains unchanged unless callers opt
into a different timeout.

commits.commit_title: feat: Release v3.0.0 (#9755)
commits.commit_message:
feat: Release v3.0.0 (#9755)

⚠️ **Breaking release.** A database migration is required before v3.0
serves traffic. Read the **[v3 Migration
Guide](https://docs.agno.com/other/v3-migration)** first, and see the
full **[v3.0 Changelog](https://docs.agno.com/other/v3-changelog)** for
every change.

## **New Features**

- **Tool result
offloading**: `Agent(offload_tool_results=True)` / `Team(...)` writes
any tool result over 16,000 chars to `AgentFS` and leaves a short
envelope (preview, size, `result_id`) in the message; the agent
gets `read_result` / `search_result` (+ async) to fetch the rest. No
model call on the write path. Tune via `ResultStore(threshold_chars=...,
ttl_seconds=...)`.
(**[#9436](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/9436)**, **[#9684](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/9684)**)
- **Media offloading**: `media_storage=S3MediaStorage(bucket=...)` on an
Agent/Team/Workflow uploads images, audio, video and files to local
disk, S3 or GCS before persistence; the row keeps a
small `MediaReference` instead of base64 (a 113 KB JPEG drops from
~151,000 chars to 2,897). No schema change.
(**[#9340](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/9340)**)
[Docs](https://docs.agno.com/sessions/persisting-sessions/media-storage/overview)
- **CodeMode**: `CodeMode(tools=[...])` swaps a wide tool schema for one
programmable IPython kernel that persists across a session — the model
writes Python and calls tools as awaitable handles, composing them
(variables, loops, helpers) without round-tripping through the
transcript.
- **FinanceTools**: One unified finance toolkit with swappable data
providers.
- **RampRouter model**: New model provider for Ramp Router
([router.com](http://router.com/)).
- **SuperGrok OAuth**: Device-code auth for the xAI model.
- **AtomicMail Toolkit:** Adds an **AtomicMail** toolkit
(`AtomicMailTools`) that gives an Agno agent its own email inbox

### **Database**

- **Runs get their own table**: each run is a row in `agno_runs` with
real columns
(`session_id`, `run_type`, `agent_id`, `team_id`, `workflow_id`, `user_id`, `parent_run_id`, `status`, `run_index`)
+ JSON payload. Takes session write amplification from O(N²) to O(N) and
removes the DynamoDB/Firestore item-size
ceiling. `session.get_messages()`, `get_chat_history()`, `db.get_session()` and
AgentOS session routes are unchanged (runs re-attach on read).
(**[#8350](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/8350)**)
- **Direct run APIs**: `db.get_run()`, `db.get_runs(session_id=...,
status=..., limit=...,
page=...)`, `db.upsert_run()`, `db.delete_run()`, `db.delete_runs()` (sync
+
async); `db.get_session(runs_limit=N)` and `db.get_sessions(include_runs=False)`.
(**[#8350](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/8350)**)
- **One-line migration**: `MigrationManager(db).up()` creates the runs
store and copies legacy runs across, non-destructively and idempotently,
on 12 sync + 4 async backends; un-migrated DBs still work (reads merge
runs table with legacy blob). Schema versions tracked on every adapter.
(**[#8350](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/8350)**)
- **Typed stale-DB
errors**: `MigrationRequiredError` / `SchemaMismatchError` name both
remedies; AgentOS carries `error_id: "migration_required_error"` in the
JSON body.
(**[#9669](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/9669)**, **[#9631](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/9631)**)
- **Three new tables**: `agno_runs`, `agno_jobs` (durable background
queue), `agno_tool_results` (offload index) — all auto-created.

### **Per-user isolation**

- Extends beyond sessions to **metrics, schedules, evals, knowledge,
components, entity memory, and 17 vector databases**. Metrics aggregate
per user per day; unowned components/knowledge are shared (readable by
all, editable by admin) so enabling isolation doesn't 404 pre-isolation
building blocks.
(**[#8245](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/8245)**, **[#8262](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/8262)**)

### **AgentOS & Studio**

- **Durable background
execution**: `AgentOS(queue=QueueConfig(durable=True))` — accepted runs
are committed rows that survive crashes/restarts/deploys, executed by
any replica. Bounded concurrency (default
32, `AGNO_BACKGROUND_MAX_CONCURRENCY`), cancellable while
queued, `Idempotency-Key` dedupe, 429 on full queue. Queue REST surface
(`GET /queue/jobs`, `.../{job_id}`, `POST .../requeue`, `GET
/queue/stats`). Redis is optional coordination, never truth.
(**[#9079](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/9079)**, **[#9504](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/9504)**)
- **Studio 3.0 — governed catalog**: `create_*` writes a DRAFT that
serves nobody until `publish_component`; compare-and-set guards (typed
409s), tombstoned deletes, archive/restore, dependent-tracking.
StudioTools returns a machine-readable envelope (`{ok, status, data,
error{...}, warnings}`) across ~31 tools.
(**[#9604](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/9604)**)

### **Tools**

- **MiniMax video generation tools**.
(**[#9529](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/pull/9529)**)
- Toolkits now have a stable `id` used by AgentOS to reference tools.

## **⚠️ Breaking Changes**

**Every 2.x user must read this. A database migration is required before
v3.0 serves traffic.**

### **Storage & migrations**

- Runs are no longer a JSON blob in the sessions table — they live
in `agno_runs`. Run `MigrationManager(db).up()` (or AgentOS `POST
/databases/all/migrate`) before serving. The v2→v3 migration preserves
the legacy `runs` column as a backup; reclaim it
with `db.cleanup_legacy_runs_column()` (SQL)
/ `db.cleanup_legacy_runs_field()` (document/KV) after verifying.
- Stale/unmigrated databases raise typed errors instead of silently
misbehaving.
- **Pagination**: `page` without a `limit` (or `page < 1`) now
raises `ValueError` instead of returning unbounded/negative results.

### **AgentOS**

- **JWT**: `secret_key` removed
from `JWTMiddleware` and `authorization_config` —
use `verification_keys` (a list).
- **Metadata routes**: `GET /models` removed (model data moved to `GET
/config` under `available_models`); `GET /` returns a minimal landing
response; `GET /info` is the single unauthenticated metadata endpoint.
- **MCP server config**: `AgentOS(enable_mcp_server=...,
mcp_config=...)` removed — pass a single `mcp_server=` instead.
- **Background execution** requires a `db` on the component (returns 400
without one). External-framework agents (LangGraph, Claude, DSPy, etc.)
stream inline for `background=true` and are not resumable.

### **Agents**

- Renamed params:
    - `enable_user_memories` → `update_memory_on_run`
    - `search_session_history` → `search_past_sessions`
    - `num_history_sessions` → `num_past_sessions_to_search`
    - `num_past_session_runs` → `num_past_session_runs_in_search`
- `reasoning=True` removed — set `reasoning_model=<native reasoning
model>` explicitly.
- `continue_run` / `acontinue_run`: `updated_tools` removed —
pass `requirements` (list of `RunRequirement` from the paused run
output).
- **Culture feature
removed**: `enable_agentic_culture`, `add_culture_to_context`, `CulturalKnowledge`,
culture tools, and the `agno_culture` table. Use Knowledge for shared
cross-user info.

### **Teams & Workflows**

- The **`Workflow` constructor is keyword-only**: `Workflow(name=...,
steps=[...])`. `Team` is unchanged — `Team([agent_1, agent_2])` still
works, though `Team(members=[...])` is preferred.
- **Flat HITL kwargs removed** on Step/Steps/Loop/Condition/Router
(`requires_confirmation`, `confirmation_message`, `on_reject`, `requires_user_input`, `user_input_message`, `user_input_schema`, `requires_output_review`, `output_review_message`, `requires_iteration_review`, `iteration_review_message`, `on_error`, `hitl_max_retries`, `hitl_timeout`, `on_timeout`).
Use `human_review=HumanReview(...)` (from `agno.workflow.types`); names
unchanged
except `hitl_max_retries` → `max_retries`, `hitl_timeout` → `timeout`.

### **Tools**

- **`MultiMCPTools` deleted** (along with `allow_partial_failure`) — use
one `MCPTools` per server.
- `MCPToolbox`: `auth_tokens` / `auth_headers` removed —
use `auth_token_getters`.
-
`DuckDuckGoTools.duckduckgo_search` → `web_search`, `duckduckgo_news` → `search_news` (now
built on `WebSearchTools`).
- **Flat Google tool modules
deleted** (`agno.tools.gmail`, `googlesheets`, `googlecalendar`, `google_maps`, `google_drive`, `google_bigquery`)
— import from `agno.tools.google.*`.
- **Google
tools**: `creds_path` / `auth_port` → `credentials_path` / `oauth_port`;
Sheets `enable_read_sheet` etc. → bare method names.
-
`FileTools.check_escape` → `Toolkit._check_path` (`LocalFileSystemTools.check_escape` unaffected).
-
**`SQLTools`**: `enable_list_tables` / `enable_describe_table` / `enable_run_sql_query` →
bare method names.
- **Seltz**: `max_documents` → `max_results`; the legacy SDK path is
removed (`seltz>=1.2.0` required).
- **`StudioTool`** alias removed — use `StudioTools`.
- `BrightData.get_screenshot`:
unused `output_path` removed. `PgVector.enable_prefix_matching` removed
(dead helper).

### **Knowledge & Vector DBs**

-
**`Knowledge.add_content` / `add_content_async` / `add_contents_async`** removed
→ use `insert()` / `ainsert()` / `ainsert_many()`.
- **`GDriveContextProvider`** renamed → `GoogleDriveContextProvider`.
- **LanceDB**: `use_tantivy` removed/ignored.
- Searching a pre-v3 vector table with
a `user_id` raises `ValueError` (directing you to the vector DB
migration) instead of returning empty results.

### **Scheduler**

- `update_schedule` is now allow-listed
(only `name`, `description`, `method`, `endpoint`, `payload`, `cron_expr`, `timezone`, `timeout_seconds`, `max_retries`, `retry_delay_seconds`, `enabled`, `next_run_at`, `disabled_reason`);
any other key raises `ValueError`. Ownership/provenance/lock state are
no longer writable via the generic path. New provenance columns added by
the v3.0.0 migration.
- The schedules unique key changes from `name` to `(user_id, name)`. If
duplicate schedule names exist across the same user, the migration
aborts — deduplicate before migrating.

### **Evals**

- **`eval_id` → `run_id`** (**#9739**): eval classes no longer
carry `eval_id`; every run gets its
own `run_id`. `store_result_in_file` renames the `eval_id` parameter
to `run_id`, the `{eval_id}` placeholder
in `file_path_to_save_results` templates is no longer accepted
(use `{run_id}`), and `POST /eval-runs` returns the id the row was
actually stored under (`run_id`). Re-runs no longer overwrite each
other.

### **Models & Learning**

- **Mistral**: `mistralai` v1 compatibility layer removed
— `agno[mistral]` requires `mistralai>=2.0.0` (and is back in
the `models` extra).
- **`agno.models.metrics` module and the `Metrics` alias removed** →
import from `agno.metrics` (`RunMetrics`).
- **`Model.classify_error` removed** →
use `ModelProviderError.classify(error)`.
- **Entity memory** under `namespace="user"` is now isolated per user
(row keys embed a `user_id` digest); pre-v3 rows re-keyed by the v3.0.0
migration
(`agno.learn.migrations.rekey_user_entity_learnings`); `EntityMemoryStore.delete`/`get` require
a keyword-only `user_id` in that namespace.
- Removed learn
aliases: `MemoriesConfig` → `UserMemoryConfig`; `MemoriesStore` → `UserMemoryStore`; `Decision` → `DecisionLog`.

## **Deprecated (still working)**

- **`knowledge_retriever(dependencies=...)`** → prefer `run_context`. A
retriever whose signature still names `dependencies` keeps working via
an explicit backward-compat branch; `run_context` wins when both are
present.
-
**Scopes**: `system:read` / `system:write` → `config:read` / `config:write`.
The old names remain valid aliases and existing tokens keep working.
- **`RedisDB`** (vector DB) → `RedisDb`.
Note `RedisVectorDb` is *also* still exported, to disambiguate from

## **Migration quick-reference**

[Docs](https://docs.agno.com/other/v3-migration): Step-by-step guide,
database migration, and a paste-into-your-coding-agent prompt

```python
import asyncio
from agno.db.migrations.manager import MigrationManager

# Step 1: run before serving v3.0 traffic (up() is async)
asyncio.run(MigrationManager(db).up())

# Step 2: VERIFY the runs landed before any cleanup
assert len(db.get_runs(limit=5)) > 0, "Migration copied nothing - do NOT clean up"

# Step 3 (optional, destructive): reclaim the legacy blob column.
# The migration preserves it as a backup, so force=True is required.
db.cleanup_legacy_runs_column(force=True)   # SQL adapters
# db.cleanup_legacy_runs_field(force=True)  # document / KV adapters
```

On AgentOS: `POST /databases/all/migrate`. Full details in the **v3.0
changelog docs**.

## Summary

This is the v3.0 release: 109 commits from `feat/v3.0` into `main`,
~1,010 files, +190,764/-25,616.

v3.0 changes how Agno stores a session, how it isolates users, and how
much of a run has to live in the model's context. Session runs move out
of the `agno_sessions.runs` JSON blob into a dedicated `agno_runs`
table, which takes write amplification for a session from O(N²) to O(N)
and removes the DynamoDB/Firestore item-size ceiling on long sessions.
Per-user isolation stops being a session-level idea and reaches evals,
metrics, schedules, components, knowledge content, entity memory and 17
vector databases. Large tool results and media bytes can be offloaded
out of the transcript and out of the database entirely. AgentOS gains a
durable background job queue, a governed Studio component catalog, and
pluggable event streams so a run can be followed from any replica.
Alongside that, roughly 50 deprecated parameters, aliases, modules and
endpoints are removed, and the framework's hot paths got measurably
faster (cold import 233 ms to 147 ms; a 25-turn in-memory conversation
38.6 ms to 12.2 ms).

Every 2.x user must read the Breaking changes and Migration sections
below. **A database migration is required before v3.0 serves traffic.**

Related: #8350, #8245, #8262, #9079, #9340, #9436, #9604, #9322, #8940,
#8354, #9560, #9515, #9554.

Release-readiness fixes found while writing this are split out into
#9712. The breaking-change and migration entries below were verified by
execution against this branch — constructing the removed API to confirm
it raises, importing each replacement, and running the migration
end-to-end — not by reading commit messages.

---

## Highlights

### Runtime

- **Tool results and member answers offload to files instead of bloating
the transcript.** `Agent(offload_tool_results=True)` /
`Team(offload_tool_results=True)` writes any tool result over 16,000
characters to AgentFS and leaves a short envelope (preview, size,
`result_id`) in the message. The agent gets `read_result` /
`search_result` (plus async twins) to fetch the rest. No model call on
the write path, nothing summarized away. Tune with
`ResultStore(threshold_chars=..., ttl_seconds=...)`. (#9436, #9684)
- **Media bytes move out of the database.**
`media_storage=S3MediaStorage(bucket=...)` on an Agent, Team or Workflow
uploads images, audio, video and files to local disk, S3 or GCS before
the run is persisted; the row keeps a small `MediaReference` instead of
base64. A 113 KB JPEG goes from ~151,000 characters in the run row to
2,897. No schema change, no migration. (#9340)
- **One HITL config object for workflow primitives.** Step, Loop,
Router, Condition, Parallel and Steps take
`human_review=HumanReview(...)` — pre-execution confirmation, user input
with a schema, post-execution output review, per-iteration review for
loops, multi-route selection for routers, plus shared `on_reject` /
`on_error` / `max_retries` / `timeout` / `on_timeout`. Conflicting flags
fail at construction. (#8354)
- **Background runs are bounded, resumable and crash-durable.**
`arun(background=True)` no longer spawns an unbounded task: a
per-event-loop semaphore caps concurrent background runs (default 32,
`AGNO_BACKGROUND_MAX_CONCURRENCY`), run-status transitions go through an
atomic generation-fenced patch, and every streamed event carries a
stream-assigned `event_index` so a reconnecting client can replay from
where it left off. (#9079)
- **Measured speedups on every hot path.** Single mocked run 65 µs,
agent construction 4.7 µs, cold import 147 ms (was 233 ms), 25-turn
in-memory conversation 12.2 ms (was 38.6 ms — from a loss against
LangGraph to a 1.8x win). Copy-on-write history messages, incremental
run persistence in `InMemoryDb`, O(1) session lookup, cached event-union
type tuples, and `to_dict` no longer deep-serializing fields it
discards. Reference table in `cookbook/performance/README.md`. (#9689,
#9700, #9678, #9693, #9699, #9707)
- **A reassigned `db` no longer serves a stale cached session.** With
`cache_session=True`, reassigning `.db` used to keep serving and growing
the same cached session across databases. The cache is now tagged with
the db it was loaded from and dropped on mismatch. (#9699)
- **A workflow session returns only its own runs.** A step's agent or
team run shared the workflow's session id and came back as one of the
workflow's top-level runs, producing `KeyError: 'steps'` or a bogus
`WorkflowRunOutput`, which made a paused workflow unresumable. Member
runs are skipped on the session read and stay retrievable via
`db.get_runs(session_id=...)`. (#9634)
- **`from agno.workflow import Workflow` works without fastapi
installed.** Two modules imported `WebSocket` at module level purely for
annotations. (#9696)
- **Workflow event serialization survives cyclic object graphs.**
Workflow HITL over the WebSocket hit `maximum recursion depth exceeded`
and silently dropped the event from every sink, including the `/resume`
replay. (#9641)

### Database

- **Runs get their own table.** Each run is a row in `agno_runs` with
real columns for the fields you filter on (`session_id`, `run_type`,
`agent_id`, `team_id`, `workflow_id`, `user_id`, `parent_run_id`,
`status`, `run_index`) and the payload as one JSON value.
`session.get_messages()`, `get_chat_history()`, `db.get_session()` and
the AgentOS session routes are unchanged — runs are re-attached on read.
(#8350)
- **Direct run APIs on the db.** `db.get_run()`,
`db.get_runs(session_id=..., status=..., limit=..., page=...)`,
`db.upsert_run()`, `db.delete_run()`, `db.delete_runs()` — sync and
async. `db.get_session(runs_limit=N)` makes "the last N runs" an indexed
query instead of a full-history load;
`db.get_sessions(include_runs=False)` skips them entirely. (#8350)
- **A migration you can run in one line.** `MigrationManager(db).up()`
creates the runs store and copies every legacy run across,
non-destructively and idempotently, on 12 sync backends and 4 async
ones. AgentOS also exposes `POST /databases/all/migrate`. Un-migrated
databases still work: reads merge the runs table with the legacy blob by
run_id. (#8350)
- **A stale database says so.** Schema mismatches raise a typed
`MigrationRequiredError` / `SchemaMismatchError` naming both remedies,
and AgentOS carries `error_id: "migration_required_error"` through to
the JSON body so a frontend can offer the migration. (#9669, #9631)
- **Per-user isolation reaches evals, metrics, schedules, knowledge and
components.** Metrics aggregate per user per day rather than one global
row. Unowned eval runs are invisible to a scoped caller; unowned
components and knowledge rows are shared — readable by everyone,
editable only by an admin — so enabling isolation does not 404 every
pre-isolation building block. (#8245, #8262)
- **Warm queries stop paying for introspection.** Table resolutions are
cached on `BaseDb`/`AsyncBaseDb` and invalidated wherever a table
actually changes. A warm Postgres `get_session` issues exactly 1 SQL
statement and 0 introspection queries. (#9623)
- **SqliteDb runs in WAL journal mode**, with `synchronous` left at FULL
so durability is unchanged; falls back gracefully where SQLite cannot
switch. The durable 25-turn benchmark went from 52.3 ms to 42.2 ms.
(#9707)
- **Custom session tables get a correctly foreign-keyed runs table.**
Two db instances with different `session_table` names collided on one
shared `agno_runs` whose FK was locked to whichever created it first;
every run from the other instance violated the FK, was swallowed to a
warning, and `run()` still returned `completed`. When `session_table` is
customized and `runs_table` is not set, the runs table name is now
derived as `{session_table}_runs`; the default session table still gets
`agno_runs`, and an explicit `runs_table` always wins. (#9388)
- **Three new tables:** `agno_runs`, `agno_jobs` (the durable background
queue) and `agno_tool_results` (the offload index). All created
automatically.

### AgentOS and Studio

- **Durable background execution.** With
`AgentOS(queue=QueueConfig(durable=True))` an accepted run is a
committed row that survives a crash, restart or deploy and is executed
by whichever replica claims it. At-most-once by default
(`max_attempts=1`), cancellable while queued, `Idempotency-Key` returns
the existing run instead of enqueueing twice, a full queue answers 429.
(#9079)
- **Queue operations REST surface.** `GET /queue/jobs`, `GET
/queue/jobs/{job_id}`, `POST /queue/jobs/{job_id}/requeue`, `GET
/queue/stats`. When the durable queue is off the prefix answers 503
naming the switch. (#9079, #9504)
- **Cross-replica live run views.** Run events flow through a pluggable
`BaseEventStream`. Default is in-memory; `QueueConfig(redis=...)` wires
distributed cancellation in and Redis Streams events out, so SSE
`/resume` and the workflow WebSocket can replay and follow a run from
any replica. (#9079)
- **Durable HITL continuations across five doors.** Continuing a paused
run is a state transition on the existing ticket (`paused → queued`), so
`run_id` stays stable across arbitrary pause/continue cycles. Inline
sync, inline SSE, durable HTTP, workflow WebSocket and MCP/AG-UI/Slack
all pass one admission gate; every other door refuses with 409, so
cross-door double execution is structurally impossible. (#9079, #9404,
#9392, #9499)
- **Studio 3.0: a governed catalog.** `create_*` writes a DRAFT that
serves nobody until `publish_component` promotes it; a draft can be
previewed as a real recorded run by its owner. Writes carry
compare-and-set guards (typed 409 conflicts), deletes are tombstoned,
components archive and restore, and dependent-tracking refuses to orphan
a team or workflow member. Every write is stamped with the acting
`user_id`. (#9604)
- **StudioTools returns a machine-readable envelope.** ~31 flat tools,
each returning `{ok, status, data, error{code, message, details,
retryable}, warnings}` with stable error codes the model branches on
instead of parsing prose. Workflow steps are a recursive
`WorkflowStepSpec`. A palette policy (`allowed_tools`/`denied_tools`)
keeps runtime-discovered tools resolvable but not buildable. (#9604)
- **Zero-config Studio, and workflows as registry citizens.** Studio
toolkits resolve their db lazily from the registry AgentOS declares
(previously an `__init__` snapshot taken too early, which left every
write answering `db_not_configured` forever). `Registry` gains a
`workflows` bucket so Studio's runner can list and dispatch OS-served
workflows. (#9639, #9692)
- **Governed schedules with provenance.** Schedules gain `user_id`,
`managed_by`, `target_type`/`target_id`, actor stamps and
`disabled_reason`. Archiving a component disables every schedule aimed
at it with a reason. The executor refuses to fire a managed schedule
whose endpoint drifted from its provenance target. (#9604)
- **Media routes.** `GET
/sessions/{session_id}/media/{storage_key:path}` streams bytes or
re-signs a URL with `?redirect=true`; session deletes accept
`delete_media=true`. AgentOS auto-discovers the backend from the first
component that declares one. (#9340)
- **One unauthenticated metadata endpoint.** `GET /` is a minimal
landing payload hidden from OpenAPI, `GET /info` is the single metadata
endpoint, `GET /models` is gone and its data moved into `GET
/config.available_models`. (#7647)
- **RBAC filtering now covers DB-loaded teams and workflows.** `GET
/teams` and `GET /workflows` filtered registry components and then
appended DB-loaded ones below the check, unfiltered. Both now mirror
`GET /agents`, and the three list endpoints page to the end instead of
truncating at 20. (#9505, #9639)
- **Unhandled 5xx responses no longer echo exception text.** Store and
driver failures routinely carry connection strings, SQL fragments and
hostnames; 5xx now returns only the exception type. (#9669)

### Tools

- **CodeMode: a persistent Python kernel as a toolkit.** The model's
Python runs in an IPython kernel that lives as long as the session —
variables, imports, helpers and parsed tool results survive across turns
and are snapshotted to AgentFS so they survive process restarts.
Toolkits passed as `CodeMode(tools=[...])` are bound into the kernel as
awaitable handles instead of appearing in the model's tool list, so a
tool call becomes an `await` the model can loop over and compose without
a transcript round-trip. (#9436, #9684)
- **FinanceTools: one finance toolkit, swappable providers.**
`FinanceTools()` uses Yahoo Finance with no API key;
`FinanceTools(provider=FinancialDatasets())` swaps the data source
without touching the agent. Eleven tools returning normalized
dataclasses; unsupported tools are dropped per provider; custom
providers subclass `FinanceProvider`. (#9606)
- **Every Toolkit has a stable id.** `Toolkit` carries an `id`, derived
deterministically from `name` when not supplied. Because every built-in
toolkit forwards `**kwargs`, any toolkit can be given one:
`Calculator(id="calc-prod")`. (#8724)
- **XAIAuth: SuperGrok sign-in as agent tools**
(`sign_in_with_supergrok`, `check_supergrok_login`) for chat and web UIs
where a terminal device-code flow will not work. (#9616)
- **SchedulerTools becomes per-user and refuses dead targets.** The
owner comes from the run's `user_id`; creating or enabling a schedule
aimed at an archived or draft-only component is refused with a typed
error instead of arming a schedule that can only 404. (#8245)
- **AgentOSTools reports failed schedules correctly.** Redaction fired
on any status code, so a failed schedule was reported as "HTTP 200";
`get_platform_metrics` forced a rescan of the current day on every call;
caller-supplied day windows are now normalized once. (#9242)
- **Tools can declare whether they change external state** via
`Function.has_side_effects`, reported by Studio's tool discovery so a
composing agent can tell a read from a write.

### Models

- **New provider: RampRouter (router.com).**
`RampRouter(id="gpt-5.6-luna")` or the model string
`"ramp:gpt-5.6-luna"` fronts OpenAI, Anthropic, Fireworks and xAI behind
one OpenAI-Responses endpoint. Hand it a candidate list
(`models=["openai:gpt-5-nano", "anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5"]`) and it
picks and fails over between them, with `provider_timeout` and
`timeout_before_headers` controlling failover. (#9626)
- **Sign in to xAI with a SuperGrok subscription, no API key.** A new
`xAIResponses` model authenticates via RFC 8628 device-code login;
`XAITokenManager` (imported from `agno.models.xai.oauth`) stores the
session encrypted on `agno_auth_tokens` and refreshes it silently across
restarts. Tokens are keyed by `user_id`, so several people on one
deployment each spend their own subscription. The existing `xAI` chat
model is untouched. (#9616)
- **Claude works on anthropic 1.0.0.** The SDK's 1.0.0 major dropped
`output_format` from `create()`, dropped `temperature`/`top_p`/`top_k`
from every messages surface, and moved from httpx to httpx2. All three
are fixed for first-party Claude, Bedrock, Vertex and Azure Foundry,
with a byte-identical wire request. Floor raised to `anthropic>=0.77.0`.
(#9686, originally reported as #7111)
- **OpenAI reasoning effort and service tier accept every value the API
takes.** Four open unions in `agno.models.openai.types` name today's
documented values and accept any other string, so the next value OpenAI
ships works on the day it ships, while editors still offer the named
values as completions. Inherited by every model built on
OpenAIChat/OpenAIResponses. (#9658)
- **Claude accepts non-PDF document URLs** (fetched and inlined rather
than sent as a `url` source), and **Moonshot file uploads survive
extension-less filenames**. (#9340)

### Knowledge and Learning

- **Per-user RAG isolation across 17 vector databases.**
`Knowledge.search(user_id="alice")` returns Alice's chunks plus the
shared bucket; `user_id=None` is the admin view. Each backend maps the
owner to its own native primitive: a real column on
pgvector/singlestore/lancedb/clickhouse, an indexed payload/keyword
field on qdrant/opensearch/weaviate/mongo, a TAG on redis/valkey, a
`__shared__` sentinel on milvus/cassandra/couchbase, a
collection-per-user on chroma. (#8245)
- **Agents scope their own knowledge searches to the run's user
automatically** — forwarded to `Knowledge.retrieve()`, to a custom
`knowledge_retriever`, to filter validation and to the
`add_to_knowledge` tool, applied after the caller's `**kwargs` merge so
callers cannot override the run owner. (#8245)
- **Knowledge content rows have an owner** and the AgentOS knowledge API
enforces it: cross-user `GET` returns 404 (existence masked rather than
403'd), modifying shared content returns 403, `DELETE
/knowledge/content` clears only the caller's rows. (#8245)
- **Entity memory is isolated per user.** Two users recording an entity
with the same name and type shared one physical row: the first writer's
facts were replaced by the second's and then appeared in the first
user's reads *and in their rendered prompt context* — a cross-user
prompt-injection channel, not just data bleed. Row keys now embed a
digest of the owner. `get`/`delete` fail-opens were closed in the same
change. (#9322, fixes #9319 and #8334)
- **Eval runs are isolated per user**; cross-user GET/PATCH returns 404,
cross-user DELETE is a no-op. The eval framework itself is unchanged.
(#8262)
- **LearningMachine becomes a named, shareable registry resource.**
Components serialize a reference to the name rather than the machine's
config, which makes learning the single memory surface a Studio-built
agent or team can be given. Store initialization is now serialized by a
per-instance lock and backfills late-bound `model`/`db`/`knowledge`.
(#9695)

## Migration

### 1. Run the database migration before v3.0 serves traffic

Back up first, then run this once from your deploy step, **before the
application accepts requests**:

```python
import asyncio
from agno.db.migrations.manager import MigrationManager
from agno.db.postgres import PostgresDb

db = PostgresDb(db_url="postgresql+psycopg://...")
asyncio.run(MigrationManager(db).up())
```

In async code, `await MigrationManager(async_db).up()` directly. It is
idempotent, non-destructive, and migrates every table type in one pass:
it creates `agno_runs` and copies every legacy run across, adds
`user_id` to evals / components / knowledge / schedules / schedule_runs
/ metrics, moves the metrics unique key onto `(user_id, date,
aggregation_period)`, adds the Studio schedule-provenance columns, and
re-keys `namespace="user"` entity-memory learnings.

There is no CLI. AgentOS also exposes `POST /databases/all/migrate` and
`POST /databases/{db_id}/migrate`, but those run with the app already
up, which is too late for the entity-memory step below.

Full guide: `libs/agno/agno/db/migrations/V3_MIGRATION_GUIDE.md` **in
this repository** — it is not included in the published wheel, so `pip
install agno` does not give you a copy.

**What self-migrates and what does not.** Session runs self-migrate:
reads merge the runs table with the legacy blob by run_id (table wins on
conflict) and active sessions move their runs across on first save, so
the run migration is strongly recommended rather than strictly
mandatory. **Entity memory does not.** Until the re-key runs, the store
writes to the new per-user key while reads still match the old row, so a
pre-upgrade entity is split across two rows: reads return the old one,
listings show it twice, and a delete removes the row reads are not
returning. This is the one step that genuinely requires downtime. Re-run
it standalone with `from agno.learn.migrations import
rekey_user_entity_learnings; rekey_user_entity_learnings(db,
dry_run=True)` — it does not consult the schema version. Only
deployments that explicitly set `namespace="user"` are affected; the
default `namespace="global"` does not re-key.

**Reclaiming the legacy column.** `db.cleanup_legacy_runs_column()`
(SQL) / `db.cleanup_legacy_runs_field()` (Mongo, Firestore, Redis,
Valkey, DynamoDB, SurrealDB, JSON, GCS-JSON) refuses while any session
still holds a non-null legacy blob. The migration deliberately copies
rather than nulls, and writes never null it, so on any database that
carried 2.x runs the unforced call will always refuse. After verifying
the migrated data against the original, call it with `force=True`.

**Reverting.**
`asyncio.run(MigrationManager(db).down(target_version="2.5.6"))`
rebuilds the session blobs from the runs table and drops the runs table.
Three caveats: the entity-memory re-key is **not** reversed (restore
from backup instead); reverting evals destroys every `user_id` value;
and the metrics revert refuses outright once per-user rows exist (the
guide ships a Postgres consolidation script to run first). SQLite
reverts need SQLite 3.35+.

### 2. Migrate your vector databases for per-user RAG isolation

See `libs/agno/migrations/v2_to_v3/README.md` and the three scripts
beside it.

- **Mandatory data backfill** (existing vectors are invisible to every
scoped caller until the `"__shared__"` sentinel is written): redis,
couchbase, cassandra — `migrate_sentinel_vectordbs.py`.
- **Schema:** pgvector, singlestore — `migrate_sql_vectordbs.py`.
milvus, lancedb, clickhouse, surrealdb — `migrate_field_vectordbs.py`;
milvus needs both the field and the sentinel backfill, and that one
script does both.
- **No migration needed:** qdrant, upstash, mongodb, pinecone, chromadb,
opensearch, valkey.
- **Weaviate cannot be migrated in place.** The shared-bucket filter
needs `index_null_state=True`, which Weaviate only accepts at collection
creation. Recreate the collection through the v3 adapter and re-ingest.
Do **not** add the `user_id` property by hand — the collection then
reports as migrated while every unscoped query throws `Nullstate must be
indexed to be filterable!`, and since `content_hash_exists` runs that
filter on every ingest, `Knowledge.insert` breaks irreparably.
- **Milvus** needs 2.6+ (`AddCollectionField`); on 2.5.x recreate and
re-ingest. Milvus Lite cannot do isolation at all — it drops scalar
fields on the search read path.
- **Couchbase** needs its FTS index updated as well as the document
backfill; pass `search_index_name` in the migration config, or add
`user_id` to the FTS mapping with `analyzer: "keyword"` manually.

### 3. Rewrite removed API surface

- Rename the memory/session params: `enable_user_memories` →
`update_memory_on_run`, `search_session_history` →
`search_past_sessions`, `num_history_sessions` →
`num_past_sessions_to_search`.
- Replace `continue_run(updated_tools=[...])` with
`continue_run(requirements=[RunRequirement(...)])`.
- Rewrite `Agent(reasoning=True)` as `Agent(reasoning_model=<a native
reasoning model>)`. Native families detected: DeepSeek-R1, Anthropic
thinking, OpenAI o-series, Groq, Ollama, Azure AI Foundry, Gemini,
VertexAI. Anything else emits an error event and produces no reasoning —
use `ReasoningTools` for manual chain-of-thought. Note that
`reasoning_agent` customizes native reasoning; it does not replace it.
- Convert positional `Team` / `Workflow` construction to keywords.
`Team([a, b])` still works; anything after `members` must be a keyword.
- Rewrite every workflow primitive that used flat HITL kwargs to
`human_review=HumanReview(...)`, and **re-save any component that was
serialized before this change** — its HITL config is dropped on load
with a warning.
- Rewrite workflow custom functions, `Condition` evaluators and `Router`
selectors that took `session_state` to accept `run_context: RunContext`.
A parameter with no default now raises a missing-argument `TypeError`; a
parameter **with** a default silently receives the default.
- Remove `culture_table=` from every db constructor before upgrading, or
construction raises `TypeError`. Drop orphaned `agno_culture` tables
yourself if you want the space back.
- Move the Google toolkit imports to `agno.tools.google.*`; rewrite
`MultiMCPTools` as a list of `MCPTools`.
- Update StudioTools call sites: the six constructor renames, drop
`db_id` from `create_agent`, and add `publish=True` (or a
`publish_component` step) anywhere 2.x code relied on `create_*`
publishing immediately. Prompts naming `list_agents` / `get_agent` /
`delete_agent` / `list_dbs` must move to `list_components` /
`get_component` / `archive_component` / `restore_component`.
- Move AgentOS clients off `GET /models` and `GET /` metadata; move A2A
clients to the entity-scoped routes; replace `enable_mcp_server=` /
`mcp_config=` with `mcp_server=`, and `secret_key=` with
`verification_keys=`.
- Anything catching `ValueError` around a database call to detect a
stale schema must catch `agno.exceptions.SchemaMismatchError` /
`MigrationRequiredError`.
- Custom `VectorDb` subclasses: add `user_id: Optional[str] = None` to
the eight abstract methods. Custom `Knowledge` implementations used with
`Agent(update_knowledge=True)` must accept `user_id` (or `**kwargs`) on
their insert method, or the `add_to_knowledge` tool returns an error
rather than storing into the shared bucket.
- Subclasses of `OpenAIResponses` / `OpenResponses` overriding
`get_request_params` must add `run_response: Optional[RunOutput] =
None`.

### 4. Enabling `user_isolation` on an existing deployment

There is no backfill or claim step. Stamp `user_id` onto pre-isolation
eval runs, components, knowledge rows, learnings and service accounts
**before** turning isolation on. Unowned components and knowledge stay
readable and runnable by everyone but editable only by an admin; unowned
eval rows become invisible to a scoped caller; a scoped write to an
unowned row is refused (403 for knowledge, learnings and service
accounts).

One metrics row is deleted as the `user_id` column lands — the unowned
`completed = false` row with the newest date, and only when that date
sits past every completed day. The recalculation rebuilds that day from
its sessions, so nothing is lost **unless you prune sessions before
migrating**. Migrate first, prune after.

### 5. Reinstall extras

`agno[postgres]` now pulls `sqlalchemy` + `psycopg[binary]`. Floors
moved: `anthropic>=0.77.0`, `openai>=1.106.0`, `mistralai>=2.0.0`,
`redis>=4.5.4`. `agno[mistral]` is re-enabled inside the `models`
aggregate.

New extras:
- `agno[code]` for CodeMode — needs **Python >= 3.10**; the pins carry
`python_version >= '3.10'` markers so the install resolves on 3.9 but
the import then raises.
- `agno[finance]` for `FinanceTools`' default YFinance provider.
- `agno[s3]` for S3 media storage; `agno[gcs]` for GCS. Local disk needs
nothing.

If you pass a custom `http_client` to any Claude class and install
`anthropic>=1.0.0`, it must now be an httpx2 client — an `httpx.Client`
is dropped with a warning and the SDK default is used instead.

### 6. Optional runtime configuration

- `AGNO_BACKGROUND_MAX_CONCURRENCY` or
`AgentOS(queue=QueueConfig(max_concurrency=...))` tunes the
background-run cap (default 32; 0 or below disables limiting).
- `QueueConfig(durable=True)` requires sync `PostgresDb`,
`AsyncPostgresDb` or `RedisDb`. SQLite raises at startup. Across a
fleet, `lock_grace_seconds`, `stop_timeout_seconds`,
`retention_seconds`, `max_attempts` and `timeout_seconds` must be
configured **uniformly**, including transiently during a rolling deploy.
- Several AgentOS deployments sharing one Redis must set
`RedisCoordination(key_prefix=...)` per deployment or they read each
other's runs by run_id.
- SuperGrok OAuth needs `XAI_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (there is
deliberately no `AGNO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` fallback) and a Postgres or SQLite
db for the auth-tokens table; other backends degrade to a 0600 file or
process memory, which cannot hold per-user sessions.

## Additional Notes

### Blocking before merge or tag

1. **Version is `3.0.0a3`.** `libs/agno/pyproject.toml` still says
`3.0.0a3`, and 3.0.0a1/a2/a3 are all already on PyPI. `release.yml`
checks whether `project.version` exists on PyPI and skips the build
**reporting success** if it does — so publishing a `3.0.0` GitHub
Release from this branch today would produce three green jobs, zero
artifacts, and no error. Bump to `3.0.0` before tagging, and consider
adding a guard step that fails when the tag name does not match the
pyproject version.
2. ~~**`agnoctl` must be bumped.**~~ Done in #9712: agnoctl 0.1.3 ->
**0.2.0**, and agno's floor raised to `agnoctl>=0.2.0`. #9600 added ~900
lines and a new hard runtime dependency (`questionary`) under the
already-published 0.1.3, so the release workflow would have skipped it
and every v3.0.0 installer would have got the stale CLI. `agno-infra` is
byte-identical to main and does not need to move.
3. ~~**`libs/agno/tests/integration/db/` (61 files) is run by no CI
job**~~ Fixed in #9712, which adds a `test-db` job and repairs the six
failing tests (all test-side debt; no product bug). Original finding:
**`libs/agno/tests/integration/db/` (61 files) was run by no CI job** —
`test-remaining` explicitly `--ignore`s it, and its service-free SQLite
subset is **red on this head**:
`test_service_accounts.py::test_token_hash_lookup_reraises_on_db_error`
fails ("DID NOT RAISE"). That test pins that a dead DB connection must
raise so the verifier returns 503 rather than misreading it as an
unknown token (401) — an auth fail-open. 12 v3.0 commits touched
`db/sqlite/`, #9623 (table-resolution cache) being the likely cause. 102
tests, 0.81 s, no infrastructure. Triage before merging.
4. **`main` branch protection requires zero status checks.**
`required_status_checks.contexts` and `.checks` are both empty, so none
of the green checks gate this merge; the only enforced gate is one
approving review (`enforce_admins: false`, `allow_force_pushes: true`).
Populate the required checks before merging, at minimum `tests
(1/5)`..`(5/5)`, the four `style-check-*` jobs and `Lint PR Title and
Body`.
5. ~~**`test-clean` / `test-clean-os` certify PyPI agno.**~~ Fixed in
#9712 — both now install the branch. Until that merges, neither gate
says anything about v3.0.
6. **`requests` is imported unguarded but declared in no extra.**
`agno/utils/location.py:3` and `agno/utils/certs.py:3` import `requests`
at module level; it appears in `pyproject.toml` only in the mypy ignore
list. `Agent(add_location_to_context=True)` — a documented public kwarg
— still *constructs* on a core-only install; every run then raises
`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'requests'` while building the
system message. Pre-existing in 2.x; it should not ship in 3.0.0.
Replace with `httpx` (already core) or declare the dependency.
(`certs.py` has no in-tree callers, so it is a latent risk only.)
7. ~~**`libs/agno/requirements.txt` pins `agnoctl==0.1.0a4`**~~ Fixed in
#9712 — regenerated, and it now also carries `questionary`,
`prompt-toolkit` and `wcwidth`, which it was missing.
8. **Real bug found by local mypy that CI cannot see:**
`libs/agno/agno/models/aws/claude.py:163` calls
`self.async_client.close()` from a sync `def get_async_client`. `close`
is a coroutine function, so the coroutine is discarded and never awaited
— the Bedrock connection pool is *not* closed, which is exactly what the
comment three lines above claims it prevents. CI's mypy job installs
only `.[dev]`, so `anthropic` is absent and the error is silenced.
9. **The migration guide does not ship.** `V3_MIGRATION_GUIDE.md` (665
lines, the most complete migration document in the release) lives inside
the package tree, but `pyproject.toml` declares `package-data =
["py.typed"]` with no `MANIFEST.in`, so setuptools packages only `.py`
files. Code references the guide by name (`v3_0_0.py:113`) but a `pip
install agno` user never gets it, and there is no cookbook and no docs
page. Publish it to docs.agno.com or add it to package-data before
release. Two content bugs to fix while doing so: the guide's Step 2 and
"How writes work now" claim that writes null the legacy `runs` column —
every adapter deliberately does the opposite (the guide's own Breaking
changes section states this correctly), which means
`cleanup_legacy_runs_column()` without `force=True` can never succeed as
Step 3 presents it; and Breaking changes #3 names only the four
Postgres/SQLite adapters as accepting `runs_table`, when MySQL,
AsyncMySQL, SingleStore and Mongo (`runs_collection`) do too.

### Known limitations shipping in 3.0

- **Three vector DBs accept `user_id` and ignore it:** `langchaindb`,
`llamaindex`, `lightrag` log a warning and return unscoped results.
Isolation covers 17 of 20 backends, not all. Release copy must not claim
otherwise.
- **A dropped `user_id` degrades to the admin view, not to an error.**
Correct for single-user deployments, but any missed plumbing is a silent
full-corpus read rather than a visible failure.
- **Studio's component catalog is sync-only on `SqliteDb` and
`PostgresDb`.** `AsyncBaseDb` raises `NotImplementedError` for every
component method, and AgentOS mounts a 503 `/components` router. AgentOS
on `AsyncPostgresDb` loses the whole catalog.
- **The durable queue works on Postgres and Redis only**; every other
adapter raises at startup. `QueueConfig(durable=True)` is also not a
blanket guarantee: remote/factory/version-pinned components, media
uploads and non-JSON-serializable kwargs fall back to the bounded
in-process path with a logged warning.
- **Tool-result offloading works on Postgres and SQLite only.** On any
other adapter it warns once and runs with offloading off. The warning is
once-per-owner, so it is easy to miss in production.
- **`ClickhouseDb` has no v3.0.0 migration branch and still stores runs
inline** (traces/spans only); `InMemoryDb` also stores runs inline. The
O(N²) → O(N) fix is not universal.
- **SingleStore's runs table cannot enforce `run_id` uniqueness**
(`PRIMARY KEY (run_id, session_id)` with `SHARD KEY (session_id)`):
`get_run` returns one row unordered, `upsert_run` inserts instead of
updating, `delete_run` removes every copy across sessions. It also keeps
no unique constraint on metrics, so two concurrent refreshes can
double-write a bucket.
- **Schedules exist on Postgres, SQLite and Mongo only**, yet the
migration adds `user_id` to `schedules`/`schedule_runs` across all seven
SQL adapters.
- **Learnings REST scope gap carried forward from #9322:** the API
filters on the owner column rather than the namespace, so a
`quarantined_user` row is still listed, patched and deleted by whichever
user the owner column names, and `DELETE /learnings/users/{other}` does
not reach it. "Quarantined" is scoped to the entity store, not absolute.
Re-run any pre-fix erasure requests after migrating.
- **`enable_agentic_memory` and a `LearningMachine` with a user-memory
store still conflict outside Studio.** Both register a tool named
`update_user_memory`; tool parsing keeps the first, and the learning
store's tool is dropped silently. Studio's create/edit path clears the
legacy pair; a code-defined `Agent(enable_agentic_memory=True,
learning=...)` is not guarded.
- **CodeMode is not a sandbox.** It runs arbitrary Python and shell with
the permissions of the agent process, and snapshot restore is `dill`
unpickling, so the snapshot store inherits the trust level of the
database holding it. This belongs in the docs prominently, not only in a
docstring.
- **`checkpoint="tools"` still raises `NotImplementedError('... reserved
for the 3.0 runs-table split and not available yet')`** — on the 3.0
branch, after the split landed. Either finish it or reword the message
and docstring.
- **The one benchmark Agno still loses:** the 25-turn durable (SQLite)
conversation at 42.2 ms vs LangGraph's 36.5 ms (0.9x), documented in
`cookbook/performance/README.md`. Remaining gap is per-turn
serialization of session state that grows with conversation length.
- **16 of 21 provider CI suites are statically disabled** (`if: false`).
Cohere, Fireworks, DashScope, Cerebras, IBM watsonx, LangDB, AImlAPI,
SambaNova, Together and NVIDIA also have no unit-level substitute, so
those model classes ship in 3.0 with zero executed tests.
`test-cerebras`'s disable has no stated reason (added in a release-batch
commit, #7494) and should be triaged or documented.
- **Two deferred removals** that will break again in a later release
rather than at 3.0: `LearningMode.HITL` is kept, and standalone SSE as
an MCP transport is kept with its deprecation upgraded from `log_info`
to `log_warning`. Both carry "will be removed in a future release" into
the whole 3.x line.
- **Toolkit parameter naming is inconsistent at 3.0.** #9690 (`enable_X`
→ `X` with back-compat) is still open. New `FinanceTools` uses
unprefixed flags, `GoogleSheetsTools`/`GoogleBigQueryTools` renamed with
`enable_*` kept as aliases, and ~100 other toolkits still take
`enable_*` as the primary name. `FinanceTools` also ships alongside
`YFinanceTools`, `FinancialDatasetsTools` and `OpenBBTools` with no
deprecation on any of the three, so there are four overlapping finance
surfaces and no signal about which is canonical.
- **`Function.has_side_effects` has no ergonomic setter** — it is not a
`@tool` decorator parameter and no in-tree toolkit sets it, so Studio's
discovery reports `None` for every shipped tool. Effectively unused at
release.
- **`agno-infra` overwrites `agno/__init__.py` with an empty file** when
installed after `agno`, breaking `from agno.os import AgentOS` and
flipping the `agno` console script. Order-dependent (a single-shot `pip
install agno[infra]` is fine), reachable via the `infra`, `docker` and
`aws` extras.
- ~~**`libs/agno/agno/table.py` is a committed scratch script**~~
Deleted in #9712. It shipped in the wheel and dropped the `agno_spans`
table on import.

### Follow-ups after 3.0.0 is published

- Regenerate the four cookbook lockfiles still pinning agno 2.x
(`cookbook/00_quickstart`, `cookbook/08_learning`, `cookbook/01_demo`,
`cookbook/data_labeling/image_search`). This must wait until a stable
tag exists, since `uv pip compile` will not resolve to a pre-release.
- Recover the Tier 4 (silent deprecations needing a warning cycle) and
Tier 5 (data-migration-gated, e.g. the Qdrant unnamed-vector layer)
lists from #9560's PR body — the audit document that drove them was
deleted from the tree by `c2a25f9bc`.
- `AgentOSConfig.available_models: List[str]` still exists but nothing
reads it after #7647 — dead configuration a user can set with no effect.
- #9667 (wake the local queue worker on enqueue) is still open, so
durable submissions wait for the worker's next poll tick.
- Re-verify `git rev-list --count $(git merge-base origin/main
origin/feat/v3.0)..origin/main == 0` immediately before merging. It is 0
today, which is the only reason the push-triggered integration matrix
and the pull_request merge-ref agree; `test_on_release.yml` has no
`pull_request` trigger, so anything landing on main first leaves the
merged state unverified.
